# Phase 1b: Forms Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Finish the spec's phase 1 catalog on the merged phase 1a foundation. That means IconButton, Link, the field parts, TextField, TextArea, Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup, Switch, SegmentedControl, Card, Heading, Text, Eyebrow, Kbd and Badge. Each one ships its CSS, React component, tests, stories, visual baselines, docs page and changeset, and replaces the docs site's hand-drawn stand-in.

**Architecture:**
- Every component draws from one CSS file in `packages/core/src/components/`, inside `@layer components` and on tokens only.
- Interactive components wrap React Aria Components and carry `'use client'`. Static ones (Heading, Text, Eyebrow, Kbd, Badge, Card and FieldCounter) are plain server components.
- Every field follows one root contract set in Task 5. Its root has the `field` class, plus `data-changed` and `data-invalid` when they apply, then a label row with a Changed chip, the control, the hint, the error and the counter. Every field uses the same internal helpers, `useChangedDescription` and `FieldHead` from Task 6, and `useValueLength` from Task 7.
- The docs site gets one page per component, listed alphabetically in the rail, and deletes each stand-in the moment the real class ships.

**Tech Stack:** the phase 1a stack, unchanged. That is pnpm 10.10, Turborepo 2.11, Node 24.5 or later, TypeScript 7 (`tsc`) beside the TypeScript 6 API, Style Dictionary 5.6, Lightning CSS 1.33, Stylelint 17, Tailwind CSS 4.3, React 19.3, react-aria-components 1.22, tsdown 0.23, Vitest 5 with jsdom 30, Testing Library, axe-core, Storybook 10.6, Playwright 1.64, Next.js 16.4, fumadocs-core 16.17, fumadocs-mdx 15.4, fumadocs-typescript 5.5, ESLint 10, Prettier 3.9, Changesets 3.0 and size-limit 14.

**Spec:** `docs/specs/2026-10-10-snapshot-ui-design.md`, sections 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11. The design authority is `docs/design-system.md`, including Appendix B. It outranks the spec's catalog notes wherever the two disagree. For example, the textarea radius is the document's 20px, not the catalog's 24px.

**Source app:** the private app this library is extracted from. Its absolute path is in `.local/SOURCE.md`, which is gitignored. Paths such as `styles/primitives/field.css` below are relative to it. Read it, but never copy its name or its class names into a committed file.

**How this plan was made:** every task was built and run in a scratch copy of the repository before it was written down. All tasks were then replayed in this order, each on top of the last, with every gate green after each one. So every code block below is the exact file the task produces at that point, and every edit to an existing file is exact text that applies on top of the previous task. Test totals are given as "the N tests this task adds", with the totals observed at that point in parentheses. If your totals differ only because a Docker step was skipped, that is expected. Any other difference is a finding.

## Global Constraints

### Runtime and packaging

- Node `>=24.5`, `"packageManager": "pnpm@10.10.0"`, every package `"type": "module"`, ESM only.
- React and React DOM are peers at `^19.0.0`. `react-aria-components` `^1.22.1` and `lucide-react` `^1.55.0` are dependencies of `@snapshot-ui/react`. `@snapshot-ui/core` is an optional peer of it.
- TypeScript runs side by side through the pnpm catalog. `typescript` is `npm:@typescript/typescript6@^6.0.2`, the API that tooling imports. `@typescript/native` is `npm:typescript@^7.0.2`, the `tsc` command.

### React components

- Every source file that imports `react-aria-components` starts with `'use client';`. The React build fails if an emitted file loses the directive.
- Static components import no React Aria and carry no directive.
- Never write `export * from 'react-aria-components...'`. Use named re-exports only.
- Use React Aria 1.22's current compositions, `CheckboxField` + `CheckboxButton`, `RadioField` + `RadioButton` and `SwitchField` + `SwitchButton`. Never use the deprecated bare `Checkbox`, `Radio` or `Switch`.
- `className` and `ref`:
  - A standalone field (TextField, TextArea, Checkbox, Switch and every group) puts them on its field root.
  - A group item (Radio, SegmentedControlItem) puts them on its visible label row.
  - `className` takes a string or React Aria's render function and merges after the library's class.

### CSS

- Component CSS lives in `packages/core/src/components/<name>.css`, inside `@layer components`, imported from `src/styles.css`, and uses only tokens.
- No literal color, radius or shadow appears outside `tokens/tokens.json`. The Stylelint rule `snapshot-ui/token-only` enforces this, and it also forbids `light-dark()`.
- `box-shadow` takes only `var(--shadow-*)` or `none`.
- The only non-token colors allowed are CSS system colors, and only inside a `@media (forced-colors: active)` block.
- Class names are unprefixed kebab-case: the block (`input`), a variant (`badge-info`) and a part (`field-label`).
- No class starts with a Tailwind utility namespace (`text-`, `row-`, `grid-`, `bg-`, `size-`, `p-` and the rest in `packages/core/stylelint.config.js`). That is why Text's classes are `copy`, `copy-small` and `copy-muted`.
- States are data attributes with React Aria's names. Every state selector also matches the native pseudo-class or the plain-HTML equivalent, so one stylesheet serves React and plain HTML: `:is(:focus-visible, [data-focus-visible])`, `:is([data-selected], :has(:checked))`. Hover rules sit inside `@media (hover: hover)`.
- The focus ring is `outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color); outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);`. A core test fails any component file whose outline uses `var(--color-ink)`. An inset ring on an ink fill uses `var(--color-canvas)`.
- Control edges use `--color-boundary` (ink 50%). Outlines and lists use `--color-frame`, inner rules use `--color-divider` and disabled fills use `--color-disabled`.
- Cursor is `pointer` on every interactive control and `not-allowed` when disabled.
- Reduced motion turns every transition off. Core components never animate their shape.

### Field states

- Changed: the field root carries `data-changed`, and a clay "Changed" chip shows in the label row. It is announced through `aria-describedby` while it shows. Its text comes from `changedLabel`, which defaults to "Changed".
- The light orange changed edge appears only on text controls (TextField, TextArea) and on the outer track or row of a composite control (SegmentedControl's track, and Switch's row ring outside its track).
- Choice groups (CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup) show changed by the chip alone, because their item edges are required 3:1 boundaries.
- Invalid always outranks changed, for edges and for the chip.

### Design rules

- Theme axes: `data-theme="light" | "dark"`, where no attribute follows the system. `data-shape="rounded" | "soft" | "square"` matches case-insensitively. Both work on any element.
- Typography: weights 400, 450, 500 and 700 only. 14px is the minimum for sentences, and 12px for short uppercase labels.
- Responsive: everything works from 320px wide with no sideways scrolling, and every touch target is at least 40px. A control drawn smaller extends its hit area with a pseudo-element.
- Reserved colors:
  - Signal orange is consent only, and no 1b component uses it.
  - Light signal orange is the attention cue: the changed edge, eyebrow and accent dots.
  - Clay means unsaved, so it is used only for the Changed chip.
  - Error means invalid or failed, and success means success.
  - None of them is ever decoration, including in sample content.
  - Taupe is only for placeholders and disabled text.
- A new text-on-ground or edge-on-ground color pairing goes into `CONTRAST_PAIRS` in `packages/core/scripts/contrast.js` with a test, and its measurement goes into the component's Appendix B section.

### Docs site

- Component pages go in `apps/docs/content/docs/components/<slug>.mdx`.
- `components/meta.json` and `apps/docs/examples/index.ts` are kept alphabetical.
- A docs stand-in whose class name a core component now owns is deleted in the same task, because same-named classes in the same layer merge rather than replace.
- Docs e2e runs on port 3100 by default. Set `DOCS_E2E_PORT` to run two checkouts at once.

### Repo, commits and releases

- The repo is public. Never commit the source company's name, its CMS's name or any client name, not even inside a test or a script. `pnpm check:public` enforces this from patterns that live only in the gitignored `.local/private-names.txt` and in CI's `PRIVATE_NAMES` secret.
- No em dashes and no emojis in code, docs or commit messages. Commit messages never mention Claude Code and never carry a Co-Authored-By line.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits, with the exact message each task gives.
- Run `pnpm format` before every commit, because CI fails on unformatted code.
- Generate visual baselines only with `pnpm --filter @snapshot-ui/storybook visual:docker`, inside `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.0-noble`, the image CI compares in. Commit the new PNGs in the task that adds the stories.
- Every component task adds a changeset releasing `@snapshot-ui/core` and `@snapshot-ui/react` together as minor.

## Review Focus

These are the five input classes or conditions the spec implies that the component tasks' own tests do not exercise, most likely first. They can only be checked once every component exists, so Task 13 pins each one with a test, and fixes any component that fails it.

1. **Windows high contrast (`forced-colors: active`).** A switch's on or off state and a segmented control's selected option are drawn with fills, which forced colors replace. A user must still be able to tell on from off, and the selected option from the others.
2. **Right-to-left layouts (`dir="rtl"` via React Aria's `I18nProvider`).** The label row, the Changed chip, the counter, the switch thumb, the check marks and the segmented track must mirror, with nothing clipped or overlapping.
3. **Native form reset.** A plain `<form>` reset must restore every field's `defaultValue` or `defaultSelected`, and the counter and the Changed chip must follow. One React Aria bug is documented in Task 8, for a CheckboxGroup reset that both adds and removes values.
4. **Long unbroken content at 320px.** A long URL or word in a label, a hint, an error, a badge, a segmented option or a card note must wrap or scroll inside its own box, with no sideways scroll on any component page.
5. **Server Component use.** Heading, Text, Eyebrow, Kbd, Badge, Card and FieldCounter must render from a React Server Component with no `'use client'`. The client components must import cleanly into one.

**Files:**
- Modify: `packages/core/tokens/tokens.json` (add `focus-ring.color`)
- Modify: `packages/core/scripts/build-tokens.js` (keep a token reference as `var()` and repeat it in every theme scope)
- Modify: `packages/core/src/base.css`, `packages/core/src/components/button.css`
- Modify: `apps/docs/app/site.css`, `apps/docs/components/shell/shell.css`, `apps/docs/app/(home)/home.css`
- Modify: `packages/react/package.json`, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` (pnpm rewrites it)
- Modify: `apps/docs/playwright.config.ts` (the e2e port can be overridden)
- Test: `packages/core/test/tokens.test.js`, `packages/core/test/css.test.js`
- Modify: `docs/design-system.md` (two additions to Appendix B)
- Create: `.changeset/focus-ring-color.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the phase 1a token pipeline (`tokens.json`, `build-tokens.js`, the generated `dist/tokens.css`) and the `--color-ink` token.
- Produces: the variable `--focus-ring-color`, written `var(--color-ink)` on `:root` and again in `[data-theme="dark"]`, `[data-theme="light"]` and the `prefers-color-scheme` block. In JavaScript, `tokens['focus-ring'].color.var` is `'var(--focus-ring-color)'`.
- Produces the focus ring rule every later task copies, exactly: `outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color); outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);`. An inset ring on an ink fill stays `outline-color: var(--color-canvas)`. `packages/core/test/css.test.js` now fails any file in `src/components` whose `outline` or `outline-color` declaration contains `var(--color-ink)`.
- Produces a build rule: a base token whose `$value` is a reference such as `"{color.ink}"` is written as `var(--color-ink)`, and any such token that refers to something a theme axis changes is declared again in each scope of that axis.
- Produces the environment variable `DOCS_E2E_PORT`: `pnpm --filter @snapshot-ui/docs test:e2e` serves and tests the production docs build on that port, default 3100, so two checkouts can run e2e at once without testing each other's build.
- Produces `@snapshot-ui/core` as an optional peer of `@snapshot-ui/react` (`workspace:^` in the repository, a concrete range such as `^0.0.0` in the packed `package.json`).

**Which way the token is emitted.** Spec 5.1 lists `--focus-ring-color` as ink. It is emitted as a reference, `--focus-ring-color: var(--color-ink);`, not as two copied values, and that needs a small build change:

- Style Dictionary resolves a reference such as `{color.ink}` before a format runs. The unchanged build writes `--focus-ring-color: #141413;` on `:root` and nowhere else, and the dark blocks only list tokens that carry a dark value, so a dark page would draw a dark ring on a dark canvas.
- The format now reads each token's `original.$value` and writes every `{path}` in it as `var(--name)`. Ink stays the single source: a theme that overrides `--color-ink` recolors the rings with it, and the dark value is never typed a second time.
- A custom property that holds `var()` resolves on the element that declares it, so `:root` alone would hand a nested `[data-theme]` scope the page's ink. Measured in Chromium with the reference on `:root` only: a dark scope inside a light page drew a `rgb(20, 20, 19)` ring on a dark surface, and a light scope inside a dark page drew a white one. The format therefore also repeats every token that refers to a token an axis changes in each scope of that axis, the same way it repeats `color: var(--color-ink)`. Today that is this one token, in the three theme blocks, and none in the shape blocks.
- Per-mode values (light `#141413`, dark `#ffffff`) were the fallback if the build could not keep a reference. It can, so they are not used.
- `dist/tokens.js` holds the resolved light value in `value` (`#141413`) and no `modes` entry for this token. Read `.var` for the live value.

In `packages/core/scripts/build-tokens.js` make four edits.

Edit 1, the file header. After the line:

add these lines, so the header comment ends with the new paragraph and `import StyleDictionary from 'style-dictionary';` follows:

```js
//
// A base $value may be a reference such as "{color.ink}". The CSS keeps it as
// var(--color-ink) instead of resolving it, so it follows the mode it is read
// in, and every scope of an axis that changes the target declares it again.
```

Edit 2, the helpers. Insert this block directly before the comment `/** Splits all tokens into base tokens and axis -> variant -> declarations. */`:

```js
const REFERENCE = /\{([^{}]+)\}/g;

/** The paths a base token's $value refers to, as written: "{color.ink}" is color.ink. */
const referencesOf = (token) =>
  typeof token.original.$value === 'string'
    ? [...token.original.$value.matchAll(REFERENCE)].map((m) => m[1])
    : [];

/** The base token a reference path names. */
function target(path, byPath) {
  const found = byPath.get(path);
  if (!found) throw new Error(`Unknown token reference {${path}}`);
  return found;
}

/**
 * The value a base token declares. A reference stays a var() to the variable it
 * names; every other value is the resolved and transformed one.
 */
function cssValue(token, byPath) {
  if (referencesOf(token).length === 0) return token.$value;
  return token.original.$value.replace(REFERENCE, (_, path) => `var(--${target(path, byPath).name})`);
}

/**
 * Base tokens that refer, directly or through each other, to a token the axis
 * changes. A custom property that holds var() resolves where it is declared, so
 * --focus-ring-color: var(--color-ink) on :root would hand a nested
 * [data-theme="dark"] scope the page's ink instead of its own. Each scope
 * declares these again, as it does `color`.
 */
function followers(base, changed, byPath) {
  const names = new Set(changed);
  const found = [];
  for (let grew = true; grew;) {
    grew = false;
    for (const t of base) {
      if (names.has(t.name)) continue;
      if (referencesOf(t).some((path) => names.has(target(path, byPath).name))) {
        names.add(t.name);
        found.push(t);
        grew = true;
      }
    }
  }
  return found;
}
```

```js
// Throwaway proof, not committed. Run from the repository root after building core.
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const require = createRequire(path.resolve('apps/docs/package.json'));
const { chromium } = require('@playwright/test');
const tokens = readFileSync(path.resolve('packages/core/dist/tokens.css'), 'utf8');

const html = (attrs) => `<!doctype html><html ${attrs}><head><style>${tokens}
.probe:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color); }
</style></head><body>
<button id="page" class="probe">page</button>
<div data-theme="dark"><button id="dark-scope" class="probe">dark scope</button></div>
<div data-theme="light"><button id="light-scope" class="probe">light scope</button></div>
</body></html>`;

const browser = await chromium.launch();
for (const [label, attrs, scheme] of [
  ['page light', 'data-theme="light"', 'light'],
  ['page dark', 'data-theme="dark"', 'light'],
  ['no attribute, system light', '', 'light'],
  ['no attribute, system dark', '', 'dark'],
]) {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ colorScheme: scheme });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.setContent(html(attrs));
  const rings = {};
  for (const id of ['page', 'dark-scope', 'light-scope']) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    rings[id] = await page.$eval(`#${id}`, (el) => getComputedStyle(el).outlineColor);
  }
  console.log(label.padEnd(28), JSON.stringify(rings));
  await context.close();
}
await browser.close();
```

Expected, one line per page setup, with the ring color of the page button, of a button inside `data-theme="dark"` and of a button inside `data-theme="light"`:

```text
page light                   {"page":"rgb(20, 20, 19)","dark-scope":"rgb(255, 255, 255)","light-scope":"rgb(20, 20, 19)"}
page dark                    {"page":"rgb(255, 255, 255)","dark-scope":"rgb(255, 255, 255)","light-scope":"rgb(20, 20, 19)"}
no attribute, system light   {"page":"rgb(20, 20, 19)","dark-scope":"rgb(255, 255, 255)","light-scope":"rgb(20, 20, 19)"}
no attribute, system dark    {"page":"rgb(255, 255, 255)","dark-scope":"rgb(255, 255, 255)","light-scope":"rgb(20, 20, 19)"}
```

(The page carries its own `.probe` rule, so the script needs no component CSS. Deleting the `--focus-ring-color` line from every block but `:root` in `dist/tokens.css` makes the `dark-scope` entry on the light page read `rgb(20, 20, 19)` and the `light-scope` entry on the dark page read white, which is the failure the repeated declaration prevents.)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `cx` from `packages/react/src/utils/cx.ts`; `expectNoA11yViolations` from `packages/react/test/a11y.ts`; the type tokens (`--text-h1` to `--text-h4`, `--text-body`, `--text-small`, `--text-eyebrow`, each with its `--line-height`, `--letter-spacing` where it has one, and `--font-weight`), `--font-sans`, `--color-slate`, `--color-signal-light`, `--radius-dot`, `--spacing-part`, and the breakpoint tokens `--breakpoint-sm` (768px) and `--breakpoint-md` (1024px). Task 1's guard in `css.test.js` applies to the new files: none of them draws a focus ring.
- Produces `Heading(props: HeadingProps): ReactElement` and `type HeadingLevel = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4`. `HeadingProps` is `HTMLAttributes<HTMLHeadingElement>` plus `level?: HeadingLevel` (default `2`, the element, `h1` to `h4`), `size?: HeadingLevel` (default `level`, the look) and `ref?: Ref<HTMLHeadingElement>`. It renders `class="heading heading-{size}"` with `className` merged last.
- Produces `Text(props: TextProps): ReactElement`, `type TextElement = 'p' | 'span' | 'div'`, `type TextSize = 'body' | 'small'` and `type TextTone = 'default' | 'muted'`. `TextProps` is `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>` plus `as?: TextElement` (default `'p'`), `size?: TextSize` (default `'body'`), `tone?: TextTone` (default `'default'`) and `ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>`. It renders `copy`, then `copy-small` when `size` is `'small'`, then `copy-muted` when `tone` is `'muted'`, then `className`.
- Produces `Eyebrow(props: EyebrowProps): ReactElement` and `type EyebrowElement = 'p' | 'span' | 'div'`. `EyebrowProps` is `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>` plus `as?: EyebrowElement` (default `'p'`) and `ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>`. It renders `eyebrow` with `className` merged last. It is a label and never a heading.
- All three are static: no `'use client'` and no `react-aria-components` import. `packages/react/src/typography/static.test.ts` pins that, and Kbd, Badge and Card follow the same pattern. Named exports from `src/index.ts`: `Eyebrow`, `Heading`, `Text`, `EyebrowElement`, `EyebrowProps`, `HeadingLevel`, `HeadingProps`, `TextElement`, `TextProps`, `TextSize`, `TextTone`.
- Produces the classes `heading`, `heading-1` to `heading-4`, `copy`, `copy-small`, `copy-muted` and `eyebrow`. Each sets `margin: 0` and `font-family: var(--font-sans)`, so spacing is the layout's job. `heading-1` is 64px, 48px under 1024px and 40px under 768px; `heading-2` is 36px, 28px under 768px; `heading-3` and `heading-4` do not scale. The eyebrow's dot is `.eyebrow::before`, 6px, hung 14px into the leading gutter with `margin-inline-start`, so a caller who has no gutter sets `margin-inline-start: 0` on it.
- Produces in `css.test.js`: the helper `blockAfter(css, header)`, which returns the text between the braces that follow a header, nested blocks included.
- Produces in the docs: core owns `.eyebrow`, so the stand-in is gone and `.eyebrow-sep` stays docs-only. The docs header keeps `<p className="eyebrow">` (shared shell chrome with the `.eyebrow-sep` breadcrumb). Prose rules on `.docs-section p` and `li` no longer reach anything inside `.stage`, so later previews show `Text`, field descriptions and card notes with their own line height and measure.
- Produces in `docs.spec.ts`: the helper `railLinkInView(link)`. Later tasks add rail pages without touching the three drawer tests again.
- Leaves alone: the docs-only `.type-h1` to `.type-h4`, `.type-small` and `.muted` stand-ins in `site.css`. They do not share a name with a core class, so they do not collide.

**What this task decides** (all of it is also in the Appendix B text of Step 2):
- `level` and `size` are two props, and `size` follows `level`. The homepage frame cards (Task 12) are `h2` elements in the card-title step, so the outline does not skip a level.
- The class for Text is `copy`, not `text`: the Stylelint class pattern forbids a class that starts with `text-`.
- Heading is a plain `h1` to `h4`, not React Aria's Heading, which is a client module. The three components are plain elements, so a server component can use them.
- Text and Eyebrow are written with `createElement`, not JSX. The tag is one of three, and JSX checks the props against all three tags at once, so a `ref` typed `Ref<HTMLElement>` fails the check. `createElement` takes the union tag and keeps the public type honest. Heading uses JSX, since `h1` to `h4` share one ref type.
- Light signal orange for the dot, slate for the label and for the muted tone. No `CONTRAST_PAIRS` entry is added: slate on every ground is already in the gate, and the dot is decoration.
- Three story files, `Components/Heading`, `Components/Text` and `Components/Eyebrow`, next to the components. Each file's `component` drives its own props table in Storybook's docs, and every other component keeps one story file, so a single `Components/Typography` file could document only one of the three.
- The Typography docs page is appended to the rail after Spinner, so the existing pages keep their places.
- The eyebrow hangs its dot everywhere in the docs, the header included. On a phone the header's dot sits 2px from the menu button, and the label lines up with the page title, which was the point. Screenshots at 375, 768 and 1440 were checked.

- [ ] **Step 1: Capture the docs before any change**

The eyebrow stand-in is replaced by a rule that moves the dot, so look at the pages first. Save this throwaway script as `compare-docs.mjs` in a scratch folder outside the repository. It is not committed:

```js
// Throwaway, not committed. Full-page screenshots of four docs pages, and a pixel diff of two runs.
//   node /path/to/compare-docs.mjs shoot <label> <port>
//   node /path/to/compare-docs.mjs diff <labelA> <labelB>
// Run from the repository root, with the production docs server listening on <port> for `shoot`.
// Screenshots go to a `shots/<label>` folder next to this script.
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const require = createRequire(path.resolve('apps/docs/package.json'));
const { chromium } = require('@playwright/test');
const here = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), 'shots');

const PAGES = [
  ['button-1440', '/docs/components/button', 1440],
  ['button-375', '/docs/components/button', 375],
  ['theming-1440', '/docs/theming', 1440],
  ['home-1440', '/', 1440],
];

const [mode, first, second] = process.argv.slice(2);
const browser = await chromium.launch();

if (mode === 'shoot') {
  const out = path.join(here, first);
  mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
  for (const [name, url, width] of PAGES) {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height: 900 }, reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${second}${url}`);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    await page.waitForTimeout(600);
    await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(out, `${name}.png`), fullPage: true, animations: 'disabled' });
    await context.close();
    console.log('shot', name);
  }
} else if (mode === 'diff') {
  const page = await browser.newPage();
  for (const file of readdirSync(path.join(here, first)).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.png'))) {
    const read = (label) => `data:image/png;base64,${readFileSync(path.join(here, label, file)).toString('base64')}`;
    const result = await page.evaluate(
      async ([a, b]) => {
        const load = (src) =>
          new Promise((resolve) => {
            const image = new Image();
            image.onload = () => {
              const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
              canvas.width = image.width;
              canvas.height = image.height;
              const context = canvas.getContext('2d');
              context.drawImage(image, 0, 0);
              resolve(context.getImageData(0, 0, image.width, image.height));
            };
            image.src = src;
          });
        const [one, two] = await Promise.all([load(a), load(b)]);
        if (one.width !== two.width || one.height !== two.height) {
          return `size ${one.width}x${one.height} against ${two.width}x${two.height}`;
        }
        let count = 0;
        let box = [Infinity, Infinity, -1, -1];
        for (let y = 0; y < one.height; y += 1) {
          for (let x = 0; x < one.width; x += 1) {
            const i = (y * one.width + x) * 4;
            const d =
              Math.abs(one.data[i] - two.data[i]) +
              Math.abs(one.data[i + 1] - two.data[i + 1]) +
              Math.abs(one.data[i + 2] - two.data[i + 2]);
            if (d > 24) {
              count += 1;
              box = [Math.min(box[0], x), Math.min(box[1], y), Math.max(box[2], x), Math.max(box[3], y)];
            }
          }
        }
        return count === 0 ? 'identical' : `${count} px differ, within x ${box[0]} to ${box[2]}, y ${box[1]} to ${box[3]}`;
      },
      [read(first), read(second)],
    );
    console.log(file.padEnd(22), result);
  }
}
await browser.close();
```

The design system has no entry for how its type scale becomes components, so write the decisions down before building. Append to `docs/design-system.md`:

```markdown
## Typography

Heading, Text and Eyebrow are the document's hierarchy table with a class on
each row, so no size, weight or tracking here is new. These are the places the
library had to decide.

**The element and the look are two props.** `level` picks the element, `h1` to
`h4`, and `size` picks the type step, 1 to 4. `size` follows `level` unless it is
given. A page outline and a visual hierarchy are different things: a card title
is a small heading under the page's `h1`, and a hero line is a large heading
that is not the page title. If one prop did both, a heading would be picked for
its size and the outline would skip a level. `level` defaults to 2, because an
`h1` is once per page and the page decides where it goes.

**They are plain elements.** React Aria has a Heading, and it is the obvious
basis. It is a client module that exists to read a dialog's context, which
nothing here has, and type should work in a server component. So Heading is a
plain `h1` to `h4`, and Text and Eyebrow are a plain `p`, `span` or `div`. None
carries a client directive or imports React Aria.

**Headings scale down on small screens.** The document's responsive table says
the hero headline is about 48px on a tablet and about 40px on a phone. The
library makes that exact and carries it to the section step, which drops from
36px to 28px under 768px:

| Step | Token | 1024px and up | Under 1024px | Under 768px |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `heading-1` | `--text-h1` | 64px | 48px | 40px |
| `heading-2` | `--text-h2` | 36px | 36px | 28px |
| `heading-3` | `--text-h3` | 24px | 24px | 24px |
| `heading-4` | `--text-h4` | 14px | 14px | 14px |

The smaller sizes are in rem, so they follow the reader's browser font size as
the tokens do. Line height is a ratio, so it scales with the size and the 1:1
display step stays 1:1 at every width. A media query cannot read a custom
property, so the two widths are written out in `heading.css`. A test compares
them with `--breakpoint-md` and `--breakpoint-sm`, so they cannot drift. Under
768px the card title and the subhead are already small enough to stay.

**The class is `copy`, not `text`.** A class may not start with a Tailwind
namespace, and `text-` is one: `text-small` would collide in any app that also
uses Tailwind. Text renders `copy`, with `copy-small` and `copy-muted` added for
the small step and the muted tone. `copy` is the `--text-body` step, 16px at
weight 450, and `copy-small` is `--text-small`, 14px.

**Muted is slate, never taupe.** A muted sentence is still read, and the test in
"Where each text color may go" is whether the reader needs to read it. Slate on
canvas measures 4.83:1 in light and 7.25:1 in dark, and it is the lowest of the
grounds the contrast gate already lists for hints and notes, so no pairing was
added. Taupe fails AA on every surface.

**Spacing is the layout's.** Each class sets `margin: 0`, so the default margin
of a paragraph or a heading never adds to a gap the layout already chose.

**The eyebrow is a label.** It is 14px, 700, +4% tracking, in capitals and in
slate, which is the document's eyebrow row set in the color its text-color test
gives an eyebrow. It renders a `p`, `span` or `div` and never a heading, because
it labels the heading beside it and is not an entry in the outline. It is
`inline-flex`, so a span sits inside a line of text.

**The eyebrow's dot is Light Signal Orange.** The document is split on the dot's
color. Its palette lists eyebrow dots among the uses of Signal Orange, and its
prompt guide asks for a Light Signal Orange dot. The library takes the second
reading, because Signal Orange is reserved for consent and an eyebrow is not
consent, and because the app's own page header already draws its dot in Light
Signal Orange. The dot is 6px, and it takes `--radius-dot`, so it stays round in
every shape. It is always lit. The app's rail group label greys its dot until the
group holds the current page, which is navigation state, and an eyebrow has none.

The dot measures 2.52:1 on canvas in light, under the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks
of a graphic that carries meaning. It carries none: the label says everything
without it, and the dot is the system's mark. It is decoration, so it is not in
the contrast gate. In dark it measures 6.73:1.

**The dot hangs into the gutter.** It sits left of the label by its own width
plus the gap, 6px and `--spacing-part`, so the label text lands on the same
left edge as the content below it. An indented label reads as a different level
of hierarchy, which is what the rail's group label learned. Where a label has
no gutter beside it, a caller sets `margin-inline-start: 0` on
`.eyebrow::before` to keep the dot inline.
```

add:

```js
/** The text between the braces that follow `header`, nested blocks included. */
function blockAfter(css, header) {
  const start = css.indexOf(header);
  if (start === -1) return '';
  const open = css.indexOf('{', start) + 1;
  let depth = 1;
  let close = open;
  while (depth > 0 && close < css.length) {
    const char = css[close++];
    if (char === '{') depth += 1;
    else if (char === '}') depth -= 1;
  }
  return css.slice(open, close - 1);
}
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { createRef } from 'react';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { Heading, type HeadingLevel } from './Heading';

const STEPS = [1, 2, 3, 4] as const satisfies readonly HeadingLevel[];
const PAIRS = STEPS.flatMap((level) => STEPS.map((size) => [level, size] as const));

describe('Heading', () => {
  it('is a level 2 heading in the section step by default', () => {
    render(<Heading>Notifications</Heading>);
    const heading = screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 2, name: 'Notifications' });
    expect(heading.tagName).toBe('H2');
    expect(heading).toHaveAttribute('class', 'heading heading-2');
  });

  it.each(PAIRS)('level %i drawn in size %i', (level, size) => {
    render(
      <Heading level={level} size={size}>
        Title
      </Heading>,
    );
    const heading = screen.getByRole('heading', { level });
    expect(heading.tagName).toBe(`H${level}`);
    expect(heading).toHaveAttribute('class', `heading heading-${size}`);
  });

  it.each(STEPS)('draws level %i in its own size when no size is given', (level) => {
    render(<Heading level={level}>Title</Heading>);
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level })).toHaveAttribute('class', `heading heading-${level}`);
  });

  it('merges a custom className after the library classes', () => {
    render(<Heading className="extra">Title</Heading>);
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading')).toHaveAttribute('class', 'heading heading-2 extra');
  });

  it('forwards a ref to the heading element', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLHeadingElement>();
    render(
      <Heading level={3} ref={ref}>
        Title
      </Heading>,
    );
    expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLHeadingElement);
    expect(ref.current?.tagName).toBe('H3');
  });

  it('passes other attributes through, so a heading can be a link target or carry its own theme', () => {
    render(
      <Heading id="notifications" data-theme="dark" aria-describedby="note">
        Title
      </Heading>,
    );
    const heading = screen.getByRole('heading');
    expect(heading).toHaveAttribute('id', 'notifications');
    expect(heading).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
    expect(heading).toHaveAttribute('aria-describedby', 'note');
  });

  it('has no axe violations in an outline whose looks differ from its levels', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <main>
        <Heading level={1} size={2}>
          Settings
        </Heading>
        <Heading level={2} size={3}>
          Notifications
        </Heading>
        <Heading level={3} size={4}>
          Email
        </Heading>
      </main>,
    );
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });
});
```

`packages/core/src/components/heading.css`:

```css
/*
 * Heading, the four heading steps of the type scale: heading-1 to heading-4
 * read --text-h1 to --text-h4 with their line height, tracking and weight. The
 * element is the caller's choice (h1 to h4), the look is the class, so a card
 * title can be an h2 drawn in the card-title step.
 *
 * Headings scale down on small screens (docs/design-system.md, "Typography"):
 * the 64px step is 48px under 1024px and 40px under 768px, and the 36px step is
 * 28px under 768px. The widths are the tablet and desktop breakpoint tokens,
 * written out because a media query cannot read a custom property;
 * test/css.test.js keeps them equal. Line height is a ratio, so it scales with
 * the size and the 1:1 display step stays 1:1.
 */
@layer components {
  .heading {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
  }

  .heading-1 {
    font-size: var(--text-h1);
    line-height: var(--text-h1--line-height);
    letter-spacing: var(--text-h1--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-h1--font-weight);
  }

  .heading-2 {
    font-size: var(--text-h2);
    line-height: var(--text-h2--line-height);
    letter-spacing: var(--text-h2--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-h2--font-weight);
  }

  .heading-3 {
    font-size: var(--text-h3);
    line-height: var(--text-h3--line-height);
    letter-spacing: var(--text-h3--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-h3--font-weight);
  }

  /* The subhead has no tracking token, so it says so: a heading inside tracked
     text must not inherit the tracking. */
  .heading-4 {
    font-size: var(--text-h4);
    line-height: var(--text-h4--line-height);
    letter-spacing: normal;
    font-weight: var(--text-h4--font-weight);
  }

  @media (width < 1024px) {
    .heading-1 {
      font-size: 3rem;
    }
  }

  @media (width < 768px) {
    .heading-1 {
      font-size: 2.5rem;
    }

    .heading-2 {
      font-size: 1.75rem;
    }
  }
}
```

```css
/*
 * Copy, the body text of a page: the body step by default, the small step for
 * hints and helper lines, and a muted tone for text that is secondary. The
 * class is `copy` and not `text` because a class may not start with a Tailwind
 * namespace such as text-, which would collide in any app that also uses
 * Tailwind.
 *
 * Muted is slate. Taupe is for placeholders and disabled text only: it fails
 * AA on every surface, and everything here is read.
 */
@layer components {
  .copy {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: var(--text-body);
    line-height: var(--text-body--line-height);
    letter-spacing: normal;
    font-weight: var(--text-body--font-weight);
  }

  .copy-small {
    font-size: var(--text-small);
    line-height: var(--text-small--line-height);
    font-weight: var(--text-small--font-weight);
  }

  .copy-muted {
    color: var(--color-slate);
  }
}
```

```css
/*
 * Eyebrow, the label above a heading: the 14px, 700, +4% tracking step, in
 * capitals, in slate, with the accent dot the design system calls the identity
 * (docs/design-system.md, "Typography"). The dot is light signal orange and
 * takes --radius-dot so it stays round in every shape.
 *
 * The dot hangs into the gutter by its own width plus the gap, so the label
 * text sits on the same left edge as the content below it. Where there is no
 * gutter beside the label, set margin-inline-start to 0 on .eyebrow::before.
 */
@layer components {
  .eyebrow {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: var(--spacing-part);
    margin: 0;
    color: var(--color-slate);
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: var(--text-eyebrow);
    line-height: var(--text-eyebrow--line-height);
    letter-spacing: var(--text-eyebrow--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-eyebrow--font-weight);
    text-transform: uppercase;
  }

  .eyebrow::before {
    content: '';
    flex: none;
    width: 6px;
    height: 6px;
    margin-inline-start: calc(-1 * (6px + var(--spacing-part)));
    border-radius: var(--radius-dot);
    background-color: var(--color-signal-light);
  }
}
```

`packages/react/src/typography/Heading.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { HTMLAttributes, ReactElement, Ref } from 'react';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

/** A heading step: the `h1` to `h4` element, or the type step that matches it. */
export type HeadingLevel = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;

export interface HeadingProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLHeadingElement> {
  /**
   * The element, `h1` to `h4`. It places the heading in the page outline, so
   * choose it by the heading's place in the page and not by how it should look.
   * @default 2
   */
  level?: HeadingLevel;
  /**
   * The look: 1 is the 64px display step, 2 the 36px section step, 3 the 24px
   * card title and 4 the 14px bold subhead. It follows `level` unless it is
   * given.
   * @default level
   */
  size?: HeadingLevel;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLHeadingElement>;
}

/**
 * A heading drawn in one of the four heading steps. A static component: it
 * renders a plain `h1` to `h4`, so it works in a server component.
 */
export function Heading({ level = 2, size = level, className, ...props }: HeadingProps): ReactElement {
  const Element = `h${level}` as const;
  return <Element {...props} className={cx('heading', `heading-${size}`, className)} />;
}
```

`packages/react/src/typography/Text.tsx`:

```tsx
import { createElement, type HTMLAttributes, type ReactElement, type Ref } from 'react';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export type TextElement = 'p' | 'span' | 'div';
export type TextSize = 'body' | 'small';
export type TextTone = 'default' | 'muted';

export interface TextProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> {
  /**
   * The element to render: `p`, `span` or `div`.
   * @default 'p'
   */
  as?: TextElement;
  /**
   * `body` is 16px; `small` is 14px, for hints and helper lines.
   * @default 'body'
   */
  size?: TextSize;
  /**
   * `default` takes the color around it; `muted` is slate, for secondary text.
   * @default 'default'
   */
  tone?: TextTone;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>;
}

/**
 * Body text in the body or small step. A static component: it renders a plain
 * `p`, `span` or `div`, so it works in a server component.
 */
export function Text({
  as: Element = 'p',
  size = 'body',
  tone = 'default',
  className,
  ...props
}: TextProps): ReactElement {
  // createElement and not JSX: JSX checks the props against all three tags at
  // once, and a ref typed for the HTMLElement they share fails that check.
  return createElement(Element, {
    ...props,
    className: cx('copy', size === 'small' && 'copy-small', tone === 'muted' && 'copy-muted', className),
  });
}
```

`packages/react/src/typography/Eyebrow.tsx`:

```tsx
import { createElement, type HTMLAttributes, type ReactElement, type Ref } from 'react';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export type EyebrowElement = 'p' | 'span' | 'div';

export interface EyebrowProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> {
  /**
   * The element to render: `p`, `span` or `div`. An eyebrow is a label, never a
   * heading.
   * @default 'p'
   */
  as?: EyebrowElement;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>;
}

/**
 * The small capitalised label above a heading, with the accent dot hanging into
 * the gutter. A static component: it renders a plain `p`, `span` or `div`, so it
 * works in a server component.
 */
export function Eyebrow({ as: Element = 'p', className, ...props }: EyebrowProps): ReactElement {
  // createElement and not JSX: see Text.
  return createElement(Element, { ...props, className: cx('eyebrow', className) });
}
```

```mdx
---
title: Typography
description: Heading, Text and Eyebrow set the type scale. They are plain elements, so they work in a server component.
icon: Type
---

<Section>

## Heading

The level picks the element and the size picks the look. The size follows the level unless you give one, so a card title can be an h2 drawn in the card-title step.

<Preview name="heading-sizes" />

Headings scale down on small screens. The display step is 48px under 1024px and 40px under 768px, and the section step is 28px under 768px.

</Section>

<Section>

## Text

Body text in the body or the small step. The muted tone is slate, for secondary text.

<Preview name="text-tones" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Eyebrow

The small capitalised label above a heading, with the accent dot. The dot hangs into the gutter, so the label lines up with the heading below it.

<Preview name="eyebrow-heading" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

None of the three needs a client boundary: they render plain elements and import no React Aria.

<Code code={`import { Eyebrow, Heading, Text } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function SectionIntro() {
  return (
    <header>
      <Eyebrow>Foundations</Eyebrow>
      <Heading level={2}>Everything a dashboard asks for.</Heading>
      <Text tone="muted">Type and color come from tokens.</Text>
    </header>
  );
}`} />

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

Each one accepts every attribute of the element it renders, and a `className` that is added after its own.

### Heading props

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/typography/Heading.tsx" type="Pick<HeadingProps, 'level' | 'size'>" />

### Text props

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/typography/Text.tsx" type="Pick<TextProps, 'as' | 'size' | 'tone'>" />

### Eyebrow props

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/typography/Eyebrow.tsx" type="Pick<EyebrowProps, 'as'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A Heading is a real h1 to h4 element, so the page outline is what assistive technology reads, whatever size it is drawn in. An Eyebrow is a label and never a heading, so it stays out of the outline. Muted text is slate, which clears 4.5:1 on every surface.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps the type in the system.

<Rules dos={['Pick the level from the page outline, then the size from the hierarchy.', 'Use one h1 per page and never skip a level on the way down.', 'Leave room beside an eyebrow: its dot hangs 14px into the gutter.']} donts={['Never pick a level for its size. Set the size instead.', 'No capitals except the eyebrow.', 'Never taupe for text a reader has to read. Muted is slate.']} />

</Section>
```

The docs prose rule `.docs-section p` has a higher specificity than a core class, so it would also override the line height and measure of every `Text` and `Eyebrow` shown in a Preview. A Preview stage shows a component, not prose. In `apps/docs/components/shell/shell.css` replace:

```css
  .docs-section p,
  .docs-section li {
```

with:

```css
  /* Prose only. What a Preview stage shows is a component drawn by its own
     class, so the page's reading measure and line height must not reach it.
     :where() keeps the specificity of the plain p and li it replaces. */
  .docs-section p:where(:not(.stage *)),
  .docs-section li:where(:not(.stage *)) {
```

`:where()` adds no specificity, so the rule keeps the specificity of the `p` and `li` selectors it replaces and everything that overrides it today still does.

Nothing needs scrolling today, with three links, so the helper changes no result yet. To see it do its job, save this throwaway script as `scroll-proof.mjs` outside the repository. It is not committed:

```js
// Throwaway, not committed. With twenty more links ahead of Spinner in the rail, the old drawer
// assertion fails and the helper the tests now use passes.
//   node /path/to/scroll-proof.mjs <port>
// Run from the repository root, with the production docs server listening on <port>.
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import path from 'node:path';

const require = createRequire(path.resolve('apps/docs/package.json'));
const { chromium, expect } = require('@playwright/test');

const browser = await chromium.launch();
const page = await (await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 768, height: 900 } })).newPage();
await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${process.argv[2]}/docs/components/button`);
await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
await page.waitForTimeout(500);
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open the menu' }).click();
await page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Menu' }).waitFor();
await page.evaluate(() => {
  const item = document.querySelector('#rail a[data-label="Spinner"]').closest('li');
  for (let index = 0; index < 20; index += 1) {
    const copy = item.cloneNode(true);
    copy.querySelectorAll('.rail-label').forEach((label) => {
      label.textContent = `Extra ${index}`;
    });
    item.before(copy);
  }
});
const link = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Spinner' });
try {
  await expect(link).toBeInViewport({ ratio: 1, timeout: 1500 });
  console.log('old assertion: passes');
} catch {
  console.log('old assertion: fails, the link is below the fold');
}
await link.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
await expect(link).toBeInViewport({ ratio: 1 });
console.log('helper: passes once the link is scrolled into view');
await browser.close();
```

The dot hangs 14px left of its label, so it needs room. With the server still up, paste this into the browser console of each page. It lists the label of every eyebrow whose dot is clipped by an `overflow` ancestor or pushed off the left edge:

```js
[...document.querySelectorAll('.eyebrow')]
  .filter((eyebrow) => {
    const { left, width } = eyebrow.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (width === 0) return false; // not drawn at this width
    const dot = left - 14; // the dot sits 14px left of the label
    let clipped = dot < 0;
    for (let ancestor = eyebrow.parentElement; ancestor; ancestor = ancestor.parentElement) {
      const { overflowX } = getComputedStyle(ancestor);
      if (['hidden', 'clip', 'auto', 'scroll'].includes(overflowX) && dot < ancestor.getBoundingClientRect().left) {
        clipped = true;
      }
    }
    return clipped;
  })
  .map((eyebrow) => eyebrow.textContent)
```

```js
// Throwaway, not committed. Sideways scroll and axe violations of one docs page, at four widths in
// both color modes.
//   node /path/to/page-check.mjs <port> <path>
// Run from the repository root, with the production docs server listening on <port>.
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import path from 'node:path';

const require = createRequire(path.resolve('apps/docs/package.json'));
const { chromium } = require('@playwright/test');
const AxeBuilder = require('@axe-core/playwright').default;

const [port, url] = process.argv.slice(2);
const browser = await chromium.launch();
for (const scheme of ['light', 'dark']) {
  for (const width of [375, 768, 1024, 1440]) {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height: 900 }, colorScheme: scheme });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${url}`);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const overflow = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth);
    const { violations } = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();
    const found = violations.map((violation) => violation.id).join(', ') || 'none';
    console.log(`${scheme} ${String(width).padEnd(4)} sideways ${overflow}, axe ${found}`);
    await context.close();
  }
}
await browser.close();
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `cx` from `packages/react/src/utils/cx.ts`, `expectNoA11yViolations` from `packages/react/test/a11y.ts`, `--focus-ring-color` from Task 1, the tokens `--color-link`, `--color-slate`, `--color-success`, `--color-error`, `--color-bone`, `--color-taupe`, `--radius-micro`, `--font-sans`, `--text-overline--letter-spacing`, `--text-overline--font-weight`, `--focus-ring-width` and `--focus-ring-offset`.
- Consumes: `CONTRAST_PAIRS` in `packages/core/scripts/contrast.js`. It already holds `link`, `success` and `error` as text on canvas, lifted, float and raised, and `slate` on canvas, lifted, bone, float and raised, so this task adds no pair.
- Produces: `Link(props: LinkProps): ReactElement`, a client component (`'use client'`) built on React Aria's Link. `interface LinkProps extends RACLinkProps { className?: RACLinkProps['className']; ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement> }`. It renders an `<a class="link">` when it has an `href`, and a `<span role="link" class="link">` when it has none or is disabled. It carries `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible` and `data-disabled`, which `link.css` styles.
- Produces: `Kbd(props: KbdProps): ReactElement`, static, no `'use client'`, no React Aria. `interface KbdProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> { children?: ReactNode; className?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLElement> }`. It renders `<kbd class="kbd">` and forwards every attribute, including `style` and `aria-hidden`.
- Produces: `Badge(props: BadgeProps): ReactElement`, `type BadgeTone = 'neutral' | 'info' | 'success' | 'error'`, static. `interface BadgeProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement> { tone?: BadgeTone; children?: ReactNode; className?: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement> }`. It renders `<span class="badge">`, plus `badge-info`, `badge-success` or `badge-error` for the other tones. Neutral is the base class alone. There is no clay and no signal tone.
- Produces the classes `link`, `kbd`, `badge`, `badge-info`, `badge-success` and `badge-error`. Every later task that puts an inline link in a description or an error message uses `Link`, which is what fixes source defect 12 (inline links with no hover, no focus and no `--color-link`). A server component may render `Kbd` and `Badge` directly.
- Produces the docs hooks `.rail-version` and `.rail-key`, still passed as `className` to `Badge` and `Kbd`. The e2e tests select them as `#rail .rail-version` and `#rail .rail-key` in `apps/docs/tests/docs.spec.ts`.
- Removes the docs stand-ins `.kbd`, `.badge`, `.badge, .kbd` (tabular figures), `.rail-link .badge`, `.meta-row a` and `.docs-section a:not([class])`, and their focus rule.

**Names.** `link`, `kbd`, `badge`, `badge-info`, `badge-success` and `badge-error` all pass the Stylelint `selector-class-pattern` (none starts with a Tailwind namespace), so no class was renamed.

**What the docs do with inline links.** Decided case by case:
- The MDX `[text](url)` links are rendered by the docs' own MDX components, and mapping `a` to `Link` is one line, so it is done. The two content links (`apps/docs/content/docs/index.mdx` and `design-principles.mdx`) become real Links, and the stand-in `.docs-section a:not([class])` and its focus rule are deleted. A core `<a class="link">` would no longer match `:not([class])` anyway.
- The two links in the Package card (`Edit this page`, `React Aria`) become `Link`, and the `.meta-row a` rule is deleted. Task 13's carry-over "meta links (`.meta-row a`) need 40px hit areas" now targets `.meta-row .link`.
- Left alone, because they are navigation chrome and not inline links: `.brand`, `.nav-links a`, `.footer-col a`, `.nav-overlay-links a` and `.toc a` (Fumadocs owns the anchor and its `data-active`).
- `.rail-link .badge` (and its collapsed-rail selector) is deleted. Nothing renders a badge inside a rail link, and at specificity 0,2,0 it would silently override the core padding if one ever did.
- Not touched: the homepage catalog chips and the footer "Components" column in `apps/docs/app/(home)/home-page.tsx` are hard-coded lists that still name only Button and Spinner.

**Why the Badge border is `currentColor`.** Each tone is its color for the text and the same color for a 1px border. One declaration, `border: 1px solid currentColor`, keeps the two the same by construction, and each tone class then only sets `color`.

**Why 12px is a literal.** The tokens have no 12px step (`--text-small` is 14px), and the document's floor for short labels is 12px. `kbd.css` and `badge.css` write `0.75rem` and the derivation in Appendix B says why.

- [ ] **Step 1: Record the derivation**

Badge is new, so derive it before building, and measure the colors with the repository's own script. Save this as `measure-badge.mjs` in a scratch folder outside the repository and run it from the repository root with `node /path/to/measure-badge.mjs`:

```js
// Throwaway measurement, not committed. Run from the repository root after building core.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const { composite, contrastRatio, paletteFor, parseColor } = await import(
  pathToFileURL(path.resolve('packages/core/scripts/contrast.js')).href
);
const tokens = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.resolve('packages/core/tokens/tokens.json'), 'utf8'));
const tones = { neutral: 'slate', info: 'link', success: 'success', error: 'error' };
const grounds = ['canvas', 'lifted', 'float', 'raised'];

const measure = (palette, text, ground) => {
  const surface = parseColor(palette[ground]);
  return contrastRatio(composite(parseColor(palette[text]), surface), surface).toFixed(2);
};

for (const mode of ['light', 'dark']) {
  const palette = paletteFor(tokens, mode);
  for (const [tone, color] of Object.entries(tones)) {
    const ratios = grounds.map((ground) => measure(palette, color, ground));
    console.log(`${mode.padEnd(5)} ${tone.padEnd(8)} ${ratios.join(', ')}`);
  }
  console.log(`${mode.padEnd(5)} slate on bone ${measure(palette, 'slate', 'bone')}`);
}
```

Expected, eight rows (the tone, then the text color on canvas, lifted, float and raised) and the two Bone rows:

```text
light info     5.16, 5.67, 5.86, 5.86
light success  6.55, 7.20, 7.44, 7.44
light error    6.58, 7.22, 7.46, 7.46
light slate on bone 4.99
dark  neutral  7.26, 6.94, 6.94, 6.44
dark  info     6.05, 5.46, 5.46, 4.81
dark  success  7.03, 6.34, 6.34, 5.59
dark  error    6.36, 5.73, 5.73, 5.06
dark  slate on bone 6.44
```

Every number is above the 4.5 that text needs, and every pair is already in `CONTRAST_PAIRS`, which Step 2 pins with a test. Link is the `info` row, and Kbd is the Bone row.

Append to the end of `docs/design-system.md`, after a blank line:

```markdown
## Link

The document names Link Blue for inline links. The app never used it for one:
its inline links were Ink with an underline, written out again inside three
panels, with no hover and no focus style, so keyboard focus showed only the
browser's default ring. Link Blue appeared only in code highlighting. The
library draws one link and gives it the states the app left out.

- **Link Blue, underlined.** The text is `--color-link`, which is lifted in dark
  as the document specifies. Color alone does not tell a link from the words
  around it, so the underline always stays: 1px, offset 0.25em, which is 4px at
  body size and the app's offset, and it scales with the type.
- **Measured.** Link Blue is already in the contrast gate as text on canvas,
  lifted, float and raised, so a link is held to 4.5:1 on every surface a page,
  card or rail can be. It measures 5.16 to 5.86 in light and 4.81 to 6.05 in
  dark. No new pair was needed.
- **Hover and press thicken the underline to 2px.** The change is not
  color-only and does not move the text. The color stays put, so the measured
  pairs are the only ones in play. Press shows the same step as hover, because
  touch has no hover to show it.
- **Focus is the standard ring**, `--focus-ring-color` at the standard width
  and offset. The link takes the micro radius so the ring follows the link in
  every shape.
- **A disabled link is Dust Taupe** with the `not-allowed` cursor. It keeps its
  underline, so the word still reads as a link that is switched off, and hover
  does nothing.
- **An inline link is exempt from the 40px target.** WCAG 2.5.8 excepts a link
  inside a sentence, and a 40px hit area would overlap the lines above and
  below it. A link used alone as a control, such as a menu entry, takes its
  height from the container it sits in.

## Kbd

The app drew its key hints twice: the rail's launcher key at 14px and the
search palette's keys at 11px. 11px is under the 12px floor for short labels,
so the library has one key, at 12px, that looks the same wherever it sits.

- Slate on Bone, the app's pairing. Slate on Bone is already in the contrast
  gate and measures 4.99 in light and 6.44 in dark.
- `--radius-micro`, the step the shape table gives key hints, so a key follows
  the shape axis.
- Weight 700 with the overline tracking, and tabular figures, so a row of keys
  such as the arrows and Enter keeps one width per key.
- Sofia Sans. A browser gives `kbd` a monospace face; the library sets the sans
  family back, since a key is a label and `--font-mono` is for code only.
- The app hid its rail key from assistive technology, so the shortcut was not
  announced there. A key inside a sentence should be read, so the library adds
  no `aria-hidden`; a caller who does not want the key announced passes it.

## Badge

The document has no badge and the app drew none, so this one is derived. It
labels a state or a count beside a name. It is not a control, so it has no
hover, no focus ring and no touch target.

- **Outlined, not filled.** A badge is a 1px border and a label in the same
  color. A tinted fill would put the text on a ground of its own and add a
  pair to measure for every tone on every surface. With no fill the text sits
  on the surface behind the badge, and every pair is one the gate already
  holds. The border is a hairline's weight: a badge labels, it is not a control
  to be found, so it does not need the 1.5px edge a control gets.
- **Four tones.** Neutral is Slate, info is Link Blue, success is the success
  color and error is the error color. Neutral is the base, so it has no class
  of its own. Clay is unsaved work and Signal Orange is consent, and Light
  Signal Orange is an attention cue that a label has no use for, so none of the
  three is a tone.
- **A short uppercase label.** 12px, the floor for short uppercase text,
  weight 700 and the overline tracking. Figures are tabular, so a column of
  counts such as 12 and 8 lines up. The corners are `--radius-micro`, the step
  the shape table gives badges, so the shape axis reaches them.
- **Color is never the only signal.** The label says what the badge means. The
  tone only repeats it.
- **A long label wraps inside the badge.** It breaks anywhere, so no label can
  push a narrow screen sideways.

Measured as the text color on each surface a badge sits on, light then dark,
for canvas, lifted, float and raised in that order. The 1px border is the same
color as the text, so it clears the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks of an edge by
the same margin. The lowest text pair is 4.81, info on raised in dark.

| Tone | Color | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Neutral | Slate | 4.84, 5.31, 5.49, 5.49 | 7.26, 6.94, 6.94, 6.44 |
| Info | Link Blue | 5.16, 5.67, 5.86, 5.86 | 6.05, 5.46, 5.46, 4.81 |
| Success | Success | 6.55, 7.20, 7.44, 7.44 | 7.03, 6.34, 6.34, 5.59 |
| Error | Error | 6.58, 7.22, 7.46, 7.46 | 6.36, 5.73, 5.73, 5.06 |

All sixteen pairs are in the contrast gate already, so Badge adds none. Slate
is also measured on Bone, 4.99 and 6.44, so a neutral badge may sit there. The
three colored tones are not measured on Bone, so they stay on the four
surfaces above.
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef } from 'react';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { Link } from './Link';

describe('Link', () => {
  it('is an anchor with the link class and its href', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Link href="/guide">Read the guide</Link>);
    const link = screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Read the guide' });
    expect(link.tagName).toBe('A');
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute('href', '/guide');
    expect(link).toHaveClass('link');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('keeps target and rel, so a link can open a new tab safely', () => {
    render(
      <Link href="https://react-aria.adobe.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">
        React Aria
      </Link>,
    );
    const link = screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'React Aria' });
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute('target', '_blank');
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute('rel', 'noopener noreferrer');
  });

  it('fires onPress on Enter and on click, and not on Space', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onPress = vi.fn();
    render(
      <Link href="#guide" onPress={onPress}>
        Read the guide
      </Link>,
    );
    const link = screen.getByRole('link');
    await user.tab();
    expect(link).toHaveFocus();
    await user.keyboard('{Enter}');
    expect(onPress).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    await user.keyboard(' ');
    expect(onPress).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    await user.click(link);
    expect(onPress).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('marks keyboard focus for the focus ring', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Link href="#guide">Read the guide</Link>);
    const link = screen.getByRole('link');
    expect(link).not.toHaveAttribute('data-focus-visible');
    await user.tab();
    expect(link).toHaveFocus();
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute('data-focus-visible', 'true');
  });

  it('is inert when disabled', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onPress = vi.fn();
    render(
      <Link href="/guide" isDisabled onPress={onPress}>
        Read the guide
      </Link>,
    );
    const link = screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Read the guide' });
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true');
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute('data-disabled', 'true');
    // Not an anchor, so there is nothing to follow.
    expect(link.tagName).toBe('SPAN');
    await user.click(link);
    expect(onPress).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('forwards data attributes, so a link can carry its own theme', () => {
    render(
      <Link href="/guide" data-theme="dark">
        Read the guide
      </Link>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByRole('link')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
  });

  it('merges a custom className', () => {
    render(
      <Link href="/guide" className="extra">
        Read the guide
      </Link>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByRole('link')).toHaveClass('link', 'extra');
  });

  it('merges a function-form className with the base class', () => {
    render(
      <Link
        href="/guide"
        aria-current="page"
        className={({ isCurrent }) => (isCurrent ? 'is-current' : 'extra')}
      >
        Read the guide
      </Link>,
    );
    const link = screen.getByRole('link');
    expect(link).toHaveClass('link', 'is-current');
    expect(link).not.toHaveClass('extra');
  });

  it('forwards a ref to the anchor element', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLAnchorElement>();
    render(
      <Link href="/guide" ref={ref}>
        Read the guide
      </Link>,
    );
    expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLAnchorElement);
  });
});
```

A disabled React Aria link is not an anchor: it renders a `<span role="link" aria-disabled="true">` and keeps a leftover `href` attribute that does nothing, so the test asserts the element is a `SPAN` and does not look at `href`.

```tsx
import { Kbd } from './Kbd';

describe('Kbd', () => {
  it('is a kbd element with the kbd class, read by assistive technology', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Kbd>&#8984;K</Kbd>);
    const key = screen.getByText('\u2318K');
    expect(key.tagName).toBe('KBD');
    expect(key).toHaveClass('kbd');
    expect(key).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('forwards the native attributes of an element', () => {
    render(
      <Kbd id="search-key" title="Search" aria-hidden="true" style={{ marginRight: 6 }}>
        esc
      </Kbd>,
    );
    const key = screen.getByText('esc');
    expect(key).toHaveAttribute('id', 'search-key');
    expect(key).toHaveAttribute('title', 'Search');
    expect(key).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    expect(key).toHaveStyle({ marginRight: '6px' });
  });

  it('merges a custom className after its own', () => {
    render(<Kbd className="extra">esc</Kbd>);
    expect(screen.getByText('esc')).toHaveAttribute('class', 'kbd extra');
  });

  it('forwards a ref to the kbd element', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLElement>();
    render(<Kbd ref={ref}>esc</Kbd>);
    expect(ref.current?.tagName).toBe('KBD');
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the CSS**

`packages/core/src/components/link.css`:

```css
/*
 * Link, the inline link. The document names Link Blue for it and the app never
 * used it, so the app's links had no hover and no focus style. This one is
 * Link Blue and always underlined, thickens its underline on hover and press
 * so the change is not color alone, and takes the standard focus ring.
 * Derived in docs/design-system.md ("Link").
 */
@layer components {
  .link {
    /* The micro radius makes the focus ring follow the link in every shape. */
    border-radius: var(--radius-micro);
    color: var(--color-link);
    text-decoration-line: underline;
    text-decoration-thickness: 1px;
    text-underline-offset: 0.25em;
    cursor: pointer;
    -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
  }

  @media (hover: hover) {
    .link:is(:hover, [data-hovered]):not([data-disabled]) {
      text-decoration-thickness: 2px;
    }
  }

  /* The same step as hover, since touch has no hover to show it. */
  .link:is(:active, [data-pressed]):not([data-disabled]) {
    text-decoration-thickness: 2px;
  }

  .link:is(:focus-visible, [data-focus-visible]) {
    outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color);
    outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);
  }

  /* Switched off, but still a link: the underline stays. */
  .link[data-disabled] {
    color: var(--color-taupe);
    cursor: not-allowed;
  }
}
```

The disabled rule is `.link[data-disabled]` and not `:is(:disabled, [data-disabled])`: an anchor is never `:disabled`, and React Aria sets `data-disabled` on the span it renders instead.

`packages/core/src/components/kbd.css`:

```css
/*
 * Kbd, a key hint such as the search shortcut. The app drew it at 14px in the
 * rail and at 11px in the search palette; 11px is under the 12px floor for
 * short labels, so there is one size, 12px. Derived in docs/design-system.md
 * ("Kbd").
 */
@layer components {
  .kbd {
    box-sizing: border-box;
    display: inline-block;
    max-width: 100%;
    padding-block: 0.125rem;
    padding-inline: 0.375rem;
    border-radius: var(--radius-micro);
    background-color: var(--color-bone);
    color: var(--color-slate);
    /* A browser draws kbd in monospace; a key is a label, and mono is for code. */
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: 0.75rem;
    line-height: 1;
    letter-spacing: var(--text-overline--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-overline--font-weight);
    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  }
}
```

`packages/core/src/components/badge.css`:

```css
/*
 * Badge, a short label for a state or a count. New to the library, so it is
 * derived in docs/design-system.md ("Badge"): a 1px border and a label in one
 * color, with no fill. With no fill the text sits on the surface behind the
 * badge, so every text pair is one the contrast gate already measures. Neutral
 * is the base; info, success and error only change the color. It is never clay
 * or signal orange, which mean unsaved work and consent.
 */
@layer components {
  .badge {
    box-sizing: border-box;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    max-width: 100%;
    padding-block: 0.125rem;
    padding-inline: 0.5rem;
    /* The border takes the text color, so it passes wherever the text does. */
    border: 1px solid currentColor;
    border-radius: var(--radius-micro);
    color: var(--color-slate);
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: 0.75rem;
    line-height: 1.4;
    letter-spacing: var(--text-overline--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-overline--font-weight);
    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  }

  .badge-info {
    color: var(--color-link);
  }

  .badge-success {
    color: var(--color-success);
  }

  .badge-error {
    color: var(--color-error);
  }
}
```

```tsx
'use client';

import type { ReactElement, Ref } from 'react';
import { Link as RACLink, type LinkProps as RACLinkProps, composeRenderProps } from 'react-aria-components';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export interface LinkProps extends RACLinkProps {
  /** A class name, or a function of the link's state, merged after the library's own class. */
  className?: RACLinkProps['className'];
  ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>;
}

/**
 * An inline link, in Link Blue and always underlined. Built on React Aria's
 * Link: an `<a>` when it has an `href`, with press, hover and focus handled.
 */
export function Link({ className, ...props }: LinkProps): ReactElement {
  return (
    <RACLink
      {...props}
      className={composeRenderProps(className, (userClassName) => cx('link', userClassName))}
    />
  );
}
```

```tsx
import type { HTMLAttributes, ReactElement, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export interface KbdProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> {
  /** The key, such as `Esc`, `K` or a symbol. One key per element, so a shortcut is as many as it has keys. */
  children?: ReactNode;
  /** Added after the library's own class. */
  className?: string;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>;
}

/**
 * A key hint, such as the search shortcut. A static `<kbd>` element, safe in a
 * server component. It is read aloud like any text; pass `aria-hidden` when
 * something nearby already names the shortcut.
 */
export function Kbd({ className, ...props }: KbdProps): ReactElement {
  return <kbd {...props} className={cx('kbd', className)} />;
}
```

```tsx
import type { HTMLAttributes, ReactElement, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export type BadgeTone = 'neutral' | 'info' | 'success' | 'error';

export interface BadgeProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement> {
  /**
   * What the badge means: `info`, `success` and `error` repeat in color what
   * the label already says. Clay and signal orange are deliberately not tones:
   * they mean unsaved work and consent.
   * @default 'neutral'
   */
  tone?: BadgeTone;
  /** The label or the count. Say what the badge means in words, since the tone is only a repeat. */
  children?: ReactNode;
  /** Added after the library's own classes. */
  className?: string;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement>;
}

/**
 * A short label for a state or a count, drawn as an outline with no fill.
 * A static `<span>`, safe in a server component.
 */
export function Badge({ tone = 'neutral', className, ...props }: BadgeProps): ReactElement {
  return <span {...props} className={cx('badge', tone !== 'neutral' && `badge-${tone}`, className)} />;
}
```

`packages/react/src/link/Link.stories.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { expect, fn } from 'storybook/test';
import { Link } from './Link';

const meta = {
  title: 'Components/Link',
  component: Link,
  args: { href: '#example', children: 'Read the guide', onPress: fn() },
} satisfies Meta<typeof Link>;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

export const Default: Story = {};

/** Where a link is almost always found: inside a sentence, in the text color around it. */
export const InSentence: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <p style={{ maxWidth: '40ch', margin: 0 }}>
      Every color pairing is checked in both modes. <Link {...args}>Read how it is measured</Link>, or go
      straight to the tokens.
    </p>
  ),
};

export const Disabled: Story = { args: { isDisabled: true } };

/** A long link wraps with its sentence, and its underline follows every line. */
export const LongText: Story = {
  args: {
    children:
      'A link whose text is long enough to wrap onto several lines in a narrow column, as the link of a real sentence often does',
  },
  render: (args) => (
    <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>
      <Link {...args} />
    </p>
  ),
};

export const Pressed: Story = {
  // A press is transient, so no screenshot can hold it. The story test still asserts it.
  // With no href it is not an anchor, so the click navigates nowhere.
  tags: ['no-visual'],
  args: { href: undefined },
  play: async ({ args, canvas, userEvent }) => {
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('link', { name: 'Read the guide' }));
    await expect(args.onPress).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  },
};

/** The ring sits outside the text, with the corners of the micro radius. */
export const KeyboardFocus: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvas, userEvent }) => {
    await userEvent.tab();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('link')).toHaveFocus();
  },
};

/** Link Blue lifts in dark, so a link inside a dark scope reads on its own ground. */
export const NestedThemes: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <div data-theme="dark" style={{ padding: 24, background: 'var(--color-canvas)' }}>
      <Link {...args} />
      <div data-theme="light" style={{ marginTop: 16, padding: 24, background: 'var(--color-lifted)' }}>
        <Link {...args} />
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
};
```

`Pressed` clears `href`. A click on an anchor whose `href` is a hash navigates the page, and in the Vitest browser run that closes the browser connection (the run ends with `Browser connection was closed while running tests`, although every test passes). With no `href` the link is a span, the press still fires `onPress`, and nothing navigates.
