The pages. Blank lines around the markdown inside each `<Section>` are required for MDX to parse it as markdown.

`apps/docs/content/docs/components/link.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: Link
description: An inline link in Link Blue, always underlined, with a thicker underline on hover and press and the standard focus ring.
icon: Link
---

<Section>

## Examples

Link Blue and an underline mark a link, so color is never the only cue. The underline thickens on hover and press.

<Preview name="link-inline" />

</Section>

<Section>

## States

A disabled link is Dust Taupe and keeps its underline, so the word still reads as a link that is switched off.

<Preview name="link-states" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

Give it an `href`. For a link that opens a new tab, pass `target` and `rel` as you would to an anchor.

<Code code={`import { Link } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function Footnote() {
  return (
    <p>
      Built on{' '}
      <Link href="https://react-aria.adobe.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">
        React Aria
      </Link>
      .
    </p>
  );
}`} />

For client-side routing in a framework, wrap your app in React Aria's `RouterProvider`. Link then navigates through your router.

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

Every React Aria Link prop is accepted. These are the ones Snapshot UI adds or shapes.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/link/Link.tsx" type="Pick<LinkProps, 'href' | 'target' | 'rel' | 'isDisabled' | 'onPress' | 'className'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A native anchor, with React Aria handling press across mouse, touch and keyboard. A disabled link is announced as disabled and cannot be followed.

<Keys rows={[['Enter', 'Follows the link.'], ['Tab', 'Moves focus to it. The 2px ink ring sits outside the text.']]} />

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps links in the system.

<Rules dos={['Say where the link goes, such as Read the guide.', 'Keep the underline. It is what marks the link.']} donts={['Never use a link for an action. Something that does a job is a Button.', 'Never style a link by color alone.']} />

</Section>
```

`apps/docs/content/docs/components/kbd.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: Kbd
description: A key hint, such as the search shortcut. One small key on a bone chip, static and safe in a server component.
icon: Keyboard
---

<Section>

## Examples

One Kbd per key, so a shortcut is as many keys as it has. Figures are tabular, so a row of keys keeps its width.

<Preview name="kbd-keys" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

A static `kbd` element with no React Aria, so it works in a server component without `'use client'`.

<Code code={`import { Kbd } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function SearchHint() {
  return (
    <p>
      Press <Kbd>&#8984;</Kbd> <Kbd>K</Kbd> to search.
    </p>
  );
}`} />

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

A Kbd accepts every attribute of an HTML element.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/kbd/Kbd.tsx" type="Pick<KbdProps, 'children' | 'className' | 'aria-hidden'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A Kbd is read aloud like any text. When something nearby already names the shortcut, such as a button whose label says it, pass `aria-hidden` so it is not announced twice.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps key hints in the system.

<Rules dos={['Show a key hint only for a shortcut that works.', 'Use the key symbol people see on their keyboard, such as the command key or Esc.']} donts={['Never use a Kbd as a button. It is a label, not a control.']} />

</Section>
```

`apps/docs/content/docs/components/badge.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: Badge
description: A short outlined label for a state or a count, in neutral, info, success or error. Static, with no fill.
icon: Tag
---

<Section>

## Tones

Neutral is the base. Info, success and error only change the color. Clay and signal orange are never tones: they mean unsaved work and consent.

<Preview name="badge-tones" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Counts

Figures are tabular, so a column of counts lines up whatever the digits.

<Preview name="badge-counts" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

A static `span` with no React Aria, so it works in a server component without `'use client'`.

<Code code={`import { Badge } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function Row() {
  return (
    <p>
      Release notes <Badge tone="info">New</Badge>
    </p>
  );
}`} />

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

A Badge accepts every attribute of an HTML element.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/badge/Badge.tsx" type="Pick<BadgeProps, 'tone' | 'children' | 'className'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

Color is never the only signal. The label says what the badge means, and the tone repeats it. A badge is not announced when it changes: if a count updates while the page is open, put it in a live region.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps badges in the system.

<Rules dos={['Keep the label to a word or a number.', 'Put it on the page, a card, a rail or a raised surface, where its colors are measured.']} donts={['Never fill a badge or add a color of your own. A tinted fill puts the text on a ground nobody measured.', 'Never use a badge as a button. It is a label, not a control.']} />

</Section>
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Check the new pages in a browser**

The e2e suite visits only the Button page for axe, so check the three new pages once by hand, in both themes at 1440px and 375px, and check what the CSS promises about Link. Save this as `new-pages-check.mjs` in a scratch folder outside the repository. Start the production docs server in a second terminal with `pnpm --filter @snapshot-ui/docs start` (it serves on 3100 and needs the build from Step 9), run the script from the repository root with `node /path/to/new-pages-check.mjs` (set `BASE=http://localhost:PORT` if the server is on another port), then stop the server with Ctrl+C:

```js
// Throwaway check, not committed. Run from the repository root with the production docs server up.
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import path from 'node:path';

const require = createRequire(path.resolve('apps/docs/package.json'));
const { chromium } = require('@playwright/test');
const AxeBuilder = require('@axe-core/playwright').default;
const base = process.env.BASE ?? 'http://localhost:3100';

const browser = await chromium.launch();
for (const slug of ['link', 'kbd', 'badge']) {
  for (const theme of ['light', 'dark']) {
    for (const width of [1440, 375]) {
      const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height: 900 }, colorScheme: theme });
      const page = await context.newPage();
      await page.addInitScript((value) => localStorage.setItem('theme', value), theme);
      await page.goto(`${base}/docs/components/${slug}`, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
      const { violations } = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();
      const sideways = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth);
      console.log(`${slug.padEnd(6)} ${theme.padEnd(5)} ${String(width).padEnd(4)} axe ${violations.length} sideways ${sideways}`);
      await context.close();
    }
  }
}

// Link in a real browser: the underline thickens on hover, and keyboard focus draws the ring.
for (const theme of ['light', 'dark']) {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 1000 }, colorScheme: theme });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.addInitScript((value) => localStorage.setItem('theme', value), theme);
  await page.goto(`${base}/docs/components/link`, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
  const link = page.locator('.docs-section a.link', { hasText: 'React Aria' }).first();
  const look = () =>
    link.evaluate((el) => {
      const style = getComputedStyle(el);
      return `${style.textDecorationThickness}, outline ${style.outlineStyle} ${style.outlineWidth} ${style.outlineColor}`;
    });
  console.log(`${theme.padEnd(5)} rest  `, await look());
  await link.hover();
  console.log(`${theme.padEnd(5)} hover `, await look());
  await page.mouse.move(5, 5);
  await link.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Shift+Tab');
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  console.log(`${theme.padEnd(5)} focus `, await look());
  await context.close();
}
await browser.close();
```

Expected: twelve lines, each with `axe 0 sideways 0`, then six lines for Link. The underline is 1px at rest and 2px under the pointer, and keyboard focus draws the standard 2px ring, ink in light and white in dark:

```text
light rest   1px, outline none 3px rgb(56, 96, 190)
light hover  2px, outline none 3px rgb(56, 96, 190)
light focus  1px, outline solid 2px rgb(20, 20, 19)
dark  rest   1px, outline none 3px rgb(108, 142, 224)
dark  hover  2px, outline none 3px rgb(108, 142, 224)
dark  focus  1px, outline solid 2px rgb(255, 255, 255)
```

(`outline none 3px` is the unset outline's default width. The text color, `rgb(56, 96, 190)` in light and `rgb(108, 142, 224)` in dark, is Link Blue, which is the measured pair.)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `cx` from `packages/react/src/utils/cx.ts`; React Aria's `Button` and `Link`; the tokens `--color-slate`, `--color-ink`, `--color-taupe`, `--radius-pill`, `--focus-ring-width`, `--focus-ring-offset` and, from Task 1, `--focus-ring-color`.
- Produces: `IconButton(props: IconButtonProps): ReactElement` and `type IconButtonVariant = 'ghost' | 'outline'`. `IconButtonProps` is a discriminated union on `href`, and the types require an accessible name:
  - Without `href`, it is React Aria's `ButtonProps` (minus `isPending`) and `ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>`. It renders a React Aria `Button`, a `<button>`.
  - With `href: string`, it is React Aria's `LinkProps` and `ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>`. It renders a React Aria `Link`, an `<a>`, with the same classes. A disabled link renders as `<span role="link" aria-disabled="true">`, which is React Aria's choice.
  - In both, `variant?: IconButtonVariant` (default `'ghost'`), and either `'aria-label': string` or `'aria-labelledby': string`. `className` is a string or React Aria's render function and merges after the library classes. `children` is the icon.
- Produces the classes `icon-button` (the ghost look, and the base of both variants), `icon-button-outline` and `icon-button-icon` (the wrapper that hides the icon from assistive technology and draws no box). The base sets `--icon-button-bg`, `--icon-button-fg`, `--icon-button-border`, `--icon-button-border-disabled` and the wash pair `--icon-button-bg-active` and `--icon-button-fg-active`; outline only sets `--icon-button-fg`, `--icon-button-border` and `--icon-button-border-disabled`. The states read them, the pattern Button uses, and a docs modifier can set them too. `.icon-button svg` is 20px.
- Produces the docs page `/docs/components/icon-button`, between Button and Kbd in the rail (the rail is alphabetical).
- Removes the docs stand-in `.icon-button`, `.icon-button-ghost`, `.icon-button svg` and the `.icon-button` selector of the shared focus rule. The docs-only modifiers `header-menu`, `rail-close`, `code-copy` and `nav-menu` stay, and the dead class `nav-close` goes.

Source values come from the source app's icon controls. It has no shared icon button: the rail collapse button (`src/snapshot/styles/shell/sidebar.css`), the menu toggle (`src/snapshot/styles/shell/header.css`) and the toast dismiss (`src/snapshot/styles/shell/toast.css`) each carry a rule of their own, and the design system's section 4 gives the shape. Corrections are recorded in Appendix B: the hover (the source's float to lifted step is invisible in dark), the cursor (the toggle and the dismiss had none), the size (a 28px and a 32px control are not carried over, so the 40px target holds), and a link form the source never needed.

**Names.** `icon-button` and `icon-button-outline` pass the Stylelint `selector-class-pattern` rule, which forbids a class that starts with `outline-`, not one that ends in `-outline`. Ghost is the base look, so there is no `icon-button-ghost` in core, and the docs stand-in of that name is deleted with the rest.

**What stays in the docs.** The rail's collapse button (`.rail-collapse` in `shell.css`) is not a use of `.icon-button`. It is its own 32px control with a 40px hit area, and the Sidebar in a later phase will own it. Leave it, and the `.satellite` link in `home.css`, alone. The modifiers `header-menu`, `rail-close`, `code-copy` and `nav-menu` position or hide an IconButton, so they stay and pass through `className`.


- [ ] **Step 1: Measure and record the derivation**

Measure the pairings the component draws. This is a throwaway script, so keep it outside the repository. Save it as `measure.mjs` in a scratch folder and run it from the repository root with `node /path/to/measure.mjs`:

```js
// Throwaway measurement, not committed. Run from the repository root.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const { composite, contrastRatio, paletteFor, parseColor } = await import(
  pathToFileURL(path.resolve('packages/core/scripts/contrast.js')).href
);
const tokens = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.resolve('packages/core/tokens/tokens.json'), 'utf8'));
const GROUNDS = ['canvas', 'lifted', 'float', 'bone', 'raised'];

for (const mode of ['light', 'dark']) {
  const palette = paletteFor(tokens, mode);
  const color = (name) => parseColor(palette[name]);
  // A translucent color is read as it sits on the ground it is drawn over.
  const over = (name, ground) => composite(color(name), composite(color(ground), color('canvas')));
  const ratio = (a, b) => contrastRatio(a, b).toFixed(2);
  const wash = (ground) => composite({ ...color('ink'), a: 0.05 }, over(ground, 'canvas'));
  console.log(`${mode}:`);
  for (const ground of GROUNDS) {
    const base = over(ground, 'canvas');
    console.log(
      `  ${ground.padEnd(6)} slate ${ratio(over('slate', ground), base)}  ink ${ratio(over('ink', ground), base)}` +
        `  ink on 5% wash ${ratio(over('ink', ground), wash(ground))}`,
    );
  }
  console.log(`  taupe on canvas ${ratio(over('taupe', 'canvas'), over('canvas', 'canvas'))}`);
}
```

Expected:

```text
light:
  canvas slate 4.84  ink 16.25  ink on 5% wash 14.70
  lifted slate 5.31  ink 17.84  ink on 5% wash 16.11
  float  slate 5.49  ink 18.43  ink on 5% wash 16.65
  bone   slate 4.99  ink 16.76  ink on 5% wash 15.15
  raised slate 5.49  ink 18.43  ink on 5% wash 16.65
  taupe on canvas 1.40
dark:
  canvas slate 7.26  ink 19.31  ink on 5% wash 17.41
  lifted slate 6.94  ink 17.42  ink on 5% wash 15.25
  float  slate 6.94  ink 17.42  ink on 5% wash 15.25
  bone   slate 6.44  ink 15.36  ink on 5% wash 13.24
  raised slate 6.44  ink 15.36  ink on 5% wash 13.24
  taupe on canvas 3.81
```

No pairing is added to `CONTRAST_PAIRS` in `packages/core/scripts/contrast.js`. The icon is slate or ink, and the outline's edge is ink, and both are already gated there on canvas, lifted, bone, float and raised, the five grounds in the output above. The 5% hover wash is a cue and not a boundary (the Appendix B rule on hover washes), so it has no pair; the icon's measurements on it are recorded in the section below. The disabled taupe is exempt from contrast, as the Button's disabled label is.

Append this section at the end of `docs/design-system.md`. Appendix B is the last part of the file, and every component adds its section after the previous one, so leave one blank line before it. It is Appendix B's `## IconButton`:

```markdown

## IconButton

Section 4 gives the icon-only circle button as transparent or white, an icon
of 10 to 20px, a 1px ink border on cream or none over media, a 50% radius and
a 40px diameter at the least. The library keeps all of it and splits the two
looks into variants. The radius is `--radius-pill`, so the circle follows the
shape axis: a circle in Rounded, 12px in Soft, square in Square.

- **Ghost** is the base. It has no fill and no edge, and its icon is slate,
  turning ink on hover. It is the document's "none over media" look, for bars,
  headers and the corner of a code block.
- **Outline** is the document's circle on cream: a transparent fill, a 1px ink
  border and an ink icon. Ink is white in dark, so the edge follows the theme.
  The edge is the ink pairing the contrast gate already holds against canvas,
  lifted, bone, float and raised. Ink measures 16.25 on canvas, 17.84 on
  lifted and 18.43 on float in light, and 19.31, 17.42 and 17.42 in dark, far
  over the 3 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks of an edge.

Hover and press are a 5% ink wash, over whatever the button sits on, in both
variants. The app stepped Float to Lifted, which are the same color in dark,
so its hover changed nothing there. Like every hover wash it is a cue and not a
boundary, so it has no pair in the contrast gate. The icon is ink on the wash,
and measures 14.70 on canvas and 16.65 on float in light, 17.41 and 15.25 in
dark. The lowest of the five grounds is 13.24, Bone in dark. A press shows the
wash too, since touch has no hover to show it. The ghost icon at rest is
slate, which measures 4.84 on canvas in light and 7.26 in dark, over the 4.5
the text gate asks of it and the 3 an icon needs.

Disabled turns the icon taupe, stops the hover and shows `not-allowed`. An
outline button's edge fades to 15% ink, as the Button's does. Taupe measures
1.40 on canvas in light and 3.81 in dark. A disabled control is exempt from
contrast, as the Button's disabled label is.

The rest follow the rules above:

- The icon is 20px, the top of the document's range. Icon libraries draw at
  24px, so the stylesheet sets the size of any `svg` inside.
- The ring is the shared focus ring, outside the circle, so ink still reads
  against the page behind it.
- The cursor is `pointer`. The app's header toggle and toast dismiss had none.
- The button is 40px. The app's rail collapse button was 28px and its toast
  dismiss 32px, and neither is carried over: a control drawn smaller extends
  its hit area instead.
- The only motion is a 120ms fade of the wash, and reduced motion removes it.

The icon holds no text, so it is hidden from assistive technology and the
types require a name: `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`. Given an `href` the
component renders an anchor with the same classes, because an icon that goes
somewhere, such as a GitHub link, is a link and not a button. The app's icon
controls were all buttons. React Aria renders a disabled link as a `span` with
`role="link"` and `aria-disabled`, which the stylesheet matches through
`data-disabled`. There is no pending state, since an icon has nowhere to show
one.
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the CSS**

`packages/core/src/components/icon-button.css`:

```css
/*
 * IconButton: a button, or a link drawn the same way, that holds one icon and
 * no text. It is 40px square, so it meets the touch target on its own, and a
 * full circle in Rounded because --radius-pill follows the shape axis.
 *
 * Ghost is the base: no fill and no edge, a slate icon that turns ink. Outline
 * is the design system's circle on cream: a transparent fill, a 1px ink edge
 * and an ink icon. Each variant only sets the --icon-button-* properties; the
 * states below read them, so a state never needs one rule per variant.
 */
@layer components {
  .icon-button {
    --icon-button-bg: transparent;
    --icon-button-fg: var(--color-slate);
    --icon-button-border: transparent;
    --icon-button-border-disabled: transparent;
    /* A wash of ink. The source stepped float to lifted, which are the same
       color in dark, so its hover changed nothing there. */
    --icon-button-bg-active: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 5%, transparent);
    --icon-button-fg-active: var(--color-ink);

    box-sizing: border-box;
    display: inline-grid;
    flex: none;
    place-items: center;
    width: 40px;
    height: 40px;
    margin: 0;
    padding: 0;
    border: 1px solid var(--icon-button-border);
    border-radius: var(--radius-pill);
    background-color: var(--icon-button-bg);
    color: var(--icon-button-fg);
    text-decoration: none;
    cursor: pointer;
    user-select: none;
    -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
    transition:
      background-color 120ms ease,
      color 120ms ease;
  }

  .icon-button-outline {
    --icon-button-fg: var(--color-ink);
    --icon-button-border: var(--color-ink);
    --icon-button-border-disabled: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 15%, transparent);
  }

  /* The icon sits in a hidden wrapper so it is never announced; the wrapper adds no box of its own. */
  .icon-button-icon {
    display: contents;
  }

  .icon-button svg {
    flex: none;
    width: 20px;
    height: 20px;
  }

  @media (hover: hover) {
    .icon-button:is(:hover, [data-hovered]):not(:disabled, [data-disabled], [aria-disabled='true']) {
      background-color: var(--icon-button-bg-active);
      color: var(--icon-button-fg-active);
    }
  }

  /* Pressed shows the same wash as hover, since touch has no hover to show it. */
  .icon-button:is(:active, [data-pressed]):not(:disabled, [data-disabled], [aria-disabled='true']) {
    background-color: var(--icon-button-bg-active);
    color: var(--icon-button-fg-active);
  }

  .icon-button:is(:focus-visible, [data-focus-visible]) {
    outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color);
    outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);
  }

  .icon-button:is(:disabled, [data-disabled]) {
    border-color: var(--icon-button-border-disabled);
    color: var(--color-taupe);
    cursor: not-allowed;
  }

  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .icon-button {
      transition: none;
    }
  }
}
```

Notes on the file:
- `.icon-button` carries the whole ghost look, so the base class alone is a ghost button. `.icon-button-outline` is the design system's circle on cream and only swaps three custom properties: the icon color, the 1px ink edge and the faded edge for a disabled button.
- Hover reads `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)` and `[data-hovered]`, and both rules skip a disabled control, a disabled link included: React Aria marks a disabled link with `data-disabled` and `aria-disabled`, not the `disabled` attribute.
- The ring is outside the circle in the focus ring token, so no canvas inversion is needed: an inset ring on an ink fill is the only case that inverts, and this control never fills with ink.
- The disabled rule reads `--icon-button-border-disabled`, so the outline's faded edge needs no rule of its own. A rule such as `.icon-button-outline:is(:disabled) { border-color: ...var(--color-ink)... }` would also trip the guard in `css.test.js` ("never in ink"): its pattern `outline...:` followed by `var(--color-ink)` before the next semicolon matches the selector text.
- The only motion is a 120ms fade of the wash and the icon color. The last rule turns it off under reduced motion, and `css.test.js` fails any file that has a `transition` and no such block.
- There is no `position`, so a docs modifier such as `.code-copy` can place the button itself, and no `display` rule in a state selector, so `display: none` on `.rail-close` and `.nav-menu` still wins. They sit in the same layer at the same specificity, and the docs stylesheets load after core.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the component**

`packages/react/src/icon-button/IconButton.tsx`:

```tsx
'use client';

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react';
import {
  Button as RACButton,
  type ButtonProps as RACButtonProps,
  Link as RACLink,
  type LinkProps as RACLinkProps,
  composeRenderProps,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export type IconButtonVariant = 'ghost' | 'outline';

/** The props both forms share. */
interface IconButtonOptions {
  /**
   * `ghost` has no fill and no edge. `outline` is the design system's circle on cream: a transparent
   * fill with a 1px ink edge.
   * @default 'ghost'
   */
  variant?: IconButtonVariant;
}

/**
 * An icon has no text to name the button, so the types require a name: a label, or the id of an
 * element that holds it.
 */
type AccessibleName =
  | {
      /** The accessible name. Required unless `aria-labelledby` gives one. */
      'aria-label': string;
      /** The id of an element that holds the accessible name. */
      'aria-labelledby'?: string;
    }
  | {
      /** The accessible name. Required unless `aria-labelledby` gives one. */
      'aria-label'?: string;
      /** The id of an element that holds the accessible name. */
      'aria-labelledby': string;
    };

/** The button form, the default. It has no pending state, because an icon has nowhere to show one. */
type IconButtonAction = Omit<RACButtonProps, 'aria-label' | 'aria-labelledby' | 'isPending'> & {
  href?: undefined;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>;
};

/** The link form: given an `href` it renders an anchor with the same classes. */
type IconButtonAnchor = Omit<RACLinkProps, 'aria-label' | 'aria-labelledby' | 'href'> & {
  /** A URL to link to. Given an `href`, the icon button renders a link instead of a button. */
  href: NonNullable<RACLinkProps['href']>;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>;
};

/**
 * A button that holds one icon, or a link drawn the same way when given an `href`. The child is the
 * icon, such as a Lucide icon. It is hidden from assistive technology, so the name comes from
 * `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which the types require.
 */
export type IconButtonProps = IconButtonOptions & AccessibleName & (IconButtonAction | IconButtonAnchor);

const classes =
  (variant: IconButtonVariant) =>
  (userClassName: string | undefined): string =>
    cx('icon-button', variant === 'outline' && 'icon-button-outline', userClassName);

const icon = (resolved: ReactNode): ReactElement => (
  <span className="icon-button-icon" aria-hidden="true">
    {resolved}
  </span>
);

/** A button for one icon. Built on React Aria's Button, or Link when given an `href`. */
export function IconButton(props: IconButtonProps): ReactElement {
  if (props.href !== undefined) {
    const { variant = 'ghost', className, children, ...link } = props;
    return (
      <RACLink {...link} className={composeRenderProps(className, classes(variant))}>
        {composeRenderProps(children, icon)}
      </RACLink>
    );
  }
  const { variant = 'ghost', className, children, ...button } = props;
  return (
    <RACButton {...button} className={composeRenderProps(className, classes(variant))}>
      {composeRenderProps(children, icon)}
    </RACButton>
  );
}
```

Add the named exports to the end of `packages/react/src/index.ts`, after the Badge export:

The edit:

Replace:

```ts
export { Badge, type BadgeProps, type BadgeTone } from './badge';
```

with:

```ts
export { Badge, type BadgeProps, type BadgeTone } from './badge';
export { IconButton, type IconButtonProps, type IconButtonVariant } from './icon-button';
```

How the types work:
- `IconButtonProps` is `options & name & (button form | link form)`. TypeScript distributes it into four members. `props.href !== undefined` narrows to the link form because the button form types `href` as `undefined`, so each branch destructures its own props and passes `className` and `children` to the right React Aria component without a cast.
- `AccessibleName` is a union of "has `aria-label`" and "has `aria-labelledby`", each allowing the other. React Aria's own optional `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` are omitted from both forms, so only the union supplies them. Removing `& AccessibleName` from `IconButtonProps` is how to see the guard work: `pnpm --filter @snapshot-ui/react exec tsc --noEmit` then reports `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive` on both directive lines of the test file (and two story errors, since `'aria-label'` stops being a known prop). Restore the line before going on.
- `isPending` is omitted from the button form. An icon has nowhere to show a pending state, and a prop that silently disables presses with no visual would be a trap.
- The child is wrapped in `<span class="icon-button-icon" aria-hidden="true">`, drawn with `display: contents`, so the icon is decorative whatever icon library it comes from. Lucide icons also set `aria-hidden` themselves.
- React Aria's Button defaults to `type="button"`, so an IconButton in a form does not submit it. The test covers that.

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { Bell, ExternalLink, Menu, Search, Settings, X } from 'lucide-react';
import { expect, fn } from 'storybook/test';
import { IconButton } from './IconButton';

const meta = {
  title: 'Components/IconButton',
  component: IconButton,
  args: { 'aria-label': 'Search', children: <Search />, onPress: fn() },
  argTypes: {
    variant: { control: 'inline-radio', options: ['ghost', 'outline'] },
  },
} satisfies Meta<typeof IconButton>;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

export const Ghost: Story = {};

export const Outline: Story = { args: { variant: 'outline' } };

export const Disabled: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12 }}>
      <IconButton {...args} isDisabled />
      <IconButton {...args} variant="outline" isDisabled />
    </div>
  ),
};

/** Given an `href` it renders an anchor with the same classes. */
export const AsLink: Story = {
  args: {
    href: 'https://github.com/amirehsan/snapshot-ui',
    'aria-label': 'Snapshot UI on GitHub',
    children: <ExternalLink />,
  },
};

const ICONS = [
  ['Search', Search],
  ['Notifications', Bell],
  ['Settings', Settings],
  ['Menu', Menu],
  ['Close', X],
] as const;

export const Row: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
      {(['ghost', 'outline'] as const).map((variant) => (
        <div key={variant} style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 12 }}>
          {ICONS.map(([name, Icon]) => (
            <IconButton key={name} variant={variant} aria-label={name}>
              <Icon />
            </IconButton>
          ))}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
};

export const Pressed: Story = {
  // A press is transient, so no screenshot can hold it. The story test still asserts it.
  tags: ['no-visual'],
  play: async ({ args, canvas, userEvent }) => {
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Search' }));
    await expect(args.onPress).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  },
};

/** The ring sits outside the circle, so ink still reads against the page. */
export const KeyboardFocus: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvas, userEvent }) => {
    await userEvent.tab();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('button')).toHaveFocus();
  },
};
```

`Pressed` is tagged `no-visual`, so it keeps its play test and skips the screenshots. The other six stories each get 5 baselines in Step 11. Lucide has no brand icons, so the link story uses `ExternalLink`.

Run: `pnpm turbo run build test --filter=@snapshot-ui/storybook`

```tsx
'use client';

import { IconButton } from '@snapshot-ui/react';
import { Check, Copy } from 'lucide-react';
import { useState, type ReactElement } from 'react';

export default function IconButtonStates(): ReactElement {
  const [copied, setCopied] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="row" style={{ justifyContent: 'center', gap: 12 }}>
      <IconButton
        aria-label={copied ? 'Copied' : 'Copy'}
        onPress={() => {
          setCopied(true);
          setTimeout(() => {
            setCopied(false);
          }, 2000);
        }}
      >
        {copied ? <Check /> : <Copy />}
      </IconButton>
      <IconButton aria-label="Copy" isDisabled>
        <Copy />
      </IconButton>
      <IconButton variant="outline" aria-label="Copy" isDisabled>
        <Copy />
      </IconButton>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```mdx
---
title: Icon button
description: A button that holds one icon and no text. Ghost for bars and headers, outline when it needs an edge, and a link when it goes somewhere.

<Section>

## Variants

Ghost has no fill and no edge. Outline draws a 1px ink edge, for a button that has to show where it is.

<Preview name="icon-button-variants" />

</Section>

<Section>

## States

Hover and press wash the circle with a little ink, in dark as well. Disabled turns the icon taupe and ignores presses.

<Preview name="icon-button-states" />

</Section>

<Section>

## As a link

Give it an `href` and it renders an anchor with the same classes and the same need for a name. Use the link form for an icon that goes somewhere, and the button form for one that does something.

<Preview name="icon-button-link" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

The child is the icon. It is hidden from assistive technology, so the name comes from `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and the types require one of them.

      <Settings />
    </IconButton>
  );
}`} />

</Section>

<Section>

Every React Aria Button prop is accepted, or every Link prop when there is an `href`. These are the ones Snapshot UI adds or shapes.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/icon-button/IconButton.tsx" type="Pick<IconButtonProps, 'variant' | 'aria-label' | 'aria-labelledby' | 'href' | 'onPress'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A native button element, or an anchor when there is an `href`, with React Aria handling press across mouse, touch and keyboard. It is 40px square, which meets the touch target on its own.

<Keys rows={[['Space Enter', 'Activates the button.'], ['Enter', 'Follows the link, when it has an href.'], ['Tab', 'Moves focus to it. The 2px ink ring sits outside the circle.']]} />

What keeps icon buttons in the system.

<Rules dos={['Name every one for its action, such as Open the menu or Copy code.', 'Use ghost in bars and headers, and outline where the button needs an edge to read as a button.']} donts={['Never use one for the main action of a view. A Button with a label says what it does.', 'Never put text in it. If it needs words, use a Button.']} />
```

The end-to-end suite visits the Button page for axe and overflow, so look at the new page yourself. This is a throwaway script, so keep it outside the repository. Save it as `page-check.mjs` in a scratch folder:

```js
// Throwaway proof, not committed. Run from the repository root while the production docs
// server is up on DOCS_E2E_PORT.
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import path from 'node:path';

const require = createRequire(path.resolve('apps/docs/package.json'));
const { chromium } = require('@playwright/test');
const AxeBuilder = require('@axe-core/playwright').default;

const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${process.env.DOCS_E2E_PORT ?? '3100'}`;
const url = `${base}/docs/components/icon-button`;
const settled = (page) => page.locator('.header input[type="radio"]:checked').first().waitFor();

const browser = await chromium.launch();
for (const theme of ['light', 'dark']) {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ colorScheme: theme, viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  const problems = [];
  page.on('console', (message) => {
    if (['error', 'warning'].includes(message.type())) problems.push(message.text());
  });
  page.on('pageerror', (error) => problems.push(String(error)));
  await page.goto(url);
  await settled(page);
  const { violations } = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();
  console.log(`${theme}: ${violations.length} axe violations, ${problems.length} console problems`);
  await context.close();
}
for (const width of [375, 768, 1024, 1440]) {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height: 900 } });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto(url);
  await settled(page);
  const overflow = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth);
  console.log(`${String(width).padStart(4)}px: ${overflow}px of sideways scroll`);
  await context.close();
}
await browser.close();
```

Start the production server for the build you just made, run the script from the repository root, and stop the server. Stop only what you started:

```bash
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3204/; do sleep 1; done
DOCS_E2E_PORT=3204 node /path/to/page-check.mjs
kill $(lsof -nP -iTCP:3204 -sTCP:LISTEN -t)
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `cx` from `packages/react/src/utils/cx.ts`; `expectNoA11yViolations` from `packages/react/test/a11y.ts`; `CONTRAST_PAIRS` and `TEXT` from `packages/core/scripts/contrast.js`; the tokens `--spacing-part`, `--container-field`, `--text-h4`, `--text-small`, `--text-eyebrow` (each with its `--line-height`, `--letter-spacing` and `--font-weight` companions where it has them), `--radius-dot`, `--color-ink`, `--color-slate`, `--color-error` and `--color-clay`; React Aria's `Label`, `Text`, `FieldError` and `composeRenderProps`. The tests and stories also use React Aria's own `TextField` and `Input`, because the library's TextField arrives in Task 6.
- Produces five exports from `@snapshot-ui/react`, each with its props type:

```ts
// 'use client'. Each wraps React Aria and merges `className` after its own class.
export function Label(props: LabelProps): ReactElement;
export interface LabelProps extends RACLabelProps { ref?: Ref<HTMLLabelElement> } // className: string
export function Description(props: DescriptionProps): ReactElement;               // <Text slot="description">
export interface DescriptionProps extends Omit<TextProps, 'slot'> { ref?: Ref<HTMLElement> } // className: string
export function FieldError(props: FieldErrorProps): ReactElement;
export interface FieldErrorProps extends RACFieldErrorProps { ref?: Ref<HTMLElement> }       // className: string or render function

// No directive and no React Aria import: server-safe, usable in plain HTML pages too.
export function FieldCounter(props: FieldCounterProps): ReactElement;
export interface FieldCounterState { count: number; budget: number; over: boolean }
export interface FieldCounterProps extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, 'children'> {
  count: number;
  budget: number;
  showFrom?: number; // default 0.7
  label?: (state: FieldCounterState) => string; // default `${count} of about ${budget}`
  ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement>;
}
export function FieldChanged(props: FieldChangedProps): ReactElement;
export interface FieldChangedProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement> {
  children?: ReactNode; // default 'Changed'
  ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement>;
}
```

- Produces the classes `field`, `field-head`, `field-label`, `field-description`, `field-error`, `field-counter` and `field-changed`, and the state attribute `data-over` on the counter. `field-head` is a class only, no component: it is the label row.
- Produces the **field root contract** that Tasks 6 to 11 follow. A component that is a field (TextField, TextArea, CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup and the others with a label row) does this:
  1. The root element carries the class `field` next to its own class (`field radio-group`), merged with `cx` and `composeRenderProps` as Button does. `field` is a grid with 8px between its parts, a shrinking column and `max-width: var(--container-field)`, so a control inside it needs no width cap of its own.
  2. When `isChanged`, the root carries the attribute `data-changed=""` (write `data-changed={isChanged ? '' : undefined}`). Never a class, never on the control.
  3. When invalid, the root carries `data-invalid`. React Aria sets it on its TextField root; a root that does not set it gets `data-invalid={isInvalid ? '' : undefined}` from the component.
  4. The label row is `<div className="field-head">` holding `<Label>` and `<FieldChanged>{changedLabel}</FieldChanged>` (`changedLabel` defaults to `'Changed'`). The chip is always rendered in the row. field.css shows it only while the root has `data-changed` and hides it while the root has `data-invalid`, so invalid outranks changed for the chip. A field with no label row has no chip.
  5. The parts follow in this order inside the root: the label row, the control, `Description`, `FieldError`, `FieldCounter`.
  6. The control draws its own border, in its own CSS file, keyed on the root: `.field[data-changed] .input { border: 1.5px solid var(--color-signal-light); }` and, written after it at equal specificity, `.field[data-invalid] .input { border: 1.5px solid var(--color-error); }`. The error rule must come second or be more specific, because invalid outranks changed here too. The chip and the changed border always show together.
  7. A screen reader reads the chip only if the field passes the chip's id (from `useId`) to React Aria as `aria-describedby`. Do it only while the chip shows, which is while `isChanged && !isInvalid`, because an element named in `aria-describedby` is read even when `display: none` hides it. Task 5 tests that the pattern works and documents it; each later task decides whether its field applies it.
- Produces the contrast gate: `CONTRAST_PAIRS` now holds clay on all five surfaces (canvas, lifted, bone, float, raised) and error on all five, next to ink and slate, which already had them. `packages/core/test/contrast.test.js` fails if any of ink, slate, clay or error loses a surface.
- Leaves for Task 6: the docs stand-ins `.input` and `.input-changed` in `apps/docs/app/site.css` stay, and so does `className="input input-changed"` in the homepage workspace field. The three examples `field-parts`, `field-states` and `field-counter` draw a native `<input className="input">` and, in `field-states`, a plain `<span className="field-error">`, because the docs app cannot import React Aria directly and the library's TextField does not exist yet. Task 6 rewrites them with TextField and FieldError and adds the changed and invalid borders in `input.css`.

**Decisions made here, recorded in Appendix B (Step 1) and repeated so no later task reopens them:**
- FieldError is 14/450, not 500: the app's per-control problem lines (list, menu and stale-icon messages) are the footer-link step in the error color, which is the same step as the hint. The app's save bar message is 500, but that is a message beside action buttons, not a line under one control.
- A counter past its budget turns to ink at 700. The app used clay. Clay is the unsaved color in the library and error is for a value that failed, and an over-budget value saves.
- The counter is a `role="status"` span that is always in the page and empty until the count is worth showing, so its live region exists before its text. It shows from 70% of the budget, as the app did. `showFrom` (a prop beyond the minimum) lets a library user move that share, since a general library cannot hide the count from everyone below 70%; `FieldCounterState` is exported because `label` takes it.
- The Changed chip is the full 14px eyebrow step, as the app's rule draws it. The app's comments (and the docs mockup, which followed them) say 12px or "eleven pixels", but the rule applies the whole eyebrow step and nothing shrinks it.
- The chip yields to an invalid field. The app gave CHECK the one label slot; the library has no check marker, because the error line is the text cue.
- `.field` stops at `--container-field`. The app capped only the control, which left a count far from the end of a narrower input.

Then append to the end of the file (after the IconButton section), keeping a blank line before the heading:

```markdown
## Field parts

A field is a label, a control, a hint and, when they apply, an error line, a
length count and a "Changed" chip. The parts are separate so any control can
carry them. The document already gives the label and the hint their steps;
everything else here is derived.

- **The wrapper** is a grid with 8px between its parts, the "parts of one
  thing" step. It stops at `--container-field`, so a count set at the end of
  the field lands under the end of the control and a hint wraps at a readable
  measure. Its column may shrink, so a long word never pushes the page sideways.
  The label row holds the label and the chip, and the chip wraps under a long
  label instead of overflowing.
- **Label** is 14/700 in ink, the h4 step. **Description** is 14/450 in slate,
  the small step. Both are the document's own, unchanged.
- **Error** is 14/450 in the error color. The app had no inline error line, but
  its per-control problem lines (a list, a menu, a stale icon) are exactly this
  step and this color, so a field's error is the same line. It is not heavier
  than the hint: the sentence says what is wrong, so color is not the only cue,
  and the control's border and `aria-invalid` carry the rest. React Aria links
  it to the control as its description, so a screen reader reads it with the
  field.

**The length counter advises and never blocks.** It sets no `maxlength` and no
validity, so a value past the budget still saves, as in the app. It reads
"62 of about 60", the app's wording, and stays empty until the value reaches
70% of the budget: "0 of about 320" beside an empty field reads as a demand
for 320 characters. `showFrom` moves that share and `label` replaces the text.
The text sits in a polite `status` region that is in the page from the start
and empty until the count appears, because a live region that arrives
together with its text is often not announced. An empty region leaves the
layout without leaving the accessibility tree, so it costs no gap. Figures are
tabular so the count does not shimmer as it changes.

**Past the budget the count turns to ink at 700.** The app set it in clay. The
library keeps clay for the "Changed" chip alone: a value over its budget is
usually a value that was just edited, and two clay words on one field read as
one status. Error is wrong for the reason the app gave, since a value over its
budget saves. Ink at 700 is the strongest text the system has and no hue is
involved, so it holds for readers who cannot tell the colors apart. The
number already says it is over, and `label` lets an app say it in words.

**The chip is the full eyebrow step**: 14px, 700, 4% tracking, uppercase, with
a 6px dot, all in clay. The app's comments call it "a smaller scale" and
"eleven pixels", but its rule applies the whole eyebrow step and nothing
shrinks it, so the library draws what the app shipped. The dot is drawn and
the word is real text, so a screen reader reads "Changed" rather than a bullet
and the word can be replaced. The chip is an element beside the label, not
text inside it, so the control's accessible name stays the label's own.

**Invalid outranks changed, and the chip steps aside.** The app gave its label
one marker slot, and when a field was both changed and invalid the "check"
marker took it. The library has no check marker, because the error line is the
text cue, so the chip hides and the field shows the error border, the error
line and no chip. `data-changed` on the field's root shows the chip and
`data-invalid` hides it. Each control draws its own border for the two states,
and the error border wins there too.

| Color | Part | Lowest on the five surfaces, light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ink | Label, count past its budget | 16.25 | 15.36 |
| Slate | Description, count | 4.84 | 6.44 |
| Error | Error line | 6.58 | 5.06 |
| Clay | Changed chip | 6.20 | 6.02 |

The five surfaces are canvas, lifted, bone, float and raised. Clay on float and
error on bone were not in the contrast gate, so they are now: every text color
a field part uses is gated on every surface.
```

The numbers come from `paletteFor` and `contrastRatio` in `packages/core/scripts/contrast.js`: the lowest value of each color over the five surfaces. The measurements are repeated by the gate in Step 3.

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef } from 'react';
import { Input, TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { Label } from './Label';

describe('Label', () => {
  it('names the input it sits beside', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextField>
        <Label>Workspace name</Label>
        <Input />
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByLabelText('Workspace name')).toBe(screen.getByRole('textbox'));
    const label = screen.getByText('Workspace name');
    expect(label.tagName).toBe('LABEL');
    expect(label).toHaveClass('field-label');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('moves focus to the input when it is clicked', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(
      <TextField>
        <Label>Workspace name</Label>
        <Input />
      </TextField>,
    );
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Workspace name'));
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox')).toHaveFocus();
  });

  it('works on its own, tied to an input by htmlFor', () => {
    render(
      <>
        <Label htmlFor="plain">Plain field</Label>
        <input id="plain" />
      </>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByLabelText('Plain field')).toBe(screen.getByRole('textbox'));
  });

  it('can be a span, for a group caption', () => {
    render(<Label elementType="span">Theme</Label>);
    expect(screen.getByText('Theme').tagName).toBe('SPAN');
  });

  it('merges a custom className', () => {
    render(<Label className="extra">Name</Label>);
    expect(screen.getByText('Name')).toHaveClass('field-label', 'extra');
  });

  it('forwards a ref to the label element', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLLabelElement>();
    render(<Label ref={ref}>Name</Label>);
    expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLLabelElement);
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef } from 'react';
import { Input, TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { Description } from './Description';
import { FieldError } from './FieldError';
import { Label } from './Label';

describe('FieldError', () => {
  it('shows nothing while the field is valid', () => {
    render(
      <TextField>
        <Label>Email</Label>
        <Input />
        <FieldError>Enter an email address.</FieldError>
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.queryByText('Enter an email address.')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox')).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid');
  });

  it('shows its message and describes the input once the field is invalid', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextField isInvalid>
        <Label>Email</Label>
        <Input />
        <Description>We never share it.</Description>
        <FieldError>Enter an email address.</FieldError>
      </TextField>,
    );
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' });
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('We never share it. Enter an email address.');
    const error = screen.getByText('Enter an email address.');
    expect(error).toHaveClass('field-error');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('shows the message from validate and clears it when the value is fixed', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(
      <TextField
        defaultValue="nope"
        validationBehavior="aria"
        validate={(value) => (value.includes('@') ? null : 'Enter an email address.')}
      >
        <Label>Email</Label>
        <Input />
        <FieldError />
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByText('Enter an email address.')).toBeInTheDocument();
    await user.type(screen.getByRole('textbox'), '@x.com');
    expect(screen.queryByText('Enter an email address.')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('merges a custom className', () => {
    render(
      <TextField isInvalid>
        <Label>Email</Label>
        <Input />
        <FieldError className="extra">Wrong.</FieldError>
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByText('Wrong.')).toHaveClass('field-error', 'extra');
  });

  it('merges a function className, which receives the validation state', () => {
    render(
      <TextField isInvalid>
        <Label>Email</Label>
        <Input />
        <FieldError className={({ isInvalid }) => (isInvalid ? 'is-invalid' : 'is-valid')}>Wrong.</FieldError>
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByText('Wrong.')).toHaveClass('field-error', 'is-invalid');
  });

  it('forwards a ref to the element', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLElement>();
    render(
      <TextField isInvalid>
        <Label>Email</Label>
        <Input />
        <FieldError ref={ref}>Wrong.</FieldError>
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(ref.current).toHaveTextContent('Wrong.');
  });
});
```

`packages/react/src/field/FieldCounter.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef, useState, type ReactElement } from 'react';
import { Input, TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { FieldCounter } from './FieldCounter';
import { Label } from './Label';

/** A field that counts what is typed against a budget of 10. */
function Counted(): ReactElement {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');
  return (
    <TextField value={value} onChange={setValue}>
      <Label>Short description</Label>
      <Input />
      <FieldCounter count={value.length} budget={10} />
    </TextField>
  );
}

describe('FieldCounter', () => {
  it('is a polite status region that is in the page while it is still empty', () => {
    render(<FieldCounter count={0} budget={60} />);
    const counter = screen.getByRole('status');
    expect(counter).toBeEmptyDOMElement();
    expect(counter).toHaveClass('field-counter');
    expect(counter).not.toHaveAttribute('data-over');
  });

  it('stays empty until the count reaches 70% of the budget', () => {
    const { rerender } = render(<FieldCounter count={41} budget={60} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toBeEmptyDOMElement();
    rerender(<FieldCounter count={42} budget={60} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('42 of about 60');
  });

  it('reads the budget as met, not over, when the count equals it', () => {
    render(<FieldCounter count={60} budget={60} />);
    const counter = screen.getByRole('status');
    expect(counter).toHaveTextContent('60 of about 60');
    expect(counter).not.toHaveAttribute('data-over');
  });

  it('marks the count over once it passes the budget', () => {
    render(<FieldCounter count={62} budget={60} />);
    const counter = screen.getByRole('status');
    expect(counter).toHaveTextContent('62 of about 60');
    expect(counter).toHaveAttribute('data-over');
  });

  it('shows the count from a different share of the budget with showFrom', () => {
    const { rerender } = render(<FieldCounter count={0} budget={60} showFrom={0} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toBeEmptyDOMElement();
    rerender(<FieldCounter count={1} budget={60} showFrom={0} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('1 of about 60');
    rerender(<FieldCounter count={59} budget={60} showFrom={1} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toBeEmptyDOMElement();
    rerender(<FieldCounter count={60} budget={60} showFrom={1} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('60 of about 60');
  });

  it('takes its text from label, which receives the count, the budget and whether it is over', () => {
    const label = ({ count, budget, over }: { count: number; budget: number; over: boolean }): string =>
      over ? `${String(count - budget)} over` : `${String(budget - count)} left`;
    const { rerender } = render(<FieldCounter count={50} budget={60} label={label} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('10 left');
    rerender(<FieldCounter count={65} budget={60} label={label} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('5 over');
  });

  it.each([0, -5, Number.NaN])('shows nothing for a budget of %s', (budget) => {
    render(<FieldCounter count={40} budget={budget} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toBeEmptyDOMElement();
  });

  it('never blocks typing: the value keeps growing past the budget and stays valid', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Counted />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Short description' });
    expect(input).not.toHaveAttribute('maxlength');
    await user.type(input, 'a'.repeat(15));
    expect(input).toHaveValue('a'.repeat(15));
    expect(input).toBeValid();
    expect(input).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid');
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('15 of about 10');
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveAttribute('data-over');
  });

  it('merges a custom className and passes other attributes through', () => {
    render(<FieldCounter count={50} budget={60} className="extra" id="count" />);
    const counter = screen.getByRole('status');
    expect(counter).toHaveClass('field-counter', 'extra');
    expect(counter).toHaveAttribute('id', 'count');
  });

  it('forwards a ref to the element', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLSpanElement>();
    render(<FieldCounter ref={ref} count={50} budget={60} />);
    expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLSpanElement);
  });

  it.each([
    ['empty', 3],
    ['near the budget', 50],
    ['over the budget', 70],
  ])('has no axe violations when %s', async (_state, count) => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextField>
        <Label>Short description</Label>
        <Input />
        <FieldCounter count={count} budget={60} />
      </TextField>,
    );
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });
});
```

`packages/core/src/components/field.css`:

```css
/*
 * The parts of a field, derived in docs/design-system.md ("Field parts").
 *
 * A field's root carries the class `field` and, as they apply, the attributes
 * `data-changed` and `data-invalid`. Those two attributes are the whole state:
 * the chip below shows on the first and gives way to the second, and each
 * control draws its own border for them in its own file. Invalid outranks
 * changed everywhere.
 */
@layer components {
  .field {
    display: grid;
    /* A column that may shrink, so one long word never pushes the page sideways. */
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
    align-content: start;
    /* Parts of one thing: label to control to hint. */
    gap: var(--spacing-part);
    /* The widest a control grows, so a count set at the end of the field lands
       under the end of the control and a hint wraps at a readable measure. */
    max-width: var(--container-field);
  }

  /* The label row. The chip sits beside the label and wraps under it when the
     label is long, so a narrow screen never scrolls sideways. */
  .field-head {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    align-items: baseline;
    column-gap: var(--spacing-part);
    min-width: 0;
  }

  .field-label {
    color: var(--color-ink);
    font-size: var(--text-h4);
    line-height: var(--text-h4--line-height);
    font-weight: var(--text-h4--font-weight);
  }

  .field-description,
  .field-error {
    display: block;
    font-size: var(--text-small);
    line-height: var(--text-small--line-height);
    font-weight: var(--text-small--font-weight);
  }

  .field-description {
    color: var(--color-slate);
  }

  .field-error {
    color: var(--color-error);
  }

  /*
   * The length count. It advises and never blocks. While it has nothing to say
   * it is empty, and an empty region leaves the layout (absolute, so it takes
   * no grid row and no gap) without leaving the accessibility tree, since a
   * live region that arrives together with its text is often not announced.
   */
  .field-counter {
    justify-self: end;
    color: var(--color-slate);
    font-size: var(--text-small);
    line-height: var(--text-small--line-height);
    font-weight: var(--text-small--font-weight);
    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  }

  .field-counter:empty {
    position: absolute;
    width: 1px;
    height: 1px;
    margin: -1px;
    overflow: hidden;
    clip-path: inset(50%);
    white-space: nowrap;
  }

  /* Past the budget: ink at 700, the strongest text the system has. Never clay,
     which means unsaved, and never error, since the value still saves. */
  .field-counter[data-over] {
    color: var(--color-ink);
    font-weight: 700;
  }

  /*
   * The "Changed" chip: the full eyebrow step in clay with a 6px dot. The dot
   * is drawn and out of flow, so the chip's baseline is its text's and it lines
   * up with the label whatever the label does.
   */
  .field-changed {
    position: relative;
    display: inline-block;
    padding-inline-start: calc(0.375rem + var(--spacing-part));
    color: var(--color-clay);
    font-size: var(--text-eyebrow);
    line-height: var(--text-eyebrow--line-height);
    letter-spacing: var(--text-eyebrow--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-eyebrow--font-weight);
    text-transform: uppercase;
    white-space: nowrap;
  }

  .field-changed::before {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    inset-block-start: 50%;
    inset-inline-start: 0;
    width: 0.375rem;
    height: 0.375rem;
    translate: 0 -50%;
    border-radius: var(--radius-dot);
    background-color: currentcolor;
  }

  /* The chip belongs to a changed field and yields to an invalid one: the error
     line is the text cue, and the control's border shows the error. */
  .field:not([data-changed]) .field-changed,
  .field[data-invalid] .field-changed {
    display: none;
  }
}
```

```tsx
'use client';

import type { ReactElement, Ref } from 'react';
import { Label as RACLabel, type LabelProps as RACLabelProps } from 'react-aria-components';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export interface LabelProps extends RACLabelProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLLabelElement>;
}

/**
 * The name of a field: 14px, bold, in ink. Inside a React Aria field it names
 * the control. On its own, tie it to an input with `htmlFor`, or set
 * `elementType="span"` for a caption that names a group.
 */
export function Label({ className, ...props }: LabelProps): ReactElement {
  return <RACLabel {...props} className={cx('field-label', className)} />;
}
```

```tsx
import type { ReactElement, Ref } from 'react';
import {

  type FieldErrorProps as RACFieldErrorProps,
  composeRenderProps,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export interface FieldErrorProps extends RACFieldErrorProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>;
}

/**
 * The error line of a field, in the error color. It renders only while the
 * field is invalid, and shows its children or, without any, the field's own
 * validation messages. It must sit inside a React Aria field.
 */
export function FieldError({ className, ...props }: FieldErrorProps): ReactElement {
  return (
    <RACFieldError
      {...props}
      className={composeRenderProps(className, (userClassName) => cx('field-error', userClassName))}
    />
  );
}
```

`packages/react/src/field/FieldCounter.tsx` (no `'use client'`, no React Aria):

```tsx
import type { HTMLAttributes, ReactElement, Ref } from 'react';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

/** The numbers a counter's text is made from. */
export interface FieldCounterState {
  /** How much has been written. */
  count: number;
  /** About how much is wanted. */
  budget: number;
  /** Whether the count is past the budget. */
  over: boolean;
}

export interface FieldCounterProps extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, 'children'> {
  /** How much has been written: usually the length of the value. */
  count: number;
  /**
   * About how much is wanted. A budget, not a limit: nothing stops a longer
   * value. A budget that is not a positive number shows nothing.
   */
  budget: number;
  /**
   * The share of the budget at which the count first appears, from 0 to 1.
   * Nothing shows while the count is 0, whatever this is.
   * @default 0.7
   */
  showFrom?: number;
  /**
   * Replaces the text. Return an empty string to show nothing.
   * @default ({ count, budget }) => `${count} of about ${budget}`
   */
  label?: (state: FieldCounterState) => string;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement>;
}

const defaultLabel = ({ count, budget }: FieldCounterState): string =>
  `${String(count)} of about ${String(budget)}`;

/**
 * A length count against a budget. It advises and never blocks: it sets no
 * maxlength and no validity. It is a polite status region that stays in the
 * page, empty, until the count is worth showing.
 */
export function FieldCounter({
  count,
  budget,
  showFrom = 0.7,
  label = defaultLabel,
  className,
  ...props
}: FieldCounterProps): ReactElement {
  const over = count > budget;
  const shown = budget > 0 && count > 0 && count >= Math.round(budget * showFrom);
  return (
    <span
      role="status"
      {...props}
      className={cx('field-counter', className)}
      data-over={shown && over ? '' : undefined}
    >
      {shown ? label({ count, budget, over }) : null}
    </span>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Stories**

The library's TextField does not exist yet, so the stories compose the parts inside React Aria's `TextField` with its `Input`, which is how a custom layout uses them, and give the input a minimal look of its own in a story-only `<style>` made of tokens. They show the parts inside a real field, which is the only place FieldError renders at all and the only place the `data-invalid` half of the contract can be seen. Showing the parts alone would leave both unseen. The three borders in the story CSS are the contract's step 6, written out once so the states read right; Task 6 owns the real ones.

The `play` functions are real-browser tests (Storybook runs them in Chromium, in light and dark), so they check the CSS contract that jsdom cannot: the chip is hidden by default, shown on a changed field and hidden again on a field that is both changed and invalid, and the over-budget count computes to weight 700.

`packages/react/src/field/Field.stories.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { useState, type ReactElement } from 'react';
import { Input, TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { expect } from 'storybook/test';
import { Description } from './Description';
import { FieldChanged } from './FieldChanged';
import { FieldCounter } from './FieldCounter';
import { FieldError } from './FieldError';
import { Label } from './Label';

// The library's TextField arrives with its own input. Until then these stories
// compose the parts inside React Aria's TextField, which is exactly how a
// custom layout uses them. The input gets a minimal look of its own, drawn in
// tokens, so the parts are seen next to a control.
const STORY_CSS = `
.story-field-input {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: 100%;
  height: 48px;
  padding-inline: 1.5rem;
  border: 1px solid var(--color-boundary);
  border-radius: var(--radius-pill);
  background-color: var(--color-raised);
  color: var(--color-ink);
  font: inherit;
}
.field[data-changed] .story-field-input {
  border: 1.5px solid var(--color-signal-light);
}
.field[data-invalid] .story-field-input {
  border: 1.5px solid var(--color-error);
}
`;

const NEAR_BUDGET = 'A shared space for the whole Northwind design team';
const OVER_BUDGET = 'A shared space for the whole Northwind design team and its guests';

interface SampleFieldProps {
  label?: string;
  description?: string;
  errorMessage?: string;
  isInvalid?: boolean;
  isChanged?: boolean;
  budget?: number;
  defaultValue?: string;
}

/** A field built from the parts: the root carries `data-changed`, and React Aria adds `data-invalid`. */
function SampleField({
  label = 'Workspace name',
  description,
  errorMessage,
  isInvalid,
  isChanged,
  budget,
  defaultValue = '',
}: SampleFieldProps): ReactElement {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(defaultValue);
  return (
    <div style={{ width: 'min(28rem, calc(100vw - 2rem))' }}>
      <style>{STORY_CSS}</style>
      <TextField
        className="field"
        data-changed={isChanged ? '' : undefined}
        isInvalid={isInvalid}
        value={value}
        onChange={setValue}
      >
        <div className="field-head">
          <Label>{label}</Label>
          <FieldChanged />
        </div>
        <Input className="story-field-input" />
        {description ? <Description>{description}</Description> : null}
        <FieldError>{errorMessage}</FieldError>
        {budget ? <FieldCounter count={value.length} budget={budget} /> : null}
      </TextField>
    </div>
  );
}

const meta = {
  title: 'Components/Field',
  component: SampleField,
  args: { description: 'Shown in the header and in every invite.' },
} satisfies Meta<typeof SampleField>;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

/** A label, a control and a hint. The Changed chip is in the page and hidden. */
export const Default: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Changed')).not.toBeVisible();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' })).toHaveAccessibleDescription(
      'Shown in the header and in every invite.',
    );
  },
};

/** `data-changed` on the root shows the clay chip and the control draws its own border. */
export const Changed: Story = {
  args: { isChanged: true, defaultValue: 'Northwind Studio' },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Changed')).toBeVisible();
  },
};

/** The error line appears with the field's invalid state and describes the control. */
export const Invalid: Story = {
  args: { isInvalid: true, errorMessage: 'Enter a name for the workspace.' },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Enter a name for the workspace.')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' })).toBeInvalid();
  },
};

/** Invalid outranks changed: the error border and the error line show, and the chip steps aside. */
export const InvalidAndChanged: Story = {
  args: {
    isChanged: true,
    isInvalid: true,
    errorMessage: 'Enter a name for the workspace.',
    defaultValue: '!',
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Changed')).not.toBeVisible();
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Enter a name for the workspace.')).toBeVisible();
  },
};

/** From 70% of the budget the count appears, quiet and slate. */
export const CounterNearBudget: Story = {
  args: {
    label: 'Short description',
    description: 'One sentence, for search results.',
    budget: 60,
    defaultValue: NEAR_BUDGET,
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('50 of about 60');
  },
};

/** Past the budget the count turns to ink at 700. Typing was never blocked, and the value still saves. */
export const CounterOverBudget: Story = {
  args: {
    label: 'Short description',
    description: 'One sentence, for search results.',
    budget: 60,
    defaultValue: OVER_BUDGET,
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const counter = canvas.getByRole('status');
    await expect(counter).toHaveTextContent('65 of about 60');
    await expect(counter).toHaveAttribute('data-over');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(counter).fontWeight).toBe('700');
  },
};

/** A long label wraps and the chip drops under it, with no sideways scroll at 375px. */
export const LongLabel: Story = {
  args: {
    label: 'The name your team sees in the header, in every invite and in the billing emails',
    isChanged: true,
    defaultValue: 'Northwind Studio',
  },
};

/** Typing past the budget is never blocked. */
export const TypingPastBudget: Story = {
  tags: ['no-visual'],
  args: { label: 'Short description', description: 'One sentence, for search results.', budget: 10 },
  play: async ({ canvas, userEvent }) => {
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Short description' });
    await userEvent.type(input, 'fourteen chars');
    await expect(input).toHaveValue('fourteen chars');
    await expect(input).toBeValid();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('14 of about 10');
  },
};
```

The page, `apps/docs/content/docs/components/field.mdx`. It has no Keys table because the parts are not interactive. The Accessibility section is prose, and the Props section has one table per part that adds props:

```mdx
---
title: Field parts
description: The label, hint, error line, length count and Changed chip that every field is made of, and the two attributes that carry a field's state.
icon: TextCursorInput
---

<Section>

## Parts

A field is a grid of parts with 8px between them. Label names the control, Description is the hint under it, and the clay chip marks an unsaved value. Type in the box to change it.

<Preview name="field-parts" />

</Section>

<Section>

## States

A field's root carries two attributes. `data-changed` shows the Changed chip. `data-invalid` hides it, because invalid outranks changed: the error line and the control's error border show instead. The first field is changed. The second is changed and invalid.

<Preview name="field-states" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Length count

A count advises and never blocks. It stays empty until the value reaches 70% of the budget, reads "34 of about 40", and past the budget turns to ink at 700. Nothing stops the value from growing, and it still saves.

<Preview name="field-counter" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

Inside a React Aria field the parts wire themselves: Label names the control, Description and FieldError become its description, and FieldError appears only while the field is invalid. Put the `field` class and `data-changed` on the field's root, and keep the chip in the label row, where the stylesheet shows or hides it.

<Code code={`import { Input, TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { Description, FieldChanged, FieldCounter, FieldError, Label } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function ShortDescription({
  value,
  onChange,
  isChanged,
}: {
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  isChanged: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <TextField
      className="field"
      data-changed={isChanged ? '' : undefined}
      value={value}
      onChange={onChange}
    >
      <div className="field-head">
        <Label>Short description</Label>
        <FieldChanged />
      </div>
      <Input className="input" />
      <Description>One sentence, for search results.</Description>
      <FieldError />
      <FieldCounter count={value.length} budget={60} />
    </TextField>
  );
}`} />

The classes are `field`, `field-head`, `field-label`, `field-description`, `field-error`, `field-counter` and `field-changed`, so the same parts work in plain HTML.

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

The count takes the numbers and the text. The chip takes its text as children. Label, Description and FieldError accept React Aria's Label, Text and FieldError props.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/field/FieldCounter.tsx" type="Pick<FieldCounterProps, 'count' | 'budget' | 'showFrom' | 'label'>" />

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/field/FieldChanged.tsx" type="Pick<FieldChangedProps, 'children'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

Label is a real label, so a click on it focuses the control. Description and FieldError join the control's accessible description. The chip sits beside the label, not inside it, so the control keeps its name. To have a screen reader read it with the field, give the chip an `id` and pass that id to the field as `aria-describedby` while the chip shows. A hidden element named in `aria-describedby` is still read.

The count is a polite status region that is in the page from the start and empty until it has something to say, so a screen reader announces it as it changes. To announce less often, pass it a count that settles after a pause.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps fields in the system.

<Rules dos={['Say what the field is in the label, in sentence case, and keep the hint for what the label cannot say.', 'Show a count only where length helps the reader. It advises; a budget is not a limit.', 'Let the control draw the changed border whenever the chip shows. They always appear together.']} donts={['Never use clay for anything but the Changed chip. It means unsaved.', 'Never block typing at the budget. Past it the count turns to ink and the value still saves.', 'Never leave the chip beside an error. Invalid outranks changed.']} />

</Section>
```
