**Decisions made here, recorded in Appendix B (Step 1) and repeated so no later task reopens them:**

- **Focus keeps the ring and firms the edge.** The design document says a dark input's focus "firms to 1.5px solid white with the outline removed", and Appendix A gives every control a 2px ink ring at 2px offset. Following the first alone makes a focused changed or invalid field look unfocused, because their 1.5px edges outrank the focus edge. So at rest focus draws the 1.5px ink edge inside the ring, and a changed or invalid field keeps its own edge with the ring alone showing focus. The ring is the token ring in every state (the app drew it in the error color on an invalid field). Two stories, `Focused` and `ChangedAndFocused`, hold both cases in the visual baselines and assert the computed outline.
- **The chip also leaves the page while React Aria finds the field invalid.** The helper's `isInvalid` option sees only the `isInvalid` prop. A required field that was emptied and submitted, or one whose `validate` returned a message, is invalid inside React Aria, so `isInvalid` stays false while the root has `data-invalid`, the chip is hidden by CSS and the stale id would still name it in `aria-describedby`, which screen readers read even from `display: none`. `FieldHead` therefore reads React Aria's `FieldErrorContext` and renders no chip while the field is invalid by any cause. A dangling id in `aria-describedby` is skipped by assistive technology and passes axe. Each half has tests that fail without it; Step 4 says how to see them fail.
- **Read-only looks like an enabled field.** The source draws no read-only input; its dashed "static" value is page text. A read-only field keeps its look, focus, selection and its place in the form, and the hooks for an app that wants another look are `readonly` on the input and `data-readonly` on the root.
- **No contrast pair was added.** Every edge the input draws is already gated (the boundary against its fill, ink, error) or deliberately quiet and measured in Appendix B: taupe placeholder 1.58:1 (light) and 3.68:1 (dark) on the raised fill, and the light signal orange changed edge 2.53 to 2.87:1 on the light surfaces, under the 3:1 a boundary asks. Adding either to `CONTRAST_PAIRS` would fail the gate, so they are recorded rather than gated.
- **The input has no transition,** so there is nothing for reduced motion to stop and `input.css` has no `prefers-reduced-motion` block (the app's has no transition, and core components never animate shape). The docs keep their shape transition on `.input`, which the global reduced-motion rule in `site.css` stops.
- **`budget` counts the value's length as typed.** The app trimmed the value and collapsed runs of spaces before counting; the library counts what the form submits.
- **The cursor stays the I-beam,** not the pointer: the pointer rule is for pressed controls. A disabled field takes `not-allowed`.
- **The input is 16px,** so iOS Safari does not zoom the page on focus.
- **The six homepage axis tiles** drew a hand-classed `<input class="input">` with no name. They become the library's `Input` with an `aria-label`, so no hand-drawn use of the class is left.
- **`Field.stories.tsx` keeps its own story-only input CSS.** It shows the parts in a custom layout on React Aria's own `TextField`, which is the case the stories are for, and changing it would move 35 baselines. Only its comment, which said the library's TextField was still to come, changes.
- **Input and TextField live in `packages/react/src/text-field/`,** one folder per component; the shared helper lives in `field/` next to the parts.

- [ ] **Step 1: Record the derivation**

Append to the end of `docs/design-system.md` (after the Field parts section), keeping a blank line before the heading:

```markdown

## TextField

The document specifies one input, the nav search field, and Appendix A derived
the settings input from it. The library keeps that input and changes a few
things, each recorded here.

- **Shape and fill** are the app's: 48px tall, `--radius-pill`, the Raised
  fill, 24px by 12px padding, and the 16px body step at weight 450 in ink. 16px
  also keeps iOS Safari from zooming the page when the field takes focus. The
  radius is a token, so the pill follows the shape axis. The field fills its
  column and `field` caps the column at `--container-field`, so the control has
  no width limit of its own.
- **The edge** is `--color-boundary`, 1px, the document's own 50% ink. The app
  dropped it to 40%, which measures 2.58:1 on white ("Four colors added").
- **Hover** darkens the edge to ink at 65%, the app's value, and only where
  hover exists. It measures 5.72 against the Raised fill in light and 7.30 in
  dark. The changed and invalid edges outrank it.
- **The cursor** stays the text I-beam. The pointer rule is for controls that
  are pressed. A disabled field takes `not-allowed`.
- **Read-only looks like an enabled field.** The app draws no read-only input.
  Its dashed "static" value is page text for a value another panel edits, not an
  input. A read-only field keeps focus, selection and its place in the form,
  so only the browser's `readonly` and React Aria's `data-readonly` on the
  field's root mark it, and an app that wants a quieter look can draw one from
  those.

**Focus firms the edge and keeps the ring.** Section 7 says a dark input's
focus "firms to 1.5px solid white with the outline removed", and Appendix A
gives every control a 2px ink ring at 2px offset. The library does both, for a
reason the section 7 sentence cannot cover: the changed and invalid edges are
1.5px already and outrank the focus edge, so with no ring a focused changed or
invalid field would look exactly like an unfocused one, on the two fields that
most need attention. At rest, focus draws a 1.5px ink edge (white in dark,
which is the document's value to the letter) inside the ring. A changed or
invalid field keeps its own edge and the ring alone shows focus. The ring is
the token ring in every state. The app drew it in the error color on an
invalid field; one color means a theme recolors focus from `--focus-ring-color`
alone and a reader learns one cue.

**Placeholder is taupe, which is quiet by design.** Taupe measures 1.58 against
the Raised fill in light and 3.68 in dark, under the 4.5 a sentence needs. It
is the document's designated whisper, so a placeholder shows an example and
never carries what the label does not: the label always names the field.
Firefox dims a placeholder on its own, so opacity is set to 1 and taupe is the
only color.

**Disabled** uses the `disabled` fill, taupe text and an ink edge at 15%, the
app's value and the same edge as a disabled Button. The edge measures 1.37
against the fill in light and 1.59 in dark. An inactive control is outside the
3:1 asked of a boundary, and in dark the recessed fill ("Four colors added") is
what sets it apart. The changed and invalid edges outrank the disabled edge,
because the chip and the changed border always show together.

**Changed and invalid are borders on the control, keyed on the field's root.**
The root carries `data-changed` and, from React Aria, `data-invalid`. Changed
is Light Signal Orange at 1.5px and invalid is the error color at 1.5px. The
invalid rule is declared after the changed one, so a field that is both shows
the error edge (the app showed the orange one).

| Edge | Lowest on the five surfaces, light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ink (the focus edge) | 16.25 | 15.36 |
| Error (invalid) | 6.58 | 5.06 |
| Light Signal Orange (changed) | 2.53 | 5.35 |

Light Signal Orange is under the 3:1 that a boundary asks on every light
surface (2.53 to 2.87), and while a field is changed it is the field's edge.
That is the document's own choice of attention cue, kept and recorded rather
than gated, since it would fail the gate. The cue is never alone: the clay chip
carries the word and is gated, the chip is read with the field, and the label,
the value and the ring still identify the control.

**The length count counts what will be saved.** `budget` counts the value's
length as typed. The app trimmed the value and collapsed runs of spaces first;
the library's count is the value the form submits, so the figure never
disagrees with what a server receives. Everything else about the count is the
field parts' own: it advises, never blocks, and appears from 70% of the budget.

**The Changed chip is announced.** The border and the chip are visual, so
TextField passes the chip's id to React Aria as `aria-describedby` while the
field is changed and shows its chip, merged with any `aria-describedby` the
caller passes. A screen reader then reads the hint and then "Changed" with the
field. An element named in `aria-describedby` is read even when `display: none`
hides it, so the chip also leaves the page while the field is invalid by any
cause and not only through `isInvalid`: a required field that was emptied and
submitted is changed and invalid, and must read its error alone. The label
row, the chip and this wiring are one internal helper (`FieldHead` and
`useChangedDescription`) that every later field with a label row uses, so
they all behave alike.

**The input does not animate.** The app's has no transition, and core
components never animate shape, so there is nothing for reduced motion to
stop. The docs site keeps its own shape transition, which its global
reduced-motion rule stops.

No pairing was added to the contrast gate. Every color the input draws is
gated already (ink, error, the boundary against its fill) or deliberately
quiet and recorded above (taupe, Light Signal Orange in light).
```

The numbers come from `paletteFor` and `contrastRatio` in `packages/core/scripts/contrast.js`. Taupe is measured over the Raised fill, the translucent dark values are composited over the surface they sit on, and the edges are measured against the surface each sits on.

`packages/react/src/field/useChangedDescription.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { renderHook } from '@testing-library/react';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { useChangedDescription } from './useChangedDescription';

describe('useChangedDescription', () => {
  it('leaves aria-describedby alone while the field is not changed', () => {
    const none = renderHook(() => useChangedDescription({ isChanged: false }));
    expect(none.result.current.describedBy).toBeUndefined();
    const caller = renderHook(() => useChangedDescription({ describedBy: 'note' }));
    expect(caller.result.current.describedBy).toBe('note');
  });

  it('names the chip while the field is changed', () => {
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useChangedDescription({ isChanged: true }));
    expect(result.current.chipId).not.toBe('');
    expect(result.current.describedBy).toBe(result.current.chipId);
  });

  it('puts the chip after the id the caller passed', () => {
    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
      useChangedDescription({ isChanged: true, describedBy: 'note other' }),
    );
    expect(result.current.describedBy).toBe(`note other ${result.current.chipId}`);
  });

  it('drops the chip while the field is invalid, and keeps what the caller passed', () => {
    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
      useChangedDescription({ isChanged: true, isInvalid: true, describedBy: 'note' }),
    );
    expect(result.current.describedBy).toBe('note');
    const alone = renderHook(() => useChangedDescription({ isChanged: true, isInvalid: true }));
    expect(alone.result.current.describedBy).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('follows the field as it changes and becomes invalid, with one id throughout', () => {
    const { result, rerender } = renderHook((props) => useChangedDescription(props), {
      initialProps: { isChanged: false, isInvalid: false, describedBy: 'note' },
    });
    const { chipId } = result.current;
    expect(result.current.describedBy).toBe('note');
    rerender({ isChanged: true, isInvalid: false, describedBy: 'note' });
    expect(result.current.describedBy).toBe(`note ${chipId}`);
    rerender({ isChanged: true, isInvalid: true, describedBy: 'note' });
    expect(result.current.describedBy).toBe('note');
    expect(result.current.chipId).toBe(chipId);
  });

  it('gives each field its own chip id', () => {
    const first = renderHook(() => useChangedDescription({ isChanged: true }));
    const second = renderHook(() => useChangedDescription({ isChanged: true }));
    expect(first.result.current.chipId).not.toBe(second.result.current.chipId);
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { Input, RadioButton, RadioField, RadioGroup, TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { FieldHead } from './FieldHead';

describe('FieldHead', () => {
  it('is the label row: the label, then the Changed chip with its id', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextField className="field" data-changed="">
        <FieldHead label="Workspace name" chipId="workspace-chip" />
        <Input />
      </TextField>,
    );
    const row = container.querySelector('.field-head');
    expect(row).not.toBeNull();
    expect([...(row?.children ?? [])].map((child) => child.className)).toEqual([
      'field-label',
      'field-changed',
    ]);
    const chip = screen.getByText('Changed');
    expect(chip).toHaveAttribute('id', 'workspace-chip');
    expect(chip.parentElement).toBe(row);
    // The chip sits beside the label, so the control's name is the label alone.
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox')).toHaveAccessibleName('Workspace name');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('takes other text for the chip', () => {
    render(
      <TextField>
        <FieldHead label="Name" changedLabel="Unsaved" chipId="chip" />
        <Input />
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByText('Unsaved')).toHaveClass('field-changed');
    expect(screen.queryByText('Changed')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('leaves the chip out of the page while the field is invalid', () => {
    const { rerender } = render(
      <TextField>
        <FieldHead label="Name" chipId="chip" />
        <Input />
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByText('Changed')).toBeInTheDocument();
    rerender(
      <TextField isInvalid>
        <FieldHead label="Name" chipId="chip" />
        <Input />
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.queryByText('Changed')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText('Name')).toHaveClass('field-label');
  });

  it('leaves the chip out when validation that React Aria runs makes the field invalid', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(
      <TextField validate={(value) => (value === '' ? 'Enter a name.' : null)} validationBehavior="aria">
        <FieldHead label="Name" chipId="chip" />
        <Input />
      </TextField>,
    );
    expect(screen.queryByText('Changed')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    await user.type(screen.getByRole('textbox'), 'a');
    expect(screen.getByText('Changed')).toBeInTheDocument();
    await user.clear(screen.getByRole('textbox'));
    expect(screen.queryByText('Changed')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('renders outside a field too, and in a group, where it names the group', () => {
    const { unmount } = render(<FieldHead label="Plain" chipId="plain-chip" />);
    expect(screen.getByText('Plain')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText('Changed')).toHaveAttribute('id', 'plain-chip');
    unmount();
    render(
      <RadioGroup>
        <FieldHead label="Size" chipId="size-chip" />
        <RadioField value="s">
          <RadioButton>Small</RadioButton>
        </RadioField>
      </RadioGroup>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Size' })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef } from 'react';
import { TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { Description } from '../field/Description';
import { Label } from '../field/Label';
import { Input } from './Input';

describe('Input', () => {
  it('is a text input with the input class', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Input aria-label="Search" placeholder="Search settings" />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' });
    expect(input).toHaveClass('input');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('placeholder', 'Search settings');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('takes the label and the hint of the React Aria field around it', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(
      <TextField>
        <Label>Email</Label>
        <Input />
        <Description>We never share it.</Description>
      </TextField>,
    );
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' });
    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('We never share it.');
    await user.type(input, 'a@b.co');
    expect(input).toHaveValue('a@b.co');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('merges a custom className after its own', () => {
    render(<Input aria-label="Search" className="extra" />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox')).toHaveClass('input', 'extra');
  });

  it('merges a function className, which receives the input state', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(
      <Input aria-label="Search" className={({ isFocused }) => (isFocused ? 'is-focused' : 'is-idle')} />,
    );
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    expect(input).toHaveClass('input', 'is-idle');
    await user.click(input);
    expect(input).toHaveClass('input', 'is-focused');
    expect(input).not.toHaveClass('is-idle');
  });

  it('forwards a ref to the input element', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLInputElement>();
    render(<Input ref={ref} aria-label="Search" />);
    expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLInputElement);
    expect(ref.current).toBe(screen.getByRole('textbox'));
  });

  it('passes its other attributes to the input', () => {
    render(<Input aria-label="Email" type="email" name="email" autoComplete="email" />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('type', 'email');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('name', 'email');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'email');
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { act, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef, useState, type ReactElement } from 'react';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { TextField, type TextFieldProps } from './TextField';

/** A field the caller controls, the way a form library would. */
function Controlled(props: TextFieldProps): ReactElement {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('Northwind');
  return <TextField {...props} value={value} onChange={setValue} />;
}

const root = (container: HTMLElement): Element => {
  const element = container.firstElementChild;
  if (!element) throw new Error('Nothing rendered');
  return element;
};

describe('TextField', () => {
  it('renders a labelled input with a hint, inside a field', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextField label="Workspace name" description="Shown in the header." placeholder="Northwind Studio" />,
    );
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    expect(input).toHaveClass('input');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('placeholder', 'Northwind Studio');
    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Shown in the header.');
    expect(screen.getByText('Workspace name')).toHaveClass('field-label');
    expect(screen.getByText('Shown in the header.')).toHaveClass('field-description');
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field');
    expect(root(container)).not.toHaveAttribute('data-changed');
    expect(root(container)).not.toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('puts its parts in the order the field contract asks for', () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextField
        label="Short description"
        description="One sentence."
        isInvalid
        errorMessage="Too vague."
        budget={10}
        defaultValue="abcdefgh"
      />,
    );
    expect([...root(container).children].map((child) => child.classList[0])).toEqual([
      'field-head',
      'input',
      'field-description',
      'field-error',
      'field-counter',
    ]);
  });

  it('types into an uncontrolled field', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    render(<TextField label="Name" defaultValue="Northwind" onChange={onChange} />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    expect(input).toHaveValue('Northwind');
    await user.type(input, ' East');
    expect(input).toHaveValue('Northwind East');
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5);
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('Northwind East');
  });

  it('follows the value of a controlled field, and tells the caller what was typed', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    const { rerender } = render(<TextField label="Name" value="one" onChange={onChange} />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    await user.type(input, 'x');
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith('onex');
    expect(input).toHaveValue('one');
    rerender(<TextField label="Name" value="two" onChange={onChange} />);
    expect(input).toHaveValue('two');
  });

  it('works with a state the caller keeps', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Controlled label="Name" />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    await user.type(input, ' East');
    expect(input).toHaveValue('Northwind East');
  });

  it('submits its value in a plain form under its name', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <TextField label="Email" name="email" defaultValue="a@b.co" />
      </form>,
    );
    const form = container.querySelector('form');
    if (!form) throw new Error('No form');
    expect(new FormData(form).get('email')).toBe('a@b.co');
    await user.type(screen.getByRole('textbox'), 'm');
    expect(new FormData(form).get('email')).toBe('a@b.com');
  });

  it('shows the error and sets data-invalid after a required field is submitted empty', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <TextField label="Name" name="name" isRequired errorMessage="Enter a name." />
        <button type="submit">Save</button>
      </form>,
    );
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: /Name/ });
    expect(input).toBeRequired();
    expect(screen.queryByText('Enter a name.')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(root(container).firstElementChild).not.toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }));
    const error = screen.getByText('Enter a name.');
    expect(error).toHaveClass('field-error');
    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Enter a name.');
    expect(container.querySelector('.field')).toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
    expect(input).toBeInvalid();
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
    // The native error stays while the field is being edited and clears when the edit is committed.
    await user.type(input, 'Northwind');
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.queryByText('Enter a name.')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(container.querySelector('.field')).not.toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
  });

  it('shows the message of a custom validate function', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(
      <TextField
        label="Email"

    expect(input).toBeValid();

  it('blocks a submit that validate rejects, with the native behavior', async () => {

  it('builds the error from a function of the validation result', () => {
    render(
      <TextField
        label="Email"
        defaultValue="nope"
        validationBehavior="aria"
        validate={() => 'Too short.'}

          `${isInvalid ? 'Invalid' : 'Valid'}: ${validationErrors.join(' ')}`
        }
      />,
    );
    expect(screen.getByText('Invalid: Too short.')).toHaveClass('field-error');
  });

  it('shows the changed chip, and a screen reader reads it with the field', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextField
        label="Workspace name"
        description="Shown in the header."
        isChanged
        defaultValue="Northwind"
      />,
    );
    expect(root(container)).toHaveAttribute('data-changed', '');
    const chip = screen.getByText('Changed');
    expect(chip).toHaveClass('field-changed');
    expect(chip.parentElement).toHaveClass('field-head');
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });

    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Shown in the header. Changed');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('takes the chip text from changedLabel', () => {
    render(<TextField label="Name" isChanged changedLabel="Unsaved" />);
    expect(screen.getByText('Unsaved')).toHaveClass('field-changed');
    expect(screen.queryByText('Changed')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox')).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Unsaved');
  });

  it('keeps the chip in the page, unannounced, while the field is not changed', () => {
    render(<TextField label="Name" description="Shown in the header." />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Shown in the header.');
    expect(input.getAttribute('aria-describedby')?.split(' ')).not.toContain(screen.getByText('Changed').id);

  it('adds the chip to the aria-describedby the caller passes', () => {
    render(

  it('draws no chip for a field without a label row', () => {

  it('lets invalid outrank changed: the chip is gone and no longer announced', async () => {
    const { container, rerender } = render(

  it('lets invalid outrank changed when React Aria finds the field invalid', async () => {

    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' });
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('type', 'email');
    expect(input).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'email');
  });

  it('forwards ref to the field and inputRef to the input', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLDivElement>();
    const inputRef = createRef<HTMLInputElement>();
    render(<TextField ref={ref} inputRef={inputRef} label="Name" />);
    expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLDivElement);
    expect(ref.current).toHaveClass('field');
    expect(inputRef.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLInputElement);
    expect(inputRef.current).toBe(screen.getByRole('textbox'));
  });

  it('merges a string className after its own', () => {
    const { container } = render(<TextField label="Name" className="extra" />);
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field', 'extra');
  });

  it('merges a function className, which receives the field state', () => {
    const className = vi.fn(
      ({
        isInvalid,
        isDisabled,
      }: {
        isInvalid: boolean;
        isDisabled: boolean;
        defaultClassName: string | undefined;
      }) => (isInvalid ? 'is-invalid' : isDisabled ? 'is-disabled' : 'is-fine'),
    );
    const { container, rerender } = render(<TextField label="Name" className={className} />);
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field', 'is-fine');
    rerender(<TextField label="Name" className={className} isInvalid />);
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field', 'is-invalid');
    rerender(<TextField label="Name" className={className} isDisabled />);
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field', 'is-disabled');
    expect(className.mock.calls[0]?.[0].defaultClassName).toBe('react-aria-TextField');
  });

  it.each([
    ['plain', {}],
    ['with a hint', { description: 'Shown in the header.' }],
    ['with a placeholder', { placeholder: 'Northwind Studio' }],
    ['changed', { isChanged: true }],
    ['invalid', { isInvalid: true, errorMessage: 'Enter a name.' }],
    ['invalid and changed', { isInvalid: true, isChanged: true, errorMessage: 'Enter a name.' }],
    ['counted', { budget: 10, defaultValue: 'abcdefgh' }],
    ['over its budget', { budget: 5, defaultValue: 'abcdefgh' }],
    ['disabled', { isDisabled: true }],
```

`packages/core/src/components/input.css`:

```css
/*
 * The text input, derived in docs/design-system.md ("TextField"): a 48px pill
 * on the raised fill. Its changed and invalid borders are keyed on the field's
 * root, as the field contract in field.css says, and invalid is declared last
 * so it outranks changed.
 */
@layer components {
  .input {
    box-sizing: border-box;
    width: 100%;
    height: 48px;
    margin: 0;
    padding-block: 0.75rem;
    padding-inline: 1.5rem;
    border: 1px solid var(--color-boundary);
    border-radius: var(--radius-pill);
    background-color: var(--color-raised);
    color: var(--color-ink);
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: var(--text-body);
    line-height: var(--text-body--line-height);
    font-weight: var(--text-body--font-weight);
  }

  /* Taupe is the whisper color. Firefox dims a placeholder by itself, so the
     opacity is set and taupe is the only color. */
  .input::placeholder {
    color: var(--color-taupe);
    opacity: 1;
  }

  @media (hover: hover) {
    .input:is(:hover, [data-hovered]) {
      border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 65%, transparent);
    }
  }

  /* The document firms the edge on focus. The ring stays as well, because the
     changed and invalid edges below are 1.5px already and outrank this one:
     without it a focused changed field would look unfocused. */
  .input:is(:focus-visible, [data-focus-visible]) {
    border: 1.5px solid var(--color-ink);
    outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color);
    outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);
  }

  /* After hover and focus, so a disabled field that is hovered stays disabled.
     Only the edge color is set, so the changed and invalid edges still win. */
  .input:is(:disabled, [data-disabled]) {
    border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 15%, transparent);
    background-color: var(--color-disabled);
    color: var(--color-taupe);
    cursor: not-allowed;
  }

  /* The field's root carries data-changed and data-invalid. These rules are
     more specific than the states above, so a changed or invalid edge holds
     through hover, focus and disabled. Invalid comes second and wins. */
  .field[data-changed] .input {
    border: 1.5px solid var(--color-signal-light);
  }

  .field[data-invalid] .input {
    border: 1.5px solid var(--color-error);
  }
}
```

Source order carries the states, so keep it: hover, focus, then disabled (a disabled field that is hovered stays disabled), then the changed and invalid borders, which are more specific (`.field[data-changed] .input` is three classes' worth against two) and so hold through hover, focus and disabled. Invalid comes second and wins. Disabled sets only `border-color`, so the changed and invalid shorthand borders still win over it.

The helper first, since TextField uses it. `packages/react/src/field/useChangedDescription.ts` (no `'use client'`: it imports nothing from React Aria):

```ts
import { useId } from 'react';

export interface ChangedDescriptionOptions {
  /** Whether the field has unsaved changes and so shows its Changed chip. */
  isChanged?: boolean;
  /** Whether the field was told it is invalid. An invalid field hides its chip. */
  isInvalid?: boolean;
  /** The `aria-describedby` the caller passed to the field, if any. */
  describedBy?: string;
}

export interface ChangedDescription {
  /** The id to give the Changed chip: pass it to `FieldHead` as `chipId`. */
  chipId: string;
  /** The `aria-describedby` to give the field: the caller's, then the chip's while the chip shows. */
  describedBy: string | undefined;
}

/**
 * Makes a field read its Changed chip aloud. The chip is a visual cue, so a
 * screen reader hears it only if the field names it in `aria-describedby`. That
 * must happen only while the chip shows (changed and not invalid), because an
 * element named there is read even when `display: none` hides it.
 *
 * Internal: every field with a label row calls it, so they all behave alike.
 * Not exported from the package.
 */
export function useChangedDescription({
  isChanged,
  isInvalid,
  describedBy,
}: ChangedDescriptionOptions): ChangedDescription {
  const chipId = useId();
  const announced = isChanged === true && isInvalid !== true;
  return {
    chipId,
    describedBy: announced ? [describedBy, chipId].filter(Boolean).join(' ') : describedBy,
  };
}
```

`packages/react/src/field/FieldHead.tsx`:

```tsx
'use client';

import { useContext, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { FieldErrorContext } from 'react-aria-components';
import { FieldChanged } from './FieldChanged';
import { Label } from './Label';

export interface FieldHeadProps {
  /** The field's label. */
  label: ReactNode;
  /**
   * The text of the Changed chip.
   * @default 'Changed'
   */
  changedLabel?: string;
  /** The id of the chip, from `useChangedDescription`. */
  chipId: string;
}

/**
 * The label row of a field: the Label and the Changed chip, in the `field-head`
 * row. It must sit inside a React Aria field, which is what ties the label to
 * the control. The stylesheet shows the chip while the field's root has
 * `data-changed`. The chip also leaves the page while the field is invalid, by
 * any cause: a chip that is only hidden is still read when `aria-describedby`
 * names it, and validation that React Aria runs (a required field, a `validate`
 * function) is not something the field's own props can see.
 *
 * Internal: every field with a label row renders it. Not exported from the package.
 */
export function FieldHead({ label, changedLabel, chipId }: FieldHeadProps): ReactElement {
  const isInvalid = useContext(FieldErrorContext)?.isInvalid === true;
  return (
    <div className="field-head">
      <Label>{label}</Label>
      {isInvalid ? null : <FieldChanged id={chipId}>{changedLabel}</FieldChanged>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
} from 'react-aria-components';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export interface InputProps extends RACInputProps {

}

/**
 * The text control: a 48px pill on the raised fill. Inside a React Aria field
 * it takes the field's label, hint and error. On its own, give it an
 * `aria-label`. `TextField` renders one; use this directly for a custom layout.
 */
export function Input({ className, ...props }: InputProps): ReactElement {

      className={composeRenderProps(className, (userClassName) => cx('input', userClassName))}
```

`packages/react/src/text-field/TextField.tsx`. The count follows the value in both modes: `typed` is a mirror that `onChange` keeps, started from `defaultValue`, and a controlled `value` wins when there is one. The caller's `onChange` is called after the mirror is set. A form reset goes through the same `onChange` (React Aria sets the field back to its default value), so the mirror follows it.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useState, type ReactElement, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react';
import {
  TextField as RACTextField,
  type TextFieldProps as RACTextFieldProps,
  type TextFieldRenderProps,
  type ValidationResult,
  composeRenderProps,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import { Description } from '../field/Description';
import { FieldCounter } from '../field/FieldCounter';
import { FieldError } from '../field/FieldError';
import { FieldHead } from '../field/FieldHead';
import { useChangedDescription } from '../field/useChangedDescription';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';
import { Input } from './Input';

export interface TextFieldProps extends Omit<RACTextFieldProps, 'children' | 'className'> {
  /** The field's name, shown above the control. Without one, give the field an `aria-label`. */
  label?: ReactNode;
  /** A hint under the control. It becomes the control's accessible description. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * The error line, shown only while the field is invalid. A function receives
   * the validation result. Without it the field shows its own validation messages.
   */
  errorMessage?: ReactNode | ((validation: ValidationResult) => ReactNode);
  /** Example text shown while the control is empty. It never replaces the label. */
  placeholder?: string;
  /**
   * Whether the value differs from the saved one. Shows the clay Changed chip
   * in the label row and the light signal orange border, and has a screen
   * reader read the chip with the field. An invalid field shows its error
   * instead.
   */
  isChanged?: boolean;
  /**
   * The text of the Changed chip.
   * @default 'Changed'
   */
  changedLabel?: string;
  /**
   * About how long the value should be. Shows a count of the value's length
   * from 70% of the budget on. It advises and never blocks typing.
   */
  budget?: number;
  /** A class name, or a function of the field's state, merged after the library's own class. */
  className?: string | ((values: TextFieldRenderProps & { defaultClassName: string | undefined }) => string);
  /** A ref to the field's root element. */
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>;
  /** A ref to the input element. */
  inputRef?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>;
}

/**
 * A single-line text field: label, control, hint, error and an optional length
 * count in one element. Built on React Aria's TextField.
 */
export function TextField({
  label,
  description,
  errorMessage,
  placeholder,
  isChanged = false,
  changedLabel,
  budget,
  className,
  inputRef,
  defaultValue,
  onChange,
  ...props
}: TextFieldProps): ReactElement {
  // The count follows the value whether the caller controls it or not.
  const [typed, setTyped] = useState(defaultValue ?? '');
  const { chipId, describedBy } = useChangedDescription({
    // Only a label row has a chip, so only a labelled field has one to read.
    isChanged: isChanged && label != null,
    isInvalid: props.isInvalid,
    describedBy: props['aria-describedby'],
  });
  return (
    <RACTextField
      {...props}
      defaultValue={defaultValue}
      aria-describedby={describedBy}
      data-changed={isChanged ? '' : undefined}
      className={composeRenderProps(className, (userClassName) => cx('field', userClassName))}
      onChange={(value) => {
        setTyped(value);
        onChange?.(value);
      }}
    >
      {label != null ? <FieldHead label={label} changedLabel={changedLabel} chipId={chipId} /> : null}
      <Input ref={inputRef} placeholder={placeholder} />
      {description != null ? <Description>{description}</Description> : null}
      <FieldError>{errorMessage}</FieldError>
      {budget === undefined ? null : <FieldCounter count={(props.value ?? typed).length} budget={budget} />}
    </RACTextField>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { expect } from 'storybook/test';
import { TextField } from './TextField';

/** The color a token paints in the current theme, read by painting it. */
function tokenColor(name: string): string {
  const probe = document.createElement('span');
  probe.style.color = `var(${name})`;
  document.body.append(probe);
  const { color } = getComputedStyle(probe);
  probe.remove();
  return color;
}

const NEAR_BUDGET = 'A shared space for the whole Northwind design team';
const OVER_BUDGET = 'A shared space for the whole Northwind design team and its guests';

const meta = {
  title: 'Components/TextField',
  component: TextField,
  args: { label: 'Workspace name', placeholder: 'Northwind Studio' },
  decorators: [
    (Story) => (
      <div style={{ width: 'min(28rem, calc(100vw - 2rem))' }}>
        <Story />
      </div>
    ),
  ],
} satisfies Meta<typeof TextField>;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

/** A label and a control. The placeholder is taupe and never replaces the label. */
export const Default: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    await expect(input).toHaveAttribute('placeholder', 'Northwind Studio');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-boundary'));
  },
};

/** The hint is the control's accessible description. */
export const WithDescription: Story = {
  args: { description: 'Shown in the header and in every invite.' },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' })).toHaveAccessibleDescription(
      'Shown in the header and in every invite.',
    );
  },
};

/** `isChanged` shows the clay chip and the light signal orange edge, and the chip is read with the field. */
export const Changed: Story = {
  args: {
    isChanged: true,
    defaultValue: 'Northwind Studio',
    description: 'Shown in the header and in every invite.',
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Changed')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-signal-light'));
    await expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Shown in the header and in every invite. Changed');
  },
};

/** The error line appears with the invalid state, and the edge turns to the error color. */
export const Invalid: Story = {
  args: { isInvalid: true, defaultValue: '!', errorMessage: 'Enter a name for the workspace.' },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Enter a name for the workspace.')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(input).toBeInvalid();
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-error'));
  },
};

/** Invalid outranks changed: the error edge and the error line show, and the chip leaves. */
export const InvalidAndChanged: Story = {
  args: {
    isChanged: true,
    isInvalid: true,
    defaultValue: '!',
    errorMessage: 'Enter a name for the workspace.',
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    await expect(canvas.queryByText('Changed')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Enter a name for the workspace.')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-error'));
    await expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Enter a name for the workspace.');
  },
};

/** From 70% of the budget the count appears, quiet and slate. */
export const WithCounter: Story = {
  args: {
    label: 'Short description',
    description: 'One sentence, for search results.',
    budget: 60,
    defaultValue: NEAR_BUDGET,
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('50 of about 60');
  },
};

/** Past the budget the count turns to ink at 700. Typing was never blocked, and the value still saves. */
export const OverBudget: Story = {
  args: {
    label: 'Short description',
    description: 'One sentence, for search results.',
    budget: 60,
    defaultValue: OVER_BUDGET,
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const counter = canvas.getByRole('status');
    await expect(counter).toHaveTextContent('65 of about 60');
    await expect(counter).toHaveAttribute('data-over');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(counter).fontWeight).toBe('700');
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('textbox')).toBeValid();
  },
};

/** The disabled fill, taupe text and a faint edge. */
export const Disabled: Story = {
  args: { isDisabled: true, defaultValue: 'Northwind Studio' },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    await expect(input).toBeDisabled();
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).cursor).toBe('not-allowed');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).backgroundColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-disabled'));
  },

/** A long label wraps and the chip drops under it, with no sideways scroll at 375px. */
export const LongLabel: Story = {
  args: {
    label: 'The name your team sees in the header, in every invite and in the billing emails',
    isChanged: true,
    defaultValue: 'Northwind Studio',
  },
};

/** Keyboard focus firms the edge to ink and draws the ring outside it. */
export const Focused: Story = {
  args: { defaultValue: 'Northwind Studio' },
  play: async ({ canvas, userEvent }) => {
    await userEvent.tab();
    // Tabbing into a field selects its text. Collapse it, so the baseline shows the ring and not a highlight.
    await userEvent.keyboard('{End}');
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    await expect(input).toHaveFocus();
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-ink'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).outlineStyle).toBe('solid');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).outlineWidth).toBe('2px');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).outlineColor).toBe(tokenColor('--focus-ring-color'));
  },
};

/** The changed edge outranks the firmer one, so the ring alone shows that a changed field has focus. */
export const ChangedAndFocused: Story = {
  args: { isChanged: true, defaultValue: 'Northwind Studio' },
  play: async ({ canvas, userEvent }) => {
    await userEvent.tab();
    await userEvent.keyboard('{End}');
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    await expect(input).toHaveFocus();
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-signal-light'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).outlineStyle).toBe('solid');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(input).outlineWidth).toBe('2px');
  },
};

/** Typing is never blocked at the budget, and the count follows. */
export const Typing: Story = {
  tags: ['no-visual'],
  args: { label: 'Short description', description: 'One sentence, for search results.', budget: 10 },
  play: async ({ canvas, userEvent }) => {
    const input = canvas.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Short description' });
    await userEvent.type(input, 'fourteen chars');
    await expect(input).toHaveValue('fourteen chars');
    await expect(input).toBeValid();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('14 of about 10');
  },
};
```

The `play` functions run in Chromium, in light and dark, so they check what jsdom cannot: each state's computed edge color against the token it should be (`tokenColor` paints the token and reads it back, so the check holds in both themes), the disabled cursor and fill, the over-budget weight, and for `Focused` and `ChangedAndFocused` the computed outline and edge. The two focus stories press End after Tab, because tabbing into a field selects its text and the baseline would otherwise show a highlight.

```tsx
        value={email}
        onChange={setEmail}
        validate={(value) =>
          value === '' || value.endsWith('@northwind.studio') ? null : 'Use an address at northwind.studio.'
        }
        errorMessage={({ validationDetails, validationErrors }) =>
          validationDetails.valueMissing ? 'Enter your work email.' : validationErrors.join(' ')
        }
      />
      <div className="row">
        <Button type="submit">Send invite</Button>
      </div>
      <p className="muted" role="status">
        {sentTo ? `Invite sent to ${sentTo}.` : ''}
      </p>
    </form>
  );
}
```

The page, `apps/docs/content/docs/components/text-field.mdx`. The first paragraph after each `##` is the section's note. The prose never uses the word "button" and never names the Spinner, so the search tests that rank those pages first are unaffected. It has a Keys table because the field is interactive.

```mdx
---
title: Text field
description: A single-line text field. One element draws the label, the control, the hint, the error line and an optional length count, and shows when a value is unsaved or invalid.
icon: TextCursor
---

<Section>

## Basic

Pass a label, and a hint if the label cannot say it all. The placeholder shows an example and never replaces the label.

<Preview name="text-field-basic" />

</Section>

<Section>

## States

The edge carries the state. A changed field gets a light signal orange edge and a clay chip beside its label. An invalid field gets the error edge and an error line, and invalid outranks changed, so the chip steps aside. A disabled field is recessed. A read-only field looks like an enabled one and still submits.

<Preview name="text-field-states" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Validation

Set `isRequired`, a `type`, or a `validate` function, and the browser's own checks run when the form is submitted. The error line then shows the message, or the one you build from the validation result. The first failed submit shows the error and moves focus to the field.

<Preview name="text-field-validation" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Length count

Pass `budget` to count the value's length against about how long it should be. The count appears from 70% of the budget and never blocks typing. [Field parts](/docs/components/field) shows it in use.

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

Every value works controlled and uncontrolled, and a field with a `name` submits in a plain form. `onChange` receives the string.

<Code code={`import { useState } from 'react';
import { TextField } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function ShortDescription({ saved }: { saved: string }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(saved);
  return (
    <TextField
      label="Short description"
      description="One sentence, for search results."
      name="description"
      value={value}
      onChange={setValue}
      isChanged={value !== saved}
      budget={60}
    />
  );
}`} />

For a custom layout, use the parts inside React Aria's own field: Label, Input, Description and FieldError. Field parts has the example.

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

Every React Aria TextField prop is accepted. These are the ones Snapshot UI adds or shapes.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/text-field/TextField.tsx" type="Pick<TextFieldProps, 'label' | 'description' | 'errorMessage' | 'placeholder' | 'isChanged' | 'changedLabel' | 'budget' | 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onChange' | 'name' | 'type' | 'isRequired' | 'isDisabled' | 'isReadOnly' | 'isInvalid' | 'validate'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A native input, labelled by the label and described by the hint and the error line, with React Aria handling the wiring. A screen reader reads the Changed chip with the field, after the hint, while the field is changed and valid. An invalid field reads its error line alone.

<Keys rows={[['Tab', 'Moves focus into the field. The edge firms to 1.5px ink and the 2px ring sits outside it.'], ['Enter', 'Submits the form the field is in.']]} />

The placeholder is taupe, which is quiet by design, so it never carries anything the label does not. The count is a polite status region.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps fields in the system.

<Rules dos={['Name the field in the label, in sentence case. Use the hint for what the label cannot say.', 'Show the chip and the changed edge together, and only while the value is unsaved.', 'Say what is wrong and how to fix it in the error line.']} donts={['Never use the placeholder as the label.', 'Never block typing at the budget. The count advises.', 'Never leave the chip beside an error. Invalid outranks changed.']} />

</Section>
```

```ts
  await send.click();
  await expect(field.locator('.field-error')).toHaveText('Enter your work email.');
  await expect(field).toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
  await expect(input).toBeFocused();
  await expect(input).toHaveCSS('border-top-color', 'rgb(163, 35, 27)');

  await expect(field.locator('.field-error')).toHaveText('Use an address at northwind.studio.');

  // Enter submits. A click would miss: the error line collapses when the field loses focus, and the button moves.
  await input.fill('ada@northwind.studio');
  await input.press('Enter');
  await expect(page.getByText('Invite sent to ada@northwind.studio.')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(field.locator('.field-error')).toHaveCount(0);
});
```

- Produces from `@snapshot-ui/react`, `'use client'`:

```ts
export function TextArea(props: TextAreaProps): ReactElement;
export interface TextAreaProps extends Omit<RACTextFieldProps, 'children' | 'className' | 'type' | 'pattern'> {
  label?: ReactNode;                 // the label row; without it there is no chip
  description?: ReactNode;           // Description under the control
  errorMessage?: ReactNode | ((validation: ValidationResult) => ReactNode); // FieldError children
  placeholder?: string;
  rows?: number;                     // lines tall; default 3; never shorter than 6rem
  isChanged?: boolean;               // data-changed on the root, the chip, the changed edge, the chip announced
  changedLabel?: string;             // default 'Changed'
  budget?: number;                   // shows FieldCounter counting the value's length; never blocks typing
  className?: string | ((values: TextFieldRenderProps & { defaultClassName: string | undefined }) => string);
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>;         // the root
  textAreaRef?: Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>; // the textarea
}
```

  `TextArea` is the same field as `TextField`, so its API is TextField's, with `rows` added, `textAreaRef` where TextField has `inputRef`, and `type` and `pattern`, which belong to a single line, left out of the props. React Aria applies `type` and `pattern` to an `<input>` only.
- **No bare textarea part is exported.** Spec 6.2 lists the parts as `Label`, `Description`, `FieldError` and `Input`, and a textarea control adds nothing a part would need: the textarea is rendered inside `TextArea` with the class pair `input textarea`. A custom layout uses React Aria's own `TextArea` with those two classes, inside React Aria's `TextField`, next to the library's `Label`, `Description` and `FieldError`.
- Produces the **internal length hook** that Task 6's TextField also uses. It is not exported from `src/index.ts` or from `field/index.ts`; a field imports it by path (`../field/useValueLength`):

```ts
// packages/react/src/field/useValueLength.ts (no directive, no React Aria import)
export interface ValueLengthOptions {
  value?: string;                      // the controlled value, if the caller controls the field
  defaultValue?: string;               // the value an uncontrolled field starts with
  onChange?: (value: string) => void;  // the caller's handler
}
export interface ValueLength {
  length: number;                      // the controlled value's length, else the length of what was typed
  onChange: (value: string) => void;   // give it to the field: it keeps the count, then calls the caller's handler
}
export function useValueLength(options: ValueLengthOptions): ValueLength;
```

  It is Task 6's counter tracking moved out of `TextField` unchanged: a mirror that `onChange` keeps, started from `defaultValue`, with a controlled `value` winning. A form reset reports the default value through the same `onChange`, so the count follows it.
- Produces the class `textarea` and, in `textarea.css`, one rule, `.input.textarea`, that sets only `height`, `min-height`, `border-radius`, `padding-block`, `padding-inline`, `line-height` and `resize`. It inherits every other rule from `input.css`: the fill, the edge, hover, the focus edge and ring, the placeholder, disabled, and the `.field[data-changed] .input` and `.field[data-invalid] .input` borders.
- Produces the docs page `/docs/components/text-area` and the three examples `text-area-basic`, `text-area-states` and `text-area-counter`.
- Removes no docs stand-in: nothing in the docs draws a textarea by hand. A search of `apps/docs` for `textarea` finds only the homepage catalog chip "Text area", a `<span>`, which Task 13 turns into a link with the other phase 1b chips. The docs' one rule on the class `input` (`site.css`: a border-radius transition, so docs inputs recut with the corner shape) also applies to the textarea, which carries that class, and the docs' reduced-motion rule stops it.

**Decisions made here, recorded in Appendix B (Step 1) where they are design decisions, and repeated so no later task reopens them:**

- **One control, two classes, one override rule.** `.input.textarea` names both classes, so it outranks the input's single-class rule in any import order, and it sets none of what the input's states set, so no state rule can lose to it or beat it. `css.test.js` holds the two files to separate properties (Step 2), and the stories check the computed edge, ring, fill and corner in Chromium (Step 5).
- **The radius is `--radius-control`**, 20px in Rounded, 10px in Soft and square in Square. The design document's dark-mode note says a textarea "keeps its 20px radius", and the spec's shape table lists "textarea parts" under `--radius-control`. The spec's catalog row for TextArea names `--radius-surface` (24px), a number that came from the source app, and the document and the shape table supersede it. Appendix B says so.
- **`rows` defaults to 3**, the source's, and the floor of 6rem is 96px: three rows are 93.2px (3 x 22.4px of line, 24px of padding, 2px of edge), so rows 1 to 3 look alike and the fourth row grows the box.
- **Vertical resize only, and no autosize.** A box dragged wider would break the field's column. The box scrolls inside rather than growing with its text, as the source's does; `field-sizing: content` is not available across the browser floor.
- **A line break counts as one character** in the budget, the value React Aria reports and `FormData` holds (measured in Chromium). A browser encodes it as two (CR LF) in the request body (measured: `t=x%0D%0Ay`), so a server that measures the request sees one more per line. The docs page and Appendix B say so.
- **A box taller than the floor can move by 1px** while its edge is 1.5px (focus, changed, invalid) on a screen that draws that width. This is reasoned from the box model and not measured: headless Chromium draws every edge at 1px, so the stories assert the edge colors and not the widths, and the default box sits on its floor. Recorded as accepted in Appendix B.
- **The resize handle is the browser's** and sits over the curve of the corner. Dragging it grows the box vertically and stops at 96px going the other way (checked in Chromium). It is not restyled.
- **The long-label story uses a short value,** so the 375px baseline shows the wrapped label and the chip and no clipped text.
- **No contrast pair was added.** The textarea draws no color of its own.

- [ ] **Step 1: Record the derivation**

Append to the end of `docs/design-system.md` (after the TextField section), keeping a blank line before the heading:

```markdown

## TextArea

The document says one thing about a textarea, in its dark-mode notes: it
"keeps its 20px radius". The spec's shape table agrees, listing "textarea
parts" under `--radius-control`, and the spec's catalog row for TextArea adds a
6rem minimum height and vertical resize only. The library draws a textarea as
the TextField control on a taller box and records each difference here.

**One control, two classes.** The textarea carries `input textarea`, so the
fill, the edge, hover, the focus edge and ring, the placeholder, disabled, and
the changed and invalid borders keyed on the field's root all come from the
input and are recorded under TextField. `textarea.css` is one rule,
`.input.textarea`, and it sets seven properties: `height`, `min-height`,
`border-radius`, `padding-block`, `padding-inline`, `line-height` and `resize`.
It sets no edge, color, outline or cursor, so no state rule of the input can
lose to it or beat it, and a test holds the two files to separate properties.
It names both classes so it outranks the input's single class in any import
order.

- **Shape** is `--radius-control`, the document's 20px: 20px in Rounded, 10px in
  Soft, square in Square, the corner a Button has, so a textarea and the
  controls beside it share one. The document's dark-mode note and the spec's
  shape table both give it. The spec's catalog row for TextArea names the surface
  radius (24px), a number that came from the source app, and the document and
  the shape table supersede it. The input's pill does not carry over: a box this
  tall would read as a lozenge.
- **Height** is auto with a floor of 6rem (96px), the source's value, so the box
  is as tall as its rows and never shorter than the floor. Body text is 22.4px a
  line (16px at 1.4), so three rows are 67.2px, plus 24px of padding and 2px of
  edge, which is 93.2px: under the floor, so rows 1 to 3 look alike and `rows`
  defaults to 3, the source's. Four rows are 115.6px and five are 138px. The box
  does not grow with its text: it scrolls inside, as the source's does, and
  `field-sizing: content`, which would grow it, is not available across the
  browser floor.
- **Resize is vertical only.** The field is one grid column capped at
  `--container-field`, and a box dragged wider would break it. Shrinking stops
  at the floor (dragged up to 20px from its top edge, a three-row box stays
  96px). The handle is the browser's, drawn in the corner over the curve of the
  radius, and is not restyled. A keyboard cannot resize, so `rows` is the way to
  a taller box and the docs say so.
- **Padding and line height** are the input's: 12px block and 24px inline, and
  the 16px body step at 1.4. The source's override sets only the block padding
  (`py-3`, the same 12px). They are restated in `textarea.css` so the height
  arithmetic above sits in one file. The 24px inline padding is more than the
  20px Rounded radius, so the first line of text clears the curve.
- **A taller box can move by 1px.** The input is a fixed 48px, so its edge
  growing from 1px to the 1.5px of the focus, changed and invalid edges moves
  nothing. A box taller than the floor (four rows or more) is as tall as its
  rows, so on a screen that draws a 1.5px edge it is 1px taller while it has
  one. The default box sits on its floor and does not move. This is reasoned
  from the box model and not measured: the headless browser the tests use draws
  every edge at 1px. It is accepted: holding the height still would need a fixed
  height, which is what a textarea is not.
- **The count** counts the value's length, a line break as one character: that
  is the value React Aria reports and `FormData` holds. A browser sends each
  line break in a form request as two characters (CR and LF; measured as
  `%0D%0A` in a posted body), so a server that measures the request sees one more
  per line. Everything else about the count is TextField's: it advises, never
  blocks, and appears from 70% of the budget.

No pairing was added to the contrast gate. The fills, edges and text are the
input's, and the textarea draws no color of its own.
```

The measurements in it were taken in Chromium with Playwright: `new FormData(form).get(name)` returns `x\ny` for a textarea holding two lines, and a posted form body is `t=x%0D%0Ay`. The heights are the box model's (22.4px is 16px at the body line height of 1.4) and match the measured boxes: 96px for three rows and 137.95px for five.

`packages/react/src/field/useValueLength.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { act, renderHook } from '@testing-library/react';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { useValueLength } from './useValueLength';

describe('useValueLength', () => {
  it('starts from the default value, and from nothing without one', () => {
    const empty = renderHook(() => useValueLength({}));
    expect(empty.result.current.length).toBe(0);
    const started = renderHook(() => useValueLength({ defaultValue: 'abcdefgh' }));
    expect(started.result.current.length).toBe(8);
  });

  it('follows what is typed', () => {
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useValueLength({ defaultValue: 'abc' }));
    act(() => {
      result.current.onChange('abcdef');
    });
    expect(result.current.length).toBe(6);
    act(() => {
      result.current.onChange('');
    });
    expect(result.current.length).toBe(0);
  });

  it('counts a line break as one character', () => {
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useValueLength({}));
    act(() => {
      result.current.onChange('one\ntwo');
    });
    expect(result.current.length).toBe(7);
  });

  it('tells the caller what was typed, after it has counted it', () => {
    const calls: string[] = [];
    const onChange = vi.fn((value: string) => {
      calls.push(value);
    });
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useValueLength({ onChange }));
    act(() => {
      result.current.onChange('abc');
    });
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(calls).toEqual(['abc']);
  });

  it('works when the caller passes no change handler', () => {
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useValueLength({}));
    expect(() => {
      act(() => {
        result.current.onChange('abc');
      });
    }).not.toThrow();
    expect(result.current.length).toBe(3);
  });

  it('counts the controlled value and not what was typed', () => {
    const { result, rerender } = renderHook((props) => useValueLength(props), {
      initialProps: { value: 'abcdefgh' },
    });
    expect(result.current.length).toBe(8);
    act(() => {
      result.current.onChange('abcdefghxyz');
    });
    expect(result.current.length).toBe(8);
    rerender({ value: 'abcdefghij' });
    expect(result.current.length).toBe(10);
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { act, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef, useState, type ReactElement } from 'react';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { TextArea, type TextAreaProps } from './TextArea';

/** A field the caller controls, the way a form library would. */
function Controlled(props: TextAreaProps): ReactElement {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('Northwind\nStudio');
  return <TextArea {...props} value={value} onChange={setValue} />;
}

const root = (container: HTMLElement): Element => {
  const element = container.firstElementChild;
  if (!element) throw new Error('Nothing rendered');
  return element;
};

describe('TextArea', () => {
  it('renders a labelled textarea with a hint, inside a field', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextArea
        label="Short description"
        description="Shown in search results."
        placeholder="A shared space"
      />,
    );
    const textarea = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Short description' });
    expect(textarea.tagName).toBe('TEXTAREA');
    expect(textarea).toHaveClass('input', 'textarea');
    expect(textarea).toHaveAttribute('placeholder', 'A shared space');
    expect(textarea).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Shown in search results.');
    expect(screen.getByText('Short description')).toHaveClass('field-label');
    expect(screen.getByText('Shown in search results.')).toHaveClass('field-description');
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field');
    expect(root(container)).not.toHaveAttribute('data-changed');
    expect(root(container)).not.toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('is a textarea and not an input: it carries no type once it has mounted', () => {
    render(<TextArea label="Notes" />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox')).not.toHaveAttribute('type');
  });

  it('puts its parts in the order the field contract asks for', () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <TextArea
        label="Short description"
        description="One sentence."
        isInvalid
        errorMessage="Too vague."
        budget={10}
        defaultValue="abcdefgh"
      />,
    );
    expect([...root(container).children].map((child) => child.classList[0])).toEqual([
      'field-head',
      'input',
      'field-description',
      'field-error',
      'field-counter',
    ]);
  });

  it('takes several lines: Enter adds a new line and does not submit the form', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onSubmit = vi.fn((event: { preventDefault: () => void }) => {
      event.preventDefault();
    });
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    render(
      <form onSubmit={onSubmit}>
        <TextArea label="Notes" onChange={onChange} />
        <button type="submit">Save</button>
      </form>,
    );
    const textarea = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Notes' });
    await user.type(textarea, 'one{Enter}two{Enter}{Enter}three');
    expect(textarea).toHaveValue('one\ntwo\n\nthree');
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('one\ntwo\n\nthree');
    expect(onSubmit).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }));
    expect(onSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('types into an uncontrolled field', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    render(<TextArea label="Notes" defaultValue="Northwind" onChange={onChange} />);
    const textarea = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    expect(textarea).toHaveValue('Northwind');
    await user.type(textarea, ' East');
    expect(textarea).toHaveValue('Northwind East');
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5);
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('Northwind East');
  });

  it('follows the value of a controlled field, and tells the caller what was typed', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    const { rerender } = render(<TextArea label="Notes" value="one" onChange={onChange} />);
    const textarea = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    await user.type(textarea, 'x');
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith('onex');
    expect(textarea).toHaveValue('one');
    rerender(<TextArea label="Notes" value={'two\nlines'} onChange={onChange} />);
    expect(textarea).toHaveValue('two\nlines');
  });

  it('works with a state the caller keeps', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Controlled label="Notes" />);
    const textarea = screen.getByRole('textbox');
    expect(textarea).toHaveValue('Northwind\nStudio');
    await user.type(textarea, '{Enter}East');
    expect(textarea).toHaveValue('Northwind\nStudio\nEast');
  });

  it('submits its lines in a plain form under its name', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <TextArea label="Notes" name="notes" defaultValue="First line" />
      </form>,
    );
    const form = container.querySelector('form');
    if (!form) throw new Error('No form');
    expect(new FormData(form).get('notes')).toBe('First line');
    await user.type(screen.getByRole('textbox'), '{Enter}Second line');
    expect(new FormData(form).get('notes')).toBe('First line\nSecond line');
  });

  it('shows the error and sets data-invalid after a required field is submitted empty', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <TextArea label="Notes" name="notes" isRequired errorMessage="Write a note." />
        <button type="submit">Save</button>
      </form>,
    );
    const textarea = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: /Notes/ });
    expect(textarea).toBeRequired();
    expect(screen.queryByText('Write a note.')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(container.querySelector('.field')).not.toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }));
    const error = screen.getByText('Write a note.');
    expect(error).toHaveClass('field-error');
    expect(textarea).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Write a note.');
    expect(container.querySelector('.field')).toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
    expect(textarea).toBeInvalid();
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
    // The native error stays while the field is being edited and clears when the edit is committed.
    await user.type(textarea, 'Northwind');
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.queryByText('Write a note.')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(container.querySelector('.field')).not.toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
  });

  it('shows the message of a custom validate function', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(
      <TextArea
        label="Notes"
        defaultValue="one line"
        validationBehavior="aria"
        validate={(value) => (value.includes('\n') ? null : 'Write at least two lines.')}
      />,
    );
    const textarea = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Notes' });
    expect(screen.getByText('Write at least two lines.')).toHaveClass('field-error');
```

`packages/core/src/components/textarea.css`:

```css
/*
 * The multi-line box, derived in docs/design-system.md ("TextArea"). The control
 * carries both classes, `input textarea`, so it takes everything from input.css:
 * the fill, the edge, hover, the focus edge and ring, disabled, and the changed
 * and invalid borders keyed on the field's root. This rule only undoes the single
 * line. It sets none of what those states set, so none of them can lose to it, and
 * it names both classes, so it outranks the input's own rule in any import order.
 */
@layer components {
  .input.textarea {
    /* The input is a 48px pill. A textarea is as tall as its rows, never under 6rem. */
    height: auto;
    min-height: 6rem;
    /* The document's 20px control radius (10px in Soft, square in Square), not the input's pill. */
    border-radius: var(--radius-control);
    /* The input's own padding and line height, restated: three rows of 1.4 at 16px
       are 67px, plus 24px of padding and 2px of edge, 93px, so the floor sets the
       height until a fourth row. */
    padding-block: 0.75rem;
    padding-inline: 1.5rem;
    line-height: var(--text-body--line-height);
    /* Up and down only. Sideways would break the field's column. */
    resize: vertical;
  }
}
```

The hook first, since both fields use it. `packages/react/src/field/useValueLength.ts` (no `'use client'`: it imports nothing from React Aria):

```ts
import { useState } from 'react';

export interface ValueLengthOptions {
  /** The value, when the caller controls the field. */
  value?: string;
  /** The value an uncontrolled field starts with. */
  defaultValue?: string;
  /** The caller's change handler. */
  onChange?: (value: string) => void;
}

export interface ValueLength {
  /** How long the field's value is: the controlled value when there is one, else what was typed. */
  length: number;
  /** Give this to the field as its `onChange`. It keeps the count, then calls the caller's handler. */
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
}

/**
 * Counts the length of a text field's value whether or not the caller controls
 * it, for `FieldCounter`. An uncontrolled field keeps its value inside React
 * Aria, so the count is kept from the changes it reports, starting from the
 * default value. A form reset reports the default value through the same
 * change, so the count follows it. A line break counts as one character, as it
 * does in the value React Aria reports.
 *
 * Internal: every text field with a `budget` calls it, so they all count alike.
 * Not exported from the package.
 */
export function useValueLength({ value, defaultValue, onChange }: ValueLengthOptions): ValueLength {
  const [typed, setTyped] = useState(defaultValue ?? '');
  return {
    length: (value ?? typed).length,
    onChange: (next) => {
      setTyped(next);
      onChange?.(next);
    },
  };
}
```

TextField now uses it. This is Task 6's tracking moved out of the component, with no change in behavior: the import of `useState` goes, the hook is imported, the mirror and its `onChange` wrapper become the hook's two return values, and the counter reads `length`.
