The page, `apps/docs/content/docs/components/radio-group.mdx`. The first paragraph after each `##` is the section's note. The prose never uses the word "button" and never names the Spinner, so the search tests that rank those pages first are unaffected. It has a Keys table because the group is interactive; the keys are written `Down Right` and `Up Left`, each word its own key cap, since the table splits on spaces and each cap is an alternative.

```mdx
---
title: Radio group
description: A choice of one from a short list. Each option is a full-pill row, and the chosen row is the ink pill with a check in its ring.
icon: CircleDot
---

<Section>

## Basic

Pass a label, and a hint if the label cannot say it all. Each `Radio` can carry a hint of its own, which sits under its row. Choose another option to see the Changed chip.

<Preview name="radio-group-basic" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Horizontal

Set `orientation="horizontal"` for a short row of options. The rows keep their width and wrap onto the next line when the row runs out of room.

<Preview name="radio-group-horizontal" />

</Section>

<Section>

## States

A changed group shows a clay chip beside its label and nothing else: unlike a text field, a choice has no control edge to recolor, so the chip is the whole cue. An invalid group draws the error edge on every row and an error line, and invalid outranks changed, so the chip steps aside. A disabled group is recessed and keeps the check of its choice, and one option can be disabled on its own.

<Preview name="radio-group-states" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Validation

Set `isRequired` or a `validate` function, and the browser's own checks run when the form is submitted. The error line shows the message, and choosing an option clears it. The first failed submit moves focus to the group.

<Preview name="radio-group-validation" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

Every value works controlled and uncontrolled, and a group with a `name` submits the chosen option's `value` in a plain form. `onChange` receives the value as a string.

<Code code={`import { useState } from 'react';
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function Frequency({ saved }: { saved: string }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(saved);
  return (
    <RadioGroup
      label="Newsletter frequency"
      name="frequency"
      value={value}
      onChange={setValue}
      isChanged={value !== saved}
    >
      <Radio value="weekly" description="Every Tuesday morning.">
        Weekly
      </Radio>
      <Radio value="monthly">Monthly</Radio>
      <Radio value="never">Never</Radio>
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}`} />

For a choice of two with the same weight, such as a setting that is simply on or off, use a switch instead. For a choice that changes the view in place, such as a mode, use a segmented control.

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

Every React Aria RadioGroup prop is accepted. These are the ones Snapshot UI adds or shapes.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/radio-group/RadioGroup.tsx" type="Pick<RadioGroupProps, 'label' | 'description' | 'errorMessage' | 'isChanged' | 'changedLabel' | 'orientation' | 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onChange' | 'name' | 'isRequired' | 'isDisabled' | 'isReadOnly' | 'isInvalid' | 'validate'>" />

Each option is a `Radio`.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/radio-group/Radio.tsx" type="Pick<RadioProps, 'value' | 'children' | 'description' | 'isDisabled' | 'inputRef'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A group of native radio inputs, named by the label and described by the hint, the error line and, while it shows, the Changed chip. React Aria keeps the group to one tab stop and moves the choice with the arrow keys. The dot and the check are decoration, so an option's name is its label text alone.

<Keys rows={[['Tab', 'Moves focus into the group, to the chosen option or the first one. The 2px ring sits outside an unchosen row and inside the ink of the chosen one.'], ['Down Right', 'Moves to the next option and chooses it.'], ['Up Left', 'Moves to the previous option and chooses it.'], ['Space', 'Chooses the focused option.']]} />

Disabled options are skipped by the arrow keys. A read-only group keeps its choice and takes no hover wash.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps radio groups in the system.

<Rules dos={['Name the group in the label, in sentence case, and keep options short enough to scan.', 'Choose a default when one is safe. A required group with nothing chosen shows the error only after a failed submit.', 'Show the chip while the choice is unsaved, and only then.']} donts={['Never use a radio group for more than about six options. Use a select.', 'Never leave the chip beside an error. Invalid outranks changed.', 'Never hide the check. Color is not the only sign of the chosen option.']} />

</Section>
```

```ts
test('the radio group page shows a failed submit as an error line on every row, and sends once a plan is chosen', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });
  await visit(page, '/docs/components/radio-group');
  const group = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Plan', exact: true });
  const rows = group.locator('label.radio');
  const submit = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue' });

  await submit.click();
  await expect(group.locator('.field-error')).toHaveText('Choose a plan to continue.');
  await expect(group).toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
  await expect(group.getByRole('radio').first()).toBeFocused();
  for (const row of await rows.all()) await expect(row).toHaveCSS('border-top-color', 'rgb(163, 35, 27)');

  // Choosing an option clears the error, and the form then sends the value.
  await group.getByText('Team').click();
  await expect(group.locator('.field-error')).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(rows.first()).toHaveCSS('border-top-color', 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
  await submit.click();
  await expect(page.getByText('You chose the team plan.')).toBeVisible();
});

test('the arrow keys move the choice of a radio group, and the chosen row draws its focus ring in canvas inside the ink', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });
  await visit(page, '/docs/components/radio-group');
  const group = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Newsletter frequency' });
  const weekly = group.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Weekly' });
  const monthly = group.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Monthly' });
  // `has` is resolved inside each row, so the radio is looked up from the page and not from the group.
  const rowOf = (name: string): Locator =>
    group.locator('label.radio', { has: page.getByRole('radio', { name }) });

  // A change from the saved choice shows the chip, and going back hides it.
  await expect(group.locator('.field-changed')).toBeHidden();
  await weekly.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  await expect(monthly).toBeFocused();
  await expect(monthly).toBeChecked();
  await expect(group.locator('.field-changed')).toBeVisible();
  const chosen = rowOf('Monthly');
  await expect(chosen).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(20, 20, 19)');
  await expect(chosen).toHaveCSS('color', 'rgb(243, 240, 238)');
  await expect(chosen).toHaveCSS('outline-style', 'solid');
  await expect(chosen).toHaveCSS('outline-color', 'rgb(243, 240, 238)');
  await expect(chosen).toHaveCSS('outline-offset', '-4px');
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowUp');
  await expect(weekly).toBeChecked();
  await expect(group.locator('.field-changed')).toBeHidden();
  // The row that lost the choice is plain again.
  await expect(rowOf('Monthly')).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
});

test('every option of a radio group is a target of 40px or more, across the whole row', async ({ page }) => {
  await visit(page, '/docs/components/radio-group');
  const group = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Newsletter frequency' });
  const { height } = await hitSize(group.locator('label.radio').first());
  expect(height).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(40);
  // A stacked row fills the group, so the empty end of the row is part of the target.
  const [row, field] = await Promise.all([
    group.locator('label.radio').first().boundingBox(),
    group.locator('.radio-items').boundingBox(),
  ]);
  expect(row?.width).toBeCloseTo(field?.width ?? 0, 0);
});
```

- Produces from `@snapshot-ui/react`, `'use client'`:

```ts
export function Switch(props: SwitchProps): ReactElement;
export interface SwitchProps
  extends Omit<RACSwitchFieldProps, 'children' | 'className' | 'isRequired' | 'isInvalid' | 'validate' | 'validationBehavior'> {
  children?: ReactNode;            // the label, in the row beside the track; without one, give the switch an aria-label
  description?: ReactNode;         // Description under the label, the switch's accessible description
  isChanged?: boolean;             // data-changed on the root, the ring around the track, the chip beside the label, the chip announced
  changedLabel?: string;           // default 'Changed'
  className?: string | ((values: SwitchFieldRenderProps & { defaultClassName: string | undefined }) => string);
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>;       // the field's root, which className also goes on
  inputRef?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>; // the input
  // from React Aria, unchanged: isSelected, defaultSelected, onChange(isSelected: boolean), name, value, isDisabled, isReadOnly, aria-label, id ...
}
```

- **Where `className` and `ref` go.** A standalone field puts them on the field root: the element with the `field` class, which also holds the hint. A Switch is standalone, so its `className` (a string or a function of `SwitchFieldRenderProps`) and its `ref` go on the `SwitchField` root, and the row keeps its own class, `switch`, for the visuals. The JSDoc in `Switch.tsx` says so, and the test `merges a string className after its own` and `forwards ref to the field and inputRef to the input` pin it.
- Produces the classes `switch` (the row: the `SwitchButton` label that holds the visually hidden input, the track and the label text), `switch-track` and `switch-thumb`. The root carries the field's own classes, `field`, plus the caller's: the field root contract of Task 5 applies, with `field-head` for the label row (here it holds the row and the chip) and `field-description` for the hint. DOM, in order: `div.field[data-changed] > div.field-head > (label.switch > (span hidden > input[role=switch]) + span.switch-track[aria-hidden] > span.switch-thumb + the label text) + span.field-changed`, then `span.field-description`.
- Produces the state hooks in `switch.css`: the row's `data-selected`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-focus-visible` (each also matched through the input it holds, `:has(input:checked)`, `:disabled` and `:focus-visible`, so markup without React Aria works), and the field root's `data-changed`. It does not use `FieldHead`, which renders a `Label`: a switch's label is inside its row.
- Produces the contrast gate: `CONTRAST_PAIRS` now holds the off track against all five surfaces and the raised thumb on it on all five, and a test pins that the on thumb (canvas on ink) is gated at the text minimum.
- Produces the docs page `/docs/components/switch` and the three examples `switch-basic`, `switch-states` and `switch-settings`.
- Removes from the docs the `.switch` stand-in rules in `apps/docs/app/site.css` (the track, its hit area, the thumb and the two `aria-checked` rules) and `DemoSwitch` in the homepage. The three frame switches and the six axis switches are the library's `Switch`, with the same labels, hints and states. `.setting` and `.settings-list` stay as the docs' row layout, with three rules added so a settings row puts its switch at the end.
- Changes the homepage hit-target test: its selector gains `.switch`, so the nine switch rows are still counted and still tested at 40px. The floor `CHECKED_ON_PAGE` stays 55 (Step 6 says why).
- Leaves for later tasks: nothing in the docs still draws `.switch` by hand.

**Decisions made here, recorded in Appendix B (Step 1) and repeated so no later task reopens them:**

- **The thumb keeps the same gap everywhere.** The source padded the 52px track by 2px and moved the thumb 22px: 2px at the start when off, 4px at the end when on. The library keeps the source's sizes (a 52 by 30px track and a 24px thumb) and gives the thumb 3px on all four sides. The travel is the track less the thumb less two gaps, 22px, the same distance as the source's: the padding changed, the number did not. It is computed from three custom properties (`--switch-width`, `--switch-thumb-size`, `--switch-inset`), so a changed size stays symmetric, and a core test and two story assertions pin it. This is also what the docs stand-in drew, so the homepage looks the same.
- **The thumb moves by its inline margin, not a transform,** so it reverses in right-to-left text with no direction selector (`:dir()` is outside the browser floor, Chrome 111).
- **The thumb follows `--radius-pill`** like the track: a circle in Rounded and Soft (12px on a 24px thumb), a square in Square. A pill imposes no nested-radius step on what it holds.
- **The thumb casts no shadow.** The source's lift shadow is invisible in light and smears a gray halo across the white on track in dark. This is a fix, recorded in Appendix B.
- **Colors.** Off track `--color-boundary`, on track `--color-ink`, the thumb `--color-raised` when off and `--color-canvas` when on. The pairs are gated on all five surfaces: off track against the surface 3.38 (light) and 4.93 (dark), raised thumb on it 3.48 and 4.24. canvas on ink was gated already (the primary Button label), so no pair was added for the on state.
- **Disabled differs between on and off.** The source drew one look for both. Off is hollow (the `disabled` fill, a 1px ink 15% edge, a taupe thumb); on is filled (a taupe track, a thumb in the `disabled` fill). The label stays ink, as a disabled field's does. A core test pins the on rule, a story pins each look.
- **Changed follows the source.** The source draws a changed cue on the switch row: a 2px light signal orange ring around the track (not a border, "a 1.5px border on a 24px pill reads as a smudge"). The library draws the same ring, in a pseudo-element outside the track, keyed on the field's root. Because it sits outside, it does not replace the off track's boundary fill, which keeps its measured 3:1; a core test fails if any `[data-changed]` rule sets a fill, and the `ChangedAndFocused` story asserts the off track is still the boundary color. The chip is `FieldChanged`, beside the label row and not inside it, so the switch's name is its label alone; it is announced through `aria-describedby` with the same hook TextField uses. A switch with no visible label draws the ring and no chip. The light orange is 2.53 to 2.87:1 against the light surfaces, under the 3:1 a boundary asks, and is recorded rather than gated for the reason TextField gives. The focus ring steps out past the changed ring by its width.
- **No required or invalid state.** The props `isRequired`, `isInvalid` and `validate` are left out of the type: a switch acts as soon as it is flipped, so no value of it can be wrong. A test pins the type.
- **Hover draws nothing,** as in the source; the pointer cursor marks the row. A read-only switch looks enabled and only its cursor becomes `default`.
- **Drawn 30px, hit 40px,** by a `::before` on the row that extends 5px above and below, so there is no layout shift. This is what the hit-target test measures.
- **Motion is the source's 160ms** on the track fill and the thumb, and `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` sets both transitions to none (the source's did not). The corners never animate; the docs stand-in's `border-radius` recut transition is not kept, since keeping it would mean restating the library's own transition list in a docs rule.
- **The state selectors match the attribute and the native state:** `.switch:is([data-selected], :has(input:checked))`, and likewise for disabled and focus. The `PlainHtml` story renders a label that holds a plain checkbox with the `switch` role and asserts the stylesheet draws it, in light and dark.
- **The hint lines up with the label text** (indented by the 52px track and the 0.75rem gap) through a selector with no specificity of its own, `:where(.field-head:has(> .switch)) ~ .field-description`, so a layout can move it. The homepage settings rows do (`.setting .field-description`).
- **The homepage rows keep their look** with three docs-only rules: `.setting .field { flex: 1 }`, `.setting .field-head > .switch { flex: 1; flex-direction: row-reverse; justify-content: space-between }` and `.setting .field-description { padding-inline-start: 0 }`, which put the track at the end of the row and the hint under the label at the start.
- **`CONTROLS` in the homepage test gains `.switch`,** so the nine rows stay in the 40px hit test. On a production build the count was 61 at 375px and 62 at 1440px before this task, 52 and 53 with the selector unchanged, and 61 and 62 with it extended. The floor was 55, six under the smaller old count. The new floor is the new smaller count less the same six: 61 - 6 = 55, so it stays. Had the selector not changed it would have been 52 - 6 = 46, and the switches would have left the 40px test.
- **One CSS file, no new classes beyond the three.** `switch`, `switch-track` and `switch-thumb` are the only classes the file declares.
- **`FieldHead` is not used.** The label is the row, so the helper's hook, `useChangedDescription`, is used on its own with `isChanged && children != null`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Record the derivation**

Append to the end of `docs/design-system.md` (after the RadioGroup section), keeping a blank line before the heading:

```markdown

## Switch

The document gives the switch one sentence: a stadium track with a round
thumb, the pill vocabulary again, for a setting that is simply on or off. The
numbers are the app's, from `js/switch-input.js` and `control.css`, and the
library changes the ones below, each recorded here.

**Size is the app's.** A 52px by 30px track and a 24px round thumb. The row is
the label, so the whole line is one target, and the label text is the body step
in ink, as in the app.

**The thumb keeps the same gap everywhere.** The app padded the track by 2px
and moved the thumb 22px, which left 2px at the start when off and 4px at the
end when on. A 24px thumb in a 30px track has 3px above and below, so the
library gives it 3px at both ends too. The travel is then the track (52px) less
the thumb (24px) less two gaps (6px), which is 22px again: the app's distance,
with the padding changed to match it. Width, thumb size and gap are three
properties and the travel is computed from them, so a size that changes stays
symmetric. The thumb follows `--radius-pill` like the track, a circle in
Rounded and Soft and a square in Square. It moves by its inline margin and not
by a transform, so it reverses in right-to-left text without a direction
selector, which the browser floor does not have.

**The off track is the boundary color and the on track is ink.** The app mixed
ink at 22% for the off track, which measured 1.62:1, and "Four colors added"
already names a switch's off track as a use of `boundary`. The thumb is the
Raised fill when off and canvas when on, which on an ink track (white in dark)
is the inverse, as the primary Button's label is. The off track is painted on
the surface itself, so each pair is measured on all five surfaces a switch can
sit on:

| Pair | Lowest on the five surfaces, light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off track against the surface | 3.38 | 4.93 |
| Raised thumb on the off track | 3.48 | 4.24 |
| Ink track against the surface (the ink text pairs) | 16.25 | 15.36 |
| canvas thumb on the ink track (the primary Button label) | 16.25 | 19.31 |

The first two rows are new in the contrast gate: the off track on each surface,
and the thumb on it on each (Lifted was there already). The last two were gated
already, at 4.5:1, and still are.

**The thumb casts no shadow.** The app gave it the lift shadow. At 4% in light
it cannot be seen, and at 40% in dark it smears a gray halo across the white on
track, so the library draws a flat thumb in both themes.

**Focus is the token ring around the track,** 2px at a 2px offset. It sits
outside the track so ink still reads against the surface when the track is ink.
The app drew the same ring, in ink; the library draws it in the focus ring
token. Nothing else on the row changes.

**Disabled is different when the switch is on and when it is off.** The app drew
ink at 10% for both, so a disabled switch told on from off by the thumb alone.
The library follows the disabled idiom of the Button
and the input and splits it. Off is hollow: the recessed `disabled` fill, a 1px
edge of ink at 15% and a taupe thumb. On is filled: a taupe track and a thumb
in the recessed fill. The fill, the thumb and its position all say which, so no
one cue carries it. A disabled control is outside the 3:1 asked of an active
one: the taupe thumb on the recessed track measures 1.44 in light and 3.81 in
dark, and the filled track against its surface 1.40 to 1.58 in light and 3.68
to 3.81 in dark. The label stays ink, as a disabled field's label does, so the
setting can still be read.

**Changed is a ring around the track and the chip beside the label.** The app's
switch draws a changed cue of its own, a 2px ring in light signal orange
("a 1.5px border on a 24px pill reads as a smudge rather than a cue"), so the
library keeps the ring and does not draw the 1.5px border that text fields use.
The ring is outside the track, so it does not replace the off track's boundary
fill: the track under it keeps the 3.38:1 measured above, on every surface. The
track draws the ring, keyed on the field's root (`data-changed`) as the field
contract asks, so it shows on an ink track and on a boundary one. The focus ring steps out
past it by its width, so a changed switch with focus shows both. The chip is
the field's `FieldChanged`, beside the label and not inside it, so the switch
is named by its label alone, and a screen reader reads it with the switch
through `aria-describedby`, exactly as TextField's chip is read. Light signal
orange measures 2.53 to 2.87:1 against the light surfaces and 5.35 to 6.73 in
dark. That is under the 3:1 a boundary asks in light, and it is kept and
recorded rather than gated, for the reason TextField gives: the cue is never
alone, because the clay chip carries the word and is gated. A switch with no
visible label draws the ring and no chip, as a field without a label row does.

**There is no invalid or required state.** The app drew an error ring on a
switch row. A switch takes effect as soon as it is flipped, so no value of it
can be wrong, and a choice that a form confirms later is a Checkbox. The
library leaves `isRequired`, `isInvalid` and `validate` out of the props.

**Drawn 30px, hit 40px.** The row extends its hit area with a pseudo-element, 5px
above and below, so the touch rule holds with no layout shift. The app's switch
was 30px with nothing extended.

**Hover draws nothing, as in the app.** The thumb moving is the feedback, and the
pointer cursor marks the row as pressable. A read-only switch looks like an
enabled one, like a read-only field, and only its cursor stops being a pointer,
since a press does nothing.

**Motion is the app's 160ms,** a fade of the track and a slide of the thumb, and
both stop under reduced motion, which the app's did not. The corners never
animate: they belong to the shape axis.

**The control is a native checkbox with the `switch` role,** from React Aria's
SwitchField and SwitchButton, so a screen reader says "switch, on" where a
checkbox would say "checked", as the app wanted. It submits its `value` (the
browser's `on` without one) under its `name` only while it is on, and is left
out of the form while disabled. The app's two-option text value, its `Yes|No`
pair and its list of fields that read as on when blank are the app's own logic
and not the library's.
```

The numbers come from `paletteFor`, `composite` and `contrastRatio` in `packages/core/scripts/contrast.js`: the off track is `boundary` composited over each surface and measured against that surface, and the thumb is measured against the track it sits on. The disabled figures use `taupe` and `disabled` composited over each surface the same way.

```js
describe('src/components/switch.css', () => {
  // The rules without their comments, which quote selectors of their own.
  const rules = () => read('src/components/switch.css').replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '');

  it('stops the track and the thumb moving under reduced motion', () => {
    const reduced = blockAfter(rules(), '@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');
    expect(reduced).toContain('.switch-track');
    expect(reduced).toContain('.switch-thumb');
    expect(reduced).toMatch(/transition:\s*none;/);
  });

  it('never animates the corners, which belong to the shape axis', () => {
    expect(rules()).not.toMatch(/transition[^;]*radius/);
  });

  it('derives the thumb travel from the track, the thumb and the gap, so the gaps match', () => {
    // Off, the thumb sits one gap from the start. On, it has moved the track
    // width less the thumb and two gaps, which leaves one gap at the end.
    expect(rules()).toMatch(
      /--switch-travel:\s*calc\(var\(--switch-width\) - var\(--switch-thumb-size\) - 2 \* var\(--switch-inset\)\);/,
    );
  });

  it('draws a disabled switch that is on differently from one that is off', () => {
    const on =
      /\.switch:is\(\[data-disabled\][^{]*\):is\(\[data-selected\][^{]*\)\s*\{[^}]*--switch-track-fill:\s*var\(--color-taupe\);/;
    const off =
      /\.switch:is\(\[data-disabled\][^{]*\)\s*\{[^}]*--switch-track-fill:\s*var\(--color-disabled\);/;
    expect(rules()).toMatch(on);
    expect(rules()).toMatch(off);
  });

  it('keys the changed ring on the field root, as the field contract asks', () => {
    expect(rules()).toContain('.field[data-changed] .switch-track::before');
  });

  it('draws the changed ring outside the track and never recolors the off track, whose boundary is a measured edge', () => {
    const changed = [...rules().matchAll(/([^{}]*\[data-changed\][^{}]*)\{([^}]*)\}/g)];
    expect(changed.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const [, selector = '', body = ''] of changed) {
      expect(body, selector.trim()).not.toMatch(/background|--switch-track-fill|--switch-edge/);
    }
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { act, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef, useState, type ReactElement } from 'react';
import { describe, expect, expectTypeOf, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { Switch, type SwitchProps } from './Switch';

/** A switch the caller controls, the way a form library would. */
function Controlled(props: SwitchProps): ReactElement {
  const [isSelected, setSelected] = useState(false);
  return <Switch {...props} isSelected={isSelected} onChange={setSelected} />;
}

const root = (container: HTMLElement): Element => {
  const element = container.firstElementChild;
  if (!element) throw new Error('Nothing rendered');
  return element;
};

const formOf = (container: HTMLElement): HTMLFormElement => {
  const form = container.querySelector('form');
  if (!form) throw new Error('No form');
  return form;
};

describe('Switch', () => {
  it('renders a switch with its label, inside a field', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Switch>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field');
    expect(root(container)).not.toHaveAttribute('data-changed');
    const row = screen.getByText('Weekly digest').closest('label');
    expect(row).toHaveClass('switch');
    expect(row).toContainElement(control);
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('draws the track and the thumb as decoration inside the row', () => {
    render(<Switch>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    const track = screen.getByText('Weekly digest').closest('label')?.querySelector('.switch-track');
    expect(track).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    expect(track?.firstElementChild).toHaveClass('switch-thumb');
    expect(track?.firstElementChild?.children).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('puts the row first and the hint after it', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Switch description="Every Tuesday morning.">Weekly digest</Switch>);
    expect([...root(container).children].map((child) => child.classList[0])).toEqual([
      'field-head',
      'field-description',
    ]);
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    expect(control).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Every Tuesday morning.');
    expect(screen.getByText('Every Tuesday morning.')).toHaveClass('field-description');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('turns on and off with a click on the label, and on the input', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    render(<Switch onChange={onChange}>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch');
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Weekly digest'));
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(true);
    await user.click(control);
    expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(false);
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('turns on and off with Space, and not with Enter', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Switch>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch');
    await user.tab();
    expect(control).toHaveFocus();
    await user.keyboard(' ');
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
    await user.keyboard(' ');
    expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
    await user.keyboard('{Enter}');
    expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
  });

  it('starts from defaultSelected when uncontrolled', () => {
    render(<Switch defaultSelected>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch')).toBeChecked();
  });

  it('marks the row with data-selected while it is on', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Switch>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    const row = screen.getByText('Weekly digest').closest('label');
    expect(row).not.toHaveAttribute('data-selected');
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('switch'));
    expect(row).toHaveAttribute('data-selected');
  });

  it('follows isSelected when controlled, and tells the caller what was asked', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    const { rerender } = render(
      <Switch isSelected={false} onChange={onChange}>
        Weekly digest
      </Switch>,
    );
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch');
    await user.click(control);
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith(true);
    expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
    rerender(
      <Switch isSelected onChange={onChange}>
        Weekly digest
      </Switch>,
    );
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
  });

  it('works with a state the caller keeps', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Controlled>Weekly digest</Controlled>);
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch');
    await user.click(control);
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
    await user.click(control);
    expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
  });

  it('submits its value in a plain form only while it is on', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <Switch name="digest" value="weekly">
          Weekly digest
        </Switch>
      </form>,
    );
    const form = formOf(container);
    expect(new FormData(form).has('digest')).toBe(false);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('switch'));
    expect(new FormData(form).get('digest')).toBe('weekly');
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('switch'));
    expect(new FormData(form).has('digest')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('submits the browser default, on, when it has no value', () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <Switch name="digest" defaultSelected>
          Weekly digest
        </Switch>
      </form>,
    );
    expect(new FormData(formOf(container)).get('digest')).toBe('on');
  });

  it('follows a form reset back to the default', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <Switch name="digest" defaultSelected>
          Weekly digest
        </Switch>
      </form>,
    );
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('switch'));
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch')).not.toBeChecked();
    act(() => {
      formOf(container).reset();
    });
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch')).toBeChecked();
    expect(new FormData(formOf(container)).get('digest')).toBe('on');
  });

  it('is named by aria-label when it has no visible label', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(<Switch aria-label="Sample" defaultSelected />);
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Sample' });
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
    await user.click(control);
    expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(container.querySelector('.switch-track')).not.toBeNull();
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('disables the control and leaves it out of the form', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <Switch name="digest" defaultSelected isDisabled onChange={onChange}>
          Weekly digest
        </Switch>
      </form>,
    );
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    expect(control).toBeDisabled();
    expect(container.querySelector('.field')).toHaveAttribute('data-disabled');
    expect(container.querySelector('.switch')).toHaveAttribute('data-disabled');
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Weekly digest'));
    await user.click(control);
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
    expect(onChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(new FormData(formOf(container)).has('digest')).toBe(false);
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);

  it('keeps a read-only switch readable, focusable and in the form, and does not let it change', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <Switch name="digest" defaultSelected isReadOnly onChange={onChange}>
          Weekly digest
        </Switch>
      </form>,
    );
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    expect(control).toHaveAttribute('aria-readonly', 'true');
    expect(screen.getByText('Weekly digest').closest('label')).toHaveAttribute('data-readonly');
    await user.tab();
    expect(control).toHaveFocus();
    await user.keyboard(' ');
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Weekly digest'));
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
    expect(onChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(new FormData(formOf(container)).get('digest')).toBe('on');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('shows the changed chip beside the label, and a screen reader reads it with the switch', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Switch isChanged description="Every Tuesday morning.">
        Weekly digest
      </Switch>,
    );
    expect(root(container)).toHaveAttribute('data-changed', '');
    const chip = screen.getByText('Changed');
    expect(chip).toHaveClass('field-changed');
    expect(chip.parentElement).toHaveClass('field-head');
    // The chip sits beside the row, not inside it, so the switch is named by its label alone.
    expect(chip.closest('label')).toBeNull();
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    expect(control.getAttribute('aria-describedby')?.split(' ')).toContain(chip.id);
    expect(control).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Every Tuesday morning. Changed');
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('takes the chip text from changedLabel', () => {
    render(
      <Switch isChanged changedLabel="Unsaved">
        Weekly digest
      </Switch>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByText('Unsaved')).toHaveClass('field-changed');
    expect(screen.queryByText('Changed')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch')).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Unsaved');
  });

  it('keeps the chip in the page, unannounced, while the switch is not changed', () => {
    render(<Switch description="Every Tuesday morning.">Weekly digest</Switch>);
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch');
    expect(control).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Every Tuesday morning.');
    expect(control.getAttribute('aria-describedby')?.split(' ')).not.toContain(
      screen.getByText('Changed').id,
    );
  });

  it('adds the chip to the aria-describedby the caller passes', () => {
    render(
      <>
        <p id="note">Visible to admins.</p>
        <Switch description="Every Tuesday morning." aria-describedby="note" isChanged>
          Weekly digest
        </Switch>
      </>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch')).toHaveAccessibleDescription(
      'Every Tuesday morning. Visible to admins. Changed',
    );
  });

  it('draws no chip for a switch without a visible label, though the root is still changed', () => {
    const { container } = render(<Switch aria-label="Sample" isChanged />);
    expect(root(container)).toHaveAttribute('data-changed', '');
    expect(screen.queryByText('Changed')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch')).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-describedby');
  });

  it('shows the chip whichever way the switch is set', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Switch isChanged>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('switch'));
    expect(screen.getByText('Changed')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('switch')).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Changed');
  });

  it('forwards ref to the field and inputRef to the input', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLDivElement>();
    const inputRef = createRef<HTMLInputElement>();
    render(
      <Switch ref={ref} inputRef={inputRef}>
        Weekly digest
      </Switch>,
    );
    expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLDivElement);
    expect(ref.current).toHaveClass('field');
    expect(inputRef.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLInputElement);
    expect(inputRef.current).toBe(screen.getByRole('switch'));
  });

  it('merges a string className after its own', () => {
    const { container } = render(<Switch className="extra">Weekly digest</Switch>);
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field', 'extra');
  });

  it('merges a function className, which receives the switch state', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const className = vi.fn(
      ({
        isSelected,
        isDisabled,
      }: {
        isSelected: boolean;
        isDisabled: boolean;
        defaultClassName: string | undefined;
      }) => (isDisabled ? 'is-disabled' : isSelected ? 'is-on' : 'is-off'),
    );
    const { container, rerender } = render(<Switch className={className}>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field', 'is-off');
    await user.click(screen.getByRole('switch'));
    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field', 'is-on');
    rerender(
      <Switch className={className} isDisabled>
        Weekly digest
      </Switch>,

    expect(root(container)).toHaveClass('field', 'is-disabled');
    expect(className.mock.calls[0]?.[0].defaultClassName).toBe('react-aria-SwitchField');
  });

  it('passes its other attributes to the input', () => {
    render(
      <Switch name="digest" value="weekly" id="digest-switch">
        Weekly digest
      </Switch>,
    );
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch');
    expect(control).toHaveAttribute('id', 'digest-switch');
    expect(control).toHaveAttribute('name', 'digest');
    expect(control).toHaveAttribute('value', 'weekly');
  });

  it('offers no required or invalid state in its types, since a switch acts as soon as it is flipped', () => {
    expectTypeOf<SwitchProps>().not.toHaveProperty('isRequired');
    expectTypeOf<SwitchProps>().not.toHaveProperty('isInvalid');
    expectTypeOf<SwitchProps>().not.toHaveProperty('validate');
  });

  it.each([
    ['off', {}],
    ['on', { defaultSelected: true }],
    ['with a hint', { description: 'Every Tuesday morning.' }],
    ['disabled and off', { isDisabled: true }],
    ['disabled and on', { isDisabled: true, defaultSelected: true }],
    ['read-only', { isReadOnly: true, defaultSelected: true }],
    ['changed', { isChanged: true }],
    ['changed with a hint', { isChanged: true, description: 'Every Tuesday morning.' }],
  ] satisfies [string, Partial<SwitchProps>][])('has no axe violations when %s', async (_state, props) => {
    const { container } = render(<Switch {...props}>Weekly digest</Switch>);
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the CSS and the contrast pairs**

`packages/core/src/components/switch.css`. Each state only sets the `--switch-*` properties and the track and the thumb read them, so a state never needs one rule per part:

```css
/*
 * The switch, derived in docs/design-system.md ("Switch"): a 52 by 30 stadium
 * track with a 24px round thumb, the pill vocabulary again. The row is the
 * label, so the whole line is the target, and the track and the thumb are drawn
 * inside it.
 *
 * Each state only sets the --switch-* properties; the track and the thumb read
 * them, so a state never needs one rule per part. State is read from the row
 * (`data-selected`, `data-disabled`, `data-focus-visible`) or, for markup
 * without React Aria, from the input the row holds. The changed ring is keyed on
 * the field's root, as the field contract in field.css says.
 */
@layer components {
  .switch {
    --switch-width: 52px;
    --switch-thumb-size: 24px;
    /* The gap between the thumb and the track on all four sides. */
    --switch-inset: 3px;
    --switch-track-fill: var(--color-boundary);
    --switch-thumb-fill: var(--color-raised);
    --switch-edge: transparent;
    --switch-travel: 0px;
    /* The width of the changed ring, which the focus ring steps out past. */
    --switch-changed-ring: 2px;

    position: relative;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 0.75rem;
    margin: 0;
    color: var(--color-ink);
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: var(--text-body);
    line-height: var(--text-body--line-height);
    font-weight: var(--text-body--font-weight);
    cursor: pointer;
    user-select: none;
    -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
  }

  /* Drawn 30px tall and hit 40px tall, so the row meets the touch target with no
     layout shift. The extra area belongs to the row, so a press on it toggles. */
  .switch::before {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    inset: -5px 0;
  }

  .switch-track {
    position: relative;
    box-sizing: border-box;
    display: flex;
    flex: none;
    align-items: center;
    width: var(--switch-width);
    height: calc(var(--switch-thumb-size) + 2 * var(--switch-inset));
    /* The 1px edge is clear but for a disabled switch that is off, and it sits
       inside the inset, so the thumb is one gap from the track either way. */
    padding: calc(var(--switch-inset) - 1px);
    border: 1px solid var(--switch-edge);
    border-radius: var(--radius-pill);
    background-color: var(--switch-track-fill);
    transition: background-color 160ms ease;
  }

  /* The thumb follows the pill, so it is a circle in Rounded and Soft and a
     square in Square, with the track. It casts no shadow: the lift shadow is
     invisible on a light track and smears a gray halo across a white one. */
  .switch-thumb {
    flex: none;
    width: var(--switch-thumb-size);
    height: var(--switch-thumb-size);
    margin-inline-start: var(--switch-travel);
    border-radius: var(--radius-pill);
    background-color: var(--switch-thumb-fill);
    transition:
      margin-inline-start 160ms ease,
      background-color 160ms ease;
  }

  /* On: an ink track and a canvas thumb. The thumb moves the track width less
     the thumb and two gaps, which leaves one gap at the end, the same as the
     gap it had at the start. */
  .switch:is([data-selected], :has(input:checked)) {
    --switch-track-fill: var(--color-ink);
    --switch-thumb-fill: var(--color-canvas);
    --switch-travel: calc(var(--switch-width) - var(--switch-thumb-size) - 2 * var(--switch-inset));
  }

  /* The ring is outside the track, so ink still reads against the surface behind
     it when the track is ink. */
  .switch:is([data-focus-visible], :has(input:focus-visible)) .switch-track {
    outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color);
    outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);
  }

  /* Disabled, off: the recessed fill with a faint edge and a taupe thumb, the
     disabled idiom of a button or an input. */
  .switch:is([data-disabled], :has(input:disabled)) {
    --switch-track-fill: var(--color-disabled);
    --switch-thumb-fill: var(--color-taupe);
    --switch-edge: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 15%, transparent);

    cursor: not-allowed;
  }

  /* Disabled, on: the track is filled, with taupe, and the thumb is the recessed
     fill. Filled against recessed is what tells on from off, with the thumb
     position, so the two never share a look (the source drew one for both). */
  .switch:is([data-disabled], :has(input:disabled)):is([data-selected], :has(input:checked)) {
    --switch-track-fill: var(--color-taupe);
    --switch-thumb-fill: var(--color-disabled);
    --switch-edge: transparent;
  }

  /* A read-only switch looks like an enabled one and keeps its place in the
     form; only the cursor stops promising a press. */
  .switch[data-readonly] {
    cursor: default;
  }

  /*
   * The field's root carries data-changed. A 1.5px border on a 30px track reads
   * as a smudge, so the changed cue is a ring outside the track instead, in
   * light signal orange. The focus ring steps out past it.
   */
  .field[data-changed] .switch-track::before {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    inset: calc(-1 * var(--switch-changed-ring) - 1px);
    border: var(--switch-changed-ring) solid var(--color-signal-light);
    border-radius: inherit;
    pointer-events: none;
  }

  .field[data-changed] .switch:is([data-focus-visible], :has(input:focus-visible)) .switch-track {
    outline-offset: calc(var(--focus-ring-offset) + var(--switch-changed-ring));
  }

  /* The row beside the chip is centered on the track, where a label row sits on
     its baseline. */
  .field-head:has(> .switch) {
    align-items: center;
  }

  /* The hint lines up with the label text, past the track (52px) and the gap. The
     lead selector adds no specificity, so a layout can move the hint. */
  :where(.field-head:has(> .switch)) ~ .field-description {
    padding-inline-start: calc(52px + 0.75rem);
  }

  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .switch-track,
    .switch-thumb {
      transition: none;
    }
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the component**

`packages/react/src/switch/Switch.tsx`. The row is a React Aria `SwitchButton`, the field around it a `SwitchField`, so the control is a native checkbox with the `switch` role. The chip is a sibling of the row inside the label row, which is why it is not part of the switch's name:

```tsx
'use client';

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react';
import {
  SwitchButton as RACSwitchButton,
  SwitchField as RACSwitchField,
  type SwitchFieldProps as RACSwitchFieldProps,
  type SwitchFieldRenderProps,
  composeRenderProps,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import { Description } from '../field/Description';
import { FieldChanged } from '../field/FieldChanged';
import { useChangedDescription } from '../field/useChangedDescription';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export interface SwitchProps extends Omit<
  RACSwitchFieldProps,
  'children' | 'className' | 'isRequired' | 'isInvalid' | 'validate' | 'validationBehavior'
> {
  /** The label, beside the track. Without one, give the switch an `aria-label`. */
  children?: ReactNode;
  /** A hint under the label. It becomes the switch's accessible description. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Whether the setting differs from the saved one. Shows the clay Changed chip
   * beside the label and a light signal orange ring around the track, and has a
   * screen reader read the chip with the switch. A switch without a visible
   * label draws the ring and no chip.
   */
  isChanged?: boolean;
  /**
   * The text of the Changed chip.
   * @default 'Changed'
   */
  changedLabel?: string;
  /**
   * A class name, or a function of the switch's state, merged after the library's own class. It goes
   * on the field's root, the element with the `field` class that also holds the hint, and not on the
   * row, which carries `switch`.
   */
  className?:
    string | ((values: SwitchFieldRenderProps & { defaultClassName: string | undefined }) => string);
  /** A ref to the field's root element, the one `className` goes on. */
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>;
  /** A ref to the input element. */
  inputRef?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>;
}

/**
 * A setting that is on or off and takes effect as soon as it is flipped: a
 * 52px track with a round thumb, a label, an optional hint and the Changed
 * chip. It submits its `value` in a form only while it is on. Built on React
 * Aria's SwitchField and SwitchButton, so the control is a native checkbox with
 * the `switch` role. It has no required or invalid state; for a choice that is
 * confirmed later, use a Checkbox.
 */
export function Switch({
  children,
  description,
  isChanged = false,
  changedLabel,
  className,
  ...props
}: SwitchProps): ReactElement {
  const hasLabel = children != null;
  const { chipId, describedBy } = useChangedDescription({
    // Only a switch with a visible label has a chip to read.
    isChanged: isChanged && hasLabel,
    describedBy: props['aria-describedby'],
  });
  return (
    <RACSwitchField
      {...props}
      aria-describedby={describedBy}
      data-changed={isChanged ? '' : undefined}
      className={composeRenderProps(className, (userClassName) => cx('field', userClassName))}
    >
      <div className="field-head">
        <RACSwitchButton className="switch">
          <span className="switch-track" aria-hidden="true">
            <span className="switch-thumb" />
          </span>
          {children}
        </RACSwitchButton>
        {hasLabel ? <FieldChanged id={chipId}>{changedLabel}</FieldChanged> : null}
      </div>
      {description != null ? <Description>{description}</Description> : null}
    </RACSwitchField>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Stories**

`packages/react/src/switch/Switch.stories.tsx`. Thirteen stories: off, on, with a hint, disabled and off, disabled and on, read-only, changed, focused, changed and focused, a long label, a dark scope inside the page, and two with no screenshot, `Toggling` and `PlainHtml`. The `play` functions run in Chromium in light and dark, so they check what jsdom cannot: the computed track and thumb fills against the tokens, the thumb's gap to the track at each end and above and below it (3px, which is the symmetry), the disabled looks and cursor, the changed ring's color and width, the focus outline and its 4px offset when the switch is changed, and in `PlainHtml` that the stylesheet draws markup with no React Aria in it. `waitFor` runs again on every change to the page, and `tokenColor` paints a probe into it, so a color is read before `waitFor`, never inside it:

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { expect, waitFor } from 'storybook/test';
import { Switch } from './Switch';

/** The color a token paints in the theme around `scope`, read by painting it. */
function tokenColor(name: string, scope: Element = document.body): string {
  const probe = document.createElement('span');
  probe.style.color = `var(${name})`;
  scope.append(probe);
  const { color } = getComputedStyle(probe);
  probe.remove();
  return color;
}

/** The row, the track and the thumb of the first switch drawn inside `scope`. */
function parts(scope: Element): { row: Element; track: Element; thumb: Element } {
  const row = scope.querySelector('.switch');
  const track = scope.querySelector('.switch-track');
  const thumb = scope.querySelector('.switch-thumb');
  if (!row || !track || !thumb) throw new Error('No switch drawn');
  return { row, track, thumb };
}

/** The gaps, in px, between the thumb and the start, the end, the top and the bottom of the track. */
function thumbGaps(scope: Element): { start: number; end: number; top: number; bottom: number } {
  const { track, thumb } = parts(scope);
  const outer = track.getBoundingClientRect();
  const inner = thumb.getBoundingClientRect();
  return {
    start: inner.left - outer.left,
    end: outer.right - inner.right,
    top: inner.top - outer.top,
    bottom: outer.bottom - inner.bottom,
  };
}

const fill = (element: Element): string => getComputedStyle(element).backgroundColor;

const meta = {
  title: 'Components/Switch',
  component: Switch,
  args: { children: 'Weekly digest' },
  decorators: [
    (Story) => (
      <div style={{ width: 'min(28rem, calc(100vw - 2rem))' }}>
        <Story />
      </div>
    ),
  ],
} satisfies Meta<typeof Switch>;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

/** Off: the boundary-colored track, a raised thumb one gap from the start, the same gap above and below. */
export const Off: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' })).not.toBeChecked();
    const { track, thumb } = parts(canvasElement);
    await expect(fill(track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-boundary'));
    await expect(fill(thumb)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-raised'));
    const gaps = thumbGaps(canvasElement);
    await expect(gaps.start).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);
    await expect(gaps.top).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);
    await expect(gaps.bottom).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);
  },
};

/** On: an ink track and a canvas thumb, one gap from the end, the same gap as it had at the start. */
export const On: Story = {
  args: { defaultSelected: true },
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' })).toBeChecked();
    const { track, thumb } = parts(canvasElement);
    await expect(fill(track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-ink'));
    await expect(fill(thumb)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-canvas'));
    const gaps = thumbGaps(canvasElement);
    await expect(gaps.end).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);
    await expect(gaps.top).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);
    await expect(gaps.bottom).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);
  },
};

/** The hint is the switch's accessible description, and lines up under the label text. */
export const WithDescription: Story = {
  args: { description: 'Every Tuesday morning.', defaultSelected: true },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' })).toHaveAccessibleDescription(
      'Every Tuesday morning.',
    );
  },
};

/** Disabled and off: a recessed track, a faint edge and a taupe thumb. */
export const DisabledOff: Story = {
  args: { isDisabled: true },
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement }) => {
    const control = canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    await expect(control).toBeDisabled();
    const { row, track, thumb } = parts(canvasElement);
    await expect(fill(track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-disabled'));
    await expect(fill(thumb)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-taupe'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(track).borderTopColor).not.toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(row).cursor).toBe('not-allowed');
  },
};

/** Disabled and on: a filled taupe track and a recessed thumb, so on and off differ without the thumb position. */
export const DisabledOn: Story = {
  args: { isDisabled: true, defaultSelected: true },
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement }) => {
    const control = canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    await expect(control).toBeDisabled();
    await expect(control).toBeChecked();
    const { track, thumb } = parts(canvasElement);
    await expect(fill(track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-taupe'));
    await expect(fill(thumb)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-disabled'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(track).borderTopColor).toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
  },
};

/** Read-only looks like an enabled switch and cannot be changed. */
export const ReadOnly: Story = {
  args: { isReadOnly: true, defaultSelected: true, description: 'Managed by your admin.' },
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement }) => {
    const control = canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    await expect(control).toHaveAttribute('aria-readonly', 'true');
    await expect(fill(parts(canvasElement).track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-ink'));
  },
};

/** `isChanged` shows the clay chip beside the label and the light signal orange ring, and the chip is read with the switch. */
export const Changed: Story = {
  args: { isChanged: true, defaultSelected: true, description: 'Every Tuesday morning.' },
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement }) => {
    const control = canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    await expect(canvas.getByText('Changed')).toBeVisible();
    const ring = getComputedStyle(parts(canvasElement).track, '::before');
    await expect(ring.borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-signal-light'));
    await expect(ring.borderTopWidth).toBe('2px');
    await expect(control).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Every Tuesday morning. Changed');
  },
};

/** Keyboard focus draws the ring around the track, outside it. */
export const Focused: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement, userEvent }) => {
    await userEvent.tab();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('switch')).toHaveFocus();
    const { track } = parts(canvasElement);
    const style = getComputedStyle(track);
    await expect(style.outlineStyle).toBe('solid');
    await expect(style.outlineWidth).toBe('2px');
    await expect(style.outlineOffset).toBe('2px');
    await expect(style.outlineColor).toBe(tokenColor('--focus-ring-color'));
  },
};

/** A changed switch that has focus: the focus ring steps out past the changed ring, so both show. */
export const ChangedAndFocused: Story = {
  args: { isChanged: true },
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement, userEvent }) => {
    await userEvent.tab();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('switch')).toHaveFocus();
    const { track } = parts(canvasElement);
    // The ring is outside the track, so an off track keeps its boundary fill.
    await expect(fill(track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-boundary'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(track).outlineStyle).toBe('solid');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(track).outlineOffset).toBe('4px');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(track, '::before').borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-signal-light'));
  },
};

/** A long label wraps beside the track and the chip drops under it, with no sideways scroll at 375px. */
export const LongLabel: Story = {
  args: {
    children: 'Email me a short summary of every comment on my posts, once a week, on Tuesday mornings',
    description: 'You can turn this off at any time from the link at the bottom of each email.',
    isChanged: true,
    defaultSelected: true,
  },
};

/** A dark scope on the page takes its own tokens: the on track is white, the thumbs are dark. */
export const InDarkScope: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <div
      data-theme="dark"
      data-testid="dark-scope"
      style={{
        display: 'grid',
        gap: 16,
        padding: 24,
        borderRadius: 24,
        background: 'var(--color-lifted)',
        color: 'var(--color-ink)',
      }}
    >
      <Switch {...args}>Off</Switch>
      <Switch {...args} defaultSelected>
        On
      </Switch>
      <Switch {...args} isDisabled>
        Disabled and off
      </Switch>
      <Switch {...args} isDisabled defaultSelected>
        Disabled and on
      </Switch>
      <Switch {...args} isChanged defaultSelected>
        Changed
      </Switch>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = canvasElement.querySelector('[data-testid="dark-scope"]');
    if (!scope) throw new Error('No dark scope');
    const on = canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'On' }).closest('.field');
    const off = canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Off' }).closest('.field');
    if (!on || !off) throw new Error('No switch drawn');
    await expect(fill(parts(on).track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-ink', scope));
    await expect(fill(parts(on).track)).toBe('rgb(255, 255, 255)');
    await expect(fill(parts(off).track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-boundary', scope));
  },
};

/** The thumb travels the same gap each way, and a press or a key flips the switch. */
export const Toggling: Story = {
  tags: ['no-visual'],
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement, userEvent }) => {
    const control = canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    await expect(thumbGaps(canvasElement).start).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByText('Weekly digest'));
    await expect(control).toBeChecked();
    // The thumb takes 160ms to settle.
    await waitFor(() => expect(thumbGaps(canvasElement).end).toBeCloseTo(3, 1));
    await userEvent.keyboard(' ');
    await expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
    await waitFor(() => expect(thumbGaps(canvasElement).start).toBeCloseTo(3, 1));
  },
};

const VISUALLY_HIDDEN = {
  position: 'absolute',
  width: 1,
  height: 1,
  margin: -1,
  overflow: 'hidden',
  clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
} as const;

/** The stylesheet also serves markup without React Aria: a label that holds a checkbox with the switch role. */
export const PlainHtml: Story = {
  tags: ['no-visual'],
  render: () => (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
      <div data-testid="plain-switch">
        <label className="switch">
          <input type="checkbox" role="switch" style={VISUALLY_HIDDEN} />
          <span className="switch-track" aria-hidden="true">
            <span className="switch-thumb" />
          </span>
          Weekly digest
        </label>
      </div>
      <div data-testid="plain-disabled">
        <label className="switch">
          <input type="checkbox" role="switch" style={VISUALLY_HIDDEN} disabled defaultChecked />
          <span className="switch-track" aria-hidden="true">
            <span className="switch-thumb" />
          </span>
          Security alerts
        </label>
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas, canvasElement, userEvent }) => {
    const plain = canvasElement.querySelector('[data-testid="plain-switch"]');
    const disabled = canvasElement.querySelector('[data-testid="plain-disabled"]');
    if (!plain || !disabled) throw new Error('No switch drawn');
    await expect(fill(parts(plain).track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-boundary'));
    await userEvent.tab();
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' })).toHaveFocus();
    await expect(getComputedStyle(parts(plain).track).outlineStyle).toBe('solid');
    await userEvent.keyboard(' ');
    // The track takes 160ms to settle on its new fill. The color is read outside waitFor, which
    // runs again on every change to the page, and reading a token paints a probe into it.
    const ink = tokenColor('--color-ink');
    await waitFor(() => expect(fill(parts(plain).track)).toBe(ink));
    await expect(fill(parts(disabled).track)).toBe(tokenColor('--color-taupe'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(parts(disabled).row).cursor).toBe('not-allowed');
  },
};
```

`apps/docs/examples/switch-settings.tsx`:

```tsx
'use client';

import { Button, Switch } from '@snapshot-ui/react';
import { useState, type ReactElement } from 'react';

const SAVED = { updates: true, digest: false, alerts: true };
type Setting = keyof typeof SAVED;

const ROWS: { key: Setting; label: string; description: string }[] = [
  { key: 'updates', label: 'Product updates', description: 'A short note when something ships.' },
  { key: 'digest', label: 'Weekly digest', description: 'Every Tuesday morning.' },
  { key: 'alerts', label: 'Security alerts', description: 'Always on for owners.' },
];

export default function SwitchSettings(): ReactElement {
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(SAVED);
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState(SAVED);
  const isDirty = ROWS.some(({ key }) => draft[key] !== saved[key]);
  return (
    <div className="stack" style={{ width: '100%', maxWidth: '24rem' }}>
      {ROWS.map(({ key, label, description }) => (
        <Switch
          key={key}
          description={description}
          isSelected={draft[key]}
          onChange={(isSelected) => {
            setDraft({ ...draft, [key]: isSelected });
          }}
          isChanged={draft[key] !== saved[key]}
        >
          {label}
        </Switch>
      ))}
      <div className="row">
        <Button
          isDisabled={!isDirty}
          onPress={() => {
            setSaved(draft);
          }}
        >
          Save changes
        </Button>
        <Button
          variant="tertiary"
          isDisabled={!isDirty}
          onPress={() => {
            setDraft(saved);
          }}
        >
          Discard
        </Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The page, `apps/docs/content/docs/components/switch.mdx`. The first paragraph after each `##` is the section's note. The prose never uses the word "button" and never names the Spinner, so the search tests that rank those pages first are unaffected. It has a Keys table because the switch is interactive.

```mdx
---
title: Switch
description: A setting that is on or off and takes effect as soon as it is flipped. One element draws the track, the label, the hint and the Changed chip, and submits its value in a form only while it is on.
icon: ToggleLeft
---

<Section>

## Basic

Pass a label, and a hint if the label cannot say it all. The whole row is the target, so a press on the label flips the switch as well as a press on the track.

<Preview name="switch-basic" />

</Section>

<Section>

## States

On is an ink track with a canvas thumb. Off is the control boundary color with a raised thumb. A disabled switch is recessed, and one that is on is filled where one that is off is hollow, so the two never look alike. A read-only switch looks like an enabled one and cannot be changed.

<Preview name="switch-states" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Unsaved changes

Pass `isChanged` while the setting differs from the saved one. A clay chip shows beside the label and a light signal orange ring goes around the track, and a screen reader reads the chip with the switch. Flip a switch below to see them.

<Preview name="switch-settings" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

Every value works controlled and uncontrolled, and a switch with a `name` submits in a plain form. It sends its `value`, or `on` when it has none, only while it is on, as a checkbox does. `onChange` receives a boolean. A switch with no visible label needs an `aria-label`.

<Code code={`import { useState } from 'react';
import { Switch } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function DigestSetting({ saved }: { saved: boolean }) {
  const [isOn, setOn] = useState(saved);
  return (
    <Switch
      name="digest"
      value="weekly"
      description="Every Tuesday morning."
      isSelected={isOn}
      onChange={setOn}
      isChanged={isOn !== saved}
    >
      Weekly digest
    </Switch>
  );
}`} />

A switch is for a setting that takes effect as soon as it is flipped. It has no required or invalid state, so for a choice that a form confirms later, such as agreeing to terms, use a checkbox.

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

Every React Aria SwitchField prop is accepted except `isRequired`, `isInvalid` and `validate`. These are the ones Snapshot UI adds or shapes.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/switch/Switch.tsx" type="Pick<SwitchProps, 'children' | 'description' | 'isSelected' | 'defaultSelected' | 'onChange' | 'name' | 'value' | 'isDisabled' | 'isReadOnly' | 'isChanged' | 'changedLabel'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A native checkbox with the `switch` role, so a screen reader says the label and then on or off. The track and the thumb are decoration. The label names the switch, the hint and the Changed chip describe it, and a press anywhere on the row flips it. The row is 40px tall to hit, though the track is drawn 30px.

<Keys rows={[['Space', 'Turns the switch on or off.'], ['Tab', 'Moves focus to the switch. The 2px ring sits outside the track.']]} />

Motion is a 160ms slide of the thumb and a fade of the track, and both stop under reduced motion.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps switches in the system.

<Rules dos={['Label what the switch controls, in sentence case, such as Weekly digest.', 'Show the chip and the ring together, and only while the setting is unsaved.', 'Let the switch act at once, or mark it changed until the page saves.']} donts={['Never write the label as an action, such as Turn on weekly digest. The thumb already says on or off.', 'Never use a switch for a choice a form confirms later.', 'Never use color alone to say a setting is on. The thumb moves too.']} />

</Section>
```

```ts
/** The gaps, in px, between the thumb and the two ends of the track of the switch row `row`. */
const thumbGaps = (row: Locator): Promise<{ start: number; end: number }> =>
  row.evaluate((element) => {
    const track = element.querySelector('.switch-track')?.getBoundingClientRect();
    const thumb = element.querySelector('.switch-thumb')?.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (!track || !thumb) throw new Error('No switch drawn');
    return { start: thumb.left - track.left, end: track.right - thumb.right };
  });

/** The switch row whose control has this name, on the page that is open. */
const switchNamed = (page: Page, name: string): Locator =>
  page.locator('.switch').filter({ has: page.getByRole('switch', { name, exact: true }) });

test('a switch flips by a press on its label and by Space, and its thumb keeps the same gap at both ends', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });
  await visit(page, '/docs/components/switch');
  const control = page.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Notify me about replies', exact: true });
  const row = switchNamed(page, 'Notify me about replies');
  await expect(control).toBeChecked();
  await expect.poll(async () => (await thumbGaps(row)).end).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);

  await row.click();
  await expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
  await expect.poll(async () => (await thumbGaps(row)).start).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);

  await control.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Space');
  await expect(control).toBeChecked();
  await expect.poll(async () => (await thumbGaps(row)).end).toBeCloseTo(3, 1);
  // The 30px track is drawn inside a row that is hit at 40px.
  expect((await hitSize(row)).height).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(40);
});

test('a disabled switch looks different when it is on and when it is off, and neither looks enabled', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });
  await visit(page, '/docs/components/switch');
  const fill = (name: string): Promise<string> =>
    switchNamed(page, name)
      .locator('.switch-track')
      .evaluate((track) => getComputedStyle(track).backgroundColor);
  const [on, off, disabledOn, disabledOff] = [
    await fill('On'),
    await fill('Off'),
    await fill('Disabled and on'),
    await fill('Disabled and off'),
  ];
  expect(new Set([on, off, disabledOn, disabledOff]).size).toBe(4);
  await expect(page.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Disabled and on', exact: true })).toBeDisabled();
  await expect(switchNamed(page, 'Disabled and off')).toHaveCSS('cursor', 'not-allowed');
  await expect(switchNamed(page, 'Read-only')).toHaveCSS('cursor', 'default');
});

test('the unsaved changes example shows the chip and the ring until the setting is saved or discarded', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });
  await visit(page, '/docs/components/switch');
  const digest = page.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest', exact: true });
  const field = page.locator('.field').filter({ has: digest });
  /** The changed ring around the track, as its width and color. It has no width until the switch is changed. */
  const ring = (): Promise<string> =>
    field.locator('.switch-track').evaluate((track) => {
      const { borderTopWidth, borderTopColor } = getComputedStyle(track, '::before');
      return `${borderTopWidth} ${borderTopColor}`;
    });
  const save = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save changes' });
  const discard = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Discard' });
  await expect(field.locator('.field-changed')).toBeHidden();
  await expect(save).toBeDisabled();
  expect(await ring()).toMatch(/^0px /);

  await switchNamed(page, 'Weekly digest').click();
  await expect(digest).toBeChecked();
  await expect(field.locator('.field-changed')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(digest).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Every Tuesday morning. Changed');
  expect(await ring()).toBe('2px rgb(243, 115, 56)');
  await expect(save).toBeEnabled();

  await discard.click();
  await expect(digest).not.toBeChecked();
  await expect(field.locator('.field-changed')).toBeHidden();

  await switchNamed(page, 'Weekly digest').click();
  await save.click();
  await expect(digest).toBeChecked();
  await expect(field.locator('.field-changed')).toBeHidden();
  await expect(save).toBeDisabled();
});
```

```ts
export function SegmentedControl(props: SegmentedControlProps): ReactElement;
export type SegmentedControlSize = 'md' | 'sm';
export interface SegmentedControlBaseProps extends Omit<RACRadioGroupProps, 'children' | 'className' | 'orientation'> {
  label?: ReactNode;                 // the label row, with the chip; without it give an aria-label
  description?: ReactNode;           // Description under the track
  errorMessage?: ReactNode | ((validation: ValidationResult) => ReactNode); // FieldError children
  isChanged?: boolean;               // data-changed on the root, the chip, the changed edge, the chip announced
  changedLabel?: string;             // default 'Changed'
  size?: SegmentedControlSize;       // default 'md': a 48px track of 40px options; 'sm': 40px track, 32px options hit at 40px
  children?: ReactNode;              // SegmentedControlItem elements
  className?: string | ((values: RadioGroupRenderProps & { defaultClassName: string | undefined }) => string);
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>;         // the root
  // value, defaultValue, onChange, name, isDisabled, isInvalid, isRequired, validate ... come from React Aria
}
// A name is required: a visible label, or an aria-label, or an aria-labelledby.
export type SegmentedControlProps = SegmentedControlBaseProps &
  ({ label: ReactNode } | { label?: undefined; 'aria-label': string } | { label?: undefined; 'aria-labelledby': string });

export function SegmentedControlItem(props: SegmentedControlItemProps): ReactElement;
export interface SegmentedControlItemProps extends Omit<RACRadioFieldProps, 'children' | 'className'> {
  value: string;
  children: ReactNode;               // a word or two
  className?: string | ((values: RadioButtonRenderProps & { defaultClassName: string | undefined }) => string);
  ref?: Ref<HTMLLabelElement>;       // the option: the label a person presses
}
```
