**Decisions made here, recorded in Appendix B (Step 1) and repeated so no later task reopens them:**

- **The stacking rule and how it is measured.** The options are all in one row or all in a column. The track is `width: max-content; min-width: 100%`, so a row that does not fit makes the track wider than its root, and the component compares the track's width with a zero-height marker as wide as the root (`segmented-room`). The marker is what a `ResizeObserver` watches, not the root, because stacking changes the root's height and a size change that an observer's own callback causes in the element it watches raises the browser's "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications" error. A stacked track is a column, so its width says nothing about the row: to learn whether the row fits again the component takes `data-stacked` off the root, reads both widths and puts the answer back, in one callback and before anything is drawn. It does this only when something that can change the answer happened: the marker's width changed, a label changed (a `MutationObserver` on the track), a web font arrived (`document.fonts`, both `loadingdone` and `ready`) or `size` changed. Choosing an option and moving focus change none of them. A row over its room by half a pixel or less still fits (the source's tolerance), and a width that cannot be read (a hidden panel) leaves the arrangement as it is. No hidden copy of the options is rendered, so there is nothing to keep in step with the real ones. The attribute is set by the hook with `toggleAttribute`, not rendered by React, so a stacking decision never costs a render.
- **The room is the root's own width.** The root is a field, so like every field it fills the column it is in, up to `--container-field`. A control inside a parent that sizes its children to their content (a flex row, a centered grid) takes its natural width and has no room to compare with: it never stacks and its row overruns the parent. A control that must stack there needs a width (`flex: 1` in a row, or a `width`). The docs examples therefore sit in a block with a width, like the text field examples do. The docs header's compact controls sit in a row that wraps and never need to stack. The page and Appendix B both say so.
- **`size` is a prop, added because the docs need it.** The docs header and the homepage's Corners switch draw 40px tracks; the real control's 48px track would change the header's height on a phone. `sm` is the stand-in's geometry: a 40px track, 32px options, 14px type, 2px between options, and a `::before` that extends each option's hit area to 40px over the track's 4px of padding and edge. A stacked compact control uses 40px rows (so neighboring hit areas never overlap) and the same 4px gap as the default size.
- **Option height is 40px (source defect 6).** The source's comment says 40px and its rule gives 38, because it left the 1px edge out of the sum. The track is `height: calc(var(--segmented-option-height) + 0.5rem)` with 3px of padding and a 1px edge, so 40px options sit at 4px inside a 48px track, the height of the input beside it. The height is set and not left to add up: the changed and invalid edges are 1.5px, a width the browser may snap to a whole device pixel (it draws 1px on a 1x screen), and a height that depended on it would jump with the state. The options are centered, so the edge is all that changes.
- **Concentric corners in every shape.** The track's corner is the custom property `--segmented-radius` (`--radius-pill`) and an option's is `calc(var(--segmented-radius) - 0.25rem)`: pills in a pill, 8px in Soft's 12px, square in square (a negative result clamps to 0). Stacked, the track takes `--radius-surface` (24px in Rounded) because a pill's corner is half the height and on a column is a blob, and the options sit 4px inside it at 20px, which is the source's own numbers.
- **Focus (source defect 3).** Focus on the chosen option, an ink fill, is an inset ring in `var(--color-canvas)`, 4px inside the pill (`calc(-1 * (var(--focus-ring-width) + var(--focus-ring-offset)))`, as far in as the standard ring sits out). canvas on ink is already in `CONTRAST_PAIRS` as "the inverted focus ring on an ink fill". Every other option takes the standard ring, outside the pill, where it covers the track's edge. The existing per-file guard in `css.test.js` (no ink in an `outline`) allows the canvas inversion.
- **Hover is a 5% ink wash and ink text,** only where hover exists and never on the chosen option (the selected rule is written after it), a disabled option or a touch screen.
- **Disabled (source defect 7) is a look.** The disabled fill on the track, an ink edge at 15%, taupe labels and `not-allowed`. The chosen option stays visible as a taupe pill with the disabled fill as its label color, so a reader can tell which value is set. The ratios (1.44 light, 3.81 dark) are recorded in Appendix B and not gated, since disabled is outside the thresholds.
- **Changed and invalid edges are on the track (source defect 4).** The source's rule looked for the tracked input inside the group, and it was the group's sibling, so the edge never fired. The root carries `data-changed` and (from React Aria) `data-invalid`, and `.segmented-track` draws them. Invalid outranks changed by source order; the chip and `aria-describedby` follow the Task 6 helper, so a changed and invalid control reads its error alone.
- **Item `className` and `ref` go to the option label.** The brief gives the item the class `segmented-option` and the label is where every state lives (`data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`), so a function `className` receives the render props that matter. The wrapper `RadioField` is structural (`segmented-item`) and keeps no user class.
- **The options' selectors are parity selectors.** Each state is written `:is([data-selected], :has(:checked))` and so on, so the file also serves plain HTML: a label with a radio inside it, the way React Aria renders it, with no script. The radio is hidden by React Aria's own inline styles, and `segmented.css` hides one in plain markup the same way.
- **Props.** `orientation` is omitted: the options are always laid out in a row and stack on their own, and the group keeps `aria-orientation="horizontal"`. The arrow keys serve both axes of a radio group, so a stacked control answers Up and Down as well. `isReadOnly` has no look of its own, as in TextField. A control needs a visible `label`, an `aria-label` or an `aria-labelledby`, and the types ask for one. Because the props are a union, Storybook cannot narrow them, so the stories are typed against `SegmentedControlBaseProps`.
- **No transition in the core file.** Core components never animate shape. The docs keep a corner transition of their own for the control, by widening the one docs-only rule Task 6 left (`.input`) to `.input, .segmented-track, .segmented-option`; the global reduced-motion rule in `site.css` stops it.
- **No contrast pair was added.** Slate and ink on Raised, canvas on ink, the boundary and the inverted ring are gated already; the hover wash, the changed edge in light (2.53 to 2.87:1) and the disabled look are recorded in Appendix B.
- **Class names and the docs rail.** `segmented-track` is allowed (see Interfaces). The docs page `segmented-control` sits between `radio-group` and `spinner` in `meta.json`, alphabetical, as the rail order asks.

```markdown

## SegmentedControl

The document specifies no segmented control. Tabs (see "Still missing" in
Appendix A) are the same row of pills with no value, and the source has one
for choosing a value. The library keeps the source's control and changes a few
things, each recorded here.

- **Shape.** The track is a pill with the Raised fill and the boundary edge:
  `--radius-pill`, which the shape table already lists for segmented tracks, so
  it follows the shape axis. The options sit inside it at 4px, and their corner
  is the track's less that 4px, so the two stay concentric in every shape: pills
  in a pill, 8px inside Soft's 12px, square inside square. The source drew the
  track with a fixed 24px corner, which is the pill's corner at this height, so
  Rounded looks the same.
- **The options are 40px tall.** The source's comment says 40px (48 less 4px of
  padding each side) and its rule gives 38, because the 1px edge was left out of
  the sum. The library sets the option to 40px and the track to 48px, the height
  of the input beside it. The track's height is set and not left to add up. The
  firmer 1.5px edge of a changed or invalid control is a width the browser may
  snap to a whole device pixel, so it draws 1px on most screens and 1.5px on a
  2x screen, and a height that depended on it would jump with the state. The
  options stay centered, and the edge is all that changes.
- **The edge** is `--color-boundary`, 1px. The source dropped it to 40%, which
  measures 2.58:1 on white ("Four colors added"). Hover does not touch it.
- **Labels** are the action step (16px, weight 500) in slate. The options are
  sized by their labels, and the room left over is shared out equally. A label
  too long for its option is cut with an ellipsis, a last resort: the control
  stacks before that happens. Labels have a line a little taller than the step,
  so an ellipsis never clips a descender.
- **The chosen option is an ink fill with canvas text**, the shape the rail's
  current link uses. canvas on ink measures 16.25:1 in light and 19.31 in dark,
  and is in the contrast gate already (the primary button's label).
- **Hover is a 5% ink wash** and the label turns ink, only where hover exists
  and never on the chosen option, a disabled one or a touch screen. The wash
  measures 1.11 against the fill in light and 1.16 in dark: a cue, not a
  boundary, and not gated. The label turns ink because the source's did; slate
  would have held 4.96 and 5.84 on the wash.

**Focus on the chosen option is an inset ring in the canvas color.** Focus and
selection move together on a radio group, so the focused option is nearly always
the chosen one, and the source drew an ink ring inside an ink fill, which
measures 1:1. The ring inverts here, as the rail's current link does: canvas on
ink is gated at 3:1 ("the inverted focus ring on an ink fill") and measures
16.25 and 19.31. It sits 4px inside the pill, as far in as the standard ring
sits out. Every other option takes the standard ring, 2px outside the pill,
which lands on the track's own edge and reads as a ring there.

**A control stacks when its row does not fit.** The options are all in one row or
all in a column, never some of each. The component compares the row's natural
width with the room the control has, and a row wider than its room, by more than
half a pixel (the width a row can overrun by and still paint inside), stacks.
Stacked, every option is 40px tall in both sizes, the labels start at the left
and the track takes the surface corner, 24px in Rounded, with the options 4px
inside it at 20px. A pill's corner is half the track's height, which on a column
is a blob. The component sets `data-stacked` on the root and the stylesheet does
the rest.

How the row is measured is the part worth recording, because a naive version
flickers. Two elements are read and nothing is copied. The track is
`width: max-content` and at least as wide as its root, so a row that does not fit
makes the track wider than the root, and no copy of the options is needed to
learn the natural width. The room is a zero-height marker as wide as the root.
It is the marker that a `ResizeObserver` watches, not the root, because stacking
changes the root's height, and a size change that an observer's own callback
causes in the element it watches raises the browser's "loop completed with
undelivered notifications" error. A stacked track is a column, so its width says
nothing about the row; to find out whether the row fits again, the component
takes `data-stacked` off, reads both widths, and puts the answer back, which is
one layout inside the observer's callback and never paints the in-between state.
It looks again only when something that can change the answer happened: the room
changed, a label changed (a `MutationObserver` on the track), a web font arrived
(the row measured in a fallback face is the wrong width), or `size` changed.
Choosing an option, hovering and moving focus change none of them. Where a width
cannot be read, as in a hidden panel, the arrangement stays as it is. The source
measured with off-screen copies of the labels; reading the real track needs no
copy and cannot disagree with it.

**The room is the root's own width.** The root is a field, so like every field
it fills the column it is in, up to `--container-field`. A control placed in a
parent that sizes its children to their content, a flex row or a centered grid,
takes its natural width and has no room to compare with, so it never stacks and
its row overruns the parent instead. A control that must stack there needs a
width (`flex: 1` in a row, or a `width` in a grid). The source measured the room
beside the control's neighbors, which is more than a field's column asks for.
The compact controls in the docs header never need it: they sit in a row that
wraps.

**The compact size, `sm`,** is for a toolbar or a header, where the 48px track
is too tall. It draws the track at 40px and the options at 32px, 14px type, with
2px between them, and each option is still hit at 40px: a pseudo-element
reaches over the 4px of padding and edge, which is all there is between the
control and what is next to it, so nothing shifts. It is a size prop and not a
docs-only rule because the docs header and the homepage's Corners switch both use
it. A stacked compact control uses 40px rows, so the hit areas of neighboring
rows never overlap.

**Disabled had no look in the source.** A disabled control is recessed, as every
field is: the disabled fill, an ink edge at 15%, and taupe labels, with the
not-allowed cursor. The chosen option keeps its place as a taupe pill with the
disabled fill for its label, so a reader can still tell which value is set; in
the source's switch a disabled control was the same whether on or off.
Disabled is outside the 3:1 asked of a boundary and the 4.5:1 asked of text:

| Disabled | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Taupe label on the disabled fill | 1.44 | 3.81 |
| Chosen pill on the disabled fill, and its label on the pill | 1.44 | 3.81 |
| Edge, ink at 15%, on the disabled fill | 1.37 | 1.59 |

**Changed and invalid are edges on the track, keyed on the field's root.** The
source's rule looked for the tracked input inside the segmented group, and the
input was the group's sibling, so the track never drew its orange edge and only
the chip showed. The root carries `data-changed` and, from React Aria,
`data-invalid`, and the track draws the edge for them, as an input does: light
signal orange for changed, the error color for invalid, both 1.5px, and the
invalid rule comes after the changed one so a control that is both shows the
error edge. The chip leaves while the control is invalid by any cause and is read
with the control while it is changed, through the same label-row helper as
TextField.

| Edge | Lowest on the five surfaces, light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Boundary, over the Raised fill | 3.06 | 4.93 |
| Error (invalid) | 6.58 | 5.06 |
| Light Signal Orange (changed) | 2.53 | 5.35 |

The boundary and the label colors are gated already (slate on Raised measures
5.49 and 6.44). Light Signal Orange is under the 3:1 a boundary asks on every
light surface, the document's own choice of attention cue, recorded and not
gated, and never alone: the clay chip carries the word.

**The options are always laid out in a row.** React Aria's `orientation` is not
a prop here. The arrow keys serve both axes of a radio group, so a stacked
control answers Up and Down as well as Left and Right, and the group stays
`aria-orientation="horizontal"` for the one arrangement it was drawn in. A
control needs a visible label or an `aria-label`, and the types ask for one.
Nothing animates, so there is no reduced-motion block; the docs site keeps its
own corner transition.

No pairing was added to the contrast gate: every color the control draws is
gated already (slate and ink on Raised, canvas on ink, the boundary, the
inverted ring, error) or recorded above (the hover wash, Light Signal Orange in
light, the disabled look).
```

The numbers come from `paletteFor` and `contrastRatio` in `packages/core/scripts/contrast.js`. Slate is measured over the Raised fill, the translucent dark values are composited over the surface they sit on, the hover wash is ink at 5% over Raised, and the edges are measured against the surface each sits on. The 40px, 48px, 4px and 1.5px figures are the geometry in `segmented.css`.

```js
describe('src/components/segmented.css', () => {
  // The rules without their comments, which quote selectors of their own.
  const rules = () => read('src/components/segmented.css').replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '');
  const SELECTED = ':is([data-selected], :has(:checked))';
  const FOCUSED = ':is([data-focus-visible], :has(:focus-visible))';

  it('declares the invalid edge after the changed one, and both after the disabled one', () => {
    const source = rules();
    const disabled = source.indexOf('.segmented[data-disabled] .segmented-track');
    const changed = source.indexOf('.segmented[data-changed] .segmented-track');
    const invalid = source.indexOf('.segmented[data-invalid] .segmented-track');
    expect(disabled).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(changed).toBeGreaterThan(disabled);
    expect(invalid).toBeGreaterThan(changed);
  });

  it('sets the track height to 40px of option and 4px each side, so a firmer edge moves nothing', () => {
    const source = rules();
    const track = blockAfter(source, '.segmented-track {');
    expect(track).toContain('--segmented-option-height: 2.5rem;');
    expect(track).toContain('height: calc(var(--segmented-option-height) + 0.5rem);');
    expect(track).toContain('border: 1px solid var(--color-boundary);');
    // The firmer edge is a width only: the track's height never reads it.
    for (const state of ['changed', 'invalid']) {
      const edge = blockAfter(source, `.segmented[data-${state}] .segmented-track`);
      expect(edge).toContain('border-width: 1.5px;');
      expect(edge).not.toContain('height');
    }
    // Stacked, the track is as tall as its rows.
    expect(blockAfter(source, '.segmented[data-stacked] .segmented-track')).toContain('height: auto;');
  });

  it('turns every option to 40px when it stacks, in both sizes', () => {
    const source = rules();
    const stacked = blockAfter(source, '.segmented[data-stacked] .segmented-track');
    expect(stacked).toContain('--segmented-option-height: 2.5rem;');
    // A pill's corner is half the height, which on a column is a blob, so a stacked track takes the surface step.
    expect(stacked).toContain('--segmented-radius: var(--radius-surface);');
    expect(blockAfter(source, '.segmented-sm .segmented-track')).toContain(
      '--segmented-option-height: 2rem;',
    );
    // The compact option reaches its 40px hit area only while it sits in a row.
    expect(source).toContain('.segmented-sm:not([data-stacked]) .segmented-option::before');
  });

  it('fills the selected option with ink and inverts its focus ring to the canvas color', () => {
    const source = rules();
    expect(blockAfter(source, `.segmented-option${SELECTED} {`)).toContain(
      'background-color: var(--color-ink);',
    );
    const ring = blockAfter(source, `.segmented-option${SELECTED}${FOCUSED} {`);
    expect(ring).toContain('outline-color: var(--color-canvas);');
    expect(ring).toMatch(/outline-offset: calc\(-1 \* /);
    // The standard ring, for every other option, is the token ring outside the pill.
    const standard = blockAfter(source, `.segmented-option${FOCUSED} {`);
    expect(standard).toContain('outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color);');
    expect(standard).toContain('outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);');
  });

  it('draws hover only where hover exists, and before the selected fill so selection wins', () => {
    const source = rules();
    const media = source.indexOf('@media (hover: hover)');
    expect(media).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(source.indexOf(':hover')).toBeGreaterThan(media);
    expect(source.indexOf(`.segmented-option${SELECTED} {`)).toBeGreaterThan(media);
  });
});
```

Then the React tests. `useStacking.test.ts` checks the pure decision, `stacksOptions`: the half-pixel tolerance and the rule that an unknown width keeps the current arrangement. `SegmentedControlItem.test.tsx` covers the option on its own: its parts, a disabled option the arrow keys skip, the ref, and both forms of `className`. `SegmentedControl.test.tsx` covers the control end to end: the field contract and part order, a name from `aria-label`, the type check that asks for a name (`@ts-expect-error`), the default value, a press, the arrow keys (all four, wrapping, one tab stop, and Tab landing on the first option while nothing is chosen), controlled and uncontrolled values (`null` is a controlled control with nothing chosen), `FormData` and a form reset, disabled, the chip shown, announced, renamed and merged with the caller's `aria-describedby`, invalid outranking changed (by prop and through React Aria's own validation after a failed submit), `size`, a `data-*` attribute, the ref, both forms of `className`, and axe in ten states.

Its second `describe` is the stacking tests. jsdom has no layout and no `ResizeObserver`, so they supply both. `getBoundingClientRect` answers the way a browser would: the marker is as wide as the room, and the track is as wide as the row (or the room, if wider) until the root carries `data-stacked`, and then as wide as the column. That is what makes the unstack test mean something: it fails if the hook measures a stacked track. A fake `ResizeObserver` stays still until the test calls `resized()`. The tests cover: one row where the row fits; stacking before anything is drawn; stacking and unstacking as the room changes (room 300, row 400, column 120: 350 is still too little, 420 is enough, 280 stacks again); the half-pixel tolerance; an unmeasurable room keeping the arrangement; the observer watching the marker and not the root and disconnecting on unmount; a label change, a `size` change and a font arriving each making it look again; stacking once on mount without `ResizeObserver`; one row where nothing can be measured; and axe while stacked.

`packages/react/src/segmented-control/useStacking.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { stacksOptions } from './useStacking';

describe('stacksOptions', () => {
  it('keeps one row while the row fits, and stacks when it does not', () => {
    expect(stacksOptions(200, 300)).toBe(false);
    expect(stacksOptions(300, 300)).toBe(false);
    expect(stacksOptions(400, 300)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('allows a row half a pixel over its room, which still paints inside it', () => {
    expect(stacksOptions(300.5, 300)).toBe(false);
    expect(stacksOptions(300.6, 300)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('keeps the current arrangement when either width is unknown', () => {
    expect(stacksOptions(0, 300, true)).toBe(true);
    expect(stacksOptions(400, 0, true)).toBe(true);
    expect(stacksOptions(0, 300, false)).toBe(false);
    expect(stacksOptions(400, 0, false)).toBe(false);
    expect(stacksOptions(Number.NaN, 300, true)).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef } from 'react';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { SegmentedControl } from './SegmentedControl';
import { SegmentedControlItem } from './SegmentedControlItem';

describe('SegmentedControlItem', () => {
  it('is a radio inside a wrapper, drawn by a label with the option class', () => {
    render(
      <SegmentedControl aria-label="Theme" defaultValue="dark">
        <SegmentedControlItem value="light">Light</SegmentedControlItem>
        <SegmentedControlItem value="dark">Dark</SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>,
    );
    const dark = screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' });
    const option = dark.closest('label');
    expect(option).toHaveClass('segmented-option');
    expect(option).toHaveAttribute('data-selected');
    expect(option?.parentElement).toHaveClass('segmented-item');
    expect(option?.parentElement?.parentElement).toHaveClass('segmented-track');
    expect(screen.getByText('Dark')).toHaveClass('segmented-label');
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Light' }).closest('label')).not.toHaveAttribute(
      'data-selected',
    );
  });

  it('keeps an option that cannot be chosen out of the keys and the form', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn<(value: string) => void>();
    render(
      <SegmentedControl aria-label="Plan" defaultValue="free" onChange={onChange}>
        <SegmentedControlItem value="free">Free</SegmentedControlItem>
        <SegmentedControlItem value="team" isDisabled>
          Team
        </SegmentedControlItem>
        <SegmentedControlItem value="business">Business</SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>,
    );
    const team = screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Team' });
    expect(team).toBeDisabled();
    expect(team.closest('label')).toHaveAttribute('data-disabled');
    await user.tab();
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Business' })).toBeChecked();
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('business');
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Team'));
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Business' })).toBeChecked();
  });

  it('forwards ref to the option label', () => {
    const ref = createRef<HTMLLabelElement>();
    render(
      <SegmentedControl aria-label="Theme">
        <SegmentedControlItem ref={ref} value="light">
          Light
        </SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>,
    );
    expect(ref.current).toBeInstanceOf(HTMLLabelElement);
    expect(ref.current).toHaveClass('segmented-option');
  });

  it('merges a string className after the option class', () => {
    render(
      <SegmentedControl aria-label="Theme">
        <SegmentedControlItem value="light" className="extra">
          Light
        </SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio').closest('label')).toHaveClass('segmented-option', 'extra');
  });

  it('merges a function className, which receives the option state', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const className = vi.fn(
      ({ isSelected }: { isSelected: boolean; defaultClassName: string | undefined }) =>
        isSelected ? 'is-on' : 'is-off',
    );
    render(
      <SegmentedControl aria-label="Theme" defaultValue="light">
        <SegmentedControlItem value="light" className={className}>
          Light
        </SegmentedControlItem>
        <SegmentedControlItem value="dark" className={className}>
          Dark
        </SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>,
    );
    const light = screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Light' }).closest('label');
    const dark = screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' }).closest('label');
    expect(light).toHaveClass('segmented-option', 'is-on');
    expect(dark).toHaveClass('segmented-option', 'is-off');
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Dark'));
    expect(light).toHaveClass('is-off');
    expect(dark).toHaveClass('is-on');
    expect(className.mock.calls[0]?.[0].defaultClassName).toBe('react-aria-RadioButton');
  });
});
```

`packages/react/src/segmented-control/SegmentedControl.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { act, render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createRef, useState, type ReactElement } from 'react';
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { SegmentedControl, type SegmentedControlProps } from './SegmentedControl';
import { SegmentedControlItem } from './SegmentedControlItem';

/** The three options most tests use. `props` supplies the label and anything else. */
function Theme(props: SegmentedControlProps): ReactElement {
  return (
    <SegmentedControl {...props}>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="light">Light</SegmentedControlItem>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="dark">Dark</SegmentedControlItem>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="system">System</SegmentedControlItem>
    </SegmentedControl>
  );
}

/** A control the caller controls, the way a form library would. */
function Controlled(props: SegmentedControlProps): ReactElement {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('light');
  return <Theme {...props} value={value} onChange={setValue} />;
}

const root = (container: HTMLElement): Element => {
  const element = container.firstElementChild;
  if (!element) throw new Error('Nothing rendered');
  return element;
};

const checked = (): string[] =>
  screen
    .getAllByRole('radio')
    .filter((radio) => (radio as HTMLInputElement).checked)
    .map((radio) => radio.closest('label')?.textContent ?? '');

describe('SegmentedControl', () => {
  it('is a labelled radio group of options, inside a field', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Theme label="Color mode" description="Follows your system by default." />);
    const group = screen.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Color mode' });
    expect(group).toBe(root(container));
    expect(group).toHaveClass('field', 'segmented');
    expect(group).not.toHaveClass('segmented-sm');
    expect(group).not.toHaveAttribute('data-changed');
    expect(group).not.toHaveAttribute('data-invalid');
    expect(group).toHaveAttribute('aria-orientation', 'horizontal');
    expect(group).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Follows your system by default.');
    expect(screen.getByText('Color mode')).toHaveClass('field-label');
    expect(screen.getByText('Follows your system by default.')).toHaveClass('field-description');
    expect(screen.getAllByRole('radio')).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('.segmented-track > .segmented-item')).toHaveLength(3);
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('puts its parts in the order the field contract asks for', () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Theme label="Color mode" description="One choice." isInvalid errorMessage="Choose one." />,
    );
    // The last child is the marker the control watches to learn how much room it has.
    expect([...root(container).children].map((child) => child.classList[0])).toEqual([
      'field-head',
      'segmented-track',
      'field-description',
      'field-error',
      'segmented-room',
    ]);
  });

  it('is named by aria-label when it has no visible label, and then has no label row', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Theme aria-label="Corners" />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Corners' })).toBe(root(container));
    expect(container.querySelector('.field-head')).toBeNull();
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });

  it('asks the types for a visible label or an aria-label', () => {
    const forgotten = (): ReactElement => (
      // @ts-expect-error A control with neither a label nor an aria-label has no name.
      <SegmentedControl>
        <SegmentedControlItem value="a">A</SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>
    );
    const byLabelledby = (): ReactElement => (
      <SegmentedControl aria-labelledby="heading">
        <SegmentedControlItem value="a">A</SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>
    );
    expect(forgotten).toBeTypeOf('function');
    expect(byLabelledby).toBeTypeOf('function');
  });

  it('selects the default value and leaves the rest', () => {
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" defaultValue="dark" />);
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Dark']);
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' }).closest('label')).toHaveAttribute('data-selected');
  });

  it('selects nothing until it is told to, and then moves with a press', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn<(value: string) => void>();
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" onChange={onChange} />);
    expect(checked()).toEqual([]);
    await user.click(screen.getByText('System'));
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['System']);
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Light'));
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Light']);
    expect(onChange.mock.calls.map(([value]) => value)).toEqual(['system', 'light']);
  });

  it('moves the selection with the arrow keys, and Tab lands on the selected option', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn<(value: string) => void>();
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" defaultValue="light" onChange={onChange} />);
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Light' })).toHaveFocus();
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' })).toHaveFocus();
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Dark']);
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowRight}{ArrowRight}');
    // Past the last option the selection wraps to the first.
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Light']);
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['System']);
    // The same keys serve a stacked column, where the options are one above the next.
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowUp}');
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Dark']);
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowDown}');
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['System']);
    expect(onChange.mock.calls.map(([value]) => value)).toEqual([
      'dark',
      'system',
      'light',
      'system',
      'dark',
      'system',
    ]);
    // One tab stop for the whole group.
    await user.tab();
    expect(document.body).toHaveFocus();
  });

  it('lets Tab land on the first option while nothing is selected, and an arrow key choose the next', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Light' })).toHaveFocus();
    await user.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Dark']);
  });

  it('follows the value of a controlled control, and tells the caller what was chosen', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onChange = vi.fn<(value: string) => void>();
    const { rerender } = render(<Theme label="Color mode" value="light" onChange={onChange} />);
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Dark'));
    expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('dark');
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Light']);
    rerender(<Theme label="Color mode" value="system" onChange={onChange} />);
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['System']);
    // null is a controlled control with nothing selected.
    rerender(<Theme label="Color mode" value={null} onChange={onChange} />);
    expect(checked()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('works with a state the caller keeps', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(<Controlled label="Color mode" />);
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Light']);
    await user.click(screen.getByText('Dark'));
    expect(checked()).toEqual(['Dark']);
  });

  it('submits the chosen value in a plain form under its name', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(
      <form>
        <Theme label="Color mode" name="theme" />
      </form>,
    );
    const form = container.querySelector('form');
    if (!form) throw new Error('No form');
    expect(new FormData(form).has('theme')).toBe(false);

    const { container } = render(<Theme {...props} />);
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);

describe('SegmentedControl stacking', () => {
  /** The widths the layout would give, which jsdom has none of. */
  const layout = { room: 300, row: 400, column: 120 };

  /**
   * Answers getBoundingClientRect the way a browser would. The marker is as wide as the room. The track
   * is as wide as the row, or as the room if that is wider, until the root says it is stacked: then
   * it is the column's width. So a test that measured the stacked track would read the wrong width.
   */
  function mockLayout(): void {
    vi.spyOn(Element.prototype, 'getBoundingClientRect').mockImplementation(function (this: Element) {
      let width = 0;
      if (this.classList.contains('segmented-room')) width = layout.room;
      else if (this.classList.contains('segmented-track')) {
        width = this.closest('.segmented')?.hasAttribute('data-stacked')
          ? layout.column
          : Math.max(layout.row, layout.room);
      }
      return new DOMRect(0, 0, width, 0);
    });
  }

  /** A ResizeObserver that stays still until the test says the size changed. */
  class FakeResizeObserver {
    static all: FakeResizeObserver[] = [];
    observed: Element[] = [];
    disconnected = false;
    constructor(private readonly callback: () => void) {
      FakeResizeObserver.all.push(this);
    }
    observe(target: Element): void {
      this.observed.push(target);
    }
    unobserve(): void {
      // Nothing is ever unobserved: a control watches one marker for as long as it lives.
    }
    disconnect(): void {
      this.disconnected = true;
    }
    fire(): void {
      this.callback();
    }
  }

  const resized = (): void => {
    act(() => {
      for (const observer of FakeResizeObserver.all) observer.fire();
    });
  };

  const stacked = (): boolean => screen.getByRole('radiogroup').hasAttribute('data-stacked');

  const setup = (): void => {
    layout.room = 300;
    layout.row = 400;
    layout.column = 120;
    FakeResizeObserver.all = [];
    vi.stubGlobal('ResizeObserver', FakeResizeObserver);
    mockLayout();
  };

  afterEach(() => {
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
    Reflect.deleteProperty(document, 'fonts');
  });

  it('stays in one row where the row fits its room', () => {
    setup();
    layout.row = 250;
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
  });

  it('stacks, before anything is drawn, where the row does not fit its room', () => {
    setup();
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    expect(screen.getByRole('radiogroup')).toHaveAttribute('data-stacked', '');
  });

  it('stacks and unstacks as the room changes, measuring the row as a row each time', () => {
    setup();
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    // Room for the row again. The stacked track is 120px wide, which would fit any room,
    // so only a measurement taken in a row can tell that 350px is still too little.
    layout.room = 350;
    resized();
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    layout.room = 420;
    resized();
    expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
    layout.room = 280;
    resized();
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('allows a row half a pixel over its room', () => {
    setup();
    layout.row = 300.5;
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
    layout.row = 300.6;
    resized();
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('keeps its arrangement while it cannot be measured, as when it is hidden', () => {
    setup();
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    layout.room = 0;
    resized();
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    layout.room = 500;
    resized();
    expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
    layout.room = 0;
    resized();
    expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
  });

  it('watches the room marker and not the root, and lets go when it unmounts', () => {
    setup();
    const { unmount } = render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(FakeResizeObserver.all).toHaveLength(1);
    const [observer] = FakeResizeObserver.all;
    expect(observer?.observed).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(observer?.observed[0]).toHaveClass('segmented-room');
    expect(observer?.observed[0]).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    expect(observer?.disconnected).toBe(false);
    unmount();
    expect(observer?.disconnected).toBe(true);
  });

  it('looks again when a label changes', async () => {
    setup();
    const Words = ({ words }: { words: string[] }): ReactElement => (
      <SegmentedControl label="Color mode">
        {words.map((word) => (
          <SegmentedControlItem key={word} value={word}>
            {word}
          </SegmentedControlItem>
        ))}
      </SegmentedControl>
    );
    const { rerender } = render(<Words words={['Light', 'Dark', 'System']} />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    layout.row = 250;
    // Same labels, same row: nothing to look at.
    rerender(<Words words={['Light', 'Dark', 'System']} />);
    await act(async () => {
      await Promise.resolve();
    });
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    rerender(<Words words={['Day', 'Night', 'Auto']} />);
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  it('looks again when the size changes, since the row is a different width', () => {
    setup();
    const { rerender } = render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    layout.row = 250;
    rerender(<Theme label="Color mode" size="sm" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
  });

  it('looks again when a web font arrives, which changes the width of every label', async () => {
    setup();
    const listeners = new Map<string, () => void>();
    Object.defineProperty(document, 'fonts', {
      configurable: true,
      value: {
        ready: Promise.resolve(),
        addEventListener: (type: string, listener: () => void) => listeners.set(type, listener),
        removeEventListener: (type: string) => listeners.delete(type),
      },
    });
    const { unmount } = render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    layout.row = 250;
    act(() => {
      listeners.get('loadingdone')?.();
    });
    expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
    layout.row = 400;
    await act(async () => {
      await Promise.resolve();
    });
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    unmount();
    expect(listeners.size).toBe(0);
  });

  it('stacks once on mount even where ResizeObserver does not exist', () => {
    setup();
    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('keeps one row in an environment that cannot measure anything', () => {
    render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(false);
  });

  it('has no axe violations while stacked', async () => {
    setup();
    const { container } = render(<Theme label="Color mode" />);
    expect(stacked()).toBe(true);
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });
});
```

```css
/*
 * The segmented control, derived in docs/design-system.md
 * ("SegmentedControl"): a field whose control is a pill track holding a few
 * short options, one of them filled with ink.
 *
 * The root is a field (field.css), so it carries data-changed and
 * data-invalid, and the track draws the edge for them. React Aria draws the
 * options as radios: .segmented-item is the wrapper React Aria adds, and
 * .segmented-option is the label a person sees and presses.
 *
 * Stacking: the row of options is all or nothing. A control whose row does
 * not fit its room stacks one option per row, and the React component sets
 * data-stacked on the root to say so. Nothing here wraps an option onto a
 * second row of its own.
 */
@layer components {
  /* Positioned, so the room marker below can sit in it without taking a grid row. */
  .segmented {
    position: relative;
  }

  /*
   * A zero-height marker as wide as the root. The React component watches it
   * to learn how much room the control has. It is watched instead of the root
   * because stacking changes the root's height, and a size change that an
   * observer's own callback causes in the element it watches is what raises
   * the browser's "loop completed with undelivered notifications" error.
   */
  .segmented-room {
    position: absolute;
    inset-block-start: 0;
    inset-inline: 0;
    height: 0;
    visibility: hidden;
    pointer-events: none;
  }

  /*
   * A row of 40px options is 48px tall, the height of the field's input: 40px
   * of option and 4px each side, which is 3px of padding and the 1px edge.
   * The height is set, not left to add up, because the firmer 1.5px edge a
   * changed or invalid control draws is a width the browser may snap to a whole
   * device pixel, and a height that depended on it would jump with the state.
   * The options stay centered, so the edge changes and nothing else moves.
   *
   * Its width is its natural one-row width, and at least the room it has. A
   * row that does not fit therefore makes the track wider than its root, and
   * that is how the component sees it: it compares the track with the room.
   */
  .segmented-track {
    --segmented-option-height: 2.5rem;
    --segmented-radius: var(--radius-pill);

    box-sizing: border-box;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 0.25rem;
    width: max-content;
    min-width: 100%;
    height: calc(var(--segmented-option-height) + 0.5rem);
    padding: 0.1875rem;
    border: 1px solid var(--color-boundary);
    border-radius: var(--segmented-radius);
    background-color: var(--color-raised);
  }

  /* The wrapper React Aria puts around each radio. It grows with the room left over. */
  .segmented-item {
    display: flex;
    flex: 1 0 auto;
    min-width: 0;
  }

  .segmented-option {
    position: relative;
    box-sizing: border-box;
    display: flex;
    flex: 1 1 auto;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: center;
    min-width: 0;
    height: var(--segmented-option-height);
    margin: 0;
    padding-inline: 1rem;
    border-radius: calc(var(--segmented-radius) - 0.25rem);
    background-color: transparent;
    color: var(--color-slate);
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: var(--text-action);
    line-height: var(--text-action--line-height);
    letter-spacing: var(--text-action--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-action--font-weight);
    cursor: pointer;
    user-select: none;
    -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
  }

  /* A little taller than the line, so a descender is never clipped by the ellipsis. */
  .segmented-label {
    min-width: 0;
    overflow: hidden;
    text-overflow: ellipsis;
    white-space: nowrap;
    line-height: 1.25;
  }

  /* The radio stays in the accessibility tree and the tab order. React Aria hides it the same way. */
  .segmented-option input {
    position: absolute;
    width: 1px;
    height: 1px;
    margin: -1px;
    padding: 0;
    overflow: hidden;
    border: 0;
    clip-path: inset(50%);
    white-space: nowrap;
  }

  @media (hover: hover) {
    .segmented-option:is(:hover, [data-hovered]) {
      background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 5%, transparent);
      color: var(--color-ink);
    }
  }

  /* After hover, so a selected option keeps its fill and its canvas text under the pointer. */
  .segmented-option:is([data-selected], :has(:checked)) {
    background-color: var(--color-ink);
    color: var(--color-canvas);
  }

  /* An option, or the whole control, that cannot be chosen. Hover shows nothing here. */
  .segmented-option:is([data-disabled], :has(:disabled)) {
    background-color: transparent;
    color: var(--color-taupe);
    cursor: not-allowed;
  }

  /* A disabled option that is selected keeps its place in the row: a taupe pill with the track's own fill for text. */
  .segmented-option:is([data-selected], :has(:checked)):is([data-disabled], :has(:disabled)) {
    background-color: var(--color-taupe);
    color: var(--color-disabled);
  }

  .segmented-option:is([data-focus-visible], :has(:focus-visible)) {
    outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color);
    outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);
  }

  /*
   * The ring inverts on an ink fill, and only there: an ink ring drawn inside
   * an ink pill measures 1:1, and focus and selection move together on a radio
   * group, so the focused option is nearly always the selected one. The ring
   * stays inside the pill, as far in as the standard ring sits out.
   */
  .segmented-option:is([data-selected], :has(:checked)):is([data-focus-visible], :has(:focus-visible)) {
    outline-color: var(--color-canvas);
    outline-offset: calc(-1 * (var(--focus-ring-width) + var(--focus-ring-offset)));
  }

  /*
   * The compact size is drawn at 32px and hit at 40px: the pseudo-element
   * reaches over the track's 4px of padding and edge, which is all there is
   * between one control and the next, so nothing shifts.
   */
  .segmented-sm .segmented-track {
    --segmented-option-height: 2rem;

    gap: 0.125rem;
  }

  .segmented-sm .segmented-option {
    padding-inline: 0.875rem;
    font-size: var(--text-small);
  }

  .segmented-sm:not([data-stacked]) .segmented-option::before {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    inset-block: -0.25rem;
    inset-inline: 0;
  }

  /*
   * Stacked: the same track and the same pills, turned to a column. Every
   * option is 40px, whatever the size, so the rows are real targets that do
   * not overlap. Labels start at the left, as a list's options do, because a
   * column is read down its left edge. The track takes the surface corner
   * instead of the pill's: a pill's corner is half the height, which on a
   * column is a blob, and the surface step is the 24px the row had, with the
   * options 4px inside it at 20px.
   */
  .segmented[data-stacked] .segmented-track {
    --segmented-option-height: 2.5rem;
    --segmented-radius: var(--radius-surface);

    flex-direction: column;
    align-items: stretch;
    gap: 0.25rem;
    width: auto;
    height: auto;
  }

  .segmented[data-stacked] .segmented-item {
    flex: none;
  }

  .segmented[data-stacked] .segmented-option {
    justify-content: flex-start;
  }

  /*
   * The track's edge, keyed on the field's root as the field contract in
   * field.css says. A disabled control is recessed. A changed one firms to
   * light signal orange and an invalid one to the error color; both come
   * after the disabled rule, so the chip and the edge always show together,
   * and invalid comes last, so it outranks changed.
   */
  .segmented[data-disabled] .segmented-track {
    border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 15%, transparent);
    background-color: var(--color-disabled);
  }

  .segmented[data-changed] .segmented-track {
    border-width: 1.5px;
    border-color: var(--color-signal-light);
  }

  .segmented[data-invalid] .segmented-track {
    border-width: 1.5px;
    border-color: var(--color-error);
  }
}
```

Source order carries the states, so keep it: hover, then the chosen fill (which comes after, so selection wins under the pointer), then disabled, then the selected-and-disabled pill (three selectors' worth), then the rings. Hover is inside `@media (hover: hover)`. `:is([data-selected], :has(:checked))` counts as one attribute for specificity, which is why a later rule of the same weight wins. The disabled, changed and invalid track rules are at the end and in that order, so the chip and the edge always show together and invalid wins.

`packages/react/src/segmented-control/useStacking.ts` (no `'use client'`: it imports nothing from React Aria). The decision is a pure function so it can be tested alone; the hook reads two widths and sets one attribute. Read its comment: it is the explanation Appendix B summarizes.

```ts
import { useLayoutEffect, type RefObject } from 'react';

/** The attribute the root carries while the options are stacked, one per row. */
const STACKED = 'data-stacked';

/** Half a pixel: how far a row may run over its room and still paint inside it. */
const ROW_SLACK = 0.5;

/**
 * Whether a row of options `rowWidth` wide has to stack to fit `room`. A width
 * that is not known (an element that is not drawn, as when it is hidden) keeps
 * the arrangement the control has.
 */
export function stacksOptions(rowWidth: number, room: number, stacked = false): boolean {
  if (!(rowWidth > 0) || !(room > 0)) return stacked;
  return rowWidth > room + ROW_SLACK;
}

/**
 * Sets `data-stacked` on the control's root while its row of options does not
 * fit the room it has, and takes it off when the row fits again. The options
 * are all in one row or all in a column, never some of each.
 *
 * Two elements are read and nothing is copied. The room marker is a
 * zero-height element as wide as the root. The track is as wide as the row,
 * and at least as wide as the room (see segmented.css), so a track wider than
 * the marker is a row that does not fit. While the options are stacked the
 * track is a column, so the row is measured by taking the attribute off, which
 * lays the options out as a row, reading both widths, and putting the answer
 * back, all inside one frame before anything is drawn.
 *
 * That is done only when something that can change the answer happened: the
 * room changed (a ResizeObserver on the marker, not on the root, whose height
 * stacking changes, which would raise the browser's loop error), a label
 * changed, a font arrived, or the size changed. Selecting an option and moving
 * focus change none of them.
 *
 * Internal: not exported from the package.
 */
export function useStacking(
  roomRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>,
  trackRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>,
  size: string,
): void {
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const room = roomRef.current;
    const track = trackRef.current;
    // The marker is the root's own child, so the root is where the attribute goes.
    const root = room?.parentElement;
    if (!room || !track || !root) return;

    let live = true;
    const arrange = (): void => {
      if (!live) return;
      const wasStacked = root.hasAttribute(STACKED);
      // Ask the layout whether the row fits by laying the options out as a row.
      if (wasStacked) root.removeAttribute(STACKED);
      const next = stacksOptions(
        track.getBoundingClientRect().width,
        room.getBoundingClientRect().width,
        wasStacked,
      );
      root.toggleAttribute(STACKED, next);
    };
    arrange();

    const resize = 'ResizeObserver' in globalThis ? new ResizeObserver(arrange) : undefined;
    resize?.observe(room);
    const text = new MutationObserver(arrange);
    text.observe(track, { childList: true, characterData: true, subtree: true });
    // Not defined everywhere (a DOM emulator has none), and a row measured in a
    // fallback face is the wrong width once the real one arrives.
    const fonts = document.fonts as FontFaceSet | undefined;
    fonts?.addEventListener('loadingdone', arrange);
    void fonts?.ready.then(arrange);

    return () => {
      live = false;
      resize?.disconnect();
      text.disconnect();
      fonts?.removeEventListener('loadingdone', arrange);
    };
  }, [roomRef, trackRef, size]);
}
```

`packages/react/src/segmented-control/SegmentedControlItem.tsx`. `RadioField` is the wrapper and gets only the structural class; the label, `RadioButton`, carries the option class, the user's `className` and the ref. `value` is redeclared so the props table can document it.

```tsx
'use client';

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react';
import {
  RadioButton,
  RadioField,
  type RadioButtonRenderProps,
  type RadioFieldProps as RACRadioFieldProps,
  composeRenderProps,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export interface SegmentedControlItemProps extends Omit<RACRadioFieldProps, 'children' | 'className'> {
  /** The value the control takes while this option is selected. It is also what a form submits. */
  value: string;
  /** What the option shows: a word or two. */
  children: ReactNode;
  /** A class name, or a function of the option's state, merged after the library's own class. */
  className?:
    string | ((values: RadioButtonRenderProps & { defaultClassName: string | undefined }) => string);
  /** A ref to the option, the label a person presses. */
  ref?: Ref<HTMLLabelElement>;
}

/**
 * One option of a segmented control, a radio drawn as a pill. Built on React
 * Aria's RadioField and RadioButton, so it must sit inside a SegmentedControl.
 */
export function SegmentedControlItem({
  children,
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: SegmentedControlItemProps): ReactElement {
  return (
    <RadioField {...props} className="segmented-item">
      <RadioButton
        ref={ref}
        className={composeRenderProps(className, (userClassName) => cx('segmented-option', userClassName))}
      >
        <span className="segmented-label">{children}</span>
      </RadioButton>
    </RadioField>
  );
}
```

`packages/react/src/segmented-control/SegmentedControl.tsx`. The root is React Aria's `RadioGroup`, with `orientation` fixed. The label row, the chip and `aria-describedby` are Task 6's helper, used the way TextField uses it. The room marker is the last child, so the parts keep the order the field contract asks for. The label union is what makes one of `label`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` required.

```tsx
'use client';

import { useRef, type ReactElement, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react';
import {
  RadioGroup as RACRadioGroup,
  type RadioGroupProps as RACRadioGroupProps,
  type RadioGroupRenderProps,
  type ValidationResult,
  composeRenderProps,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import { Description } from '../field/Description';
import { FieldError } from '../field/FieldError';
import { FieldHead } from '../field/FieldHead';
import { useChangedDescription } from '../field/useChangedDescription';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';
import { useStacking } from './useStacking';

export type SegmentedControlSize = 'md' | 'sm';

export interface SegmentedControlBaseProps extends Omit<
  RACRadioGroupProps,
  'children' | 'className' | 'orientation'
> {
  /**
   * The control's name, shown above it with the Changed chip. Without one,
   * give the control an `aria-label` (or an `aria-labelledby`).
   */
  label?: ReactNode;
  /** A hint under the control. It becomes the group's accessible description. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * The error line, shown only while the control is invalid. A function
   * receives the validation result. Without it the control shows its own
   * validation messages.
   */
  errorMessage?: ReactNode | ((validation: ValidationResult) => ReactNode);
  /**
   * Whether the value differs from the saved one. Shows the clay Changed chip
   * in the label row and the light signal orange edge on the track, and has a
   * screen reader read the chip with the control. An invalid control shows its
   * error instead.
   */
  isChanged?: boolean;
  /**
   * The text of the Changed chip.
   * @default 'Changed'
   */
  changedLabel?: string;
  /**
   * `md` is a 48px track of 40px options. `sm` is a 40px track whose 32px
   * options are still hit at 40px, for a toolbar or a header.
   * @default 'md'
   */
  size?: SegmentedControlSize;
  /** The options: SegmentedControlItem elements, each with its own `value`. */
  children?: ReactNode;
  /** A class name, or a function of the control's state, merged after the library's own classes. */
  className?: string | ((values: RadioGroupRenderProps & { defaultClassName: string | undefined }) => string);
  /** A ref to the control's root element. */
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>;
}

/** What names the control: a visible label, or an `aria-label`, or an `aria-labelledby`. */
interface LabelledByLabel {
  label: ReactNode;
}
interface LabelledByAriaLabel {
  label?: undefined;
  'aria-label': string;
}
interface LabelledByElement {
  label?: undefined;
  'aria-labelledby': string;
}

export type SegmentedControlProps = SegmentedControlBaseProps &
  (LabelledByLabel | LabelledByAriaLabel | LabelledByElement);

/**
 * A few short options seen at once, of which one is chosen. Built on React
 * Aria's RadioGroup, so it is a radio group to a screen reader and to a form.
 * When its row of options does not fit the room it has, it stacks them one
 * per row.
 */
export function SegmentedControl({
  label,
  description,
  errorMessage,
  isChanged = false,
  changedLabel,
  size = 'md',
  children,
  className,
  ...props
}: SegmentedControlProps): ReactElement {
  const roomRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const trackRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  useStacking(roomRef, trackRef, size);
  const { chipId, describedBy } = useChangedDescription({
    // Only a label row has a chip, so only a labelled control has one to read.
    isChanged: isChanged && label != null,
    isInvalid: props.isInvalid,
    describedBy: props['aria-describedby'],
  });
  return (
    <RACRadioGroup
      {...props}
      orientation="horizontal"
      aria-describedby={describedBy}
      data-changed={isChanged ? '' : undefined}
      className={composeRenderProps(className, (userClassName) =>
        cx('field', 'segmented', size !== 'md' && `segmented-${size}`, userClassName),
      )}
    >
      {label != null ? <FieldHead label={label} changedLabel={changedLabel} chipId={chipId} /> : null}
      <div ref={trackRef} className="segmented-track">
        {children}
      </div>
      {description != null ? <Description>{description}</Description> : null}
      <FieldError>{errorMessage}</FieldError>
      <span ref={roomRef} className="segmented-room" aria-hidden="true" />
    </RACRadioGroup>
  );
}
```

`packages/react/src/segmented-control/SegmentedControl.stories.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { useState, type ComponentType, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { expect, waitFor } from 'storybook/test';
import { SegmentedControl, type SegmentedControlBaseProps } from './SegmentedControl';
import { SegmentedControlItem } from './SegmentedControlItem';

/** The color a token paints in the current theme, read by painting it. */
function tokenColor(name: string): string {
  const probe = document.createElement('span');
  probe.style.color = `var(${name})`;
  document.body.append(probe);
  const { color } = getComputedStyle(probe);
  probe.remove();
  return color;
}

/** One option for each entry: the key is the value and the text is what the option shows. */
function options(entries: Record<string, string>): ReactNode {
  return Object.entries(entries).map(([value, text]) => (
    <SegmentedControlItem key={value} value={value}>
      {text}
    </SegmentedControlItem>
  ));
}

const TWO = options({ light: 'Light', dark: 'Dark' });
const THREE = options({ light: 'Light', dark: 'Dark', system: 'System' });
const FIVE = options({
  daily: 'Daily',
  weekly: 'Weekly',
  monthly: 'Monthly',
  quarterly: 'Quarterly',
  yearly: 'Yearly',
});

const meta = {
  title: 'Components/SegmentedControl',
  // The component's props are a union, since it needs a label or an aria-label, and Storybook
  // cannot narrow a union. The stories are written against the props every member shares.
  component: SegmentedControl as ComponentType<SegmentedControlBaseProps>,
  args: { label: 'Color mode', defaultValue: 'light', children: TWO },
  decorators: [
    (Story) => (
      <div style={{ width: 'min(44rem, calc(100vw - 2rem))' }}>
        <Story />
      </div>
    ),
  ],
} satisfies Meta<SegmentedControlBaseProps>;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

/** Two options. The track is a 48px pill with the boundary edge, and the selected option is an ink fill. */
export const Default: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const group = canvas.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Color mode' });
    const track = group.querySelector('.segmented-track');
    const selected = canvas.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Light' }).closest('label');
    if (!track || !selected) throw new Error('No track or option');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(track).borderTopColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-boundary'));
    await expect(track.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(48);
    await expect(selected.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(40);
    await expect(getComputedStyle(selected).backgroundColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-ink'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(selected).color).toBe(tokenColor('--color-canvas'));
    await expect(group).not.toHaveAttribute('data-stacked');
  },
};

/** Three options share the room left over equally, each at least as wide as its label. */
export const ThreeOptions: Story = {
  args: {
    defaultValue: 'system',
    children: THREE,
    description: 'System follows the setting of the device.',
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('radiogroup')).toHaveAccessibleDescription(
      'System follows the setting of the device.',
    );
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('radio', { name: 'System' })).toBeChecked();
  },
};

/** Five short options still fit one row where there is room. On a phone they stack. */
export const FiveOptions: Story = {
  args: { label: 'Report cadence', defaultValue: 'weekly', children: FIVE },
};

/** The compact size draws 32px options in a 40px track, and still hits each at 40px. */
export const Compact: Story = {
  args: {
    label: undefined,
    'aria-label': 'Corners',
    size: 'sm',
    defaultValue: 'soft',
    children: options({ rounded: 'Rounded', soft: 'Soft', square: 'Square' }),
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const group = canvas.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Corners' });
    const track = group.querySelector('.segmented-track');
    const option = canvas.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Soft' }).closest('label');
    if (!track || !option) throw new Error('No track or option');
    await expect(track.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(40);
    await expect(option.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(32);
    await expect(getComputedStyle(option, '::before').height).toBe('40px');
  },
};

/**
 * The row does not fit 320px, so the options stack one per row. It is the whole
 * row or none of it: no option sits alone on a second line.
 */
export const Stacked: Story = {
  args: { label: 'Report cadence', defaultValue: 'weekly', children: FIVE },
  decorators: [
    (Story) => (
      <div style={{ width: 320 }}>
        <Story />
      </div>
    ),
  ],
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const group = canvas.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Report cadence' });
    await waitFor(() => expect(group).toHaveAttribute('data-stacked'));
    const track = group.querySelector('.segmented-track');
    if (!track) throw new Error('No track');
    const rows = [...group.querySelectorAll('.segmented-option')].map((option) =>
      option.getBoundingClientRect(),
    );
    await expect(rows).toHaveLength(5);
    for (const [index, row] of rows.entries()) {
      await expect(row.height).toBe(40);
      await expect(row.left).toBe(rows[0]?.left);
      await expect(row.width).toBe(rows[0]?.width);
      if (index > 0) await expect(row.top).toBeGreaterThan(rows[index - 1]?.top ?? Infinity);
    }
    // The column fits the room, and nothing scrolls the page sideways.
    await expect(track.getBoundingClientRect().right).toBeLessThanOrEqual(
      group.getBoundingClientRect().right + 0.5,
    );
    await expect(document.documentElement.scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(window.innerWidth);
  },
};

/** Recessed, with every label in taupe. The selected option keeps its place as a quiet taupe pill. */
export const Disabled: Story = {
  args: { isDisabled: true, defaultValue: 'dark', children: THREE },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const group = canvas.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Color mode' });
    const track = group.querySelector('.segmented-track');
    const selected = canvas.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' }).closest('label');

    await expect(getComputedStyle(track).backgroundColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-disabled'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(selected).backgroundColor).toBe(tokenColor('--color-taupe'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(other).color).toBe(tokenColor('--color-taupe'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(other).cursor).toBe('not-allowed');
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Light' })).toBeDisabled();
  },

/** A room that resizes: narrow stacks the options, wide puts them back in one row. */
function Resizing(): ReactElement {
  const [width, setWidth] = useState(640);
  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, marginBottom: 16 }}>
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => {
            setWidth(300);
          }}
        >
          Narrow
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => {
            setWidth(640);
          }}
        >
          Wide
        </button>
      </div>
      <div style={{ width }}>
        <SegmentedControl label="Report cadence" defaultValue="weekly">
          {FIVE}
        </SegmentedControl>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export const Resized: Story = {
  tags: ['no-visual'],
  render: () => <Resizing />,
  play: async ({ canvas, userEvent }) => {
    const group = canvas.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Report cadence' });
    await waitFor(() => expect(group).not.toHaveAttribute('data-stacked'));
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Narrow' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(group).toHaveAttribute('data-stacked'));
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Wide' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(group).not.toHaveAttribute('data-stacked'));
    // Choosing an option while stacked leaves the arrangement alone.
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Narrow' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(group).toHaveAttribute('data-stacked'));
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByText('Monthly'));
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Monthly' })).toBeChecked();
    await expect(group).toHaveAttribute('data-stacked');
  },
};
```

The `play` functions run in Chromium, in light and dark, so they check what jsdom cannot: the real geometry (a 48px track of 40px options, a 40px compact track of 32px options hit at 40px through the `::before`), each state's computed edge color against the token it should be (`tokenColor` paints the token and reads it back, so the check holds in both themes), the track keeping its 48px while changed, the disabled fill and cursor and taupe pill, and for the two focus stories the computed outline color and offset (canvas and -4px on the chosen option, the token ring and 2px on any other). `Stacked` sits in a 320px box and waits for the real `ResizeObserver` to set `data-stacked`, then checks that the five rows are 40px tall, one under the next at the same left and width, that the column fits its root, and that the page does not scroll sideways. `Resized` (no visual baseline) narrows and widens the room with two buttons and asserts that `data-stacked` follows both ways and survives choosing an option while stacked. `Dark` is a `data-theme="dark"` region on the page, three controls (plain, changed, disabled), so the white fill and the near-black label show next to the light page.

`FiveOptions` fits one row in the 44rem the stories give it and stacks at 375px, which is the visual baseline `--light-rounded-375.png` showing stacking on a phone. `Choosing` is a press and the arrow keys, tagged `no-visual`, since a press is transient. The stories are typed against `SegmentedControlBaseProps` because Storybook cannot narrow the union.

The page, `apps/docs/content/docs/components/segmented-control.mdx`. The first paragraph after each `##` is the section's note. It has a Keys table because the control is interactive, two props tables (the control, then the option), and design rules. It never names the Button or the Spinner, so the search tests that rank those pages first are unaffected.

```mdx
---
title: Segmented control
description: A few short options seen at once, of which one is chosen. When its row does not fit, it stacks one option per row.
icon: Columns3
---

<Section>

## Basic

Pass a label, and the options as children, each with its own `value`. The chosen option is the ink pill. A segmented control is for a few short options that are all worth seeing at once. For more, or for options that need explaining, use a list.

<Preview name="segmented-control-basic" />

</Section>

<Section>

## States

The track's edge carries the state, as in every field. A changed control gets a light signal orange edge and a clay chip beside its label. An invalid control gets the error edge and an error line, and invalid outranks changed, so the chip steps aside. A disabled control is recessed, and its chosen option stays in view as a quiet taupe pill. The compact size, `sm`, draws 32px options in a 40px track and still hits each one at 40px.

<Preview name="segmented-control-states" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Stacking

The options are all in one row or all in a column, never some of each. When the row does not fit the room the control has, it stacks one option per row, each 40px tall. When the room comes back, the row does too. The control compares its own row with its own width, so give it a column to fill, as you would a text field. A control sized to its content, in a flex row or a centered grid, has no room to compare with and never stacks.

<Preview name="segmented-control-stacking" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

Every value works controlled and uncontrolled, and a control with a `name` submits the chosen `value` in a plain form. `onChange` receives the value. A `value` of `null` is a controlled control with nothing chosen.

<Code code={`import { useState } from 'react';
import { SegmentedControl, SegmentedControlItem } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function Appearance({ saved }: { saved: string }) {
  const [mode, setMode] = useState(saved);
  return (
    <SegmentedControl
      label="Appearance"
      name="appearance"
      value={mode}
      onChange={setMode}
      isChanged={mode !== saved}
    >
      <SegmentedControlItem value="light">Light</SegmentedControlItem>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="dark">Dark</SegmentedControlItem>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="system">System</SegmentedControlItem>
    </SegmentedControl>
  );
}`} />

Without a visible label, name the control with `aria-label`, as a toolbar's switch is named by what it sits beside. One of the two is required.

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

Every React Aria RadioGroup prop is accepted, except `orientation`: the options are always laid out in a row, and stack on their own. These are the ones Snapshot UI adds or shapes.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/segmented-control/SegmentedControl.tsx" type="Pick<SegmentedControlBaseProps, 'label' | 'aria-label' | 'description' | 'errorMessage' | 'isChanged' | 'changedLabel' | 'size' | 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onChange' | 'name' | 'isRequired' | 'isDisabled' | 'isInvalid' | 'validate'>" />

Each option is a SegmentedControlItem.

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/segmented-control/SegmentedControlItem.tsx" type="Pick<SegmentedControlItemProps, 'value' | 'children' | 'isDisabled' | 'className'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A native radio group: each option is a radio, the control is named by its label, and React Aria handles the wiring. A screen reader reads the Changed chip with the control, after the hint, while the control is changed and valid. An invalid control reads its error line alone. The group is one tab stop, and focus lands on the chosen option.

<Keys rows={[['Tab', 'Moves focus into the control, onto the chosen option, or the first when nothing is chosen.'], ['Right Down', 'Chooses the next option, and wraps from the last to the first.'], ['Left Up', 'Chooses the previous option, and wraps from the first to the last.'], ['Space', 'Chooses the focused option.']]} />

The 2px ring sits outside an option that is not chosen. On the chosen option, which is an ink fill, the ring is drawn inside it in the canvas color, so it still reads. A disabled option is skipped by the arrow keys.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps segmented controls in the system.

<Rules dos={['Use two to five options of a word or two each, all worth seeing at once.', 'Name the control in the label, in sentence case.', 'Show the chip and the changed edge together, and only while the value is unsaved.']} donts={['Never use it to switch what a page shows. That is tabs, and they hold no value.', 'Never let the options wrap onto a second row of their own. The control stacks them or it does not.', 'Never leave the chip beside an error. Invalid outranks changed.']} />

</Section>
```
