End-to-end tests. Append to `apps/docs/tests/docs.spec.ts` (after the last test, which uses `hitSize`, `hitsAt` and `sideways`, all already imported). Three tests, one of them run at 375 and at 1440: the header switches are segmented controls named for what they set and hit at 40px (the compact option is drawn at 32px, and the extra area must be on the option itself, which `hitsAt` checks 18px above and below its center); the page keeps a wide room in one row, stacks a narrow one with 40px rows, stacks the wide one when the window narrows to 375px and puts the row back when it widens again (the sideways check is polled because the shell eases into its narrow layout); and the page chooses with the arrow keys and draws each state on the track edge in the colors the tokens give (`rgb(243, 115, 56)` for changed, `rgb(163, 35, 27)` for invalid, the disabled fill `rgb(244, 244, 244)` and the taupe pill `rgb(209, 205, 199)`).

```ts

for (const width of [375, 1440]) {
  test(`the header switches are segmented controls, named for what they set and hit at 40px at ${String(width)}px`, async ({
    page,
  }) => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width, height: 900 });
    await visit(page);
    for (const [name, options] of [
      ['Color mode', ['Light', 'Dark']],
      ['Corners', ['Rounded', 'Soft', 'Square']],
    ] as const) {
      const group = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name, exact: true });
      await expect(group).toHaveClass(/segmented-sm/);
      await expect(group.getByRole('radio')).toHaveCount(options.length);
      for (const text of options) {
        const option = group.locator('.segmented-option', { hasText: text });
        // The option is drawn at 32px and hit at 40px, with the extra area on the option itself.
        const size = await hitSize(option);
        expect(size.height).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(40);
        expect(size.width).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(40);
        expect(await hitsAt(option, '.segmented-option', -18)).toBe(true);
        expect(await hitsAt(option, '.segmented-option', 18)).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });
}

test('the segmented control page keeps a wide room in one row and stacks a narrow one, and follows the window', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1440, height: 900 });
  await visit(page, '/docs/components/segmented-control');
  const wide = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Report cadence in a wide room' });
  const narrow = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Report cadence in a narrow room' });
  await expect(wide).not.toHaveAttribute('data-stacked');
  await expect(narrow).toHaveAttribute('data-stacked');
  const options = await narrow.locator('.segmented-option').all();
  expect(options).toHaveLength(5);
  for (const option of options) expect((await option.boundingBox())?.height).toBeCloseTo(40, 1);
  // The window narrows and the wide room no longer fits its row. Widened, the row comes back.
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 375, height: 900 });
  await expect(wide).toHaveAttribute('data-stacked');
  // The shell eases into the narrow layout, so the page settles a moment after the control does.
  await expect.poll(() => sideways(page)).toBe(0);
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1440, height: 900 });
  await expect(wide).not.toHaveAttribute('data-stacked');
});

test('the segmented control page chooses with the arrow keys and draws each state on the track edge', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });
  await visit(page, '/docs/components/segmented-control');
  const mode = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Appearance' });
  await expect(mode.getByRole('radio', { name: 'System' })).toBeChecked();
  await mode.getByRole('radio', { name: 'System' }).focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
  await expect(mode.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' })).toBeChecked();
  await expect(mode.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' })).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  await expect(mode.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Light' })).toBeChecked();

  // A changed control draws the light signal orange edge and its chip.
  const changed = page.locator('.segmented[data-changed]');
  await expect(changed.locator('.field-changed')).toBeVisible();
```

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/core/src/components/card.css`
- Modify: `packages/core/src/styles.css` (import it)

- Modify: `apps/docs/content/docs/components/meta.json`, `apps/docs/examples/index.ts`
- Modify (the stand-ins the docs drew by hand): `apps/docs/app/site.css`, `apps/docs/components/shell/shell.css`, `apps/docs/app/(home)/home-page.tsx`, `apps/docs/app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`, `apps/docs/components/mdx/section.tsx`, `apps/docs/examples/theme-shapes.tsx`
- Modify: `docs/design-system.md` (append `## Card` to Appendix B)
- Create: `.changeset/card.md`
- Create (Step 14): 25 baselines, `apps/storybook/tests/visual/__screenshots__/components-card--*.png`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `cx` from `packages/react/src/utils/cx.ts`; the tokens `--spacing-part` (8px), `--spacing-peer` (24px), `--spacing-separate` (32px), `--radius-stadium`, `--radius-surface`, `--color-lifted`, `--color-hairline`, `--color-frame`, `--color-divider`, `--color-ink`, `--color-slate`, `--font-sans`, the `--text-h3*` and `--text-body*` families; `expectNoA11yViolations` from `packages/react/test/a11y.ts`. React Aria is not used: Card is a static server component, with no `'use client'` and no `react-aria-components` import.
- Produces, all in `packages/react/src/card/Card.tsx` and re-exported as named exports from `@snapshot-ui/react`:
  - `Card(props: CardProps): ReactElement`. `CardProps` is `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>` plus `as?: 'div' | 'section' | 'article'` (default `'div'`) and `ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>`. Renders `<div class="card">`.
  - `CardHeader(props: CardHeaderProps): ReactElement`. `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` plus `ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>`. Renders `<div class="card-header">`.
  - `CardTitle(props: CardTitleProps): ReactElement`. `HTMLAttributes<HTMLHeadingElement>` plus `level?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4` (default `2`, the heading element) and `ref?: Ref<HTMLHeadingElement>`. Renders `<h2 class="card-title">` by default. The look is the h3 type step at every level.
  - `CardNote(props: CardNoteProps): ReactElement`. `HTMLAttributes<HTMLParagraphElement>` plus `ref`. Renders `<p class="card-note">`, in slate.
  - `CardBody(props: CardBodyProps): ReactElement`. `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` plus `ref`. Renders `<div class="card-body">`.
  - Every part merges `className` after its own class with `cx` and spreads the rest of its attributes, so `data-theme`, `id`, `aria-*` and `style` pass through.
- Produces the classes `card`, `card-header`, `card-title`, `card-note` and `card-body`. None starts with a Tailwind namespace. The CSS is in `packages/core/src/components/card.css`, imported from `styles.css`.
- Produces the cascade other tasks rely on: a card is `--radius-stadium` with 32px padding; a card placed in a card, directly or inside a `card-body`, is `--radius-surface` with a `--color-frame` border. The 32px is exact: the docs shell's Section rule reaches a card's edges with negative margins of the same size.
- Removes from the docs the `.card` and `.card-header` stand-in rules in `site.css`. Every docs use is now `<Card>` and its parts.

**Decisions made in this task** (each is also in the Appendix B text of Step 2 or in a code comment):

- **`CardHeader` is a `div`, not a `header`.** A `<header>` outside sectioning content is the page's banner, and a card is a `div` by default. Measured with axe in jsdom: two page-level `div` cards that each contain a `<header>` fail `landmark-no-duplicate-banner` and `landmark-unique`; the same markup in two `section` cards passes. `Card.test.tsx` fails if the element ever becomes a `header` (checked by making the change: 2 tests fail).
- **The padding is `--spacing-separate`.** That token is emitted as `32px`, not `2rem`. The docs Section rule (`shell.css`, the paragraph after a section's title) used `-2rem`, `2rem` and `1.5rem`, which equal the tokens only while the root font size is 16px, so that rule now reads the tokens too (`--spacing-separate`, `--spacing-peer`). Nothing moves at 16px.
- **The card does not step down on a phone.** The design document says about 24px of padding on mobile. A component cannot see the width of the column it sits in, so core stays at 32px, and the docs keep their own phone rules for `.card` and `.card-header` in `shell.css` and `home.css` (those rules are overrides of the real class now, and they stay).
- **Nested means in a card or in its body, not "anywhere inside".** The obvious selector is `.card .card`, but it also restyles a card that only sits deeper, on a well of its own: the docs preview stage puts the `/docs/theming` shape samples inside a section card, and `.card .card` changed them (stadium to surface, plus an outline). `.card > .card, .card-body .card` covers `Card > Card` and `Card > CardBody > ... > Card`, and leaves the docs untouched with no docs-only override. The inner card also takes `border-color: var(--color-frame)`: in light a card on a card is Lifted on Lifted and `--color-hairline` is transparent, so without it the nested card has no visible edge at all (seen in a screenshot; it looked like an indented block).
- **The body owns the vertical rhythm.** `.card-body` is the source's grid (24px rows, 32px columns) and its children get `margin-block: 0`, so a paragraph's default margin never adds to the 24px. The title and note carry `margin: 0` for the same reason: base.css leaves headings and paragraphs alone.
- **The title and note set `font-family: var(--font-sans)`,** as Button does, so a card in an app that has not imported base.css still draws its header in the system's face.
- **A long word wraps inside the card.** `overflow-wrap: break-word` on the title and note, and `min-width: 0` on the children of the header and body. Without the second, a long URL in a note widens the grid track and spills out of the card at 375px (seen in the `LongContent` story before the fix).
- **The docs keep a four-line `.card` transition rule** (`border-radius` and `background-color`, 200ms) in `site.css`. Core components carry no transition (Button has none), and deleting it would make the docs cards snap when the corner shape or color mode changes while every other docs surface animates. The global reduced-motion rule at the end of `site.css` still stops it.
- **Docs examples have no `'use client'`.** Card is static, so its examples show it used from a server file. The Button inside `card-parts.tsx` is a client component by itself.

```js
import { mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { join } from 'node:path';

const [repo, outDir, port] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!repo || !outDir || !port) throw new Error('usage: node card-shots.mjs <repo root> <out dir> <port>');

};

mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
const browser = await chromium.launch();
for (const scheme of ['light', 'dark']) {
  for (const [width, viewport] of Object.entries(SIZES)) {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport, colorScheme: scheme, reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    for (const [name, path] of Object.entries(PAGES)) {

      await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
      await page.waitForTimeout(400);

      });

await browser.close();
```

and `$SHOTS/card-diff.mjs`:

```js
// Throwaway, never committed: exact pixel comparison of two screenshot folders.
// usage: node card-diff.mjs <repo root> <folder A> <folder B>
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { join } from 'node:path';

const [repo, a, b] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!repo || !a || !b) throw new Error('usage: node card-diff.mjs <repo root> <folder A> <folder B>');
// pngjs is a dependency of Playwright, so it sits in the pnpm store.
const store = join(repo, 'node_modules/.pnpm');
const pngjs = readdirSync(store).find((name) => name.startsWith('pngjs@'));
if (!pngjs) throw new Error(`pngjs not found in ${store}`);
const { PNG } = createRequire(join(store, pngjs, 'node_modules/pngjs/package.json'))('pngjs');

let differing = 0;
for (const file of readdirSync(a).filter((name) => name.endsWith('.png')).sort()) {
  const x = PNG.sync.read(readFileSync(join(a, file)));
  const y = PNG.sync.read(readFileSync(join(b, file)));
  if (x.width !== y.width || x.height !== y.height) {
    differing++;
    console.log(file.padEnd(34), `size ${x.width}x${x.height} vs ${y.width}x${y.height}`);
    continue;
  }
  let count = 0;
  let minX = Infinity, minY = Infinity, maxX = -1, maxY = -1;
  for (let i = 0; i < x.data.length; i += 4) {
    if (x.data[i] !== y.data[i] || x.data[i + 1] !== y.data[i + 1] || x.data[i + 2] !== y.data[i + 2] || x.data[i + 3] !== y.data[i + 3]) {
      count++;
      const pixel = i / 4;
      const px = pixel % x.width;
      const py = Math.floor(pixel / x.width);
      minX = Math.min(minX, px); maxX = Math.max(maxX, px); minY = Math.min(minY, py); maxY = Math.max(maxY, py);
    }
  }
  if (count > 0) differing++;
  console.log(file.padEnd(34), `${x.width}x${x.height}`, count === 0 ? 'identical' : `${count} px differ in x ${minX}-${maxX}, y ${minY}-${maxY}`);
}
console.log(differing === 0 ? 'ALL IDENTICAL' : `${differing} file(s) differ`);
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Record the derivation**

Append to `docs/design-system.md`, after the end of the `## SegmentedControl` section, which is the end of Appendix B:

```markdown

## Card

The document's panel section becomes `Card`, with a header, a title, a note
and a body. Lifted Cream, the stadium corner and 32px of padding come straight
from the document. Six things were derived.

- **The padding is a spacing step.** It reads `--spacing-separate`, the step
  for "section header to its body", so the space around a card's content and
  the space between its header and body are one number. The header's rule
  reaches the card's edges through negative margins of the same size, so the
  two cannot drift apart. The rule is `--color-divider`, the app's ink at 10%
  under its own token, and the border is `--color-hairline`, which is why the
  box does not move when the color mode changes.
- **The card does not narrow on a phone.** The document asks for about 24px of
  padding on mobile. A card cannot know how wide the column around it is, only
  the page can, and a card in a narrow dialog on a wide screen would never
  step down. So the card is 32px everywhere, and a site that wants less on a
  phone sets it where it knows the width.
- **The header is a div.** A `<header>` outside sectioning content is the
  page's banner. A card is a div unless it is told otherwise, so every card
  header at page level would add a banner, and axe fails two of them as
  duplicate landmarks. The title is what names a card, so the structure is
  carried by the heading and not by the wrapper.
- **The title's level is not its look.** The app's section title was always an
  `h2`. In a library the card cannot know where it sits in the page's outline,
  so `level` picks the element, `h1` to `h4`, and the type stays the h3 step at
  every level, so the same card looks the same wherever it is placed.
- **A card in a card steps down.** The app never put a card in a card. The
  library does, and the nested radii table already says what to do: a 40px
  holder holds 24px cards. A card placed in another card, directly or in its
  body, takes `--radius-surface`, which is 12px in Soft and 0 in Square. The
  rule is those two placements and not any descendant: a card that sits on a
  well of its own, such as the docs preview stage, is not on the card's
  surface and keeps its corner. In light a nested card is Lifted on Lifted and
  the hairline is transparent, so nothing would show its edge. It takes the
  frame outline a list takes. The outline is a cue and not a boundary, since
  nothing depends on seeing the edge: it measures 1.28 against Lifted in light
  and 1.43 in dark.
- **The body owns the rhythm.** It is the app's body grid: 24px between peers
  down the page and 32px between them across it, which only shows once the body
  is given columns. Its children carry no vertical margin of their own, so a
  paragraph's default one never adds to the 24px.

The title is ink and the note is slate, both on Lifted, and both pairings are
in the contrast gate. Ink measures 17.84 in light and 17.42 in dark, and slate
5.31 and 6.94. The app's collapse toggle is not part of Card. It arrives with
the collapsible card.
```

```tsx
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import type { ReactElement } from 'react';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { expectNoA11yViolations } from '../../test/a11y';
import { Card, CardBody, CardHeader, CardNote, CardTitle } from './Card';

interface PartProps {
  className?: string;
  ref?: (node: HTMLElement | null) => void;
  'data-testid'?: string;
}

/** Every part, with the element it renders and the class it always carries. */
const parts: [name: string, tag: string, baseClass: string, part: (props: PartProps) => ReactElement][] = [
  ['Card', 'DIV', 'card', (props) => <Card {...props}>Text</Card>],
  ['CardHeader', 'DIV', 'card-header', (props) => <CardHeader {...props}>Text</CardHeader>],
  ['CardTitle', 'H2', 'card-title', (props) => <CardTitle {...props}>Text</CardTitle>],
  ['CardNote', 'P', 'card-note', (props) => <CardNote {...props}>Text</CardNote>],
  ['CardBody', 'DIV', 'card-body', (props) => <CardBody {...props}>Text</CardBody>],
];

describe.each(parts)('%s', (_name, tag, baseClass, part) => {
  it(`renders a ${tag.toLowerCase()} with the ${baseClass} class and nothing else`, () => {
    render(part({ 'data-testid': 'part' }));
    const element = screen.getByTestId('part');
    expect(element.tagName).toBe(tag);
    expect(element).toHaveAttribute('class', baseClass);
    expect(element).toHaveTextContent('Text');
  });

  it('merges a className after its own class', () => {
    render(part({ 'data-testid': 'part', className: 'extra' }));
    expect(screen.getByTestId('part')).toHaveAttribute('class', `${baseClass} extra`);
  });

  it('forwards a ref to its element', () => {
    let received: HTMLElement | null = null;
    render(
      part({
        'data-testid': 'part',
        ref: (node) => {
          received = node;
        },
      }),
    );
    expect(received).toBe(screen.getByTestId('part'));
  });
});

describe('Card', () => {
  it.each(['div', 'section', 'article'] as const)('as renders a %s element', (as) => {
    render(
      <Card as={as} data-testid="card">
        Text
      </Card>,
    );
    const card = screen.getByTestId('card');
    expect(card.tagName).toBe(as.toUpperCase());
    expect(card).toHaveClass('card');
    // as chooses the element and is not an attribute.
    expect(card).not.toHaveAttribute('as');
  });

  it('passes other HTML attributes through, data-theme included', () => {
    render(
      <Card id="notifications" data-theme="light" style={{ width: 320 }} data-testid="card">
        Text
      </Card>,
    );
    const card = screen.getByTestId('card');
    expect(card).toHaveAttribute('id', 'notifications');
    expect(card).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'light');
    expect(card).toHaveStyle({ width: '320px' });
  });

  it('is a region when it is a section named by its title', () => {
    render(
      <Card as="section" aria-labelledby="notifications-title">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle id="notifications-title">Notifications</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
      </Card>,
    );
    expect(screen.getByRole('region', { name: 'Notifications' })).toHaveClass('card');
  });

  it('nests: a card inside a card is another card with its own parts', () => {
    render(
      <Card data-testid="outer">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Workspace</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardBody>
          <Card data-testid="inner">
            <CardHeader>
              <CardTitle level={3}>Danger zone</CardTitle>
            </CardHeader>
            <CardBody>Delete this workspace.</CardBody>
          </Card>
        </CardBody>
      </Card>,
    );
    const outer = screen.getByTestId('outer');
    const inner = screen.getByTestId('inner');
    expect(outer).toContainElement(inner);
    expect(inner).toHaveAttribute('class', 'card');
    // The corner step is the stylesheet's `.card .card`, so the markup is the same at every depth.
    expect(outer.querySelectorAll('.card')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(inner.querySelectorAll('.card-header, .card-title, .card-body')).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 2, name: 'Workspace' })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 3, name: 'Danger zone' })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('stays a server component: no use client directive and no React Aria import', () => {
    const source = readFileSync(join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), 'Card.tsx'), 'utf8');
    expect(source).not.toMatch(/use client/);
    expect(source).not.toMatch(/react-aria-components/);
  });
});

describe('CardHeader', () => {
  it('adds no banner landmark, however many cards sit at page level', async () => {
    // A <header> outside sectioning content is the page's banner, so two cards that each used one
    // would fail axe's landmark-no-duplicate-banner. A card is a div by default, so its header is a div.
    const { container } = render(
      <>
        <Card>
          <CardHeader>
            <CardTitle>Notifications</CardTitle>
          </CardHeader>
        </Card>
        <Card>
          <CardHeader>
            <CardTitle>Workspace</CardTitle>
          </CardHeader>
        </Card>
      </>,
    );
    expect(screen.queryByRole('banner')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });
});

describe('CardTitle', () => {
  it('is a level 2 heading by default', () => {
    render(<CardTitle>Notifications</CardTitle>);
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 2, name: 'Notifications' })).toHaveClass('card-title');
  });

  it.each([1, 2, 3, 4] as const)('level %i renders the matching heading element', (level) => {
    render(<CardTitle level={level}>Notifications</CardTitle>);
    const heading = screen.getByRole('heading', { level });
    expect(heading.tagName).toBe(`H${level}`);
    // The element changes with the level; the look does not.
    expect(heading).toHaveAttribute('class', 'card-title');
    expect(heading).not.toHaveAttribute('level');
  });
});

describe('a composed card', () => {
  it('has no axe violations as a section, an article or nested', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <>
        <Card as="section" aria-labelledby="one">
          <CardHeader>
            <CardTitle id="one">Notifications</CardTitle>
            <CardNote>Where we reach you, and how often.</CardNote>
          </CardHeader>
          <CardBody>
            <p>Product updates</p>
            <Card as="article" aria-labelledby="two">
              <CardHeader>
                <CardTitle id="two" level={3}>
                  Digest
                </CardTitle>
              </CardHeader>
              <CardBody>Every Tuesday morning.</CardBody>
            </Card>
          </CardBody>
        </Card>
        <Card>Just content</Card>
      </>,
    );
    await expectNoA11yViolations(container);
  });
});
```

`packages/core/src/components/card.css`:

```css
/*
 * Card, the design system's panel section: Lifted Cream laid on the canvas,
 * a stadium corner and 32px of padding. The header is a band ruled off from
 * the body; its negative margins take the rule to the card's edges, which is
 * what makes it a band rather than an underline on the text. Derived in
 * docs/design-system.md ("Card").
 */
@layer components {
  .card {
    box-sizing: border-box;
    min-width: 0;
    padding: var(--spacing-separate);
    /* Transparent in light and white 12% in dark, so the box never reflows
       when the color mode changes. */
    border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline);
    border-radius: var(--radius-stadium);
    background-color: var(--color-lifted);
  }

  /* Rounded inside rounded takes the next step down the scale. In light, a
     card on a card has no tone step to separate it, and the hairline is
     transparent there, so it takes the outline a list takes. Nested means
     placed in a card or in its body. A card that only sits somewhere deeper,
     on a well of its own, is not on this surface and keeps its corner. */
  .card > .card,
  .card-body .card {
    border-color: var(--color-frame);
    border-radius: var(--radius-surface);
  }

  .card-header {
    display: grid;
    gap: var(--spacing-part);
    margin: 0 calc(var(--spacing-separate) * -1) var(--spacing-separate);
    padding: 0 var(--spacing-separate) var(--spacing-peer);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-divider);
  }

  /* The element is the reader's outline and the look is the system's, so the
     title draws at the h3 step whatever heading level it renders. */
  .card-title {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: var(--text-h3);
    line-height: var(--text-h3--line-height);
    letter-spacing: var(--text-h3--letter-spacing);
    font-weight: var(--text-h3--font-weight);
    color: var(--color-ink);
    overflow-wrap: break-word;
  }

  .card-note {
    margin: 0;
    font-family: var(--font-sans);
    font-size: var(--text-body);
    line-height: var(--text-body--line-height);
    font-weight: var(--text-body--font-weight);
    color: var(--color-slate);
    overflow-wrap: break-word;
  }

  /* Peers sit 24px apart down the page and 32px apart across it. The column
     gap only shows when the body is given columns. The body owns the vertical
     rhythm, so a child carries no margin of its own: a paragraph's default one
     would add to the gap. */
  .card-body {
    display: grid;
    column-gap: var(--spacing-separate);
    row-gap: var(--spacing-peer);
    align-content: start;
  }

  .card-body > * {
    margin-block: 0;
  }

  /* A long unbroken word wraps inside the card instead of widening its track. */
  .card-header > *,
  .card-body > * {
    min-width: 0;
  }
}
```

`packages/react/src/card/Card.tsx`:

```tsx
import { createElement, type HTMLAttributes, type ReactElement, type Ref } from 'react';
import { cx } from '../utils/cx';

export interface CardProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> {
  /**
   * The element to render. A `section` or an `article` is a landmark of its
   * own once it has an accessible name; a `div` is not.
   * @default 'div'
   */
  as?: 'div' | 'section' | 'article';
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>;
}

/** A lifted surface laid on the page. Static: it adds no JavaScript. */
export function Card({ as: tag = 'div', className, ...props }: CardProps): ReactElement {
  // createElement rather than JSX: the three tags take one HTMLElement ref type between them.
  return createElement(tag, { ...props, className: cx('card', className) });
}

export interface CardHeaderProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>;
}

/**
 * The band above the body that holds the title and the note, ruled off from
 * the body. A div, not a header: a header outside sectioning content is the
 * page's banner, and a card is a div by default.
 */
export function CardHeader({ className, ...props }: CardHeaderProps): ReactElement {
  return <div {...props} className={cx('card-header', className)} />;
}

export interface CardTitleProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLHeadingElement> {
  /**
   * The heading element, `h1` to `h4`, so the card fits the page's outline.
   * The look is the same at every level.
   * @default 2
   */
  level?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;
  ref?: Ref<HTMLHeadingElement>;
}

/** The card's heading. */
export function CardTitle({ level = 2, className, ...props }: CardTitleProps): ReactElement {
  const Heading = `h${level}` as const;
  return <Heading {...props} className={cx('card-title', className)} />;
}

export interface CardNoteProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLParagraphElement> {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLParagraphElement>;
}

/** A line of slate text under the title. */
export function CardNote({ className, ...props }: CardNoteProps): ReactElement {
  return <p {...props} className={cx('card-note', className)} />;
}

export interface CardBodyProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>;
}

/** The card's content, stacked with 24px between peers. */
export function CardBody({ className, ...props }: CardBodyProps): ReactElement {
  return <div {...props} className={cx('card-body', className)} />;
}
```

`Card` calls `createElement` and not JSX on purpose: with `as` typed as `'div' | 'section' | 'article'`, JSX asks for a ref that is assignable to each element's own type at once, and `Ref<HTMLElement>` is not assignable to `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`. `createElement` takes the three tags as one `HTMLElementType`.

`packages/react/src/card/Card.stories.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { expect } from 'storybook/test';
import { Card, CardBody, CardHeader, CardNote, CardTitle } from './Card';

const meta = {
  title: 'Components/Card',
  component: Card,
  decorators: [
    (Story) => (
      <div style={{ width: 'min(480px, calc(100vw - 48px))' }}>
        <Story />
      </div>
    ),
  ],
} satisfies Meta<typeof Card>;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

/** The top-left corner in pixels, so a story reads the shape the toolbar has chosen. */
const radius = (element: HTMLElement): number => parseFloat(getComputedStyle(element).borderTopLeftRadius);

/** A token's value in pixels, read where the toolbar's data-shape applies. */
const token = (name: string): number =>
  parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name));

/** A lifted surface with 32px of padding and a stadium corner. */
export const Basic: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <Card {...args}>
      <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>Anything can sit in a card: a form, a list, a paragraph.</p>
    </Card>
  ),
};

/** The title is the card's heading and names the region when the card is a section. */
export const WithHeaderAndNote: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <Card {...args} as="section" aria-labelledby="notifications-title">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle id="notifications-title">Notifications</CardTitle>
        <CardNote>Where we reach you, and how often.</CardNote>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>
        <p>Product updates, when something ships.</p>
        <p>A weekly digest, every Tuesday morning.</p>
        <p>Security alerts, always on for owners.</p>
      </CardBody>
    </Card>
  ),
};

/**
 * A card inside a card steps its corner down one place, from the stadium to the
 * surface radius, and takes an outline, since in light a card on a card has no
 * tone step to separate it.
 */
export const Nested: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <Card {...args} as="section" aria-labelledby="workspace-title" data-testid="outer-card">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle id="workspace-title">Workspace</CardTitle>
        <CardNote>Shown in the header and in every invite.</CardNote>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>
        <p>Northwind Studio</p>
        <Card as="section" aria-labelledby="danger-title" data-testid="inner-card">
          <CardHeader>
            <CardTitle id="danger-title" level={3}>
              Danger zone
            </CardTitle>
            <CardNote>Deleting a workspace cannot be undone.</CardNote>
          </CardHeader>
          <CardBody>
            <p>Every member loses access at once.</p>
          </CardBody>
        </Card>
      </CardBody>
    </Card>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(radius(canvas.getByTestId('outer-card'))).toBe(token('--radius-stadium'));
    const inner = canvas.getByTestId('inner-card');
    await expect(radius(inner)).toBe(token('--radius-surface'));
    await expect(getComputedStyle(inner).borderTopColor).not.toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
  },
};

/** A card placed directly in a card, with no body between them, steps down too. */
export const NestedWithoutBody: Story = {
  // The corner is the whole point and the visual suite already shoots Nested, so no screenshot.
  tags: ['no-visual'],
  render: (args) => (
    <Card {...args} data-testid="outer-card">
      <Card data-testid="inner-card">A card inside a card.</Card>
    </Card>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(radius(canvas.getByTestId('outer-card'))).toBe(token('--radius-stadium'));
    await expect(radius(canvas.getByTestId('inner-card'))).toBe(token('--radius-surface'));
  },
};

/**
 * The tokens decide, so a card takes the theme of the block it sits in. A card
 * with its own data-theme takes that one instead, and its text follows.
 */
export const InsideDarkBlock: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <div
      data-theme="dark"
      style={{
        display: 'grid',
        gap: 16,
        padding: 24,
        borderRadius: 'var(--radius-stadium)',
        background: 'var(--color-canvas)',
      }}
    >
      <Card {...args} as="section" aria-labelledby="dark-title" data-testid="dark-card">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle id="dark-title">Notifications</CardTitle>
          <CardNote>A card inside a dark block.</CardNote>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardBody>
          <p>It takes the dark tokens without being told to.</p>
        </CardBody>
      </Card>
      <Card {...args} as="section" aria-labelledby="light-title" data-theme="light" data-testid="light-card">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle id="light-title">Workspace</CardTitle>
          <CardNote>A light card inside the same block.</CardNote>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardBody>
          <p>It asks for light, and its text follows.</p>
        </CardBody>
      </Card>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const dark = canvas.getByTestId('dark-card');
    await expect(dark).toHaveStyle({ backgroundColor: 'rgb(26, 26, 25)' });
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Notifications' })).toHaveStyle({
      color: 'rgb(255, 255, 255)',
    });
    const light = canvas.getByTestId('light-card');
    await expect(light).toHaveStyle({ backgroundColor: 'rgb(252, 251, 250)' });
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Workspace' })).toHaveStyle({
      color: 'rgb(20, 20, 19)',
    });
  },
};

/** Titles, notes and bodies wrap inside the card. The visual suite shoots every story at 375px. */
export const LongContent: Story = {
  render: (args) => (
    <Card {...args} as="section" aria-labelledby="long-title">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle id="long-title">Notification preferences for every workspace you belong to</CardTitle>
        <CardNote>
          Choose how each workspace reaches you. Changes apply to all of them at once, including workspaces
          you join later, and you can always override one from its own settings page at
          https://example.com/settings/notifications/workspaces.
        </CardNote>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>
        <p>
          Product updates are a short note when something ships. The weekly digest arrives every Tuesday
          morning and lists what changed across every workspace you can see, grouped by project.
        </p>
        <p>
          Security alerts are always on for owners, because a sign-in from a new device or a changed billing
          contact is something an owner needs to know about the same day.
        </p>
      </CardBody>
    </Card>
  ),
};
```

Two stories assert in a real browser, and both read the computed style so they hold in every shape and both themes: `Nested` and `NestedWithoutBody` compare each card's corner with the `--radius-stadium` and `--radius-surface` tokens read from the document, and `InsideDarkBlock` checks the dark and light fills and the title colors. `NestedWithoutBody` carries `no-visual`, so it adds no screenshot.

```mdx
<Section>

## Header and body

The header holds a title and a note and is ruled off from the body. The title is the card's heading.

<Preview name="card-parts" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Nesting

A card placed in another card, directly or in its body, steps its corner down to the surface radius and takes an outline, because a card on a card has no tone step to set it apart.

<Preview name="card-nested" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Usage

Card is static. It renders on the server and ships no JavaScript. Choose the element with `as` and the heading level with `level`, so the card fits the page's outline.

<Code code={`import { Card, CardBody, CardHeader, CardNote, CardTitle } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function Notifications() {
  return (
    <Card as="section" aria-labelledby="notifications-title">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle id="notifications-title" level={2}>
          Notifications
        </CardTitle>
        <CardNote>Where we reach you, and how often.</CardNote>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>...</CardBody>
    </Card>
  );
}`} />

</Section>

<Section>

## Props

Every part takes `className`, which is merged after its own class, `ref`, and the rest of its HTML attributes. These are the props that choose an element.

### Card

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/card/Card.tsx" type="Pick<CardProps, 'as' | 'className'>" />

### CardTitle

<PropsTable path="../../packages/react/src/card/Card.tsx" type="Pick<CardTitleProps, 'level' | 'className'>" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Accessibility

A card is a div unless `as` says otherwise. A section or an article with a name, from `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label`, is a landmark region, and without a name it is not announced.

The header is a div rather than a header element. A header outside sectioning content is the page's banner, so two cards at page level would add two. The title renders the heading level you choose and looks the same at every level.

</Section>

<Section>

## Design rules

What keeps cards in the system.

<Rules dos={['One title per card, and make it the heading that names the card.', 'Nest a card only for something that stands apart, such as a danger zone.', 'Let the body space its children at 24px and leave their margins alone.']} donts={['Never trim the 32px padding to fit more in. It is what separates a card from its content.', 'Never use a card for a single control or a short label. A card holds a section.']} />

</Section>
```

The first paragraph after each `##` is the section's note, ruled off from the body, as on the Button page. The example titles are `level={3}` and `level={4}` so they nest under the section's own `h2`. The prose never uses the word "Button", so the search tests that rank the Button page first are unaffected.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: React Aria's `I18nProvider` (from `react-aria-components`), `userEvent`, `expect` and `waitFor` from `storybook/test`, Playwright's `emulateMedia({ forcedColors })` through `test.use({ forcedColors: 'active' })`. The classes and attributes every component already ships: `.switch`, `.switch-track`, `.switch-thumb`, `.segmented-option`, `.segmented-track`, `.checkbox-box`, `.radio-indicator`, `.field`, `.field-changed`, `.field-counter`, `[data-selected]`, `[data-changed]`, `[data-stacked]`.
- Produces in commit 1: no new public API and no new class. Two `@media (forced-colors: active)` blocks (`switch.css`, `segmented.css`), which are the only places besides `checkbox.css` and `radio.css` where a color that is not a token may be written, and which a new core test now enforces for every component file. A wrapping chip and a wrapping switch label.
- Produces in commit 2:
  - `COMPONENT_PAGES: { slug: string; title: string }[]`, exported from `apps/docs/tests/support.ts`. It is read from `components/meta.json` and each page's frontmatter, so every test that loops over it covers a page added later.
  - `remarkCode(): (tree: MdastNode) => void` in `apps/docs/lib/remark-code.ts`: a remark plugin that turns a fenced block into the docs' `<Code code lang />`. A page now writes code in a fence.
  - `SearchDialog` takes an optional `onNavigate?: () => void`, called when a result is chosen. `DocsShell` passes the function that closes the drawer.
  - The class `search-body` around the status line and the results. `Keys` renders `table.keys[aria-label="Keyboard"]` and `PropsTable` renders `div.props > table[aria-label="Props"]`, each row `tr` holding a `th[scope="row"]` and a `td`.
  - Removes the docs stand-ins `.type-h1` to `.type-h4`, `.type-small` and `.muted`.
  - A "Components" section in both package READMEs, `scripts/readmes.test.js` to keep it complete, and a patch changeset.
- Produces in commit 3: the `if:` guard on the release workflow's `select-mode` job, and `cancel-in-progress` that is true only for pull requests.

**Decisions made in this task** (each is also in the Appendix B text of commit 1, in a code comment, or in a test):

- **Forced colors is tested in the docs end-to-end suite, with Playwright.** `test.use({ forcedColors: 'active' })` makes Chromium repaint the page with a real forced palette, and the test reads computed styles after that repaint, so it checks what a reader sees. A Storybook play function runs inside the page, where there is no `emulateMedia`. The check compares what a state is drawn with (fill, edge, thumb, mark) rather than a screenshot, because a screenshot of two states differs by the thumb's place alone and would pass the failure it is meant to catch.
- **Right to left is tested in Storybook, in one file.** Layout needs a browser, and the stories already run in one in two themes. The seven stories are in `packages/react/src/rtl/RightToLeft.stories.tsx` and not in each component's own file because the condition is one thing across components: the wrapper that makes the page read right to left is written once, and a new field's author finds one place to add to. They use Arabic words so a line really runs right to left, and they are `no-visual`, since they assert positions and a baseline would depend on which font a machine falls back to for Arabic. Each story was run with `dir="ltr"` as a mutation check: all seven fail.
- **Form reset is one file for seven fields.** `packages/react/test/form-reset.test.tsx` holds a harness per field that does what an app does: it compares the value it is told about with the saved one, and passes the result as `isChanged`. The chip is always in the markup and the stylesheet draws it while the field's root has `data-changed`, so the tests read `data-changed` and the accessible description, which is what the chip is for.
- **Narrow screens put the long web address into the real examples, in the browser.** The test replaces the text of the example's label, hint, error, option, badge, card title and note with an address that has no break in it, and reads the page's sideways overflow. That needs no fixture page and ships no route to a public site. Each target must match at least one element, so a renamed class cannot turn the test into one of nothing.
- **Server Components are proved with React itself, in Node.** The static components (Heading, Text, Eyebrow, Kbd, Badge, Card and its parts, FieldCounter, FieldChanged) are rendered against React's `react-server` build, which has no state, no effects, no refs and no context, so a hook in any of them throws. A docs route would ship a test-only page to a public site, no docs example uses FieldCounter on the server, and the Next.js build would not fail if a static component became a client one. The client components are rendered to HTML in Node, where there is no window and no document, which is what a server page asks of them. The docs end-to-end suite then reads every component page with JavaScript off.
- **Code in an MDX page is written in a fence.** MDX strips up to two columns of indentation from every continuation line of a JS expression, and a template literal inside `<Code code={`...`} />` is one (see the comment in `lib/remark-code.ts`). A fence is markdown and is left alone. The plugin turns each fence into the same `<Code>` the pages used, so nothing else about a code block changes.
- **The props and keys tables have row headers and no header row.** A table that has a header cell for each row needs no column headers, and a visually hidden header row would need `position: absolute` on a `thead`, which some browsers answer by dropping the table's semantics. They keep the same look: a bordered frame (a `div`, so the corner can clip) around a native table. On a phone each row is stacked as a grid, as it was.
- **The package card's rows are 20px apart, not 12px.** A 20px link needs 10px of hit area above and below it. With 12px between the rows the two areas would overlap, and a press between the links would go to the second. At 20px they meet in the middle.
- **The homepage hit-target floor is 73.** The homepage now has 79 controls on a phone with the footer open and 80 on a desktop (it had 61 and 62). The floor keeps the margin it had: 6 under the smaller count.
- **The docs headings now take the library's phone line heights.** `.type-h1` and `.type-h2` set 1.05 and 1.2 under 768px, and Heading keeps its tokens' 1 and 1.222 (Task 2's ruling). Measured on its own, that change left every 1440px screenshot identical. At 375px the pages moved by one pixel, and restoring the old two values made everything else identical again (Step 12 has the numbers).

**What the five checks found** (each fix is in the commit that pins it):

- Forced colors, failed: a switch drew a canvas thumb on a canvas track, so on and off were the same border, and the chosen option of a segmented control was the same canvas as its track and its neighbors. Fixed with a forced-colors block in `switch.css` and one in `segmented.css`. The checkbox, the selected radio, the text field and every focus ring passed unchanged.
- Right to left, passed: every field mirrors, because the stylesheets use logical properties throughout. Nothing was changed.
- Native form reset, passed: all seven fields come back to their defaults, and the count and the chip follow. The documented CheckboxGroup limitation is kept as a comment, and the two cases that work are asserted.
- Narrow screens, failed twice in commit 1: a switch label with a long word was 15px wider than a 320px screen, and a Changed chip with a long `changedLabel` was 782px wider. Both fixed. Extending the loop in commit 2 found a third, in the docs themselves: the props table clipped descriptions on a phone, behind its frame, on seven pages.
- Server Components, passed: all static components render against React's server build, and all client components render to HTML in Node.

`apps/docs/tests/components.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { expect, test, type Locator, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { settled, sideways } from './support';

/**
 * Checks that run across every component page: Windows high contrast, and a
 * narrow screen with a long unbroken word. Each component's own behavior is
 * tested in docs.spec.ts and in its package; these are the conditions the
 * component tests cannot reach from jsdom, which has no layout and no media.
 */

/** Opens a docs page and waits for hydration, so the keys and clicks a test sends are not lost to a page still booting. */
const visit = async (page: Page, url: string): Promise<void> => {
  await page.goto(url);
  await settled(page);
};

/** The slug of every page in the Components section, in the rail's order. */
const COMPONENT_PAGES: string[] = (
  JSON.parse(
    readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../content/docs/components/meta.json', import.meta.url)), 'utf8'),
  ) as { pages: string[] }
).pages;

test('the Components section lists the pages the loops below visit', () => {
  expect(COMPONENT_PAGES.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(15);
  expect(COMPONENT_PAGES).toContain('switch');
  expect(COMPONENT_PAGES).toContain('segmented-control');
});

// ---- Windows high contrast ----------------------------------------------------------------------

/** What an element, or its ::before or ::after, paints with: its fill, its edge and its text. */
const paint = (
  locator: Locator,
  pseudo?: '::before' | '::after',
): Promise<{ fill: string; edge: string; text: string }> =>
  locator.evaluate((element, which) => {
    const style = getComputedStyle(element, which);
    return { fill: style.backgroundColor, edge: style.borderTopColor, text: style.color };
  }, pseudo ?? null);

/**
 * The focus ring an element draws: its outline, and the color it is drawn over. An inset ring (a negative
 * offset) is drawn over the element's own fill; an outset one over the first fill found going up the tree.
 */
const ring = (locator: Locator): Promise<{ style: string; width: number; color: string; behind: string }> =>
  locator.evaluate((element) => {
    const clear = (color: string): boolean => /(?:, 0\)|transparent)$/.test(color);
    const style = getComputedStyle(element);
    let behind: Element | null = parseFloat(style.outlineOffset) < 0 ? element : element.parentElement;
    while (behind && clear(getComputedStyle(behind).backgroundColor)) behind = behind.parentElement;
    return {
      style: style.outlineStyle,
      width: parseFloat(style.outlineWidth),
      color: style.outlineColor,
      behind: getComputedStyle(behind ?? document.documentElement).backgroundColor,
    };
  });

/** A focus ring that can be seen: drawn, 2px or more, and not the color of what it sits on. */
const expectVisibleRing = async (locator: Locator): Promise<void> => {
  const drawn = await ring(locator);
  expect(drawn.style).toBe('solid');
  expect(drawn.width).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
  expect(drawn.color).not.toBe(drawn.behind);
};

test.describe('forced colors', () => {
  // The browser repaints every author color with the reader's palette, so a state drawn by a fill alone
  // disappears. Computed styles are read after that repaint, so they are what the reader sees.
  test.use({ forcedColors: 'active', colorScheme: 'light' });

  /** The switch row whose control has this name, on the page that is open. */
  const switchNamed = (page: Page, name: string): Locator =>
    page.locator('.switch').filter({ has: page.getByRole('switch', { name, exact: true }) });

  test('a switch tells on from off, and its thumb shows against its track', async ({ page }) => {
    await visit(page, '/docs/components/switch');
    const look = async (name: string) => {
      const row = switchNamed(page, name);
      const track = row.locator('.switch-track');
      const thumb = row.locator('.switch-thumb');
      const [trackBox, thumbBox] = [await track.boundingBox(), await thumb.boundingBox()];
      if (!trackBox || !thumbBox) throw new Error('No switch drawn');
      return {
        track: await paint(track),
        thumb: await paint(thumb),
        // Where the thumb sits is the second cue: nearer the start when off and the end when on.
        place: thumbBox.x + thumbBox.width / 2 > trackBox.x + trackBox.width / 2 ? 'end' : 'start',
      };
    };
    const states = {
      on: await look('On'),
      off: await look('Off'),
      disabledOn: await look('Disabled and on'),
      disabledOff: await look('Disabled and off'),
    };
    // A thumb the color of its track is invisible: that was the failure, canvas on canvas.
    for (const state of Object.values(states)) expect(state.thumb.fill).not.toBe(state.track.fill);
    expect(states.on.place).toBe('end');
    expect(states.off.place).toBe('start');
    // On and off differ in paint and not only in place, and so do the disabled pair.
    expect(states.on.track).not.toEqual(states.off.track);
    expect(states.on.thumb).not.toEqual(states.off.thumb);
    expect(states.disabledOn.track).not.toEqual(states.disabledOff.track);
    // A disabled switch does not look enabled.
    expect(states.disabledOn.track).not.toEqual(states.on.track);
    expect(states.disabledOff.thumb).not.toEqual(states.off.thumb);
  });

  test('the focus ring of a switch is drawn', async ({ page }) => {
    await visit(page, '/docs/components/switch');
    await page.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Off', exact: true }).focus();
    await expectVisibleRing(switchNamed(page, 'Off').locator('.switch-track'));
  });

  test('the chosen option of a segmented control is told from the others and from its track', async ({
    page,
  }) => {
    await visit(page, '/docs/components/segmented-control');
    const group = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Appearance' });
    const chosen = await paint(group.locator('.segmented-option[data-selected]'));
    const other = await paint(group.locator('.segmented-option:not([data-selected])').first());
    const track = await paint(group.locator('.segmented-track'));
    expect(chosen.fill).not.toBe(track.fill);
    expect(chosen.fill).not.toBe(other.fill);
    // The label shows on the chosen fill.
    expect(chosen.text).not.toBe(chosen.fill);
    expect(other.text).not.toBe(track.fill);

    // A disabled control still shows its choice, in a paint of its own.
    const disabled = page.locator('.segmented[data-disabled]');
    const kept = await paint(disabled.locator('.segmented-option[data-selected]'));
    const rest = await paint(disabled.locator('.segmented-option:not([data-selected])').first());
    const frame = await paint(disabled.locator('.segmented-track'));
    expect(kept.fill).not.toBe(frame.fill);
    expect(kept.fill).not.toBe(rest.fill);
    expect(kept.text).not.toBe(kept.fill);
    expect(kept).not.toEqual(chosen);
  });

  test('the focus ring of the chosen segmented option shows against its fill', async ({ page }) => {
    await visit(page, '/docs/components/segmented-control');
    const group = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Appearance' });
    await group.getByRole('radio', { name: 'System' }).focus();
    await expectVisibleRing(group.locator('.segmented-option[data-selected]'));
  });

  test('a checked box shows its mark and a selected radio shows its check', async ({ page }) => {
    await visit(page, '/docs/components/checkbox');
    const remember = page.locator('label.checkbox').filter({ hasText: 'Remember me on this device' });
    const show = page.locator('label.checkbox').filter({ hasText: 'Show service descriptions' });
    await expect(remember.getByRole('checkbox')).toBeChecked();
    await expect(show.getByRole('checkbox')).not.toBeChecked();
    const checked = await paint(remember.locator('.checkbox-box'));
    const empty = await paint(show.locator('.checkbox-box'));
    const mark = await paint(remember.locator('.checkbox-box'), '::after');
    expect(checked.fill).not.toBe(empty.fill);
    // The mark is not the color of the box it is drawn on.
    expect(mark.fill).not.toBe(checked.fill);
    await remember.getByRole('checkbox').focus();
    await expectVisibleRing(remember.locator('.checkbox-box'));

    await visit(page, '/docs/components/radio-group');
    const group = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Newsletter frequency' });
    const chosen = group.locator('label.radio[data-selected]');
    const rest = group.locator('label.radio:not([data-selected])').first();
    const check = await paint(chosen.locator('.radio-indicator'), '::after');
    const none = await paint(rest.locator('.radio-indicator'), '::after');
    const dot = await paint(chosen.locator('.radio-indicator'));
    // A drawn check in a color that shows on the dot, against a row with none.
    expect(check.fill).not.toBe(none.fill);
    expect(check.fill).not.toBe(dot.fill);
    await group.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Weekly' }).focus();
    await expectVisibleRing(chosen);
  });

  test('the focus ring of a text field is drawn', async ({ page }) => {
    await visit(page, '/docs/components/text-field');
    const input = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    await input.focus();
    await expectVisibleRing(input);
  });
});

// ---- Narrow screens -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** A web address with no break in it: nothing for the browser to wrap at. */
const LONG = `https://example.com/${'segment-'.repeat(12)}end`;

/**
 * What a long unbroken word is put into, per page: the places a person writes their own text. Each
 * selector must match, so a class that is renamed cannot turn this into a test of nothing. Scoped to the
 * preview stage, so the page's own chrome (its package card, its headings) is not the thing under test.
 */
const LONG_TARGETS: Record<string, string[]> = {
  badge: ['.stage .badge'],
  card: ['.stage .card-title', '.stage .card-note'],
  checkbox: [
    '.stage .field-label',
    '.stage .field-description',
    '.stage .field-error',
    '.stage .checkbox-text',
  ],
  field: ['.stage .field-label', '.stage .field-description', '.stage .field-error', '.stage .field-changed'],
  'radio-group': ['.stage .field-label', '.stage .field-description', '.stage .field-error', '.stage .radio'],
  'segmented-control': ['.stage .field-label', '.stage .segmented-label'],
  switch: ['.stage .switch', '.stage .field-description'],
  'text-area': ['.stage .field-label', '.stage .field-description', '.stage .field-error'],
  'text-field': ['.stage .field-label', '.stage .field-description', '.stage .field-error'],
};

for (const slug of COMPONENT_PAGES) {
  test(`the ${slug} page fits 320px and 375px, with a long web address in its text`, async ({ page }) => {
    for (const width of [320, 375]) {
      await page.setViewportSize({ width, height: 800 });
      await visit(page, `/docs/components/${slug}`);
      expect(await sideways(page), `${slug} at ${String(width)}px`).toBe(0);

      for (const selector of LONG_TARGETS[slug] ?? []) {
        const targets = page.locator(selector);
        expect(await targets.count(), `${selector} on the ${slug} page`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        // The text is replaced in the browser, so the test needs no fixture page and ships no extra route.
        await targets.evaluateAll((elements, text) => {
          for (const element of elements) {
            // A row holds its control and then its words, so only the last run of text is replaced.
            const words = [...element.childNodes]
              .reverse()
              .find((node) => node.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE && node.textContent?.trim());
            if (words) words.textContent = text;
            else element.textContent = text;
          }
        }, LONG);
        // A segmented control restacks a moment after its text changes.
        await expect
          .poll(() => sideways(page), { message: `${selector} on the ${slug} page at ${String(width)}px` })
          .toBe(0);
      }
    }
  });
}

// ---- Server rendering ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * What each component page's examples must draw before any script runs. The pages are server components
 * and the examples are modules a server page imports: the static components (Heading, Text, Eyebrow, Kbd,
 * Badge, Card, FieldCounter) render there directly, and the client ones (everything React Aria) are
 * rendered to HTML on the server and hydrated in the browser. The packages' own tests render both kinds in
 * Node; this proves the production build puts them in the page.
 */
const SERVER_RENDERED: Record<string, string[]> = {
  badge: ['.stage .badge'],
  button: ['.stage .button'],
  card: ['.stage .card', '.stage .card-title', '.stage .card-note'],
  checkbox: ['.stage .checkbox-box'],
  field: ['.stage .field-counter', '.stage .field-changed'],
  'icon-button': ['.stage .icon-button'],
  kbd: ['.stage .kbd'],
  link: ['.stage .link'],
  'radio-group': ['.stage .radio-indicator'],
  'segmented-control': ['.stage .segmented-option'],
  spinner: ['.stage .spinner'],
  switch: ['.stage .switch-thumb'],
  'text-area': ['.stage .textarea'],
  'text-field': ['.stage .input'],
  typography: ['.stage .heading', '.stage .copy', '.stage .eyebrow'],
};

test('every component page is listed as server rendered', () => {
  // A page added to the rail must say what its examples draw, so it cannot skip this check.
  expect(Object.keys(SERVER_RENDERED).sort()).toEqual([...COMPONENT_PAGES].sort());
});

test.describe('without JavaScript', () => {
  test.use({ javaScriptEnabled: false });

  for (const slug of COMPONENT_PAGES) {

      await expect(page.locator('.panel-side .link').first()).toHaveAttribute('href', /^https:\/\//);
    });
  }
});
```

```js
const FORCED_COLORS = '@media (forced-colors: active)';

/** The CSS without its comments and without its forced-colors blocks. */
function outsideForcedColors(css) {
  let rest = css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '');
  for (;;) {
    const start = rest.indexOf(FORCED_COLORS);
    if (start === -1) return rest;
    const end = rest.indexOf('{', start) + 1 + blockAfter(rest, FORCED_COLORS).length + 1;
    rest = rest.slice(0, start) + rest.slice(end);
  }
}
```

```markdown
and not the library's.

**In forced colors the track and the thumb take system colors.** The browser
paints every background canvas, so a canvas thumb sat on a canvas track and an
on switch and an off one drew the same border and nothing else: only the
thumb's place was left to tell them apart. A `@media (forced-colors: active)`
block sets the three properties every state reads. Off is an empty track in
the text color with a solid CanvasText thumb. On is a Highlight track with a
HighlightText thumb, so the pair the system guarantees to read together is the
pair drawn. Disabled off is a GrayText edge and thumb on an empty track, and
disabled on is a GrayText track with a canvas thumb, so the disabled pair still
differ from each other and from the enabled pair. The changed ring and the
focus ring are borders and outlines, which the browser keeps. This block, and
the ones in the checkbox, the radio group and the segmented control, are the
only places in the library that write a color that is not a token.

**A long word in the label breaks inside the row.** The row is a flex box, and
its label is one anonymous item that cannot shrink below its longest word, so
an address in a label widened the row past a 320px screen. The row now has
`min-width: 0`, `max-width: 100%` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`.
```

`packages/react/src/rtl/RightToLeft.stories.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react';
import { I18nProvider } from 'react-aria-components';
import { expect, userEvent, waitFor } from 'storybook/test';
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '../checkbox';
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from '../radio-group';
import { SegmentedControl, SegmentedControlItem } from '../segmented-control';
import { Switch } from '../switch';
import { TextArea } from '../text-area';
import { TextField } from '../text-field';

/**
 * Right-to-left text, checked for every field in a real browser: layout needs a
 * browser, and a jsdom test cannot place a box. Each story renders a field under
 * React Aria's I18nProvider with an Arabic locale, inside a wrapper whose `dir`
 * is `rtl`, and its play function measures where the parts landed. The words are
 * Arabic so the line really reads right to left; the assertions are about edges,
 * which do not depend on which font draws the letters.
 *
 * The stories are `no-visual`: they assert positions, and a baseline of Arabic
 * text would depend on the font a machine falls back to.
 */

/** The width of a form column, in a wrapper that reads right to left. */
function Rtl({ children }: { children: ReactNode }): ReactElement {
  return (
    <I18nProvider locale="ar-EG">
      <div dir="rtl" lang="ar" style={{ width: 'min(28rem, calc(100vw - 2rem))' }}>
        {children}
      </div>
    </I18nProvider>
  );
}

const rect = (element: Element): DOMRect => element.getBoundingClientRect();

function find(scope: ParentNode, selector: string): HTMLElement {
  const element = scope.querySelector<HTMLElement>(selector);
  if (!element) throw new Error(`Nothing matches ${selector}`);
  return element;
}

/** The box of the last run of text in an element, which is how a row holds its words beside its control. */
function lastText(element: Element): DOMRect {
  const walker = document.createTreeWalker(element, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT);
  let last: Node | null = null;
  for (let node = walker.nextNode(); node; node = walker.nextNode()) {
    if (node.textContent?.trim()) last = node;
  }
  if (!last) throw new Error('No text in the element');
  const range = document.createRange();
  range.selectNodeContents(last);
  return range.getBoundingClientRect();
}

/** Two edges are the same edge: less than a pixel apart. */
async function expectSameEdge(a: number, b: number): Promise<void> {
  await expect(Math.abs(a - b)).toBeLessThan(1);
}

/** The box lies inside the other, with half a pixel of rounding. */
async function expectInside(inner: DOMRect, outer: DOMRect): Promise<void> {
  await expect(inner.left).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(outer.left - 0.5);
  await expect(inner.right).toBeLessThanOrEqual(outer.right + 0.5);
}

const meta = {
  title: 'Checks/Right to left',
  tags: ['no-visual'],
} satisfies Meta;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

/**
 * The label starts at the right edge of the field, the Changed chip follows it
 * to its left, and the count sits under the left end of the control, where a
 * line of Arabic ends. The chip's dot is at the chip's start, which is its right.
 */
export const TextFieldMirrored: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Rtl>
      <TextField
        label="اسم مساحة العمل"
        description="يظهر هذا الاسم للفريق كله."
        isChanged
        budget={20}
        defaultValue="مساحة عمل الفريق"
      />
    </Rtl>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const root = rect(find(canvasElement, '.field'));
    const label = rect(find(canvasElement, '.field-label'));
    const chipElement = find(canvasElement, '.field-changed');
    const chip = rect(chipElement);
    const input = rect(find(canvasElement, '.input'));
    const counter = rect(find(canvasElement, '.field-counter'));
    await expectSameEdge(label.right, root.right);
    await expect(chip.right).toBeLessThan(label.left);
    await expectSameEdge(counter.left, input.left);
    for (const box of [label, chip, input, counter]) await expectInside(box, root);
    const dot = getComputedStyle(chipElement, '::before');
    await expect(dot.right).toBe('0px');
    await expect(parseFloat(getComputedStyle(chipElement).paddingRight)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    await expect(getComputedStyle(chipElement).paddingLeft).toBe('0px');
  },
};

/** The same arrangement on a text area: label and chip from the right, the count under the left end. */
export const TextAreaMirrored: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Rtl>
      <TextArea
        label="وصف قصير"
        description="جملة واحدة تظهر في نتائج البحث."
        isChanged
        budget={30}
        defaultValue="مساحة مشتركة لفريق التصميم وضيوفه."
      />
    </Rtl>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const root = rect(find(canvasElement, '.field'));
    const label = rect(find(canvasElement, '.field-label'));
    const chip = rect(find(canvasElement, '.field-changed'));
    const area = rect(find(canvasElement, '.textarea'));
    const counter = rect(find(canvasElement, '.field-counter'));
    await expectSameEdge(label.right, root.right);
    await expect(chip.right).toBeLessThan(label.left);
    await expectSameEdge(counter.left, area.left);
    for (const box of [label, chip, area, counter]) await expectInside(box, root);
  },
};

/**
 * The box is at the right end of its row with the words to its left, and the
 * hint is indented past the box on the right, which is the start side.
 */
export const CheckboxMirrored: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Rtl>
      <Checkbox defaultSelected description="رسالة قصيرة كل أسبوع.">
        أرسل لي ملخصًا أسبوعيًا
      </Checkbox>
    </Rtl>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const root = rect(find(canvasElement, '.checkbox-field'));
    const row = rect(find(canvasElement, '.checkbox'));
    const box = rect(find(canvasElement, '.checkbox-box'));
    const text = rect(find(canvasElement, '.checkbox-text'));
    const hint = find(canvasElement, '.field-description');
    await expectSameEdge(row.right, root.right);
    await expectSameEdge(box.right, row.right);
    await expect(text.right).toBeLessThanOrEqual(box.left + 0.5);
    await expectInside(text, root);
    await expect(getComputedStyle(hint).paddingRight).toBe('32px');
    await expect(getComputedStyle(hint).paddingLeft).toBe('0px');
  },
};

/** Every box of a group is at the right end of its row, down a column and along a row alike. */
export const CheckboxGroupMirrored: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Rtl>
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: '2rem' }}>
        <CheckboxGroup label="أبلغني عبر" defaultValue={['email']}>
          <Checkbox value="email">البريد</Checkbox>
          <Checkbox value="sms">رسالة نصية</Checkbox>
          <Checkbox value="push">إشعار</Checkbox>
        </CheckboxGroup>
        <CheckboxGroup label="أيام الأسبوع" orientation="horizontal" defaultValue={['sat']}>
          <Checkbox value="sat">السبت</Checkbox>
          <Checkbox value="sun">الأحد</Checkbox>
          <Checkbox value="mon">الإثنين</Checkbox>
        </CheckboxGroup>
      </div>
    </Rtl>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const [column, row] = [...canvasElement.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.checkbox-group')];
    if (!column || !row) throw new Error('Two groups expected');
    const columnBoxes = [...column.querySelectorAll('.checkbox-box')].map(rect);
    const columnItems = rect(find(column, '.checkbox-items'));
    await expect(columnBoxes).toHaveLength(3);
    for (const box of columnBoxes) await expectSameEdge(box.right, columnItems.right);
    await expectSameEdge(rect(find(column, '.field-label')).right, rect(column).right);

    // A row of boxes starts at the right: the first option is the rightmost.
    const rowBoxes = [...row.querySelectorAll('.checkbox-box')].map(rect);
    await expect(rowBoxes).toHaveLength(3);
    await expect(rowBoxes[0]?.left ?? 0).toBeGreaterThan(rowBoxes[1]?.left ?? Infinity);
    await expect(rowBoxes[1]?.left ?? 0).toBeGreaterThan(rowBoxes[2]?.left ?? Infinity);
    for (const box of rowBoxes) await expectInside(box, rect(row));

/** The dot is at the right of its row, ahead of the words, and the hint is indented past it. */
export const RadioGroupMirrored: Story = {

    <Rtl>
      <RadioGroup label="تكرار النشرة" defaultValue="weekly">

 * the track, the Changed chip is to the left of the row, and the hint is

export const SwitchMirrored: Story = {

    <Rtl>
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: '1.5rem' }}>

    const gaps = (row: HTMLElement): { start: number; end: number } => {

      const thumb = rect(find(row, '.switch-thumb'));

    await expect(parseFloat(getComputedStyle(hint).paddingRight)).toBeGreaterThan(40);
```
