```tsx
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '../src/checkbox';
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from '../src/radio-group';
import { SegmentedControl, SegmentedControlItem } from '../src/segmented-control';
import { Switch } from '../src/switch';
import { TextArea } from '../src/text-area';
import { TextField } from '../src/text-field';

/**
 * A plain <form> is reset by the browser, with no help from the app: every
 * field must come back to its default value, and what the field draws from its
 * value (the count, the Changed chip) must follow. The chip is the app's to
 * show, as it knows the saved value, so each harness below does what an app
 * does: it compares the value it is told about with the saved one.
 *
 * These checks sit together because the same event reaches seven different
 * pieces of React Aria, each with its own way of listening for it.
 */

const CHANGED = 'Changed';

const formOf = (container: HTMLElement): HTMLFormElement => {
  const form = container.querySelector('form');
  if (!form) throw new Error('No form');
  return form;
};

/** The submitted value of a name, as the browser would send it. */
const sent = (container: HTMLElement, name: string): FormDataEntryValue[] =>
  new FormData(formOf(container)).getAll(name);

/**
 * Whether the field shows its Changed chip. The chip is always in the markup and the stylesheet draws it
 * while the field's root has `data-changed`, which is therefore what a test can see; the chip is read
 * with the control while the root has it.
 */
const showsChip = (container: HTMLElement): boolean => container.querySelector('[data-changed]') !== null;

function ResetButton(): ReactElement {
  return <button type="reset">Reset</button>;
}

function TextFieldForm(): ReactElement {
  const [changed, setChanged] = useState(false);
  return (
    <form>
      <TextField
        label="Workspace name"
        name="workspace"
        defaultValue="Northwind"
        budget={12}
        isChanged={changed}
        onChange={(value) => {
          setChanged(value !== 'Northwind');
        }}
      />
      <ResetButton />
    </form>
  );
}

function TextAreaForm(): ReactElement {
  const [changed, setChanged] = useState(false);
  return (
    <form>
      <TextArea
        label="Welcome message"
        name="welcome"
        defaultValue="Hello there"
        budget={14}
        isChanged={changed}
        onChange={(value) => {
          setChanged(value !== 'Hello there');
        }}
      />
      <ResetButton />
    </form>
  );
}

function CheckboxForm(): ReactElement {
  return (
    <form>
      <Checkbox name="terms" defaultSelected>
        I accept the terms
      </Checkbox>
      <Checkbox name="news">Send me the newsletter</Checkbox>
      <ResetButton />
    </form>
  );
}

function CheckboxGroupForm({ defaults }: { defaults: string[] }): ReactElement {
  const [changed, setChanged] = useState(false);
  return (
    <form>
      <CheckboxGroup
        label="Notify me by"
        name="channels"
        defaultValue={defaults}
        isChanged={changed}
        onChange={(value) => {
          setChanged(value.join() !== defaults.join());
        }}
      >
        <Checkbox value="email">Email</Checkbox>
        <Checkbox value="sms">Text message</Checkbox>
        <Checkbox value="push">Push</Checkbox>
      </CheckboxGroup>
      <ResetButton />
    </form>
  );
}

function RadioGroupForm(): ReactElement {
  const [changed, setChanged] = useState(false);
  return (
    <form>
      <RadioGroup
        label="Newsletter frequency"
        name="frequency"
        defaultValue="monthly"
        isChanged={changed}
        onChange={(value) => {
          setChanged(value !== 'monthly');
        }}
      >
        <Radio value="weekly">Weekly</Radio>
        <Radio value="monthly">Monthly</Radio>
        <Radio value="never">Never</Radio>
      </RadioGroup>
      <ResetButton />
    </form>
  );
}

function SwitchForm(): ReactElement {
  const [changed, setChanged] = useState(false);
  return (
    <form>
      <Switch
        name="digest"
        defaultSelected
        isChanged={changed}
        onChange={(isSelected) => {
          setChanged(!isSelected);
        }}
      >
        Weekly digest
      </Switch>
      <ResetButton />
    </form>
  );
}

function SegmentedControlForm(): ReactElement {
  const [changed, setChanged] = useState(false);
  return (
    <form>
      <SegmentedControl
        label="Appearance"
        name="theme"
        defaultValue="dark"
        isChanged={changed}
        onChange={(value) => {
          setChanged(value !== 'dark');
        }}
      >
        <SegmentedControlItem value="light">Light</SegmentedControlItem>
        <SegmentedControlItem value="dark">Dark</SegmentedControlItem>
        <SegmentedControlItem value="system">System</SegmentedControlItem>
      </SegmentedControl>
      <ResetButton />
    </form>
  );
}

describe('a native form reset', () => {
  it('puts a TextField back, with its count and without its chip', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(<TextFieldForm />);
    const input = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Workspace name' });
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('9 of about 12');
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);

    await user.type(input, ' East');
    expect(input).toHaveValue('Northwind East');
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('14 of about 12');
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(true);
    expect(input).toHaveAccessibleDescription(CHANGED);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }));
    expect(input).toHaveValue('Northwind');
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('9 of about 12');
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);
    expect(input).not.toHaveAccessibleDescription(CHANGED);
    expect(sent(container, 'workspace')).toEqual(['Northwind']);
  });

  it('puts a TextArea back, with its count and without its chip', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(<TextAreaForm />);
    const area = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Welcome message' });
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('11 of about 14');

    await user.type(area, '{Enter}and welcome');
    expect(area).toHaveValue('Hello there\nand welcome');
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('23 of about 14');
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(true);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }));
    expect(area).toHaveValue('Hello there');
    expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('11 of about 14');
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);
    expect(sent(container, 'welcome')).toEqual(['Hello there']);
  });

  it('puts each Checkbox back to checked or unchecked as it started', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(<CheckboxForm />);
    const terms = screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'I accept the terms' });
    const news = screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Send me the newsletter' });

    await user.click(terms);
    await user.click(news);
    expect(terms).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(news).toBeChecked();
    expect(sent(container, 'terms')).toEqual([]);
    expect(sent(container, 'news')).toEqual(['on']);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }));
    expect(terms).toBeChecked();
    expect(news).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(sent(container, 'terms')).toEqual(['on']);
    expect(sent(container, 'news')).toEqual([]);
  });

  // React Aria cannot yet do the one case this leaves out: a reset that must both re-check a default
  // box and uncheck another in the same event loses the re-checked box, because `removeValue` in
  // react-stately's useCheckboxGroupState filters a stale list while `addValue` does not. It is a
  // known issue, recorded in Appendix B and not worked around here. A reset that only adds, or only
  // removes, works, and each is checked below.
  describe('on a CheckboxGroup', () => {
    it('re-checks a default box that was unchecked, and follows with the chip', async () => {
      const user = userEvent.setup();
      const { container } = render(<CheckboxGroupForm defaults={['email', 'sms']} />);
      expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);

      await user.click(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Text message' }));
      expect(sent(container, 'channels')).toEqual(['email']);
      expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(true);

      await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }));
      expect(sent(container, 'channels')).toEqual(['email', 'sms']);
      expect(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Text message' })).toBeChecked();
      expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);
    });

    it('unchecks a box that was added, and follows with the chip', async () => {
      const user = userEvent.setup();
      const { container } = render(<CheckboxGroupForm defaults={['email']} />);

      await user.click(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Push' }));
      expect(sent(container, 'channels')).toEqual(['email', 'push']);
      expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(true);

      await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }));
      expect(sent(container, 'channels')).toEqual(['email']);
      expect(screen.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Push' })).not.toBeChecked();
      expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  it('puts a RadioGroup back on its default choice, without its chip', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(<RadioGroupForm />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Monthly' })).toBeChecked();
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Never' }));
    expect(sent(container, 'frequency')).toEqual(['never']);
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(true);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }));
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Monthly' })).toBeChecked();
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Never' })).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(sent(container, 'frequency')).toEqual(['monthly']);
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('puts a Switch back to on, without its chip', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(<SwitchForm />);
    const control = screen.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Weekly digest' });
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);

    await user.click(control);
    expect(control).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(sent(container, 'digest')).toEqual([]);
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(true);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }));
    expect(control).toBeChecked();
    expect(sent(container, 'digest')).toEqual(['on']);
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('puts a SegmentedControl back on its default option, without its chip', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const { container } = render(<SegmentedControlForm />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' })).toBeChecked();
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);

    await user.click(screen.getByText('System'));
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'System' })).toBeChecked();
    expect(sent(container, 'theme')).toEqual(['system']);
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(true);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset' }));
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'Dark' })).toBeChecked();
    expect(screen.getByRole('radio', { name: 'System' })).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(sent(container, 'theme')).toEqual(['dark']);
    expect(showsChip(container)).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

```tsx
// @vitest-environment node
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import type { ReactElement } from 'react';
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from 'react-dom/server';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

// React as a server component sees it: the react-server build, which has no state, no effects, no refs
// and no context. A component that calls one of those throws here, as it does in a Next.js server tree.
// react-dom/server is outside this module graph, so it renders the elements with the ordinary React.
vi.mock('react', async () => {
  const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
  const entry = join(dirname(require.resolve('react/package.json')), 'react.react-server.js');
  const server = (await import(/* @vite-ignore */ pathToFileURL(entry).href)) as { default: object };
  return { ...server.default, default: server.default };
});

import * as react from 'react';
import { Badge } from '../src/badge';
import { Card, CardBody, CardHeader, CardNote, CardTitle } from '../src/card';
import { FieldChanged, FieldCounter } from '../src/field';
import { Kbd } from '../src/kbd';
import { Eyebrow, Heading, Text } from '../src/typography';

/** The static components: the ones that carry no `'use client'`, so a server component may use them directly. */
const STATIC: [name: string, element: ReactElement, markup: string][] = [
  [
    'Heading',
    <Heading level={1} size={3}>
      Settings
    </Heading>,
    '<h1 class="heading heading-3">Settings</h1>',
  ],
  [
    'Text',
    <Text as="span" size="small" tone="muted">
      Saved a minute ago.
    </Text>,
    '<span class="copy copy-small copy-muted">Saved a minute ago.</span>',
  ],
  ['Eyebrow', <Eyebrow>Workspace</Eyebrow>, '<p class="eyebrow">Workspace</p>'],
  ['Kbd', <Kbd>Esc</Kbd>, '<kbd class="kbd">Esc</kbd>'],
  ['Badge', <Badge tone="info">Beta</Badge>, '<span class="badge badge-info">Beta</span>'],
  [
    'Card and its parts',
    <Card as="section" aria-label="Danger zone">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle level={3}>Delete the workspace</CardTitle>
        <CardNote>This cannot be undone.</CardNote>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardBody>Everything goes.</CardBody>
    </Card>,
    '<section aria-label="Danger zone" class="card"><div class="card-header"><h3 class="card-title">Delete the workspace</h3>' +
      '<p class="card-note">This cannot be undone.</p></div><div class="card-body">Everything goes.</div></section>',
  ],
  [
    'FieldCounter',
    <FieldCounter count={9} budget={12} />,
    '<span role="status" class="field-counter">9 of about 12</span>',
  ],
  ['FieldChanged', <FieldChanged />, '<span class="field-changed">Changed</span>'],
];

describe('the static components in a server component', () => {
  it('are rendered against a React that has no client APIs', () => {
    // Guards the setup: if the mock stopped applying, every test below would pass for the wrong reason.
    const names = Object.keys(react);
    for (const client of [
      'useState',
      'useReducer',
      'useEffect',
      'useLayoutEffect',
      'useRef',
      'useContext',
      'createContext',
      'Component',
    ]) {
      expect(names).not.toContain(client);
    }
    expect(names).toContain('createElement');
  });

  it.each(STATIC)('%s renders to plain markup', (_name, element, markup) => {
    expect(renderToStaticMarkup(element)).toBe(markup);
  });

  it('pass a class and attributes through, so a server page can shape them', () => {
    const html = renderToStaticMarkup(
      <Heading level={2} className="page-title" id="top" data-testid="title">
        Title
      </Heading>,
    );
    expect(html).toBe('<h2 id="top" data-testid="title" class="heading heading-2 page-title">Title</h2>');
  });
});
```

```tsx
// @vitest-environment node
import type { ReactElement } from 'react';
import { renderToString } from 'react-dom/server';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { Button } from '../src/button';
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '../src/checkbox';
import { IconButton } from '../src/icon-button';
import { Link } from '../src/link';
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from '../src/radio-group';
import { SegmentedControl, SegmentedControlItem } from '../src/segmented-control';
import { Spinner } from '../src/spinner';
import { Switch } from '../src/switch';
import { TextArea } from '../src/text-area';
import { TextField } from '../src/text-field';

/**
 * The client components, rendered on the server. A Next.js server page imports them as client references and
 * the server renders them once to HTML before the browser takes over, so each must render with no window, no
 * document and no layout. This file runs in Node, which has none of the three: a component that reads one
 * while it renders throws here. (Effects and observers do not run during a server render, so they may.)
 */
const CLIENT: [name: string, element: ReactElement, contains: string[]][] = [
  ['Button', <Button>Save</Button>, ['<button', 'class="button button-primary', '>Save<']],
  ['Spinner', <Spinner aria-label="Loading" />, ['role="progressbar"', 'class="spinner']],
  ['Link', <Link href="/docs">Docs</Link>, ['<a', 'href="/docs"', 'class="link']],
  [
    'IconButton',
    <IconButton aria-label="Search">
      <svg />
    </IconButton>,
    ['<button', 'aria-label="Search"', 'class="icon-button'],
  ],
  [
    'TextField',
    <TextField label="Name" description="Shown to your team." budget={20} defaultValue="Northwind" />,
    [
      'class="field',
      'class="field-label"',
      'value="Northwind"',
      'Shown to your team.',
      'class="field-counter"',
    ],
  ],
  [
    'TextArea',
    <TextArea label="Notes" defaultValue="Hello" />,
    ['<textarea', 'class="input textarea"', '>Hello<'],
  ],
  [
    'Checkbox',
    <Checkbox defaultSelected>Remember me</Checkbox>,
    ['type="checkbox"', 'checked', 'class="checkbox-box"'],
  ],
  [
    'CheckboxGroup',
    <CheckboxGroup label="Notify me by" defaultValue={['email']}>
      <Checkbox value="email">Email</Checkbox>
      <Checkbox value="sms">Text message</Checkbox>
    </CheckboxGroup>,
    ['role="group"', 'class="field checkbox-group"', 'Text message'],
  ],
  [
    'RadioGroup',
    <RadioGroup label="Frequency" defaultValue="weekly">
      <Radio value="weekly">Weekly</Radio>
      <Radio value="monthly">Monthly</Radio>
    </RadioGroup>,
    ['role="radiogroup"', 'class="radio-indicator"', 'Monthly'],
  ],
  [
    'Switch',
    <Switch defaultSelected>Weekly digest</Switch>,
    ['role="switch"', 'class="switch-track"', 'Weekly digest'],
  ],
  [
    'SegmentedControl',
    <SegmentedControl label="Appearance" defaultValue="dark">
      <SegmentedControlItem value="light">Light</SegmentedControlItem>
      <SegmentedControlItem value="dark">Dark</SegmentedControlItem>
    </SegmentedControl>,
    ['role="radiogroup"', 'class="segmented-track"', 'class="segmented-room"', 'Dark'],
  ],
];

describe('the client components on the server', () => {
  it('has neither a window nor a document, so the renders below prove something', () => {
    expect(typeof window).toBe('undefined');
    expect(typeof document).toBe('undefined');
  });

  it.each(CLIENT)('%s renders to HTML with no browser', (_name, element, contains) => {
    const html = renderToString(element);
    for (const part of contains) expect(html).toContain(part);
  });
});
```

```js
// Throwaway, never committed: full-page screenshots of the production docs build.
// usage: node shots.mjs <repo root> <out dir> <port>
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { join } from 'node:path';

const [repo, outDir, port] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!repo || !outDir || !port) throw new Error('usage: node shots.mjs <repo root> <out dir> <port>');
const { chromium } = createRequire(join(repo, 'apps/docs/package.json'))('@playwright/test');

const components = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(repo, 'apps/docs/content/docs/components/meta.json'), 'utf8')).pages;
const PAGES = {
  home: '/',
  'docs-index': '/docs',
  installation: '/docs/installation',
  theming: '/docs/theming',
  principles: '/docs/design-principles',
  ...Object.fromEntries(components.map((slug) => [slug, `/docs/components/${slug}`])),
};
const SIZES = { 1440: { width: 1440, height: 900 }, 375: { width: 375, height: 812 } };

mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
const browser = await chromium.launch();
for (const scheme of ['light', 'dark']) {
  for (const [width, viewport] of Object.entries(SIZES)) {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport, colorScheme: scheme, reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    for (const [name, path] of Object.entries(PAGES)) {
      await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${path}`, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
      await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
      await page.waitForTimeout(300);
      await page.screenshot({ path: join(outDir, `${name}--${scheme}-${width}.png`), fullPage: true, animations: 'disabled' });
    }
    await context.close();
  }
}
await browser.close();
console.log(`wrote ${outDir}`);
```

```js
// Throwaway, never committed: exact pixel comparison of two screenshot folders.
// usage: node diff.mjs <repo root> <folder A> <folder B>
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { join } from 'node:path';

const [repo, a, b] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!repo || !a || !b) throw new Error('usage: node diff.mjs <repo root> <folder A> <folder B>');
const store = join(repo, 'node_modules/.pnpm');
const pngjs = readdirSync(store).find((name) => name.startsWith('pngjs@'));
if (!pngjs) throw new Error(`pngjs not found in ${store}`);
const { PNG } = createRequire(join(store, pngjs, 'node_modules/pngjs/package.json'))('pngjs');

let differing = 0;
for (const file of readdirSync(a).filter((name) => name.endsWith('.png')).sort()) {
  const x = PNG.sync.read(readFileSync(join(a, file)));
  const y = PNG.sync.read(readFileSync(join(b, file)));
  if (x.width !== y.width || x.height !== y.height) {
    differing++;
    console.log(file.padEnd(40), `size ${x.width}x${x.height} vs ${y.width}x${y.height}`);
    continue;
  }
  let count = 0;
  let minX = Infinity, minY = Infinity, maxX = -1, maxY = -1;
  for (let i = 0; i < x.data.length; i += 4) {
    if (x.data[i] !== y.data[i] || x.data[i + 1] !== y.data[i + 1] || x.data[i + 2] !== y.data[i + 2] || x.data[i + 3] !== y.data[i + 3]) {
      count++;
      const pixel = i / 4;
      const px = pixel % x.width;
      const py = Math.floor(pixel / x.width);
      minX = Math.min(minX, px); maxX = Math.max(maxX, px); minY = Math.min(minY, py); maxY = Math.max(maxY, py);
    }
  }
  if (count > 0) differing++;
  console.log(file.padEnd(40), `${x.width}x${x.height}`, count === 0 ? 'identical' : `${count} px differ in x ${minX}-${maxX}, y ${minY}-${maxY}`);
}
console.log(differing === 0 ? 'ALL IDENTICAL' : `${differing} file(s) differ`);
```

Build the docs with `--force` (a cached build of an earlier state would be served otherwise), serve them and shoot them twice. The second set proves the shots are deterministic, so any later difference is the change and not noise.

```bash
pnpm turbo run build --filter=@snapshot-ui/docs --force
lsof -nP -iTCP:3100 -sTCP:LISTEN
(cd apps/docs && exec node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next start -p 3100 -H 127.0.0.1) > "$SHOTS/next.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$SHOTS/next.pid"
sleep 5 && curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:3100/
node "$SHOTS/shots.mjs" "$PWD" "$SHOTS/before" 3100
node "$SHOTS/shots.mjs" "$PWD" "$SHOTS/before-again" 3100
node "$SHOTS/diff.mjs" "$PWD" "$SHOTS/before" "$SHOTS/before-again" | tail -1
kill "$(cat "$SHOTS/next.pid")"
lsof -nP -iTCP:3100 -sTCP:LISTEN
```

Each shot run writes 80 images: twenty pages (`/`, `/docs`, the installation, theming and design principles pages, and the 15 component pages) in light and dark at 1440 and 375. The comparison ends in `ALL IDENTICAL`. The last `lsof` prints nothing.

```ts
test('the search dialog keeps its height while the query changes', async ({ page }) => {
  await visit(page, '/docs');
  await page.keyboard.press('ControlOrMeta+k');
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Search the docs' });
  const field = dialog.getByRole('searchbox', { name: 'Search' });
  const height = async (): Promise<number> => (await dialog.boundingBox())?.height ?? 0;

  // Nothing typed yet: the floor under the results, 20rem, plus the field and the footer.
  const resting = await height();
  await expect(dialog.locator('.search-body')).toHaveCSS('min-height', '320px');
  expect(resting).toBeGreaterThan(320);
  await field.fill('zzzzqx');
  await expect(dialog.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('Nothing matches "zzzzqx"');
  expect(await height()).toBeCloseTo(resting, 0);

  // Typing never takes it under that floor: not while a search is still out and its results are not
  // listed, and not once they have come back.

    await field.fill(text);
    expect(await height()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(resting - 0.5);
  }
  await expect(dialog.getByRole('link', { name: /Spinner/ }).first()).toBeVisible();
  expect(await height()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(resting - 0.5);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Code blocks keep their indentation**

The root cause is in MDX, not in the page: `micromark-factory-mdx-expression` eats up to two columns of whitespace from the start of every continuation line of a JS expression, so `<Code code={`...`} />` loses them (the Button page's `return (` was flush left, and `<Button` two columns short). A fenced block is markdown, which is not touched. The plugin turns each fence into the `<Code>` the pages used.

`apps/docs/lib/remark-code.ts`:

```ts
/** The part of an mdast node this plugin reads and writes. The full types live in @types/mdast, which the docs do not depend on. */
interface MdastNode {
  type: string;
  value?: string;
  lang?: string | null;
  children?: MdastNode[];
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

/**
 * Turns every fenced block in an MDX page into the docs' own `<Code>` block.
 *
 * Code is written in a fence and not in `<Code code={`...`} />` because MDX
 * strips up to two columns of indentation from every continuation line of a JS
 * expression, a template literal included (micromark-extension-mdx-expression
 * eats `indentSize` = 2 so that an expression nested in markdown reads like the
 * JS around it). A fence is markdown and is not touched, so the code on the page
 * is the code in the file, and so is the text the copy button copies.
 */
export function remarkCode(): (tree: MdastNode) => void {
  const convert = (parent: MdastNode): void => {
    const { children } = parent;
    if (!children) return;
    children.forEach((child, index) => {
      if (child.type !== 'code') {
        convert(child);
        return;
      }
      const attributes = [{ type: 'mdxJsxAttribute', name: 'code', value: child.value ?? '' }];
      if (child.lang) attributes.push({ type: 'mdxJsxAttribute', name: 'lang', value: child.lang });
      children[index] = { type: 'mdxJsxFlowElement', name: 'Code', attributes, children: [] };
    });
  };
  return convert;
}
```

It must run before Fumadocs' own plugins, and naming MDX options for a collection replaces Fumadocs' defaults, so the preset is applied again with the plugin in front.

In `apps/docs/lib/source.ts`, replace:

```ts
import { lucideIconsPlugin } from 'fumadocs-core/source/lucide-icons';

import { defineDocs } from 'fumadocs-mdx/macro';

const docs = defineDocs({
  dir: 'content/docs',
  docs: { schema: pageSchema },
  meta: { schema: metaSchema },
});
```

with:

```ts
import { metaSchema, pageSchema } from 'fumadocs-core/source/schema';
import { applyMdxPreset } from 'fumadocs-mdx/config';
import { defineDocs } from 'fumadocs-mdx/macro';
import { remarkCode } from './remark-code';

const docs = defineDocs({
  dir: 'content/docs',
  docs: {
    schema: pageSchema,
    // Naming MDX options here replaces Fumadocs' defaults, so the preset is applied again, with the
    // fence plugin ahead of the others.
    mdxOptions: applyMdxPreset({ remarkPlugins: (defaults) => [remarkCode, ...defaults] }),
  },

});
```

In `apps/docs/content/docs/components/field.mdx`, replace:

```mdx
[Text field](/docs/components/text-field) renders all of this in one element. For a custom layout, put the parts inside a React Aria field: Label names the control, Description and FieldError become its description, and FieldError appears only while the field is invalid. Put the `field` class and `data-changed` on the field's root, and keep the chip in the label row, where the stylesheet shows or hides it.

<Code code={`import { TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { Description, FieldChanged, FieldCounter, FieldError, Input, Label } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function ShortDescription({
  value,
  onChange,
  isChanged,
}: {
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  isChanged: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <TextField
      className="field"
      data-changed={isChanged ? '' : undefined}
      value={value}
      onChange={onChange}
    >
      <div className="field-head">
        <Label>Short description</Label>
        <FieldChanged />
      </div>
      <Input />
      <Description>One sentence, for search results.</Description>
      <FieldError />
      <FieldCounter count={value.length} budget={60} />
    </TextField>
  );
}`} />

The classes are `field`, `field-head`, `field-label`, `field-description`, `field-error`, `field-counter` and `field-changed`, so the same parts work in plain HTML.
```

with:

````mdx
[Text field](/docs/components/text-field) renders all of this in one element. For a custom layout, put the parts inside a React Aria field: Label names the control, Description and FieldError become its description, and FieldError appears only while the field is invalid. Put the `field` class and `data-changed` on the field's root, and keep the chip in the label row, where the stylesheet shows or hides it.

```tsx
import { TextField } from 'react-aria-components';
import { Description, FieldChanged, FieldCounter, FieldError, Input, Label } from '@snapshot-ui/react';

export function ShortDescription({
  value,
  onChange,
  isChanged,
}: {
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  isChanged: boolean;
}) {

      value={value}
      onChange={onChange}
    >
      <div className="field-head">
        <Label>Short description</Label>
        <FieldChanged />
      </div>
      <Input />
      <Description>One sentence, for search results.</Description>
      <FieldError />
      <FieldCounter count={value.length} budget={60} />
    </TextField>
  );
}
```

The classes are `field`, `field-head`, `field-label`, `field-description`, `field-error`, `field-counter` and `field-changed`, so the same parts work in plain HTML.
````

In `apps/docs/content/docs/installation.mdx`, replace:

```mdx
Both packages, with React 19 or later.

<Code lang="bash" code="pnpm add @snapshot-ui/react @snapshot-ui/core" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Import the stylesheet

Once, at the root of your app. `styles.css` holds the tokens and every component. `base.css` is optional: it sets the page background, the body type, the font rendering details and an ink focus ring for your own links and fields.

<Code code={`import '@snapshot-ui/core/styles.css';
import '@snapshot-ui/core/base.css';`} />

The CSS sits in cascade layers, so your own unlayered CSS always wins, and Tailwind's utilities win over the components.

</Section>

<Section>

## Load the font

Snapshot UI sets body text at weight 450, which only a variable font has. In Next.js, `next/font` self-hosts it and sets the family the tokens read:

<Code code={`import { Sofia_Sans } from 'next/font/google';

const sofia = Sofia_Sans({ subsets: ['latin'], display: 'swap', variable: '--font-sans' });

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" className={sofia.variable}>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}`} />

Anywhere else, install `@fontsource-variable/sofia-sans` and import it once. The font stack already includes its family name.

</Section>

<Section>

## Next.js server components

Every component file carries `'use client'`, so a server component or an MDX page can render them directly. React Aria itself must never be imported into a server component.

</Section>

<Section>

## Tailwind CSS, if you use it

`tailwind.css` exposes the tokens as utilities, such as `bg-canvas`, `text-slate`, `rounded-control` and `p-part`. It also removes Tailwind's default radii, text sizes and shadows, so an off-system value like `rounded-lg` compiles to nothing.

<Code lang="css" code={`@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@snapshot-ui/core/tailwind.css';
@import '@snapshot-ui/core/styles.css';`} />

</Section>
```

with:

````mdx
Both packages, with React 19 or later.

```bash
pnpm add @snapshot-ui/react @snapshot-ui/core
```

</Section>

<Section>

## Import the stylesheet

Once, at the root of your app. `styles.css` holds the tokens and every component. `base.css` is optional: it sets the page background, the body type, the font rendering details and an ink focus ring for your own links and fields.

```tsx
import '@snapshot-ui/core/styles.css';
import '@snapshot-ui/core/base.css';
```

The CSS sits in cascade layers, so your own unlayered CSS always wins, and Tailwind's utilities win over the components.

</Section>

<Section>

## Load the font

Snapshot UI sets body text at weight 450, which only a variable font has. In Next.js, `next/font` self-hosts it and sets the family the tokens read:

```tsx
import { Sofia_Sans } from 'next/font/google';

const sofia = Sofia_Sans({ subsets: ['latin'], display: 'swap', variable: '--font-sans' });

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" className={sofia.variable}>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

Anywhere else, install `@fontsource-variable/sofia-sans` and import it once. The font stack already includes its family name.

</Section>

<Section>

## Next.js server components

Every component file carries `'use client'`, so a server component or an MDX page can render them directly. React Aria itself must never be imported into a server component.

</Section>

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@snapshot-ui/core/tailwind.css';
@import '@snapshot-ui/core/styles.css';
```

</Section>
````

```mdx
Set `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on any element. With no attribute on the page, dark follows the system setting.

<Code code={`<html data-theme="dark">`} />

With `next-themes`, use the attribute mode:

</Section>

<Section>

## Corner shape

Set `data-shape` to `rounded`, `soft` or `square`. Every corner in the library comes from one scale, so one attribute recuts all of them. Dots, such as a radio's indicator, stay round in every shape, because there roundness carries meaning.

<Preview name="theme-shapes" />

</Section>

<Section>

## Nesting

Both attributes work on any element, and the nearest one wins. A light card inside a dark page takes its own colors and its own text color.

<Code code={`<main data-theme="dark">
  <section data-theme="light" data-shape="square">...</section>
</main>`} />

</Section>

<Section>

## Tokens

Every value is a CSS variable you can read, such as `var(--color-ink)`, `var(--radius-control)` or `var(--spacing-peer)`. The same tokens are available in JavaScript, with each mode's value:

tokens.color.slate.var; // 'var(--color-slate)'
tokens.radius.pill.modes.shape.soft; // '12px'`} />

</Section>
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Search closes the drawer, and keeps its height**

`SearchDialog` tells its parent when a result is chosen, and closes itself first. The order matters: a dialog that closes returns focus to what opened it, which is a button inside the drawer, and the drawer's own cleanup then moves focus to the menu button, so the last word is the drawer's. (Reversed, the focus ends on a hidden button.)

```tsx
   * behind the search belongs to the page it was opened on, and a result may
   * leave that page, or stay on it and move to a heading, which no change of
   * path announces.
   */
  onNavigate?: () => void;
}): ReactElement {
  const dialog = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null);
```

with:

```tsx
import type { ReactElement } from 'react';

/**
 * A keyboard table: each row is the keys, then what they do. The keys are the
 * row's header, so a screen reader announces them with the action.
 */
export function Keys({ rows }: { rows: [keys: string, action: string][] }): ReactElement {
  return (
    <table className="keys" aria-label="Keyboard">
      <tbody>
        {rows.map(([keys, action]) => (
          <tr className="key-row" key={keys}>
            <th scope="row">
              {keys.split(' ').map((key) => (
                <Kbd key={key} style={{ marginRight: 6 }}>
                  {key}
                </Kbd>
              ))}
            </th>
            <td>{action}</td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}
```

```tsx

/**
 * Props from the library's own types and JSDoc. `type` is usually a Pick of
 * the component's props: React Aria's inherited props include dozens of DOM
 * events nobody needs listed.
 */
export async function PropsTable({ path, type }: { path: string; type: string }): Promise<ReactElement> {
  const [doc] = await generator.generateTypeTable(
    { path, type },
    { typeSimplifier: { shouldSimplify: () => false } },
  );
  const entries = [...(doc?.entries ?? [])].sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
  return (
    <div className="props">
      {entries.map((entry) => {
        const fallback = entry.tags.find((tag) => tag.name === 'default')?.text;
        return (
          <div className="prop" key={entry.name}>
            <div>
              <div className="prop-name">{entry.name}</div>
              <span className="prop-type">{entry.type.replace(/ \| undefined$/, '')}</span>
            </div>
            <div>
              <p>{inline(entry.description)}</p>
              {fallback ? <p className="prop-default">Default: {fallback}</p> : null}
            </div>
          </div>
        );
      })}
    </div>
  );
```

with:

```tsx

/**
 * Props from the library's own types and JSDoc, as a table whose rows are named
 * by the prop. `type` is usually a Pick of the component's props: React Aria's
 * inherited props include dozens of DOM events nobody needs listed.
 */
export async function PropsTable({ path, type }: { path: string; type: string }): Promise<ReactElement> {
  const [doc] = await generator.generateTypeTable(
    { path, type },
    { typeSimplifier: { shouldSimplify: () => false } },
  );
  const entries = [...(doc?.entries ?? [])].sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
  return (
    <div className="props">
      <table aria-label="Props">
        <tbody>
          {entries.map((entry) => {
            const fallback = entry.tags.find((tag) => tag.name === 'default')?.text;
            return (
              <tr className="prop" key={entry.name}>
                <th scope="row">
                  <div className="prop-name">{entry.name}</div>
                  <span className="prop-type">{entry.type.replace(/ \| undefined$/, '')}</span>
                </th>
                <td>
                  <p>{inline(entry.description)}</p>
                  {fallback ? <p className="prop-default">Default: {fallback}</p> : null}
                </td>
              </tr>
            );
          })}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  );
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Check every page in a browser**

The suites run axe on the component pages and read the sideways scroll at two phone widths, so check the rest yourself with a throwaway script: the homepage, the four guide pages and the 15 component pages, in light and dark, at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440 pixels, with axe and the page's sideways overflow. Create `$SHOTS/scan.mjs`:

```js
// Throwaway: every docs page and the homepage, axe in light and dark and sideways scroll at four widths.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { join } from 'node:path';
const [repo, port] = process.argv.slice(2);
const require = createRequire(join(repo, 'apps/docs/package.json'));
const { chromium } = require('@playwright/test');
const AxeBuilder = require('@axe-core/playwright').default;
const components = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(repo, 'apps/docs/content/docs/components/meta.json'), 'utf8')).pages;
const paths = ['/', '/docs', '/docs/installation', '/docs/theming', '/docs/design-principles', ...components.map((s) => `/docs/components/${s}`)];
const browser = await chromium.launch();
let problems = 0;
for (const scheme of ['light', 'dark']) {
  for (const width of [375, 768, 1024, 1440]) {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height: 900 }, colorScheme: scheme });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    for (const path of paths) {
      await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${path}`, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
      const over = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth);
      const { violations } = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();
      if (over !== 0 || violations.length > 0) {
        problems++;
        console.log(`${scheme} ${width} ${path}: overflow ${over}, axe ${violations.map((v) => v.id).join(',')}`);
      }
    }
    await context.close();
  }
}
await browser.close();
console.log(`${paths.length} pages x 2 themes x 4 widths: ${problems} problem(s)`);
```

```bash
(cd apps/docs && exec node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next start -p 3100 -H 127.0.0.1) > "$SHOTS/next.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$SHOTS/next.pid"
sleep 5
node "$SHOTS/scan.mjs" "$PWD" 3100
kill "$(cat "$SHOTS/next.pid")"
lsof -nP -iTCP:3100 -sTCP:LISTEN
```

Expected: `20 pages x 2 themes x 4 widths: 0 problem(s)`. The last `lsof` prints nothing.

- [ ] **Step 12: Take the "after" screenshots and compare**

The docs build from Step 9 is the one to serve.

```bash
pnpm turbo run build --filter=@snapshot-ui/docs --force
lsof -nP -iTCP:3100 -sTCP:LISTEN
(cd apps/docs && exec node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next start -p 3100 -H 127.0.0.1) > "$SHOTS/next.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$SHOTS/next.pid"
sleep 5 && curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:3100/
node "$SHOTS/shots.mjs" "$PWD" "$SHOTS/after" 3100
node "$SHOTS/diff.mjs" "$PWD" "$SHOTS/before" "$SHOTS/after"
kill "$(cat "$SHOTS/next.pid")"
lsof -nP -iTCP:3100 -sTCP:LISTEN
```

Expected: the result line is `80 file(s) differ`, and each difference is one of these (the numbers are the ones observed; light and dark are alike):
- At 1440, `home` is 370px taller (`1440x5061` becomes `1440x5431`): the footer's Components column lists 15 pages where it listed 3. Nothing else on the homepage differs in size.
- At 1440, `docs-index`, `principles` and `spinner` differ only in the package card (`x 1077-1407`, a strip about 100px tall: the rows are 20px apart and the links are 20px tall).
- At 1440, the 16 other pages also differ in the code blocks that have indented lines (for example `button`: `x 410-988, y 1452-1658` is the SaveBar block). Lines that were flush left are indented now; no other region moves.
- At 375, every page is 17 to 18px taller (the package card: 8px more between each of its three rows, 16px in all, and a link row a fraction of a pixel taller), except `home`, which is 1px shorter (`7589` becomes `7588`), and the pages with a props table that was clipped on a phone, which are taller because the descriptions now wrap: `link` (`3962` to `4100`), `radio-group` (`9104` to `9549`), `segmented-control` (`8799` to `9142`), `switch` (`6595` to `6792`), `text-area` (`8379` to `8697`), `text-field` (`7731` to `8040`) and `checkbox` (`10972` to `11640`).

About the typography stand-ins, measured while building with that change alone (before the catalog, the footer and the package card were touched): at 1440 all 40 images were identical to before. At 375 the pages moved by about a pixel under the docs title, because `.type-h2` set a 1.2 line height under 768px and Heading keeps its token's 1.222 (and the old `.type-h1` set 1.05 where Heading's is 1). To prove that is the only reason, the same shots were taken again with `@media (width < 768px) { .heading-1 { line-height: 1.05 } .heading-2 { line-height: 1.2 } }` added to every page (Playwright's `page.addStyleTag`): of the 80 images, every one was then pixel for pixel what it was before, except the two 375px shots of the typography page, whose own Heading examples that same rule changes.

The last `lsof` prints nothing.

## Commit 3: the workflows

- [ ] **Step 1: Guard the release workflow**

The job every other job needs is the one that gets the guard, so a fork runs none of them (a skipped job skips the jobs that need it).

In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, replace:

```yaml
jobs:
  select-mode:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
```

with:

```yaml
jobs:
  select-mode:
    # A fork has no release to make and no npm environment to publish from. The other jobs need this one,
    # so on a fork they are skipped with it.
    if: github.repository == 'amirehsan/snapshot-ui'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Cancel only what is stale**

A newer push to a pull request makes the older run pointless. A push to `main` must keep its own result, so it is never cancelled by the next one.

In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, replace:

```yaml
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
```

with:

```yaml
  contents: read

# A newer push to a pull request makes the older run stale. A push to main never does: every commit on
# main keeps its own result.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Validate both files, and check that no pin moved**

```bash
ruby -ryaml -e 'ARGV.each { |f| YAML.load_file(f); puts "#{f}: parsed" }; r = YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/release.yml"); puts "if: #{r["jobs"]["select-mode"]["if"]}"; c = YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/ci.yml"); puts "cancel-in-progress: #{c["concurrency"]["cancel-in-progress"]}"' .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/release.yml
git diff -U0 -- .github | grep '^[-+]' | grep -c 'uses:'
pnpm format:check
```

Expected: both files parse, `if: github.repository == 'amirehsan/snapshot-ui'` and `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}` are printed, the `grep -c` prints `0` (no `uses:` line was added or removed, so every SHA pin is as it was), and the format check passes. (The `yaml` package, which Phase 1a used, does the same job: `YAML.parseDocument(text).errors` is empty for both.)

- [ ] **Step 4: Run everything**

```bash
pnpm verify
```

Expected: it exits 0, with the same totals as commit 2 (the workflows are not tested by the suites).

```bash
git add .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/release.yml
git commit -m "ci: guard the release workflow and keep runs on main"
```
